News.title: Student hikers’ chilling final warning to friends before pair were found dead just one mile from their abandoned tent
News.content:
Next

TWO college students who were found dead during a weekend hiking trip had sent friends a map of their planned route and chillingly warned they would turn back if conditions became too dangerous.

Jackson “Jack” Donlon, 20, and Kaden Matsuda, 19, were discovered near each other in a snow-filled basin on West Apostle Mountain in Colorado.



The pair had left Colorado Mountain College’s Leadville campus on Friday, October 23, for what was supposed to be a weekend hiking and climbing trip in the Collegiate Peaks.

Before heading into the backcountry, Donlon and Matsuda sent friends a map showing Ice Mountain as their intended destination, with the area around Winfield and the trailhead also marked.



The Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement reported by ABC7, “According to friends, Kaden and Jackson planned on returning from the hike on Saturday if they didn’t feel safe. If they continued to Ice Mountain, they would return on Sunday.”

The sheriff’s office did not identify which friend received the message or warning, but said interviews established the pair’s intended route and expected return plans.

Hikers TRAIL TRAGEDY Three hikers found dead at Grand Canyon as temperatures hit triple digits

Those final communications would take on a haunting significance after Saturday passed without an early return and Sunday then came and went without either student making it back to campus.

By Monday morning, staff at Colorado Mountain College contacted the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office and a major search operation was launched.

Donlon was from Queensbury, New York, while Matsuda was from Ridgway, Colorado, and both had moved to Leadville to study subjects closely tied to their passion for the outdoors.

Friends and relatives described both men as experienced hikers who were expected to have appropriate clothing with them, while their technical climbing equipment also appeared to have been taken into the mountains.



Conditions deteriorated dramatically after they set out, with days of rain followed by heavy snow that dumped between one and two feet on Ice Mountain and produced even deeper drifts in places.

Ice Mountain rises to almost 14,000 feet and is considered a difficult technical climb even in good weather, with the heavy snow making conditions even more treacherous.

Deputies found Matsuda’s vehicle near the Mount Huron trailhead, where snow had built around it and provided another clue that the students had entered the wilderness before the storm arrived.



Investigators also discovered that neither student’s phone had been used for at least 48 hours, although authorities cautioned that reception was extremely poor and the devices may have been switched off to preserve their batteries.

The search took a more worrying turn on Tuesday when a helicopter crew spotted the pair’s collapsed tent near Lake Ann, prompting rescuers to make their way to the campsite on foot.

Inside were sleeping bags, a stove and clothing, but neither student was there and investigators found no visible footprints surrounding the campsite in the newly fallen snow.

Authorities said there was no snow underneath the tent, suggesting it had been erected before the storm, while the absence of fresh tracks raised the possibility that the students had not returned to camp after the snowfall began.

Their climbing equipment was also missing from the tent, vehicle and dorm rooms, leading investigators to believe Donlon and Matsuda had taken it with them when they headed farther into the mountains.



The difficult conditions prompted an extensive operation involving around 60 search-and-rescue volunteers as well as helicopters, drones, dogs and other specialist resources across the rugged mountain terrain.

Colorado has previously seen other deadly incidents involving experienced outdoorsmen in its mountain wilderness, while severe snowfall has also complicated searches for a missing snowboarder in the state.

Search teams ultimately found Donlon and Matsuda at around 3.30pm on Wednesday, October 28, near each other in a basin of West Apostle Mountain, roughly a mile from the campsite they had left behind.

Authorities said foul play was not suspected and stressed that they would not speculate about what caused the students’ deaths before autopsies and a detailed investigation had been completed.

The deaths devastated Colorado Mountain College, where both students had quickly made an impression on classmates and staff.



Matsuda, who was studying to become a wildland firefighter, was remembered by classmates and faculty as “kind, intelligent and welcoming.”

CMC Leadville vice president and campus dean Ben Cairns said the pair had come to the college “to learn, to explore and to build their futures.”

Friend Jack Adirondack said some of the best days he and others had spent out skiing were with Donlon, adding that everyone at Ski Or Die NY was “devastated and overall lost for words by all of this.”

He signed off his tribute, “Rest easy buddy. We all love you and will miss you greatly.”

Meredith Montgomery wrote on Facebook, “When I think about growing up, I think about how I did it with Jack,” describing him as one of her first true friends and recalling years of chairlift rides, ski trips and sleepovers.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She remembered Donlon collecting her coat at the top of a race course so she would not have to ride alone in the cold, and said he “always went out of his way” to include her younger brother and ask about her older siblings.

Ski Or Die NY described Donlon as “a friend, an adventurer, and someone who was always hungry for what was next,” before ending its tribute, “Rest easy, JD. Until we meet again. We love you. Ski in Peace.”

News.title: Girlfriend reveals chilling final words after ‘kidnapped’ boyfriend’s severed head washes up in Bali on Valentine’s trip
News.content:
Next

THE girlfriend of a Ukrainian businessman whose severed head was found on a Bali beach has revealed his final words begging her not to call the police.

Ukrainian tourist Igor Komarov, 28, was allegedly abducted on February 15 while holidaying on the Indonesian island with his girlfriend.



His head and other body parts were discovered on a shoreline weeks after he vanished during a romantic Valentine’s Day trip.

Heartbroken influencer Yeva Mishalova, 25, has broken her silence over the horrific alleged murder of Igor.



She said she received desperate voice messages from her severely injured boyfriend as his captors demanded a £7.5million ransom.

He told her: “Kitten, I love you. Don’t worry.



Igor promised he would return and urged her not to check out of their hotel.

“I’ll be back soon. Everything will be fine. Just don’t worry. And don’t go to the police,” he said.



Yeva said she could see his face was black and blue.

She explained: “He was having such difficulty speaking that I realised he was really in a terrible state, that he was very badly hurt.”

Speaking to Ukrainian interviewer Vasyl Tymoshenko, Yeva revealed the couple’s final happy hours together.



She said they took a motorcycle lesson which led to his kidnapping.

They had been enjoying Bali’s beaches, waterfalls and the freedom to spend entire days together, away from their busy lives in Kyiv, she said.

On the night of his disappearance, Yeva said they had been watching Netflix period drama Bridgerton in their hotel room.



He left between 8pm and 9pm for motorcycle training but promised to return shortly.

“I’ll text you in half an hour. Order me a club sandwich,” he told her.

He returned at about 9.30pm to collect his helmet, saying his instructor wanted to take him beyond the hotel grounds to practise cornering.

She was “washing my hair” and barely saw his face but warned him that riding outside the hotel in the dark sounded dangerous.

He told her: “No, no, kitten, kitten, don’t worry. I’ll be back soon.”



At around 10pm, he sent her a loving message then an hour later he stopped answering, she explained.

Around midnight, chilling voice recordings came from an unknown number, along with videos showing Igor’s injuries.

They also demanded she send over cash, she alleged.

“They started sending videos and saying, ‘Ten million, ten million, ten million,’” she said.

An urgent search operation was launched involving authorities and loved ones.



It went on for five days before he was found.

Yeva said: “First they beat him very badly. Then there was what they did to his fingers. Then his ribs.

“I don’t know who exactly cut off his fingers, who broke his ribs, or who did everything else.

“They all did it together. All of them. Every single one of them took part…

“They’re not human.”



She also revealed there were additional unpublished torture videos beyond those revealed at the time of his death.

“I’m the only one who has them,” she said.

“I’m trying not to listen to them again now, because they’re the last things he said.”

Yeva said she deliberately continued posting old photos on Instagram while the search continued in a bid to keep her parents finding out so she could stay and help find her boyfriend.

“I understood that if my parents found out, they would do everything to get me out of there,” she said.



“And I wasn’t leaving without Igor.”

She claimed the motorcycle instructor Igor was with had left Bali for Thailand the day after her partner vanished.

Yeva alleged he was likely an accomplice.

An international manhunt is underway for six suspects, including Russian, Ukrainian and Kazakh nationals.

In May, private investigators working with Komarov’s family announced a £75,000 reward for information leading to their capture.



Investigators have revealed the operation was professionally organised.

They even pointed out the possible involvement of intelligence services.

Igor’s business dealings are still shrouded in mystery.

Kidnap videos allegedly show him admitting involvement in fraudulent call-centre operations targeting Russians.

The influencer insisted his businesses were legitimate, involving metals and grain.



It has been claimed he was forced to read scripted statements while being tortured, according to Yeva.

“Someone who is being tortured will say absolutely anything,” she said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Even if they’d written ‘I am Elon Musk’ on that piece of paper, he would have read out that he was Elon Musk.”

No suspects have been arrested and the investigation is ongoing.

News.title: Pedestrian dies after being hit by bus near town centre as busy A-road closed
News.content:
CRASH TRAGEDY Pedestrian dies after being hit by bus near town centre as busy A-road closed







Next

A MAN has died after being hit by a bus this morning.

A Manchester Bee Network bus hit the pedestrian on the A6 in Stockport at 10.40am.



Emergency services rushed to the scene and taped off a section of the road.

The Bee Network is Manchester’s combined public transport system under local government control, a plan spearheaded by Andy Burnham when he was the Mayor.



Greater Manchester Police said the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

A spokesperson for the force said: “Emergency services were called to reports of a road traffic collision involving a bus and a pedestrian on A6 Buxton Road near Winifred Road, Stockport, at 10.40am today (30 October).

“Sadly, the pedestrian, a man, was pronounced dead at the scene. The road remains closed while investigations are ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the collision.

“Please avoid the area and make alternative travel arrangements where possible.”

Alison Chew, the Bee Network Director, said: “We are deeply saddened by the death of a pedestrian following an incident involving a Bee Network bus this morning.

“Our thoughts are with the man’s family and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.



“The incident happened on the A6 Buxton Road, near Winifred Road in Stockport at around 10:45am.

“Emergency services are on the scene, with road closures in place and the 192 service is currently diverted.

“We’re working closely with the police and our bus operator to provide support as they respond at the site, and will do all we can to support the investigation into the circumstances.”

News.title: Vicar spends £20k on ‘first-ever’ kids’ soft play INSIDE Grade I church to give them ‘somewhere to shelter from rain’
News.content:
'COME AND PLAY' Vicar spends £20k on ‘first-ever’ kids’ soft play INSIDE Grade I church to give them ‘somewhere to shelter from rain’







Next

A VICAR has spent £20k on a soft play area inside a Grade I church to give kids and parents “somewhere to shelter from the rain”.

Children’s play equipment has been set up in the nave alongside the rows of pews at St Mary’s Church in Dorset.



Reverend Andrew Rawding decided to install the indoor play area after noticing kids from the local school sheltering in the porch to escape the drizzle.

He hoped the play centre would encourage parents and children to peek into the historic church and make use of the space – which is largely unused for most of the week.





He said: “The church is next to a primary school and I noticed parents were dropping off older children and then hovering outside the church at pick up time with younger children

“And when it rained they took shelter in the porch but never came inside.”



He said that he tentatively gauged interest in a soft play unit on Facebook and was inundated with positive feedback.

But the Reverend admitted not everyone welcomed the project with open arms.

“Some of the older members had a few reservations and thought the children would break the stained glass windows which was just really over the top,” he said.

“Yes, the play area does take up part of the church that might be used on a couple of occasions of the year but my point is this is an area for children and parents and carers to use all year round.

“It is more important we are here for those people in the community than we are for niche groups.”



He added that the church was there to serve the community.

“I would say this is the first time that a soft play has been put in a 15th-century church.”

The area is free to use and is unsupervised, with parents politely asked to keep an eye on their kids.

Holly Varndell-Paulley, the interim head teacher of Burton Bradstock CofE School, said: “We can bring our younger children over here on a rainy day and they can have a playtime in there.

“Children who might need a bit more of a movement break, they can come over and use this – it’s just an additional space to add to our school.”

News.title: How bosses could have STOPPED ‘Savile of the Nursery’ abusing kids as young as 3 – as parents demand answers
News.content:
Next

HE was such a prolific child abuser that Vincent Chan was dubbed ‘Savile of the nursery’.

The twisted paedophile, who abused tiny tots in his care and hoarded tens of thousands of horrifying images of child abuse, was allowed to carry out his reign of terror in plain sight – like Jimmy Savile.





BBC bosses turned a blind eye to Savile’s predatory behaviour for years, and furious parents say Bright Horizons nurseries did the same.

And now, to add to their pain, horrified parents have just had it confirmed that bosses at Bright Horizons nurseries may not have notified Ofsted in 2021 of chilling complaints about Vincent Chan.

This was a legal requirement.

Sarah and Graham*, whose traumatised little boy is among the victims preyed upon by one of Britain’s most prolific sex offenders, are horrified by their fresh discovery.

Chan is now behind bars but Bright Horizons repeatedly dismissed concerns from parents – giving Chan free reign to continue his sickening spree of sexual abuse against three-year-old girls.

Dad Graham, whose son must remain anonymous, says: “This is an absolute disgrace.

“Bright Horizons failed to report serious safeguarding concerns about Vincent Chan to Ofsted, despite being legally required to do so.

“Why? What were they so afraid Ofsted might uncover if inspectors came knocking?





“Chan was allowed back to work with children, where he went on to commit horrific crimes.

“Chan is behind bars. But who is holding Bright Horizons accountable?

“Their failure to report could itself constitute a criminal offence, yet families are still fighting for answers five years later.

“Enough of the excuses and hiding behind a safeguarding review delayed until 2027.

“We want answers, we want accountability, and we want those responsible held to account.”

A senior executive at Ofsted confirmed in an email this week that complaints were not shared with either Ofsted.

She said: “In response to your question, Ofsted was neither notified about the about the 2021 concerns nor about the referral to the LADO as was required in line with the EYFS framework that applied at that time.”

Astonishingly Chan had been cleared by another safeguarding investigation three years before he was arrested for his sickening crimes.



Bright Horizons nursery in north London simply dismissed allegations about Chan’s vile behaviour and allowed the monster to carry on working with babies and toddlers.

The chilling revelation that Camden Council and nursery bosses were aware of concerns about Chan long before his arrest infuriated parents who now know there were missed opportunities to stop him.

In February, after he admitted 56 charges of child sex offences, including sexual assault by penetration, possession of indecent images and voyeurism, Chan was sentenced to 18 years in jail.

He had been routinely filming himself sexually abusing babies and toddlers in his care.

After his conviction, prosecutors described Chan as a “prolific sexual predator”.

The anguished parents of his young victims have joined forces and are demanding to know how on earth he was allowed to continue in his job for so long.

They contacted police, but cops are unable to investigate health and safety offences unless somebody dies and it becomes corporate manslaughter – until then it is a matter for the local council.

But Camden Council have delayed publication of an investigation which followed ‘significant concerns’ raised with the nursery back in 2021 about Chan’s conduct.

Chan was temporarily put on duties that involved no contact with children while the investigation took place.

But after it was completed, Chan was cleared to return to his role caring for young children. Just a year later, in 2022, he filmed himself sexually abusing three-year-old girls at the nursery, which is now permanently closed.



It has since emerged that Chan had also committed sexual offences in his previous job, including upskirting female pupils.

Chan worked at Bright Horizons from 2017 to 2024. He was suspended after a colleague raised concerns when he filmed a child falling asleep and shared it to “entertain” them.

Police found Chan had more than 25,000 indecent images of children on his computer, including videos of himself sexually assaulting children at the nursery while they were sleeping at nap time.

The youngest child he indecently filmed was only six months old.

A Camden Council spokesperson said: “We have shared all relevant documents and information with the independent review team. We want families to get the answers they deserve, in full, through the outcome of the independent review.

“We are ready to receive the review’s recommendations once it is published and take action.

“In the meantime, we are committed to making continual improvements to safeguarding. We are determined to make a real and tangible impact on national safeguarding arrangements for the future.”

A spokesperson for Bright Horizons said: “Our thoughts remain with the victims of Chan’s heinous crimes and their families.

“We encourage families to participate in the ongoing Child Safeguarding Practice Review and are hopeful that learnings can be taken from it, including for the Early Years’ industry as a whole.”

A spokesperson for Bright Horizons said: “We are fully committed to participating in the ongoing Children’s Safeguarding Practice Review which we hope will robustly consider all the relevant issues. We do not wish to prejudice that Review and its important role in obtaining information for victims and their families. As a result, we are not able to comment further at this time.



“We take our Ofsted notification requirements seriously and have policies and procedures in place to facilitate compliance. The safety and wellbeing of the children entrusted to our care is of paramount importance to us.

“Since the case came to light, Bright Horizons has worked tirelessly to further strengthen safeguarding across our nurseries. This has included improving monitoring and oversight, drawing on external expertise, expanding training, and establishing a dedicated senior team to ensure our policies are consistently applied. We have also commenced the roll out of cameras in settings alongside strengthening image-handling and device controls.

“We are truly sorry for the impact Vincent Chan’s crimes have had on the children and families affected. Our priority is making sure Bright Horizons and the wider sector learns the lessons from this case.”

STREET CHAOS Homes evacuated as bomb squad probe ‘small items’ inside house after cops forced entry & arrested 2 over neighbour row







Next

A STREET has been shut off and homes evacuated while a bomb squad examines “small items” found after two arrests.

Officers detained two people after forcing their way into a property in Brentwood, Essex, this morning before ordering the “safe examination of small items found”.



A 100-metre cordon was put in place in Sawyers Grove at around 7.20am.

Essex cops said: “Officers were initially called to reports of a neighbour dispute in Sawyers Grove at around 7.20am today, Friday 30 October.



“It was reported that a door had been damaged.

“Officers swiftly attended and forced entry to an address, where a man and a woman were arrested.

“During a subsequent search of the address, a number of small items were found which required specialist assessment.

“Explosive Ordnance Disposal experts were called to the scene and are examining the items to establish what they are.

“A number of homes within the 100-metre cordon have been evacuated as a precaution while this work continues.

“We thank to the public for their patience and will issue an update as soon as we can.”

News.title: Xi Jinping purges record 33 officials to drive out ‘serious hidden dangers’ in party after corruption probe
News.content:
IRON FIST Xi Jinping purges record 33 officials to drive out ‘serious hidden dangers’ in party after corruption probe







Next

XI Jinping has purged a record 33 officials as he vows to drive out “serious hidden dangers” from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP).

The Chinese president is tightening his iron grip, even firing his highest-ranking general, following a months-long corruption probe into the military boss’s conduct.



Zhang Youxia was the most senior name to be cut as the CCP ended its annual meeting with mass expulsions.

He had long been seen as Xi’s closest military ally before the Chinese president launched an investigation into his “suspected serious violations of discipline and law” in January.



Youxia was previously second-in-command to China’s leader in the country’s military hierarchy.

Sources told the Wall Street Journal that the general had been accused of accepting bribes and of leaking information about Chinese nukes to the US.



Authorities confirmed that a record 33 figures had been kicked out in the huge purge of China’s top officials this week.

Ma Xingrui, a top Xinjiang official, was also purged from the CCP.

He had already been stripped of all other posts over accusations of nepotism, bribery and paying for sex.

Xi ejected the Communist top brass as his party’s annual meeting wrapped up and adopted a decision on “advancing full and rigorous governance of the party”.



The president has cracked down hard on committee members during his time in power, purging dozens of members of the powerful Central Committee and a string of top military brass over the course of his decade at the helm.

Pro-Xi figures claim he is eradicating corruption, but critics say the communist president is paving the way to extend his rule at a Party Congress due in the second half of 2027.

Securing a fourth term would make Xi the longest serving leader of China since Chairman Mao.



Chinese official Zhang Fuhai said the committee, “with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core”, had “eliminated serious hidden dangers within the Party, the state and the military”.

He told reporters that the communist party “would rather offend thousands than let down 1.4 billion people”.

Fuhai claimed that discipline watchdogs in the country have punished 7.9million people since 2012 and vowed that efforts to weed out corruption would be “deepened”.

It comes as China has revealed plans to build a huge 15-storey tall nuclear bomb-proof “mobile island”.

The aircraft-carrier sized science island will be typhoon and nuclear-blast proof, designed to survive being battered by storms and waves of up to 66ft.



It is set to be completed by 2030 and will be the world’s first offshore platform with the power to cruise while hosting more than 200 scientists.

Officially named the Deep-Sea All-Weather Resident Floating Research Facility, the ship is being built by Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU).

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The university has signed a £304million contract with a shipbuilding company to construct the super ship.

Research equipment often can’t work properly as ships are rocked by violent waves, but this science ship is set to survive the most brutal storms while remaining stable enough for research.

News.title: Christa Pike breaks silence & says ‘there’s pain in my mind and my soul’ after returning to jail from botched execution
News.content:
Next

CHRISTA Pike has spoken publicly for the first time following her botched execution.

The 50-year-old killer, who remains on death row, has described the physical and emotional pain she says she has endured since surviving two doses of pentobarbital during Tennessee’s attempt to execute her.



In a stunning statement, Pike said, “One month ago on September 30, I walked into the execution chamber at Riverbend men’s prison prepared to die. I had made my peace.

“I had told the people who loved me, supported me and stood by me through the years I was grateful for them.



“I had also told the people in the room and who were there to witness my execution that I was leaving them in loving kindness.”

Pike said she woke up several days later in hospital confused and in severe pain, adding that she has suffered constantly since the execution attempt and still struggles to speak.

“There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain,” she said, describing pain in her body, arms, hands and throat as well as what she called pain “in my mind and in my soul.”

She said she had never contemplated surviving the execution and was deeply hurt by what she described as the incompetence that had left so many people in a terrible position.

Pike also said she continued to think about her victim’s family and the pain and loss they had endured.

“I am recovering, and I know that I am getting stronger,” she said. “But healing is not the same as being okay.”



She said she has been largely isolated in the prison’s medical ward since returning to custody on October 10, away from the human contact she values, and compared the experience to the 28 years she spent in solitary confinement.

Pike said she was now trying to find meaning in what happened and had drawn strength from an outpouring of support from people around the world, including both longtime supporters and complete strangers.

“To know that so many people care about me, that they see me as a human being whose life matters, is something I cannot fully put into words,” she said. “It is humbling, and it has touched me more deeply than I can explain.”



She also thanked the first responders, doctors and nurses who treated her after the failed execution, saying they had shown her compassion, dignity and respect.

Pike also thanked her attorneys and supporters, saying they had continued to stand by her and refused to give up on her.

“I don’t know why I survived that night. I don’t know what comes next,” she said.

“Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time.”

Pike was supposed to be put to death at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.



But the execution descended into chaos after staff allegedly struggled to establish IV lines.

She was given two doses of the lethal drug but continued breathing and was eventually rushed to hospital.

She remained unconscious on a ventilator for days before unexpectedly waking up on October 6.

Pike was discharged from hospital and returned to the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center after regaining her ability to walk while suffering serious injuries to her arms.

Her attorneys have previously said she suffered severe swelling in her arms, pneumonia and a blood clot following the failed lethal injection.



A minute-by-minute court filing claimed staff used around 10 needles while repeatedly trying to establish IV lines.

It alleged staff questioned whether her veins had “blown,” while Pike later complained that her arm was burning and felt as though it was going to burst.

Witnesses could still hear her breathing and making snoring sounds after the lethal drugs had been administered.

Pike’s future remains unclear after Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused the state’s remaining executions for 2026 while officials investigate what went wrong.

In his latest comments, Lee said she remains incarcerated under Tennessee law and suggested her sentence would stay the same unless the courts determine otherwise.



Her lawyers have questioned whether Tennessee should be allowed to make another attempt to execute her and have called for Lee to commute her sentence.

The governor had denied Pike clemency before the September 30 execution attempt.

Pike was sentenced to death for the brutal 1995 murder of fellow Knoxville Job Corps student Colleen Slemmer.

Prosecutors said Pike became convinced Slemmer was interested in her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, before the teenager was lured to a wooded area and tortured and killed.

Pike struck Slemmer with a piece of asphalt and took a fragment of her skull from the scene.



She was the only one of the three teenagers implicated in the killing to receive a death sentence.

Shipp was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy, while Shadolla Peterson pleaded guilty to being an accessory after the fact and testified against Pike and Shipp.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The U.S. Sun previously revealed where they are now and why neither received the death penalty.

Pike would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years.

News.title: Driver guilty of hitting cyclist and dragging him to death under car
News.content:
Warning: This article contains distressing content

A man has been found guilty of murdering a head teacher who was dragged to his death for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car.

Simon Richardson crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was cycling home from his job at Stretford Grammar School on the evening of 20 April in the village of Warburton in Trafford, Greater Manchester.

Prosecutors claimed Richardson, 35, fled the scene of the crash before stopping to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist and then driving on with Mr Mullins still lodged underneath the vehicle.

Richardson was also convicted of dangerous driving and will return to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court to be sentenced on Monday.

There were shouts of "Yes!" from the court's public gallery as the guilty murder verdict was announced.

Others could also be heard crying.

The judge, Mrs Justice Brunner KC, told Richardson that there was only one sentence for murder, namely life imprisonment.

News.title: Police watchdog to investigate Met over letter about Meghan's father
News.content:
The UK police watchdog is to investigate the Metropolitan Police's handing of a letter containing allegations against Thomas Markle that was handed to his daughter, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had decided an investigation was required into the force's "failure to pass on allegations of serious offending... to relevant overseas authorities at the time".

The letter, written by Markle's first wife Roslyn Loveless, is believed to have contained claims about Meghan's father.

He has strongly denied recent allegations that he had possessed images of child abuse, describing them as "sick lies".

On Thursday the Met said it had voluntarily referred itself to the IOPC.

The letter at the heart of the IOPC investigation was sent to the Met's royal protection team by Loveless, who divorced Thomas Markle in 1975 and died in 2024.

The handwritten letter was then passed to Meghan in January 2019, with the duchess saying last week that it had "made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father".

Meghan did not provide any details but said it had given her sufficient reason to not visit Thomas Markle and not allow him to meet his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet.

Scotland Yard said the letter contained claims about offending outside the UK and that it had been forwarded to "the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness".

The IOPC will consider why the Met did not share the contents of the letter with other law enforcement agencies, in the UK or overseas.

The Met said on Thursday that it intended to make further referrals to "relevant overseas law enforcement agencies", a process which it expected to be completed "in the coming days".

The letter was forwarded by officers to the Sussexes' royal office rather than to Meghan personally, while there have been reports that the Met did not keep a copy of the letter and had to ask for one from the Sussexes.

The watchdog will have to consider how the contents of the letter were treated by the force at the time.

Noel Rasmussen, Thomas Markle's granddaughter and niece of the Duchess of Sussex, previously told the BBC she was "deeply troubled by the questions surrounding the Metropolitan Police's handling of the information it received".

"If allegations of this seriousness were brought to the attention of authorities, it is reasonable to ask what steps were taken [and] why the information was not shared with other law enforcement agencies."

Reports of the Met's handline of the letter emerged as Thomas Markle's son had told the police in the Philippines about material which was alleged to contain sexual images of children, which he had claimed to have found in possessions belonging to Meghan's father.

Thomas Markle had been in the Philippines in December 2025, undergoing hospital treatment, when Meghan wrote to him to end all contact.

Authorities in the Philippines have begun investigating the claims. Police there have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from Markle's former home.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week.

However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they can examine the items.

Thomas Markle Sr has strongly denied all the allegations against him. He has been backed by his daughter Samantha, who has dismissed the claims against her father as "fake".

News.title: Streeting denies 'kicking can down the road' in defence spending row
News.content:
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has denied "kicking the can down the road" over how much the UK spends on defence.

The government has faced criticism for not setting out a pathway at Wednesday's Budget to hit its target of spending 3% of GDP on defence by 2030.

Streeting is at odds with MPs on the Commons defence committee over the issue.

It comes as Chancellor John Healey and Streeting announce that foreign firms which are awarded defence contracts of more than Â£50m will need to invest an equal value back into the UK.

Under the new investment rules, described as an "offset strategy", these companies will need to spend an equivalent amount on British factories, jobs and training.

The Ministry of Defence will apply the rules on a "case-by-case" basis from April 2027, the government said. Healey and Streeting will unveil the policy on a visit to UK defence contractor BAE's shipbuilding site in Glasgow later.

Countries including Poland, Norway and the Netherlands have mandated similar rules to "boost the economic benefit from defence procurement", the government said.

While ministers hope the rules increase investment in Britain's defence industry, they appear designed to do so in a politically palatable way rather than committing to spending cuts.

Tan Dhesi, Labour chair of the cross-party Commons defence committee, said on Wednesday that decisions had been "kicked into the long grass" to next year's government spending review, rather than announced in the Budget.

He warned that without building capabilities now, "we risk leaving ourselves seriously vulnerable in the event of a major conflict".

Streeting hit back at these comments as "unfair" and "unfounded".

Speaking on Thursday, Dhesi said the committee stands by its criticism.

"We had hoped to see that the chancellor would set out a precise pathway to spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030," Dhesi told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.

"But instead some of those key decisions on defence have lamentably been delayed until next year's spending review."

He praised the government for plugging a Â£4.7bn hole in the Defence Investment Plan in the Budget, through asking government departments to cut their capital budgets by 1%.

News.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost concerns
News.content:
US stocks have continued to slide as concerns continue to intensify over the increasing costs of the artificial intelligence (AI) build out.

Shares in Intel continued their overnight slide into early trading on Friday, falling as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market even as it plans to increase spending on AI.

Amazon shares fell as far as 6% before recovering after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%, as other tech stocks including Reddit and Roblox continued to fall.

The losses follow the value of Google owner Alphabet plunging by more than $500bn on Thursday after it revealed its own AI summaries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.

Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 1% after Thursday's massive slide.

The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value after its earnings update rattled investors.

On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect positive cash flow this year, and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.

"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.

In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

News.title: Sir Ian McKellen leads tributes to 'beloved actor' Sir Patrick Stewart after his death at 86
News.content:
Comedian Ricky Gervais, whose BBC programme Extras Sir Patrick guest starred in, described him as a "legend".

Sharing a video of the pair giggling in a set of bloopers for the series, Gervais said: "I still can't believe he agreed to do this scene. And he didn't even mind when I ruined every take."

Sir Patrick was a lifelong supporter of English Football League club Huddersfield Town, which called him a "titan of his craft".

"Fiercely proud of his Yorkshire roots, Sir Patrick was a Terrier in every sense, and we're proud to have counted him as one of our own," the club added.

Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, while Lewy Body Dementia is another common form caused by abnormal protein deposits, which cause a loss of cognitive function.

The Alzheimer's Society CEO Michelle Dyson said Sir Patrick was an "extraordinarily talented and much-loved actor, admired by millions around the world", adding: "His death is a heartbreaking reminder of the devastating impact dementia has on people and families across the globe."

The actor became a campaigner on domestic violence in later life, including becoming an ambassador for domestic abuse charity Refuge in 2007, after witnessing his mother suffer violence at the hands of his father.

Hetti Barkworth-Nanton, Refuge's board chair, said it had been a privilege to "watch his endless devotion" to the cause, adding that he "broke down barriers and taboos on the subject".

Andy Burnham considered Sir Patrick to be "one of the very best" who "never forgot his working-class Yorkshire roots".

"He brought joy to millions," the prime minister's spokesman said on his behalf. "He always stood up for what he believed in, including through his campaigning to help those affected by domestic violence.

News.title: Wettest week for two years but still not enough rain to get out of drought
News.content:
The recent stormy weather brought England's wettest week in two years, according to the Environment Agency.

However, despite the rain, Wales and most of England are still in drought with parts of southern England in severe drought.

Met Office provisional statistics for October show that the UK received above average rainfall.

However, the National Drought Group have said it will take sustained and above average rainfall over a seven month period for conditions to improve to normal.

Over the last week we had the first two named storms of the season - Austen and Boelo - which gave much of the UK significant and much needed rain.

Rainfall totals ranged from 38mm in central England to 87mm in the south-west and according to Enviroment Agency (EA) monitoring, it was the wettest week across England since October 2024.

In some parts of southern England there was nearly 50% more rainfall than normal throughout the month.

As a whole, England has had 111% of it's long-term monthly rainfall, according to the EA.

News.title: 'I run a spotless kitchen', says Michelin-star restaurant chef in wake of food hygiene debacle
News.content:
Ynyshir was previously ordered to stop serving raw lobster after Ceredigion council found "significant hazards" were not properly identified.

The restaurant received its first Michelin star in 2014 and its second in 2022, becoming the first and only restaurant in Wales to hold two.

It missed out on a third star at the ceremony this year.

The 16-seat restaurant serves Japanese-inspired raw dishes as part of its nearly Â£500 a head 30-course tasting menu, and accused inspectors of not understanding its specialised procedures.

By August, the council had reinstated its five-star hygiene rating after it found the "business had addressed all matters identified during the original inspection".

But, for Ynyshir, the scrutiny was a major setback, and Ward shared his frustration in the documentary.

"I'm very proud of my whole team and my business, and what we've achieved," he said.

"It's obviously massive in the media, which anyone instantly jumps on and thinks it's about cleanliness," he said. "I run a spotless kitchen.

"When something like this happens you're a bit blown away."

Ward said the restaurant served a lot of raw food and did a lot of things "that aren't normal".

"We have done some things wrong, but we don't deserve everything [we were accused of]," he said.

"It's just, we dare to be different."

He said the inspection left him feeling the weight of responsibility, with more than 30 members of staff and the business potentially at risk.

Management of food safety at Ynyshir was categorised by inspectors as needing major improvement, as was cleanliness and condition of facilities, while "hygienic food handling" was rated "generally satisfactory".

A dirty floor, inadequate hand-washing facilities in some areas and broken equipment posing a potential contamination risk were also identified in the inspectors' report.

Ynyshir responded at the time, saying the inspection "identified a small number of minor issues typical of a busy professional kitchen situated in the countryside of rural Wales" which had been "rectified immediately and in full".

It said biological testing, at "significant cost" to the restaurant, had "conclusively confirmed that our techniques are safe, compliant and appropriate".

It said at the time it was prepared to work constructively with the council but expected "an informed, consistent and fair assessment process that recognises the realities of modern, non-conventional restaurants".

When Ynyshir was reinspected, Ceredigion council said the "business had addressed all matters identified during the original inspection".

News.title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say
News.content:
King's College London has been experimenting in its canteen, external, offering staff and students root-to-tip meals, such as banana skin curry.

At home, people might want to try leaving skins on kiwi fruit, using broccoli stalks in stir-fries or adding bell pepper seeds to dishes, the researchers suggest.

While cooking can change the fibre content, it doesn't usually destroy it all.

Steaming, microwaving or quick sautÃ©ing tends to preserve nutrients best.

Gibson said: "This isn't about perfection and this isn't about forcing people to eat unpalatable food â it's about recognising the nutritional value in components we've been conditioned to discard."

She acknowledges some may be hesitant to try it.

Some diners raised concerns during the canteen trial.

Over the nine-week period, "root-to-tip" dishes made up a third of total daily hot menu sales at the university.

Those choosing the new dishes were less likely to finish their meals than diners eating from the conventional menu.

Kirsten Jackson, a dietitian with the British Dietetic Association who specialises in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), says the food hacks are useful as long as produce is washed thoroughly.

She suggests blending pineapple cores into smoothies, but says the tough skins are not something she would recommend.

Some stalks may need to be cooked or finely chopped to make them more palatable, she adds.

"Just because a broccoli stalk doesn't fit into tonight's meal doesn't mean it needs to go in the bin. Chop it up, freeze it and add it to a soup or stir-fry another day," she said.

She advises increasing fibre intake gradually to avoid bloating, noting that people who have IBS may find it harder to tolerate.

And there are some things to avoid entirely, said the British Nutrition Foundation.

Green potatoes and rhubarb leaves contain toxic compounds, while tough stalks and seeds may not be suitable for young children.

News.title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded
News.content:
Yorkshire Water's chief executive has announced she is to step down, just 24 hours after the company was given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency.

Nicola Shaw, who has led the firm since 2022, will leave the role on 1 January to be replaced by Nicola Medalova, a chartered environmental health officer who previously worked for the National Grid.

In a statement on Friday, Shaw said it had been a "privilege" to lead the company but that it was the "right time" to leave her post.

Shaw has faced criticism in recent years, including for taking Â£1.9m in undisclosed payments between 2023 and 2026, while the company has come under scrutiny for its performance.

The payments were made by Yorkshire Water's parent company, Kelda Holdings, for what the firm said was "investor engagement" and "financial oversight".

On Thursday, the Environment Agency gave the firm one star out of four - its lowest possible rating - meaning Yorkshire Water was classed as a "poorly performing company".

The EA said Yorkshire Water was responsible for 260 pollution incidents in 2025, which was its highest total since 2011.

In 2024, Ofwat announced it was fining the company Â£47m for historic sewage leaks.

News.title: Heart attack patient, 83, had to drive four hours for hospital appointment
News.content:
An 83-year-old recovering cancer patient who has suffered two heart attacks was forced to drive himself on a four-hour round trip for medical tests.

Charles Swift was referred to Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest, Pembrokeshire, for tests on his heart in August - he lives in Borth, Ceredigion - which is 70 miles away.

He made inquiries about getting non-emergency transport but was refused by a call handler from the Welsh Ambulance Services Trust (WAST) when he told them he owned a car.

"I can't understand why pensioners have to run about in their own car," he said.

WAST said it was not always able to meet the increasing demand for transport, and changes were underway to improve the service.

Swift, who has been treated for three types of cancer and has had two heart attacks, said when he rang hospital taxis, he was asked if he could walk, climb stairs and owned a car.

When he replied yes to all three, he said he was told: "You'll have to use that then.

"I don't understand. What's the difference if you've got a car or not? I'm 83. It's not a good journey to do. It was tiring."

On another occasion, Swift was told on a Friday afternoon that his hospital transport for an appointment in Haverfordwest on the Monday had been cancelled, leading him to cancel the appointment.

When he got hospital transport for a subsequent appointment, he said it was "very pleasant, no problem at all".

Hywel Dda University Health Board's website says patients travelling to and from hospital are normally expected to organise their own transport.

When that is not possible, some patients could be eligible for non-emergency patient transport provided by the Welsh Ambulance Service, but must meet eligibility criteria.

This includes receiving regular dialysis or cancer treatment, needing a stretcher or oxygen or needing to travel in their own wheelchair.

Public transport is not a realistic option as trains from Borth to Haverfordwest take a minimum of three-and-a-half hours in each direction.

News.title: Academic says he has been barred from UK over event with Palestine Action founder
News.content:
A Swedish climate academic says he has been barred from entering the UK because he was due to speak on a panel with a co-founder of Palestine Action.

Andreas Malm told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he had received a letter from the Home Office notifying him that his presence was "not conducive to the public good", with no further details given.

He said he could not "see any other explanation" for being denied entry than his scheduled appearance with Huda Ammori, a founder of the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

The Home Office said it did not comment on individual cases.

Malm is a senior lecturer in human ecology at Sweden's Lund University, whose work includes the 2021 book How to Blow up a Pipeline and 2025's The Destruction of Palestine is the Destruction of the Earth.

He said he had asked the Home Office to explain its decision, but could not see a reason beyond the upcoming talk in London with Ammori organised by the left-wing magazine Tribune - calling the move a "severe restriction on the free exchange of ideas".

Malm said he was not a member of Palestine Action, had never publicly endorsed it, nor had he given it any financial support.

"The only link to Palestine Action is her as a person," he said, criticising the UK government for ascribing "guilt by association".

The academic acknowledged that he had previously described the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks on Israel - in which about 1,200 people were killed and another 251 taken hostage - as "fundamentally an act of liberation".

Malm said it was possible that these remarks, during a December 2023 talk in which he also condemned the "deplorable" killing of civilians in the cross-border attack, had been the reason for the Home Office's decision.

But he argued that these views had been in the public realm for a long time, including when he was last allowed into the UK to deliver a talk in May.

"I don't expect the British state to agree with me on Palestine or climate or anything. What I expect the British state to do is to continue to let me enter the country and to discuss with colleagues, with people who disagree with me - as I have done for years."

News.title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be
News.content:
A couple who went for a beach walk shortly after getting engaged had to be rescued by the Irish Coast Guard after an incoming tide trapped them against a coastal cliff.

The bride and groom-to-be were hauled approximately 150m (490 ft) to the top of the cliff to safety because rescuers could not reach them by boat or by helicopter.

The dramatic rescue took place during gale-force winds on Achill Island, off the west coast of Ireland, on Monday afternoon.

Coast Guard volunteer Peter McManamon, who coordinated the operation, told BBC News NI: "They were two very lucky people."

It is believed the pair are originally from overseas but live in Ireland and were on a visit to Achill Island, off the County Mayo coast, when the incident happened.

McManamon said the couple had gone for a walk along Keel Beach when the tide began to come in behind them - at one point reaching above knee-level.

"They got engaged in Achill and they were just walking along [the beach] and they went out too far on the rocks," he explained.

"The weather conditions were atrocious there, and in that particular area the tide has come in very quick."

Unable to get off the sand because of the towering cliff behind them, the couple called 999 and asked for a coast guard rescue.

"It was too rough for a rib (rigid inflatable boat) to be tasked - it was blowing Force 8 to 10 at the time and the wave conditions wouldn't let us," McManamon said.

"We tried to walk out along the rocks to them but... the waves were just coming in and it was just too dangerous to put the crew in, so the helicopter was tasked."

News.title: Hazardous driving conditions for morning commuters as fog warning issued by Met Office
News.content:
Thick fog has formed on Friday morning across parts of the United Kingdom which could lead to hazardous driving conditions.

The Met Office has issued a yellow severe weather warning for fog from Lincolnshire, the East Midlands, the Home Counties into parts of Greater London.

Fog will be dense in places with visibility below 100 metres at times and it will be most extensive and disruptive during the morning rush hour.

It will slowly begin to thin, lift and clear later this morning but in some rural spots in eastern England it may not clear until this afternoon.

News.title: 8 essential boiler checks every homeowner should do before winter
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

If you've had your heating switched off for months, the last thing you want is to discover your boiler isn't working when the first cold snap arrives. Yet it's often only when temperatures drop that homeowners realise something isn't quite right with their central heating.

The good news is you don't need to be a heating expert to carry out a few basic checks. Testing your boiler, checking the pressure and making sure your radiators are heating properly can help you spot potential problems before they turn into costly repairs.

Here's how to check your boiler is ready for winter, what you can safely do yourself and when it's time to call a professional.

Get a boiler installation quote for your home

Use our comparison tool to get a range of free quotes from leading boiler installers across the UK.



Eight essential boiler checks before winter

1. Turn your heating on and check it works

The simplest way to check your boiler is ready for winter is to turn the central heating on before you actually need it. Start by checking that your boiler is switched on and, if it has a summer or hot-water-only setting, change it to central-heating mode.

Next, turn your room thermostat up a few degrees above the current room temperature. This should tell the heating system to start warming your home. Let the heating run for around 20–30 minutes, then check that your radiators are beginning to warm up.

If nothing happens, check your heating programmer or timer. Your boiler might be working perfectly well but simply isn't scheduled to come on. If your boiler won't start despite the controls being set correctly, check for any warning lights or error codes before attempting anything else.

2. Check your boiler pressure

Low boiler pressure is a common reason for central heating systems to stop working properly. Fortunately, checking it is usually pretty straightforward. Most modern boilers have a pressure gauge on the front or underneath the unit. Some newer models show the pressure on a digital display.

In many sealed central heating systems, pressure should be between 1 and 1.5 bar when the heating is cold. However, the correct range varies between boilers, so make sure you check your manufacturer's instructions.

If the pressure is below the recommended level, your boiler may need repressurising. On some systems, this involves opening a filling loop beneath the boiler to allow more water into the heating system.

The exact process depends on your boiler, so follow the manufacturer's instructions and only attempt this when the system is switched off and cool. If you're unsure, ask a heating engineer.

Keep an eye on the pressure afterwards. If it repeatedly falls, there could be a leak or another underlying fault that needs professional attention. Unusually high pressure should also be investigated.

3. Check your radiators and bleed them if necessary

Once your heating has been running for a while, check that each radiator is warming up. If a radiator is cold at the top but warm at the bottom, there may be trapped air inside, which prevents the hot water from circulating properly. This can usually be fixed by bleeding the radiator.

Here's how to do it:

Switch off the central heating and allow the radiator to cool Place a cloth or small container beneath the bleed valve, usually found at the top of the radiator Insert a radiator key and slowly turn the valve anticlockwise You should hear a hissing sound as the trapped air escapes When water begins to appear, close the valve carefully without over-tightening it Check your boiler pressure afterwards, as bleeding radiators can cause it to drop

If a radiator is cold at the bottom, this could indicate a build-up of sludge or another circulation problem. If one radiator remains completely cold, check that its valves are open before calling an engineer.

4. Check your thermostat and heating controls

Heating controls can easily be overlooked, particularly if you haven't used them since the spring. Check that your thermostat is working and that your heating schedule still suits your routine. If you have a smart thermostat, make sure it's connected and that any programmed schedules are correct.

Ian Palmer-Smith, appliance repair expert at Domestic & General, says problems with heating coming on unexpectedly can sometimes have a simple explanation. "If you're noticing your boiler is turning on or off sporadically throughout the day, you may need to simply adjust your timer settings using your boiler manual for help."

It's also worth checking the thermostatic radiator valves (TRVs) on individual radiators, as these may have been turned down or switched off during the warmer months.

Remember, if your room is already warmer than the temperature set on your thermostat, the heating won't come on. But rest assured, that's normal rather than a sign of a faulty boiler.

For more information on heating settings, read our guide to the ideal temperature for every room in your home.

5. Look for leaks and listen for unusual noises

While your heating is running, take a few minutes to look around the boiler, any visible pipework and your radiators for signs of problems.

Check for water dripping from pipes or valves, any damp patches beneath radiators and any visible corrosion. Even a small leak can cause your heating system to lose pressure over time, so it's worth getting it checked before the problem becomes worse.

Listen to your boiler, too. It’s normal to hear a bit of noise during normal operation, but persistent banging, whistling or gurgling could indicate trapped air, circulation problems or another fault.

Unusual noises aren't always a sign of something serious, but if they're new or getting louder, it's a good idea to have the system inspected by a qualified heating engineer.

6. Check your condensate pipe

If you have a modern condensing boiler, it will have a condensate pipe that carries away waste water produced during operation. In some homes, part of this plastic pipe runs outside the property, but during prolonged freezing weather, the water inside can freeze, potentially causing the boiler to stop working.

Before winter, check whether any accessible external sections are properly insulated and that the pipe outlet isn't visibly blocked.

If your boiler stops working during freezing weather, a frozen condensate pipe could be responsible, particularly if the boiler is making gurgling noises or displaying an error code. Palmer-Smith recommends gently warming the frozen section of pipe by "applying a hot water bottle directly to the pipes".

You can also use warm water, but never boiling water, which could damage the plastic pipe. Only attempt this if the pipe is safely accessible from ground level, and don't use a naked flame.

Worcester Bosch, for example, advises that once the pipe has thawed, you may need to reset the boiler according to its instructions. If the problem persists, contact a heating engineer.

7. Test your carbon monoxide alarm

It’s very important to have a working carbon monoxide (CO) alarm in any home with a gas boiler. Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas that can't be seen, smelled or tasted, and it can be produced when gas appliances like your boiler aren't burning fuel correctly.

Press the test button on your alarm, following the manufacturer's instructions, and check that it hasn't reached its replacement date. If it has a replaceable battery, make sure that's working too.

A carbon monoxide alarm is an important safeguard, but also it isn't a substitute for having your boiler serviced regularly. If the alarm sounds, leave the property immediately, get into fresh air and seek emergency assistance. Don't ignore the warning or assume the alarm is faulty.

8. Check when your boiler was last serviced

Even if your boiler appears to be working perfectly, it's important to check when it was last professionally serviced. An annual boiler service can help identify developing faults and check that it’s operating safely. "Having your boiler serviced annually is a great action to take to prevent boiler breakdowns, as well as improve its efficiency," says Palmer-Smith.

Servicing may also be necessary to keep your manufacturer's warranty valid. If you haven't had your boiler serviced within the past 12 months, now is a good time to arrange one before engineers get busier during winter. Gas boilers should always be serviced by a Gas Safe registered engineer.

If your boiler is older and you're experiencing repeated faults, it may also be worth considering whether repairs are still economical. Our guide to how much a new boiler costs in the UK explains what to expect if replacement becomes necessary.

When should you call a Gas Safe engineer?

While homeowners can carry out basic checks, some problems should always be left to professionals.

Call a Gas Safe registered engineer if your boiler repeatedly loses pressure, develops persistent faults, leaks, makes unusual noises or stops working despite basic troubleshooting. Never remove the boiler casing or attempt to repair the gas components yourself.

If you smell gas or suspect a gas leak, don't operate electrical switches, smoke or use naked flames. Open your doors and windows if safe to do so, leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999 when you get to a safe location.

Ultimately, checking your boiler before winter is about identifying problems while there's still time to deal with them. A few minutes spent testing your heating now could save you from discovering a fault on the coldest day of the year.

And once you've confirmed everything is working, you can turn your attention to reducing its running costs. Our guide to energy-saving tips for your home explains how to keep bills down during the colder months.

News.title: Gaza charities on Macklemore support: 'We are incredibly grateful'
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Macklemore is bringing his Free Palestine tour to a close at the OVO Arena Wembley on Friday evening.

The 43-year-old announced the run of shows after being dropped as Ed Sheeran’s support act in September due to comments he made about Gaza.

The US rapper called for a “Free Palestine” during two performances at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium on 4 and 5 September.

All proceeds from the sold-out three-show tour will go to 12 organisations and charities which support the Palestinian movement.

Gaza charities have said they are “incredibly grateful” for Macklemore’s support, ahead of the conclusion of the rapper’s tour in London on Friday.

Shabby Amini, director of fundraising and marketing at Medical Aid for Palestinians, said: “We are incredibly grateful to Macklemore for his generous support and for using his platform to keep the experiences of Palestinians in the spotlight, especially at a time when many are choosing to stay silent.

“Macklemore’s support is a powerful reminder that Palestinians must not be forgotten when the headlines move on.”

Ed Sheeran (L) and rapper Macklemore perform during the 2014 iHeartRadio Music Festival at the MGM Grand Garden Arena on September 20, 2014 ( Getty )

A spokesman for aid organisation Anera, which supports displaced Palestinians, said: “Music has always had the power to bring people together, inspire action and unite us in the pursuit of something greater.

“Seeing thousands of people come together through song and love in solidarity with the people of Gaza moves us deeply.”

The Seattle-based artist announced his tour 10 days after being dropped from Sheeran’s The Loop tour. He has already played shows in Dublin and Paris.

Macklemore claimed that Robert Kraft, the CEO of Kraft Group who owns Gillette Stadium, personally called Sheeran to say he would not be allowed to perform at the venue.

Meanwhile, Sheeran said it was his promoter’s decision to remove the rapper from the tour and several other support acts pulled out of the tour in solidarity with Macklemore.

The organisations being supported by Macklemore’s tour include: Anera, Glia, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Taawon, Heal Palestine, Palestinian Youth Movement, Middle East Children’s Alliance, Jewish Voice for Peace, Medical Aid for Palestinians, Institute for Middle East Understanding, Palestine Children’s Relief Fund and UNRWA USA.

News.content:

At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.
