News.title: Masked Singer judge Jenny McCarthy says she’s living in a tent due to toxic mold poisoning
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Media personality Jenny McCarthy has claimed that she’s living in a tent as she detoxes her home from mold toxicity.

The Masked Singer judge, 53 — who is a well-known supporter of the anti-vaccine movement — had previously revealed that mycotoxin poisoning, also known as toxic mold, had left her with a range of symptoms including “oozing” eye growths and tooth decay.

In the latest episode of her podcast, the Jenny McCarthy Wahlberg Show, she revealed that she has been “so desperate to heal” that she moved into a tent.

McCarthy said previously that she underwent several surgeries as she tried to figure out the source of her symptoms, which began with an infected root canal.

She claimed that before her doctor considered mold exposure, she went “down a rabbit hole of doctors, surgeries, teeth being pulled, mysterious growths popping up in places you are not expecting, implants literally falling out, and eventually realizing my immune system was fighting something so much bigger.”

open image in gallery Jenny McCarthy has claimed she is living in a tent because she is ‘too paranoid’ to live indoors as she detoxes her home from mold ( Jenny McCarthy Show )

McCarthy said she was “going through medical fatigue” when her doctor considered mold exposure. She was tested and then received a call from her physician, who apparently warned, “Jenny, you’ve got serious mold. You’ve got the type of mold that causes seizures.”

Her doctor told her the mycotoxin poisoning diagnosis explained why her immune system had been “so under attack.”

McCarthy, who is married to Boston Blue star Donnie Wahlberg, said she has now remediated the mold in their Los Angeles home, but she was still living in the tent because she was “too paranoid.”

She said: “I’m still in my mold detox, you guys. I’m still in it, like, I’m knee-deep in it….I’m in month seven of detox and I’m too paranoid to honestly live anywhere else other than a tent.”

McCarthy became one of the most prominent faces of the anti-vaccine movement in the mid 2000s. She has heavily promoted the scientifically discredited claim that child immunizations caused her son’s autism diagnosis. Scientific research has found no link between the two.

open image in gallery McCarthy became one of the most prominent figures of the anti-vaccine movement in the mid-2000s ( Getty )

Mycotoxins are products of certain fungi and molds that can cause illness in animals and people. According to the Cleveland Clinic, exposure to mycotoxins might make people feel like they have the flu, but long-term exposure can lead to more serious complications like chronic illness.

Mycotoxins can enter your body through skin absorption, ingestion or inhalation, and short term symptoms can include fever, dizziness, brain fog, headache, short-term memory loss, nausea and vomiting.

News.title: Are Liverpool in a title challenge? Andoni Iraola reveals stance before Arsenal test
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andoni Iraola says it would still be too early to say whether Liverpool are in a Premier League title challenge – even if his side beat champions Arsenal on Sunday.

The Reds are enjoying their best run under Iraola, winning four games in a row before progressing past Chelsea in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup in midweek.

open image in gallery Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool could move three points behind Arsenal with a win at Anfield ( Reuters )

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said the Reds could emerge as Arsenal’s closest challengers due to the uncertainty surrounding Manchester City this season, a feeling that could become stronger should they win against the champions and move three points behind Mikel Arteta’s team.

"It's good if the fans have expectations and think we can win. But if you ask me, it is still very early in the season,” Iraola said.

“I said before, it's still October, take one game at a time and I always say the first reference is normally when we have played against each other once, halfway through the season, and then you can start looking at the standings.

“Now we are in a position where we need to improve, keep getting better.”

open image in gallery There is a chance Szoboszlai is available for Liverpool ( Getty )

Liverpool, meanwhile, could be boosted by the return of Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz.

Szoboszlai’s return form injury against Brentford two weeks ago lasted only 31 minutes but there is a chance the midfielder, who scored a stunning free-kick in Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Arsenal last season, is available.

“We still have two days,” Iraola said. “I think they have a chance, yes."

News.title: Christa Pike breaks silence after botched execution: ‘I am searching for meaning in what happened to me’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Christa Pike, the Tennessee death row inmate who survived a botched execution, has broken her silence after the failed attempt to describe the physical and emotional pain she has felt in the weeks that followed.

The 50-year-old convicted murderer was administered two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution on September 30 before officials halted the execution. She was rushed to the hospital and is recovering after the attempt, though her future health condition and whether the state will try to execute her again remain unclear.

“I am searching for meaning in what happened to me,” Pike said in a lengthy statement released Friday to Knoxville news station WBIR.

She also described the lasting physical and emotional toll of the procedure.

“There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak,” Pike said. “And the pain isn't just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul.”

open image in gallery Christa Pike survived a botched execution attempt in Tennessee on September 30 after receiving two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital ( Tennessee Department of Correction )

Pike said she had made peace with her impending death before entering the execution chamber and had not considered the possibility of surviving. Days later, she woke up in a hospital, confused and in pain.

“I had not contemplated life beyond that night, and I’m deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position,” she said.

Although Pike said she is recovering and getting stronger, she is still struggling emotionally.

“But healing is not the same as being OK,” she said.

Pike was sentenced to death in March 1996 for the 1995 murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a fellow student at a Job Corps center in Knoxville, Tennessee. Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, 17, lured Slemmer into a wooded area, tortured her and killed her.

“I continue to think about my victim’s family and the terrible pain and loss they have endured,” Pike wrote in her statement.

Shipp remains behind bars. He was denied parole in October and will not be eligible for another review until October 2031. He has been in custody since January 1995.

Pike was scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. However, the execution was halted after Pike remained alive. Media witnesses reported hearing her make snoring sounds after the second dose, while her attorneys sought emergency medical intervention. She was eventually transported by ambulance to a hospital.

The failed execution has brought up questions about Tennessee's lethal injection procedures and the medical care Pike received. Her attorneys say staff struggled to insert the IV needed to deliver the drugs, with one lawyer claiming they stuck Pike with about 10 needles trying to find a vein.

open image in gallery Pike, pictured here in 2007, was scheduled to become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years ( Knoxville News Sentinel )

Pike was hospitalized for several days before being discharged on October 10 and returned to the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville, where she had been held before the execution attempt. She continues to receive medical care in the prison's medical ward.

She said Friday that the isolation has been particularly difficult, especially after spending 28 years in solitary confinement before the failed execution.

"Much of what I am experiencing today is a repeat of that condition," Pike said, citing the lack of human connection as another source of pain.

Despite her circumstances, Pike said support from people around the world has helped her find strength. She thanked those who have sent prayers and messages, as well as the first responders, hospital staff and attorneys who helped her.

"To know that so many people care about me, that they see me as a human being whose life matters, is something I cannot fully put into words," she said.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee halted the state's remaining scheduled executions for the rest of 2026 following Pike's failed execution and ordered a review of the incident. Pike's attorneys have also sought to have her death sentence commuted to life imprisonment.

Pike said she does not know why she survived or what will happen next, but is trying to focus on her recovery.

"Some days, finding hope is harder than others," she said. "For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time."

open image in gallery Pike was 18 and her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp was 17 when they lured her 19-year-old classmate, Colleen Slemmer, into the woods, tortured her and killed her (Slemmer is pictured at a media event before Pike’s execution was halted September 30) ( AP )

Read Pike’s statement in full:

“One month ago on September 30, I walked into the execution chamber at Riverbend men’s prison prepared to die. I had made my peace. I had told the people who loved me, supported me and stood by me through the years I was grateful for them. I had also told the people in the room and who were there to witness my execution that I was leaving them in loving kindness.”

“Several days later I woke up alone in a hospital confused and in pain. There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn't just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul.”

“I had not contemplated life beyond that night, and I’m deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position. I continue to think about my victim’s family and the terrible pain and loss they have endured.”

“I am recovering, and I know that I am getting stronger. But healing is not the same as being okay.”

“Since that night, I have been largely isolated in the prison’s medical ward, away from other people and the human connections that mean so much to me. That isolation brings its own kind of pain. I spent 28 years in solitary confinement and much of what I am experiencing today is a repeat of that condition.”

“I am searching for meaning in what happened to me. One thing that has given me strength is the extraordinary love and support I have received from people around the world. I am overwhelmed by the kindness and prayers of people I have known for years and complete strangers who have never met me. To know that so many people care about me, that they see me as a human being whose life matters, is something I cannot fully put into words. It is humbling, and it has touched me more deeply than I can explain.”

“I also want to thank the first responders, doctors, nurses and everyone at the hospital who cared for me. They treated me with compassion, dignity and respect. I will never forget their kindness. I also want to thank my attorneys and everyone who has fought for me, stood beside me and refused to give up on me.”

“I don't know why I survived that night. I don't know what comes next. Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time. And I am holding on to the love and kindness of so many people who have reminded me that I am not alone.”

News.title: South African court allows anti-illegal immigration marches under strict conditions
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A South African court ruled Friday that anti-illegal immigration groups could hold demonstrations in the South African city of Durban under strict conditions, after police sought to ban the protests over fears of violence.

Police had asked the court to block planned marches by the March and March movement, alleging that demonstrators intended to burn down a refugee reception center during a protest scheduled for Thursday.

That march did not take place after the KwaZulu-Natal High Court issued a temporary order against the protests.

Under the new ruling, protesters must follow designated routes and cannot carry sticks or conceal their faces. They can only demonstrate between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m.

Police argued that although South Africa protects the right to protest, that right is limited when demonstrations become disruptive.

“With the application, we don’t intend to prohibit lawful marches and protests of whatever nature, but what we’re against is breaking the law, damage to property, attacking people and injuring people,” South African national police chief Fannie Masemola said Friday.

Protesters have accused foreigners who are in the country illegally of stealing their jobs as the country's unemployment rate remains high. They also blame them for overburdening public services and for high crime rates in the country.

Some African countries, including Ghana and Nigeria, have repatriated their citizens following violence that began several weeks before an unofficial June 30 deadline set by protesters for immigrants living in the country illegally to leave.

Earlier this month, protests over a court ruling easing access to asylum turned violent, with at least 24 cars torched and shops looted.

March and March leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma has accused the government and the police of trying to deprive demonstrators of their right to protest.

The government recently deployed over 500 soldiers to KwaZulu-Natal province, which includes Durban.

With South Africans set to vote in local elections next week, the issue of illegal immigration has featured prominently in the campaign.

News.title: Greenland opens new international airport to lure tourists as it eyes future independence
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Greenland has opened a new international airport, seeking to lure visitors from around the world as the Arctic island looks toward eventual independence from Denmark.

Thursday's inaugural international flight between Copenhagen, Denmark, and Ilulissat, Greenland, was part of the island government's efforts to grow its tourism industry to boost and diversify an economy still reliant on fishing.

Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen described the new airport as “one of the biggest investments” in the island’s history. Nielsen was one of 169 passengers on Thursday's 4.5-hour flight on an Airbus A330neo. An Associated Press journalist also took the flight, operated by government-owned Air Greenland, as part of a trip organized by tourism agency Visit Greenland, for this story.

“If Greenland wants to be independent, we need to have a strong foundation, both economically and in terms of industry and business,” Nielsen told the AP before the plane departed.

The strategic island, home to roughly 56,000 people, has been a focus of U.S. President Donald Trump since his first term, when he initially expressed his desire to acquire Greenland. His repeated threats to seize the territory from Denmark, a NATO ally, during his second term prompted months of tensions with other NATO allies. In September, Trump signed an agreement with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.

“There’s no doubt that it has been a shadow over the entire Kingdom of Denmark, but especially Greenland,” said Danish Finance Minister Peter Hummelgaard, who also took the inaugural flight. “The opening of this new international airport marks, I think, hope and optimism.”

New international airports seek to lure new visitors

Ilulissat, known as the "City of Icebergs," sits along the island's western coast and is home to some 5,000 people. Greenland's third-largest city is also one of the island's most-visited destinations. More than 550 kilometers (342 miles) north of the capital, Nuuk, its tourism offerings range from sled dog tours to icefjord cruises in picturesque Disko Bay, known for its towering icebergs.

Previously, travelers reaching Ilulissat had to arrive by cruise ship, take a small plane from Iceland or fly to one of Greenland’s international hubs and connect to smaller aircraft. There are no road connections from other big towns.

For decades, Greenland’s main international aviation gateways were former U.S. military air bases, distant echoes of World War II, in Kangerlussuaq and Narsarsuaq. Locals and international visitors had to land there before catching smaller aircraft to the island's major towns, including Ilulissat and Nuuk. That changed in late 2024, when an international airport opened in Nuuk.

United Airlines last year began a new seasonal route between Nuuk and Newark, New Jersey. The inaugural flight was the first direct from the U.S. to Greenland by an American airline.

The Ilulissat airport, meanwhile, has a 5,000-square-meter (53,820 square feet) terminal and a new 2,200-meter (1.37-mile) runway, long enough to accommodate larger passenger aircraft. Air Greenland has committed to as many as six weekly flights between Copenhagen and Ilulissat during next year’s peak summer months, and Icelandair will also fly large jets from its Keflavik hub. Jens R. Lauridsen, CEO of Greenland Airports, said the company is also hoping to lure airlines in the U.S. and mainland Europe to serve Ilulissat.

“It’s quite wonderful that you can go directly right now,” said Kirsten Berthelsen, a 35-year-old Ilulissat resident and student who booked a ticket for Thursday's flight without realizing it was the inaugural service. “Sometimes it’s quite difficult to travel from Nuuk and to other countries.”

Tourism boom remains elusive

While the number of international visitors to Greenland has grown by at least 65% since 2018, reaching almost 150,000 in 2024, the expected travel boom has yet to materialize. In 2024, tourism accounted for less than 5% of the territory's GDP. Infrastructure, including hotel capacity, remains limited.

Aalborg University associate professor Carina Ren, who specializes in Arctic tourism, said some U.S. tourists were even deterred from visiting the island because of the recent Trump standoff, with a few canceling their flights.

“I’ve heard of people canceling their bookings, but also others canceling because they were afraid that perhaps they would not be welcomed,” she said, adding that many Americans still visit, particularly on cruise ships.

Even so, there are some local concerns about mass tourism and potential damage to Greenland’s fragile nature.

Palle Jerimiassen, a former regional mayor, said he fears the city's environment, population and infrastructure may be overwhelmed by too many visitors.

“How many can we invite?” he said. “We are welcoming all the tourists, it’s a possibility to earn some new money."

He added: "But we have to be careful.”

News.title: Embarrassing England on brink of historic World Cup exit
News.content:
It is, because they showed their quality and offered themselves a sniff with their Gallic heroics. They had to maintain that pace on Friday to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. “It looks like we’re going out of the tournament,” McDermott said. “That second half got scrappy and we should have handled that a lot better.”

McDermott is not blameless. The directives were clearly to offload when they could, and perhaps when they should not have, and the call to start Jez Litten over Brad O’Neill at hooker was, on reflection, a mistake. Litten has so much more impact off the bench and the Hull KR livewire could have been the spark England required when it proceeded to fall flat. It was also strange to see Lewis coming on in the No 9 role.

Yet it must be noted that this was just McDermott’s third match in charge and that Tonga was his first. With no warm-up game and with his English-based players at a disadvantage because of travel and the jet lag, that all-important opener was appallingly timed. Yet having been a member of the exclusive top three for so long, England must now concede they are merely in the top five. This tournament proved as much.

News.title: Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot
News.content:
David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

News.title: Trump administration loses grip on bird flu, experts warn
News.content:
The Trump administration has been criticised for losing control of a bird flu outbreak that has spread among mink and cattle farms across the United States.

The H5N1 virus has infected around 1,000 people since it was first detected in the late 1990s, killing roughly half of them. While it currently does not spread among humans, scientists have long worried that it could trigger a pandemic, and that each human infection raises the risk of the virus mutating.

A new variant emerged in 2020 and has since spread to millions of birds and hundreds of animal species across the globe, leading to devastating losses in both wildlife and farmed livestock and poultry.

While some countries have introduced tough measures to curb its spread, including mandatory culls of infected animals, “flockdowns” (where birds are kept indoors) and vaccination of farm workers who handle at-risk livestock, experts say the US is allowing the virus to run rampant.

For more than two months, an outbreak has raged unchecked on a Utah farm that raises thousands of mink for fur, news outlet ProPublica reported last week.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

Mink have very similar respiratory systems to humans, increasing the risk that a virus can spread between the animals and people, and undergo a process known as “reassortment”, when two or more viruses mix together to make a new, more dangerous strain.

News.title: Britain faces unprecedented squeeze on incomes, IFS says
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has ruled out making “crude cuts” to welfare after he failed to tackle the rising benefits bill in Wednesday’s Budget.

The Chancellor acknowledged last night that the current benefits system is “unsustainable” but said he will only look to make cuts “in a Labour way”.

Speaking to the BBC in the wake of Wednesday’s Budget, Mr Healey promised that “there will be a reduction in the benefits bill” before the next election.

However, he said this will not include “crude cuts” to payments.

He said: “We will do that in a Labour way, and we will do that because it is simply not good for Britain, or progressive, to have a bigger and bigger benefits bills.

“This system is unsustainable. I’ve been clear about that. The Prime Minister’s been clear about that. It’s what you do about it.”

He added: “We have to bring the benefits bill down. You don’t do that by crude cuts, especially when people are feeling the cost of living pressures.”

His comments on welfare come after Tory leader Kemi Badenoch accused Labour of presiding over a Government that had left Britain “overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system”.

She said: “Next year, under Labour, the tax burden will be the highest in our country’s history and our benefits bill is going up by tens of billions of pounds because this Government has put welfare first.”

The latest figures from the Office for Budget Responsibility released on Wednesday revealed that benefits spending is expected to jump by almost 30pc to £431bn by 2032.

Almost half the total is pensions and disability benefits for pensioners, despite the planned abolition of the triple lock. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey launches tax raid on savers as welfare bill spirals | Chancellor to pull in £4.3bn from landlords and savers as Badenoch calls for ‘tough love’ on benefits

2) Gulf states face tax raid on UK property investments | John Healey’s changes risk driving investment away from Britain, industry experts warn

3) UK hands Rolls-Royce £1.25bn to fund new jet engines | British engineering giant confirms plans for £2.5bn to be invested during next decade

4) Petrol drivers face threat of stealth tax raid to boost EVs | Official review recommends forcing fuel suppliers to fund new renewable energy subsidies

5) JP Morgan lashes out at ‘unprincipled’ bank tax | Wall Street giant criticises John Healey’s Budget announcement on surcharge increase

What happened overnight

The Chancellor will have woken up to jittery markets after Google-owner Alphabet revealed higher spending on AI.

Alphabet dropped 10pc in after-hours trading, wiping nearly $400 billion off its market value. Microsoft, by contrast, beat forecasts with better-than-expected cash flows that lifted its shares by 3pc.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan dropped 0.7pc, while Japan’s Nikkei fluctuated between gains and losses and was last ⁠up 1pc.

Oil prices retreated as investors latched onto hopes that peace talks to resolve the Middle East conflict could be back on the table.

European stocks were on track to edge higher at the open after the US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady as widely expected on Wednesday. The European Central Bank announces its next interest rate decision on Thursday.

News.title: Risk of Ebola spread in UK is low, experts stress
News.content:
Infectious disease experts have stressed the likelihood of Ebola spreading to the UK is low after the head of Africa’s health agency warned that the haemorrhagic fever could reach Britain.

The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the deadly virus that began in the volatile eastern region of the country. There have been 10,000 cases, including nearly 5,000 deaths, since the outbreak was first reported in May and it has now become the second largest Ebola epidemic in history.

In recent weeks the virus has spread to Kenya, where there have been nine cases including two deaths, and Nigeria. The case in Nigeria is concerning because the patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, the country’s capital, had no history of travel to the affected region of DRC. She has now been evacuated to Switzerland.

In comments reported by the Guardian Jean Kaseya, head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, described the outbreak as “unprecedented” as it was the first time that the disease had spread to three geographic regions of the continent. He warned that there was scope for further spread.

“We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”

On Wednesday the United States announced that travellers arriving by air would have to sign a statement affirming that they had not been in the DRC within the previous 21 days. Anyone found to provide false or misleading information would face imprisonment or a fine.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stressed that the risk to the UK is low. Dr Sam Collins, head of guidance, clinical and public health response at the agency, said the Ebola outbreak in DRC is serious but “the UK is well prepared to respond safely and effectively to the risk of imported cases arising here”.

UKHSA is monitoring travel routes from the affected countries and is providing information on symptoms.

The UKHSA said it is rare for Ebola to occur in returning travellers and the NHS has “well established procedures in place” for such a situation.

News.title: Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out
News.content:
It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

News.title: Burnham rules out calling early election
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has promised to offer households “breathing space” in his maiden Budget today.

The Chancellor insisted the economy has shown “resilience” in the face of the energy shock from the Iran war.

However, he admitted the conflict has pushed up the cost of living, “piling pressure on the families, on businesses, and on our public finances”.

Among the measures the Chancellor is expected to announce are plans to scrap standing charges on household gas bills – saving families up to £50 a year.

Mr Healey said: “We can’t stop these shocks that hit Britain, but we can make Britain more resilient when they do.

“So, this Budget is designed to give households breathing space from some of the everyday costs, provide targeted support for businesses and self-employed people, and to start the long-term action needed to get energy costs down for good.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey prepares to slash household gas bills by £50 | Chancellor to scrap standing charges on gas bills and curb Energy Secretary’s power

2) Minimum wage rise will drive up food prices, Healey warned | Manufacturers say they are already struggling to cover soaring production costs

3) Poundland directors quit in stand-off over administration | Board members fear owner wants to steer retailer into insolvency

4) Google attacks UK over ‘unlawful’ AI plans | Search giant fights plans by competition regulator to force it to promote rivals

5) Netherlands to cut 25,000 civil service jobs in AI push | Police and defence will be exempt from plans to trim 15pc of government workforce in next decade

What happened overnight

Ahead of the Budget, oil prices rose after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, which has renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East.

Brent crude was up 1.7pc to nearly $116 a barrel, maintaining inflationary pressure on the global economy. It traded around $70 before the start of the Iran war.

Meanwhile, Asia stocks rallied amid fresh enthusiasm about AI.

South Korea’s Kospi surged more than 6pc and was on track for its largest one-day gain since July, after chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold jump in quarterly profit and said it would return about $75 billion to shareholders this year.

The AI rally faces its next test when technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft report earnings after market close later today, with investors looking for evidence of returns that would justify the hefty cost of the AI build-out.

In Asia, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.7pc, with Japan’s Nikkei adding 1.1pc and ⁠China’s CSI300 blue-chip index climbing 0.7pc.

Sports.title: ‘I’m sure’ – Enzo Fernandez picks future club months after £125m transfer as Man City face exodus after guilty verdict
Sports.content:

ENZO FERNANDEZ insists he is “sure” about one club he will sign for in the future.

The World Cup-winning midfielder only completed his club-record £125million move to Manchester City in September.



But he has already revealed that he will not be finishing his career at the Etihad.

Fernandez, 25, is intent on returning to River Plate before he hangs up his boots.



And the strength of his comments suggests that fans of the Buenos Aires giants can take him for his word.

The ex-Chelsea midfielder learned his trade in River’s academy, making 51 first-team appearances and scoring 12 goals before leaving for Benfica in 2022.



Fernandez told Los Edul: “I want to return to River at some point.

“I’ve said it several times. I’m going to return, I’m sure. It’s something I really want.

“I stand by my words and what’s on record. If I say it, it’s because I feel it and know I need to return to win things and enjoy the River Plate world for many more years than I did.

“Today, I’m here with a long contract at Man City. There’s still a long way to go, but it will happen.”

Fernandez penned a bumper five-year deal at City, tying him to the club until the summer of 2031.

But the controversy surrounding the club could see big names like him – and others – jump ship sooner rather than later.

City have been found guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League’s financial rules, and face a range of punishments including points deductions and expulsion from the top flight.

Before signing with the Blues, Fernandez had flirted with a move to Real Madrid, but in an unusual twist, the Bernabeu side published an official statement distancing themselves from a move for the Argentine.

Sports.title: Man Utd Munich air disaster memorial smashed and looted by thieves with medals stolen in ‘disgusting’ act of vandalism
Sports.content:
Next

CHERISHED medals have been snatched by thieves after a Manchester United Munich air disaster memorial was vandalised.

Eight Old Trafford stars were among 23 people tragically killed in a plane crash on February 6, 1958.



And a display case at Manchesterplatz, where the catastrophe took place, has been vandalised.

Munich Police say the glass was smashed with a stone, with the incident believed to have happened on Monday.



Robbers escaped from the tribute to fallen United heroes, which was previously visited by Red Devils skipper Bruno Fernandes, with unique medals and a glass sculpture.

And Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation chair Ifty Ahmed released an emotional statement following the theft.



He said: “The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation is deeply saddened by this act of vandalism and theft.

“Manchesterplatz is a place of enormous significance to the families of the 23 people who lost their lives as a result of the Munich air disaster, and to Manchester United supporters across the world.

“We are particularly grateful to our friends in Munich, especially the Red Docs, for their continued care and dedication to this very special place, and for acting so swiftly to repair the damage.

“Those responsible may have damaged a display case and stolen treasured items, but they cannot steal our memories, diminish our friendship or destroy the legacy of those we remember.



“Their memory will endure, and the bond between Manchester and Munich will remain unbreakable.”

The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation paid to repair the broken glass window on the same day despite United offering to foot the bill.

And Red Devils fans raced onto social media to hit out at the shameless vandals.

One said: “This is simply mindless and a disgusting, disrespectful act. Hopefully those responsible are caught very soon and face the full force of the law.”



Another added: “Stealing from a memorial to people who lost their lives is a new low, hope every item is recovered.”

A third furious United supporter chimed in: “I knew this had been attacked in some way but to actually steal from this on top of that – horrible.”

A fourth noted: “Whoever has done this is the lowest of the low.”



And a fifth simply wrote: “Unacceptable.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A memorial stone was first installed at Manchesterplatz in 2004, before a display case was later added.

Close to 1,500 people attended the annual remembrance service at the site in February.

Sports.title: Chelsea vs Man Utd has had THIRTEEN different managers in last 13 meetings with both clubs stuck in sacking doom loop
Sports.content:
BOSS AROUND Chelsea vs Man Utd has had THIRTEEN different managers in last 13 meetings with both clubs stuck in sacking doom loop







Next

MANCHESTER UNITED and Chelsea are set to lock horns with their ELEVENTH different managerial pair after a sacking loop that has seen THIRTEEN different bosses working as many meetings.

United and the Blues will face off on Saturday in a crunch Premier League clash at Stamford Bridge with Michael Carrick and Xabi Alonso in charge of each respective team.



This is the latest managerial pairing amid an ongoing sack-athon that started back in 2020.

That was when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s Man Utd and the West Londoners’ Frank Lampard played out a goalless draw on October 24 at Old Trafford.



Lampard‘s dismissal brought in Thomas Tuchel at Stamford Bridge and the current England manager picked up another 0-0 draw against Solskjaer on February 28, 2021 in London.



Carrick then replaced Solskjaer on an interim capacity and played out a 1-1 draw against Tuchel on November 28 of that same year at Stamford Bridge.

United made another caretaker appointment in Ralf Rangnick, who oversaw the exact same result on the return fixture at Old Trafford on April 28, 2022.

Then both clubs switched managers the following season as Graham Potter was hired at Chelsea after Tuchel’s acrimonious exit and Erik ten Hag became the Red Devils’ permanent boss.

That led to another 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge on October 22, 2022 with Potter getting the sack soon after.



Lampard returned to his beloved club’s dugout until the end of the season but suffered a 4-1 loss to Ten Hag and co at the Theatre of Dreams on May 25, 2023.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Mauricio Pochettino returned to the Premier League the following season but suffered a 2-1 loss to United, who were still led by the Dutchman, on December 6, 2023 at Old Trafford.

The pair met again on April 4, 2024 at Stamford Bridge where the Blues finally beat the Manchester giants 4-3.



Ten Hag’s time then came to an end and was replaced by Ruud van Nistelrooy on an interim capacity, while Pochettino was succeeded by Enzo Maresca.

The new pair played out a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford on November 3, 2024 before Ruben Amorim replaced Van Nistelrooy as United’s permanent boss.

Amorim, though, lost the return fixture on May 16, 2025 in West London with Maresca and co winning 1-0.

The Portuguese tactician, though, got his revenge on September 20 of that same year as he won 2-1 at the Theatre of Dreams.

But Amorim didn’t last and Carrick returned for another caretaker stint that proved to be successful as he also beat Liam Rosenior’s Chelsea 1-0 away on April 18 of this year.



And the now permanent Man Utd boss will lock horns with Alonso this weekend.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It doesn’t look like the cycle will end any time soon as Carrick’s position is becoming increasingly untenable after overseeing the Red Devils’ worst league start in 40 years.

Alonso also hasn’t been stellar as he has only won half of his first eight Premier League matches, of which he lost three.

Sports.title: England U15s stars PROTECT referee during World Cup brawl vs Bolivia just days after alleged racist incident
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND Under-15s jumped in to protect a referee during a World Cup and Festival match against Bolivia.

At the very end of the match, the Young Lions were awarded what was deemed to be a controversial penalty.

But as the No11 stepped up to take it, the Bolivia goalkeeper moved over to the left side and refused to attempt the save.



The England star was then able to pass the ball into the empty net to give the nation a 3-2 lead.



It proved to be the last kick of the match, with the referee blowing the final whistle just seconds later.

While the Young Lions celebrated, some Bolivia players ran over to the referee to confront him.

And when the England stars realised, they cut the celebrations short.

The players ran over to the centre of the pitch, with some appearing to make an attempt to protect the referee.

As the offical made his own way off, a melee took place between the two teams and staff.

Fifa declined to comment on the incident at this stage but SunSport understands the world body has asked for formal reports from the officials and both sides before any update is announced.

The FA also declined to comment.



It happened four days after England walked off the pitch following an alleged incident of racism during a match against Ireland.

Young Lions boss Matt Thorpe withdrew his players in the 40th minute of the clash on Monday.

An England player claimed an opponent had allegedly made a racist comment towards him.

Fifa later announced that it was investigating the incident.

DREAM TEAM managers have until 11am on Saturday to confirm their transfers for Gameweek 9.

We published our latest batch of differential options yesterday but today it’s time to get sensible with some logical recommendations.

Marcus Tavernier (£3.6m) and/or Evanilson (£4.1m)

It’s all eyes on Bournemouth after they made it five wins in a row (and five clean sheets) with a 3-0 victory over Aston Villa in the Carabao Cup.



This purple patch has yielded a lot of Dream Team points and a quick look at the schedule gives gaffers good reason to expect plenty more in the coming weeks.



The Cherries will face Leeds and Sparta Prague this coming Gameweek before taking on Ipswich, Nottingham Forest, Celta Vigo and Fulham before the end of November.

Tavernier has been a gift for Dream Team bosses this season, racking up 84 points via six goals while remaining affordable throughout.

He ranks third among midfielders after eight Gameweeks and yet his ownership remains at 9.2%.

Evanilson is equally strong as the game’s most in-form striker after a run of four goals and two assists in five games.

John McGinn (£4.4m)

At the time of writing, Nicolas Jackson (£4m) is the most popular recruit ahead of Saturday’s deadline after his fantastic brace against Manchester City but gaffers should seek out an availability update from Unai Emery before fully committing.

The Senegal international was not even named among the substitutes at Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup, sparking rumours of an injury.

The reliable Scotsman has quietly amassed 73 points this season, putting him eighth among midfielders.

Sports.title: How Suzuki has wowed Villa fans since replacing Martinez
Sports.content:
Aston Villa fans still sing about having the world's number one goalkeeper. But what started as a chant for Emiliano Martinez and morphed into defiant support for young Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has become something else. They actually believe it.

Suzuki has been superb since joining from Parma in the summer. Not only has Martinez not been as missed as many anticipated, there is growing optimism that in his 24-year-old replacement, Villa have a goalkeeper who has even more facets to his game.

There have been some standout displays already. Suzuki was excellent in the win over Manchester City last time out, ending their 100-per-cent Premier League record under Enzo Maresca. The contrast with Gianluigi Donnarumma at the other end was stark.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the match between Aston Villa and Manchester City

While the Champions League winner allowed Nicolas Jackson's decider to go through him, Suzuki pulled off a series of stops, relieved pressure with his claims and looked far more composed with the ball at his feet. Only one of the two looked world class.

Image: Suzuki saves from Vedat Muriqi in Aston Villa's win over Fenerbahce

Suzuki had been identified by Paris Saint-Germain as a potential long-term replacement for Donnarumma, who left last year. But mooted plans to loan him out to continue his development helped convince the player that the plans at Villa were preferable.

"He is ambitious," explained his manager Unai Emery when asked about Suzuki following that performance against City. "It is very important, his mentality. He is very ambitious himself. He chose to be here with us when we spoke with him about our project."

Suzuki is one of the reasons why fans are excited about Villa's refresh. The challenge given the changes in personnel was always going to be embracing Emery's ideas quickly given that they famously take time to grasp. But the goalkeeper has adapted swiftly.

It is Suzuki's work in the build-up that has caught the eye. It had to be a strength because it is so important in Emery's system. "We need one 'keeper first to save us in the goal. But as well we need one 'keeper to try to help us in our build-up," the Villa boss explained.

Interestingly, the figures for expected goals do not include those openings for the opposition that did not result in shots. In the case of Suzuki, in particular, that is significant because his ability to come off his line and sweep up behind Villa's high line is a major asset.

Sports.title: Doyle: Glad to be back in the saddle
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing’s ambassador prepares for her first rides back at Southwell on Saturday and previews the key contests from Keeneland at the Breeders' Cup on Saturday.

Back with eight rides at Southwell

It's been a long, difficult road, but I'm finally back in the saddle at Southwell on Saturday, five months after breaking my left leg in a horrible fall at Bath. I comfortably passed my mandatory 'return to riding' test in midweek which clears me to take eight rides on the All-Weather.

There are so many people to thank for helping my recovery, in particular the Injured Jockeys Fund. Rob Treviss and Joe Baker at Oaksey House in Lambourn and my physiotherapist Daloni Lucas have all been amazing.

I've been working with those guys five days a week since I left hospital a few weeks after my fall and, in my mind, always aimed for an early November comeback, so I'm delighted to be on track and feeling good.

Injuries are part and parcel of being a jockey and I've had plenty but none that has kept me out of action for this long. I'm just grateful that such a bad injury has allowed me another chance to do what I love.

For now, I aim to concentrate on building up my race-riding fitness on the All-Weather before finalising my plans for the winter, but I'm hopeful I will be riding overseas at some stage.

Sunny looks my best chance of comeback winner

It would be amazing to come back with a winner at Southwell on Saturday night and Simon Crisford's Always Sunny​ looks my best chance in the All-Weather Trials Day - Lingfield 2nd Jan 2027 Fillies' Novice Stakes (5.40).​

She showed a lot of promise on debut at Newcastle, finishing a close second to the odds-on favourite despite being badly hampered by a loose horse.

I'm also hoping for a big run from Ralph Beckett's classy filly Chantilly Lace​ in the feature race, the Midnite Ain't Your Grandad's Bookie Handicap (6.15)​. I rode work on this lovely big filly last week and expect her to appreciate the drop in grade on a surface she should enjoy.

I also sat on Ralph's Drum Bay​ last week and got a nice enough feel off him to suggest he will go well in the All-Weather Championship Is Back Nursery Handicap (5.05)​ after being gelded, though he has Godolphin's 92-rated National Honour​ to beat.

Hoping for memorable first ride on Circus

My first ride back is Oxford Circus in the first division of the ARC All Weather Bonus Is Back Handicap (4.00). James Owen's ex-Irish gelding showed promise at Brighton recently and will hopefully sharpen up for the fitting of a visor in an open race.

In the second division (4.35)​, I'm on Mike Murphy's reliable filly Desert Charm​ who is so consistent and is drawn well in stall one after beating all but the favourite in a Yarmouth handicap earlier this month.

I ride again for James Owen in the AWC Finals Day At Newcastle 26th March EBF 'Confined' Restricted Maiden Stakes (6.50)​. Al Alami​ showed promise over seven-furlongs at Kempton on debut when racing up with the pace so should enjoy stepping back a furlong.

Strong pace will suit Beckett sprinter

Bolo Neighs should also go well in the Make The Move To Midnite Handicap (7.25). Ralph Beckett's gelding enjoys being produced off a strong pace which he should get if he can overcome a tricky wide draw in stall 11.

My final ride is for champion All-Weather trainer Tony Carroll in the Midnite A Next Generation Betting App Handicap (8.00). I've won twice on Midnight Call around Wolverhampton - the last time just a few days before my accident in May. She's done all her winning round a bend, so we'll have to see how she copes with the straight 5f.

Watch the 2026 Breeders' Cup from Keeneland live on Sky Sports Racing (Sky 415 | Virgin 512) on Friday 30th and Saturday 31st October.

Blue is the colour at Breeders' Cup

It would be wonderful to see Andrew Balding crown a magnificent season with victory in the Makers Mark Breeders' Cup Filly & Mare (7.04) at Keeneland on Saturday.

His beautiful filly Blue Bolt is the worthy favourite despite a difficult draw. She definitely has the gears she needs for a track like that and should confirm her superiority over Aidan O'Brien's nimble filly Precise, who has chased her home three times already this year.

I have similar expectations of Godolphin's Notable Speech in the FanDuel Breeders' Cup Mile (8.20). Charlie Appleby's colt is so professional on turning tracks and couldn't have had a better 'prep' than his Group 1 win in the Woodbine Mile.

Nunthorpe hero Bacio to be crowned Sprint King

It's going to take a massive performance to deny Wesley Ward's US ace Bacio in the Prevagen Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint (5.48) at Keeneland.

British racing fans saw how potent he is when he won the Group One Nunthorpe Stakes at York in the summer, and he should have too much speed on his home patch for Donnacha O'Brien's July Cup hero Comanche Brave who may just find this test too sharp.

I'm keeping my fingers crossed that Mick Appleby's Big Mojo gets a run, too. He's first reserve with my husband Tom (Marquand) on stand-by to ride him. It will be disappointing for everyone connected with him if he misses out.

Surprised to see Ryan on Cellini

I was surprised to see Ryan Moore on Benvenuto Cellini rather than stable companion Diamond Necklace in the Longines Breeders' Cup Turf (9.36). To get so close to Daryz in the Arc was an unreal performance from the latter who does have a bad draw to overcome, while Benvenuto Cellini will undoubtedly enjoy this test.

I would love to see Jessie Harrington's Irish Champion Stakes winner Hotazhell run a big race. I don't feel this colt gets the credit he deserves for what he's achieved and finds himself at big odds again.

The Longines Breeders' Cup Classic (10.16) will be worth waiting for and I'm hoping Japan will claim the glory with the brilliant Forever Young, who is entitled to sharpen up for his comeback run at Belmont and can overcome the huge threat presented by Bill Mott's Sovereignty.

Watch the 2026 Breeders' Cup from Keeneland live on Sky Sports Racing (Sky 415 | Virgin 512) on Friday 30th and Saturday 31st October.

Sports.title: What does Djokovic need to do to qualify for ATP Finals in Turin?
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic needs at the very least a semi-final at the Paris Masters to have a chance to make the ATP Finals in Turin; a final would likely do it, and a title would surely do it; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports from Monday November 2

Novak Djokovic: After shock defeat in Basel former world No 1 heads to Paris Masters in race to make ATP Finals in Turin

Highlights of the Swiss Indoors match between Novak Djokovic and Jan-Lennard Struff

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Novak Djokovic missed a big chance to strengthen his push for a place at the end-of-year ATP Finals after a loss ‌to Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel on Thursday night.

Defeat has left the Serb with precious few opportunities to make up ground in the race to Turin.

Back ‌in Basel for the first time in 15 years, 39-year-old Djokovic fell 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (5-7) in the second round, his first defeat by German veteran Struff in nine meetings.

The result left Djokovic 11th in the qualification race for the eight-player season finale, ​319 points behind ninth-placed Rafael Jodar, who currently occupies the final qualifying spot with ⁠Jannik Sinner not playing in Turin due to injury.

A total of five main-draw spots now remain, with as many as 10 players still in contention.

Alexander ⁠Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton all have places in the ATP Finals starting on November 15, leaving Djokovic battling for one of the remaining spots ‌with next week's Paris Masters offering him another opportunity to pick up points.

It seems likely that Daniil Medvedev and Arthur Fils will claim two of the five remaining spots. This would leave three places available for a group of eight players: Djokovic, Jodar, Flavio Cobolli, Frances Tiafoe, Alex de Minaur, Taylor Fritz, Tommy Paul and Jakub Mensik.

However, Cobolli suffered an injury during his match against Matteo Berrettini in Vienna, leaving him visibly emotional and in tears on court, leaving a big question mark about whether he will be able to compete for the remainder of the season.

There are five players currently separated by fewer than 500 points, with Djokovic firmly in the middle of that group.

He will head to the French capital as a record seven-time champion but would likely need at least a semi-final appearance alongside early exits for some of the players around him in the rankings to put himself in a position to qualify.

Who would write off Djokovic?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gigi Salmon is joined by Tim Henman and Ryan Harrison to debate whether Djokovic should consider retirement after ongoing health issues and a shock first-round exit at the 2026 US Open

Djokovic may even consider ‌entering the ATP 250 event in Stockholm afterwards if he still needs points to secure a spot in Turin.

He missed the previous two editions of the ATP Finals due to injury but had indicated that he intended to return to the event aiming to claim a record-extending eighth title.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion ⁠has endured another tough season physically, though his run to the Australian Open final, ​a Wimbledon semi-final and his Beijing triumph have provided notable highs.

Few will ​write off Djokovic's chances of reaching Turin even at this stage, given the resilience that ​he has shown throughout his glittering career.

"I won the title in Beijing a few weeks ago, ⁠which was definitely my best week this year apart from the Grand Slam final in Australia," Djokovic said in Basel.

"It's been a year with a lot of struggles, particularly physically, but I'm still here ⁠and as competitive as anybody. If somebody beats me, well ​done, good job, but I'm definitely going to fight and not give these youngsters too easy ​a stroll on court. They have to earn their victories.

"That's also what motivates me: seeing how I can match up with players 15-plus years younger than me. ‌It's been quite an interesting process ​to experience."

Sports.title: Dart into Guangzhou Open semi as Rybakina injured in Tokyo
Sports.content:
Harriet Dart continued her sparkling run at the Guangzhou Open, beating former world No 2 Paula Badosa to reach her second WTA semi-final.

The British No 3 looked up against it after losing the first set 6-3 but rebounded brilliantly to win the next two sets 6-2 6-4, securing her fifth victory in a row and one of the finest of her career.

"It was an incredible battle," Dart said in her on-court interview on Sky Sports. "I thought Paula started really strongly. I was always behind, but I knew going in that it was going to be an incredibly tough match.

"I really needed to hang in there in the tough moments, and maybe I'd get a chance. Luckily I was able to take my chances today and I'm really excited to be in the semi-final.

"It's been a very long time since I've been in the business end of a (WTA) tournament, so I'm very proud of that."

Dart is into her first WTA semi-final since the Transylvania Open in 2024, having beaten Tatiana Prozorova and Janice Tjen in the earlier stages after coming through two qualifying rounds.

Rybakina withdraws from Pan Pacific Open with injury

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Elena Rybakina against Alina Charaeva from the China Open

World No 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew injured against Leylah Fernandez in the Pan Pacific Open to exit the tournament at the quarter-final stage.

The Kazakh player withdrew from the match before a point was played, giving the Canadian Fernandez safe passage into the last four in Tokyo, where she will play Kamilla Rakhimova for a place in the final.

"I just wanted to say thank you so much for coming today, but unfortunately I won't be able to play," the 27-year-old said on-court.

"I've been struggling for a couple of days with a little injury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Elena Rybakina gives her reaction after winning the US Open

"It's difficult for me to come and play at 100 per cent since there is also a very important tournament coming up."

Rybakina beat Yulia Putintseva 6-2, 6-3 to advance to the quarterfinals and will stay the world No 1 at the conclusion of a year in which she won two Grand Slams - the Australian Open and the U.S. Open.

Having won Wimbledon in 2022, Rybakina - a 27-year-old born in Russia but representing Kazakhstan - is only a French Open title away from completing the career Grand Slam.

She described her year-end status as "an incredibly special moment for me."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rybakina beats Sabalenka to win US Open!

"I'm really proud of what I've achieved this season and the consistency I've shown throughout the year," said Rybakina, who also won titles in Stuttgart and Ningbo and rose to No. 1 in the world for the first time by winning the U.S. Open.

Rybakina will be honoured with a trophy to mark the achievement during a special presentation at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells from November 8-15.

Sports.title: Vilips takes first-round lead at Mexico Open
Sports.content:
Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country.

Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey.

The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver.

"Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round of the Grand Final in Spain

Kensai Hirata of Japan was a stroke back, and Ben Griffin was at 64 with Marco Penge, Garrick Higgo and Jeffrey Kang.

Alvaro Ortiz of Mexico opened with a 65. He earned his PGA Tour card for next year through the Korn Ferry Tour.

"It was lovely," Ortiz said. "Bogey-free, played really solid. I felt like I was just flowing the whole day. Gave myself a lot of chances. I think I did very well from tee to green, which makes it very nice on this golf course."

Ortiz won the event in 2021 when it was part of the PGA Tour Latinoamerica schedule. The World Wide Technology Championship is next week at El Cardonal at Diamante in Los Cabos.

Vilips won the 2025 Puerto Rico Open for his lone PGA Tour title, making him exempt on the tour through next season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Two-time winner of the Ballon d’Or and double World Cup champion Ronaldo turns his hand to golf as he tees off at the DP World India Championship in Delhi. Credit: DP World Tour

The former Stanford player is 141st in the FedEx Cup Fall standings, with many players fighting to get into the final top 100 to remain on the tour.

Hirata is trying to move up from 170th. He made a 20-foot eagle putt on No. 3 and holed two birdie putts outside 20 feet.

"It was a perfect 7-wood distance and I hit a perfect 7-wood shot, which left me a really easy left-to-righter," Hirata said about the eagle. "Then that went in and kept the momentum going the rest of the back nine."

Penge is 112th in the standings. He had an 18-foot eagle putt on No. 3.

"I feel like I haven't actually played that much this year," Penge said "I've only played 18 tournaments due to, obviously, health issues. I'm just trying to get back fit really."

Defending champion Brian Campbell shot a 67.

Tom Kim also was at 67. He's playing for the first time since he won the gold medal in the Asian Games, which excuses him from mandatory military serve in South Korea.

U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark had a 69. He's the only player from the top 10 in the world in the field.

John Daly II, the son of the two-time major champion, opened with a 70. He's playing on a sponsor exemption.

4m ago 10.27 EDT Fenerbahce name Kuyt as interim manager Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt ⁠will be in the Fenerbahce dugout when his old ⁠club visit Istanbul in the Champions League next week after the Turkish club named him as interim manager. Kuyt, 46, took over from Ismail Kartal, who resigned ⁠following Monday’s 2-1 derby defeat ​by ​Galatasaray and Fenerbahce’s baord have now confirmed the Dutchman will remain in charge until the next international break. “The committee established by our board will carry out the work ‌to appoint our new head coach, and the process ​will be accelerated,” Fenerbahce said in a statement. The former Netherlands international ​spent six seasons at ​Liverpool ‌between 2006 ​and ​2012 before joining Fenerbahce, where he won the Turkish league title in 2014. Share Updated at 10.27 EDT

11m ago 10.21 EDT Louise Taylor ‘Where we want to be’: Le Bris stays positive as faltering Sunderland face Coventry reunion Twenty seconds of stoppage time remained when Enzo Le Fée picked up the ball and kissed it before taking a corner. As intended, the Frenchman’s perfect, right-footed delivery dropped into the corridor of uncertainty that leaves goalkeepers torn between leaving their line or standing firm. It also dipped at the right moment for Dan Ballard to power a header in off the crossbar. Extra time in the 2025 Championship playoff semi-final second leg was almost over and Sunderland had secured a 1-1 draw that consigned Coventry to a 3-2 aggregate defeat. As an outpouring of the loudest, most raucous emotion imaginable left the Stadium of Light feeling as if it was literally shaking, Régis Le Bris momentarily looked bewildered. By the time joyous comprehension began spreading across the Sunderland manager’s face, Frank Lampard was already a study in misery. Sunderland were on their way to Wembley, leaving Coventry in the Championship for another year. Asked whether Saturday’s result could be key for both sides, the Sky Blues manager replied: double quotation mark No, it’s too early for that. It’s a good opponent who are a very strong team. To find the consistency is what top teams manage to do. Some of our players in terms of Premier League experience are learning in real time. We have to learn quickly, improve quickly. We’ve all been given another challenge and they have to relish it and take it head on. Share Updated at 10.08 EDT
