37m ago 09.54 EDT Maresca on 'aggressive' Brighton and City's right direction Round two of Man City v Brighton at the Etihad after their midweek Carabao Cup game there went all the way to penalties. “They are doing very good, on and off the ball, they are very aggressive, man-to-man oriented, they attack very good with so many players. It’s going to be a tough game,” City manager Enzo Maresca said in a press conference, adding that they score many goals against teams. No Premier League side has more than Brighton (23) this season. Asked whether there is no more established Premier League Big Six, he replied: “You can have one or two surprises every season but now the level is so similar, you can drop points against any team and win against any team. It’s more of a similar level. It’s very good for the Premier League, that’s why so many people probably love the Premier League because you never know.” Four months have passed since Maresca’s appointment. Unsurprisingly, he is happy with how his table-toppers are faring. “I think we go in the right direction. I said in the last press conference, after changing manager and many players after so many years, it takes time to compete again – and we are competing in all competitions.” View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City side are ahead of Arsenal on goal difference in the Premier League table Photograph: Dave Howarth/CameraSport/Getty Images Share Updated at 09.58 EDT

51m ago 09.41 EDT Paul MacInnes More details from England’s controversial U15 World Cup win over Bolivia, sealed with an uncontested penalty: It appears that the Bolivian goalkeeper chose not to try and save England’s decisive penalty in protest at what he saw as an inaccurate call by the referee. Bolivia felt the foul which led to the spot kick had occurred outside the box. After England then loudly celebrated their goal, Bolivian players then ran over to the ref to berate him. While they were held back by coaching staff from both countries, one player was ultimately shown the red card. FIFA are awaiting the officials’ report on the game. This was, remarkably, the 936th game of the tournament, and England’s last, after they finished in Tier B of the competition. The Tier A final will be contested later today by Czechia and Spain. Share Updated at 09.41 EDT

1h ago 09.30 EDT Munich air disaster memorial targeted by thieves The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF) charity has said it is “deeply saddened” after items were stolen from a memorial to the Munich air disaster in the German city. The memorial display in Manchesterplatz honours the 23 victims of the disaster, which occurred when the plane transporting Manchester United home from a European Cup tie in Belgrade crashed after refuelling in Munich on February 6, 1958. The tragedy took the lives of eight United players. The MMMF said it was notified earlier this week that the memorial display case had been vandalised and that items had been taken. They said United had offered to pay for repairs but that it had already agreed to cover the costs. MMMF chair Ifty Ahmed said: “The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation is deeply saddened by this act of vandalism and theft. “Manchesterplatz is a place of enormous significance to the families of the 23 people who lost their lives as a result of the Munich air disaster, and to Manchester United supporters across the world. “Those responsible may have damaged a display case and stolen treasured items, but they cannot steal our memories, diminish our friendship or destroy the legacy of those we remember. Their memory will endure, and the bond between Manchester and Munich will remain unbreakable.” Press Association Share Updated at 09.31 EDT

1h ago 09.19 EDT Forest Green launch legal proceedings against former manager Savage's departure Forest Green owner Dale Vince says the club have started legal proceedings over their former manager Robbie Savage’s departure to Peterborough. Vince told Sky Sports News: “We are suing Peterborough and Robbie Savage for £2m, which was the buyout clause that we were cheated out of. And that process began last week.” Vince claimed there was “an abundance of evidence of an approach” made by Peterborough’s chair, Darragh MacAnthony. Peterborough declined to comment on the latest development, but Posh chairman Darragh MacAnthony has previously posted on X that the appointment of Savage was “100 per cent proper, following all rules”. Savage left National League side Forest Green four weeks ago. View image in fullscreen Robbie Savage moved up two divisions to manage Peterborough United, who are 21st in League One. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images Share Updated at 10.23 EDT

1h ago 09.13 EDT David Pleat Under-21 football should be scrapped. There are 18-year-olds retained only so clubs have a big enough squad to support the one player who could become a diamond. A boy should be released at latest 18. Those who stay should be in the first team or on loan. Young players need the competitiveness of senior football as soon as possible. Academy football is tidy and highly technical but has little resemblance to the frenetic, physical senior game. It also doesn’t test whether a boy has the mentality to cope in a tough dressing room where older players don’t want you taking their place. As a young player at Nottingham Forest I dribbled in training past an older teammate who warned: “Do that again, son, and I’ll break your leg.” It’s not like that any more but you need a certain character. Full story: The academy system needs a refresh but now is the time for Carrick to trust in youth Read more View image in fullscreen Manchester United academy graduate Shea Lacey has made five appearances this season. Photograph: Will Palmer/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock Share

1h ago 09.02 EDT Arbeloa: Fulham need to be more clinical After two Premier League wins on the trot, Fulham took a back-step on Wednesday with a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace in the Carabao Cup, despite controlling play and dominating possession. “I think we can do better in the final third,” manager Álvaro Arbeloa said in his press conference this morning. “We controlled the game, we had the possession but even with that, we could have created more chances. It’s something we need to improve. We need to work on it and do better in the final pass and be more clinical in the finishing.” He said that front men Gonzalo García and Rodrigo Muniz needed better service. In a clash of Spanish managers, his side face Unai Emery’s Aston Villa tomorrow evening. “We are in a process as a team; in every process, there are ups and downs. I think we need to learn from our mistakes,” he said. He also said that Emile Smith-Rowe, a peripheral player this season, needed to be patient for his chance. “Emile is a very talented player, like others,” he said. “They need to keep working as they are doing and they need to wait for their opportunity.” Share Updated at 09.03 EDT

2h ago 08.49 EDT Brighton hope to have Chema Andres and Ferdi Kadioglu available for their second trip to Manchester City of the week. Andres and Kadioglu sat out Wednesday’s Carabao Cup tie at the Etihad Stadium after suffering hip injuries at Liverpool on Saturday. But both are expected to return for the Premier League visit this weekend, when Charalampos Kostoulas will also be available after he was rested in midweek. However, Pascal Struijk will not be available when Brighton look for revenge after being knocked out of the cup on penalties. Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said at a press conference in Manchester on Thursday: “A positive was that (Yankuba) Minteh and Mats Wieffer had their comeback yesterday. “Ferdi, Chema, also Kostoulas (who) we rested yesterday, we are quite convinced that he will be an option for Saturday.” PA Share

2h ago 08.45 EDT Michael Carrick: United players have 'hunger to do better' Should he stay or should he already have gone? It doesn’t get any easier for under-fire Michael Carrick as his side face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in tomorrow’s early kick-off. Following their 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, Manchester United are 16th in the Premier League and on their worst run without a victory in all competitions since 2015. “The boys, I have to say, are hungry,” Carrick said in a press conference today. “We’re hurting because we haven’t won enough football games, but there’s an intensity, there’s a bit of an edge, there’s a disappointment, there’s a hunger to do better, for sure.” Surely this match is Carrick’s last chance. He appears to be ignoring all the noise. “My responsibility is the players,” he said. “The outside is not anything for me to focus on. “I know what we can affect, I know what we need to improve. I know as a group, leading a group, what help they need a little bit as well and a bit of guidance at certain times and dealing with certain things.” Carrick also confirmed that Bruno Fernandes retains the club captaincy and is “fully committed” to the cause. View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick looked downcast on the touchline as Bournemouth won at Old Trafford. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at 08.46 EDT

2h ago 08.12 EDT Cristiano Ronaldo moves closer to 1,000-goal milestone 985 not out… yes, that shy and not retiring (yet) Portuguese mega-star is nearing the magical mark. He scored a 15-minute hat-trick to help Al-Nassr to a 5-3 win over Al Kholood yesterday. His club are second in the Saudi Pro League behind Al Qadsiah on goal difference. Never mind his 30-day suspension for walking out on a Portugal training camp – at this rate, the 41-year-old could hit four figures in early 2027. View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates after completing his hat-trick for Al-Nassr. Photograph: Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images Share Updated at 08.17 EDT

2h ago 08.04 EDT News to wound hipster football fans: Inter and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the San Siro from the 2031-32 season. It will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost £1bn. Say it ain’t so. Looks nice, but it’s not got the beauty or dignity of the spiral walkways, has it? View image in fullscreen With a new stadium sponsored by Italy’s largest insurance company on the way, the San Siro is into its last few seasons of use. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP Compare and contrast: Inter and Milan unveil plans for new shared stadium to replace San Siro Read more View image in fullscreen An image of the planned new stadium, designed by Norman Foster and David Manica, which will be built on the San Siro site. Photograph: Foster + Partners Share Updated at 08.04 EDT

3h ago 07.45 EDT Arsenal’s appeal against Max Dowman’s red card in their Carabao Cup defeat at Fleetwood has been rejected by an independent commission. That means no wonder boy in the squad when they play Liverpool on Sunday, as well as their next games against Hull and Newcastle. (To be fair, Dowman has had precious few Premier League minutes so far this season.) A headline-making minor setback in the 16-year-old’s embryonic career then. I still don’t think his reaction warranted a red card, mind. What do you readers make of it? Full story: Max Dowman to miss three games after Arsenal’s red card appeal rejected Read more View image in fullscreen Max Dowman’s reaction to a tackle in Arsenal’s surprise loss to Fleetwood earned him a three-match ban. Photograph: James Harrison/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock Share Updated at 07.46 EDT

3h ago 07.38 EDT Uncontested penalty seals England win in U15 World Cup More drama involving England. They beat Bolivia 3-2, with the goalkeeper standing passively by the goalpost and making no effort to save the match-winning spot kick. According to the PA, Bolivia players then appeared to confront the referee, as well as England players, before both sides finally left the pitch in Azerbaijan, which is hosting the tournament. This comes four days after the abandonment of their match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. The matter has been referred to a FIFA independent disciplinary committee. Share Updated at 07.40 EDT

3h ago 07.21 EDT Ballard and Mundle out for Sunderland The Premier League’s bottom two teams play on Saturday, as Sunderland travel to Coventry. Wearsiders will have fond memories of Dan Ballard’s late winner in the 2024-25 Championship play-off semi-final against Frank Lampard’s side. No chance of a similar intervention this time round, with the centre-back absent due to a thigh issue. Romain Mundle is also out, with knee problems. With two wins in their last three matches, Coventry are on the up and “competitive”, according to Régis Le Bris, who spoke in his press conference about what changes with promotion to the top tier: “Now you don’t have the same amount of possession so it’s a new balance and you have to learn. “It’s always a new story. Coming from last year to this season, we had the World Cup, a few injuries and a tough start in the Premier League with a busy schedule. “It means they have to adapt and to learn with this new I won’t say overload, but this new journey and schedule and it takes time.” Share Updated at 07.26 EDT

3h ago 07.05 EDT In case you missed it last night: Everton left Jack Grealish out of their squad for yesterday’s 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United following a “breach of club discipline”. It is understood the 31-year-old missed training on Monday without permission and the decision to drop him was taken by manager David Moyes in conjunction with the club’s chief executive Angus Kinnear. Everton paid £12m in total to have Grealish on loan last season and are paying a similar sum for this campaign. He will become a free agent at the end of this season when his lucrative contract with City expires. Full story: Everton drop Jack Grealish from Carabao Cup tie over ‘breach of club discipline’ Read more View image in fullscreen Jack Grealish was dropped by Everton for the Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images Share

4h ago 06.53 EDT The 'nervous system changes' behind Kulusevski’s comeback Dejan Kulusevski returned to competitive action for Tottenham after a 17-month injury layoff to play the last few minutes in the club’s 3-1 home victory against Coventry last week and followed that up with another substitute appearance in Saturday’s win at Chelsea. Kulusevski had multiple setbacks after knee surgery in May 2025. But a second procedure in March finally set him on the road to recovery. Speaking ahead of Saturday’s match against Crystal Palace, the 26-year-old Kulusveski told SpursPlay: “It had been like one year and a couple of months and I still can’t walk on the stairs. I can’t walk on the stairs like a normal guy. I have to play football so in my head I’m not going to give up, but I have to think that if this doesn’t work out, what do I do? “I went to a physio in Sweden. He was able to change my nervous system and then it felt different. When I did the exercises, I said, ’I don’t have pain, like this hurt yesterday. Why is this not hurting today?’ He added: “There was still pain but it was different. Now I had control of my leg and then that is when the grind started that summer. I started to play football and it got better every day. I was limping and everything, but it was different now. “I got much stronger in a short time and I went from ’this guy will not play football any more’ to playing really good football in just a couple of weeks.” AFP Share Updated at 06.54 EDT

4h ago 06.29 EDT Alas, my time on the blog is up for now. Good news, Andy McGrath is here to take over. Share

Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s “ambition” was to have “equality” for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.” There had, therefore, been widespread hope across the women’s game that 2027’s prize pot would match the men’s on at least a per-team basis. 4h ago 06.05 EDT Kroupi not yet ready to start for Bournemouth Marco Rose will hold Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi back for a little longer despite more minutes in midweek. A foot injury sidelined Kroupi for the first three months of the campaign, but the highly rated French attacker returned in the 3-0 win over Manchester United and was introduced in the 80th minute of Wednesday’s Carabao Cup triumph over Aston Villa. Ahead of Saturday’s visit of Leeds, Rose told a press conference: “We still need to build up his game time. I’m really happy to have him back, to have his quality, but he knows that he has to be patient in this situation to not get in a difficult situation with another injury. “We need to get him fit, in a good spot with more and more match time in between good sessions of training.” The Cherries remain without Alex Scott, but he could return from a thigh injury next week. Share

5h ago 05.52 EDT Brighton hope to have key duo back for round two with City Head coach Fabian Hurzeler said he is confident that Chema Andres and Ferdi Kadioglu will be available as Brighton seek immediate revenge on Manchester City after being knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the Etihad Stadium on penalties in midweek. Andres and Kadioglu suffered hip injuries at Liverpool last weekend, but both are expected to return at the Etihad after sitting out the cup tie, while Charalampos Kostoulas will also be available after he was rested on Wednesday night. However, summer signing Pascal Struijk will not be available, he is out with an undisclosed knock. Hurzeler told media in Manchester on Thursday: “A positive was that (Yankuba) Minteh and Mats Wieffer had their comeback yesterday. “Ferdi, Chema, also Kostoulas (who) we rested yesterday, we are quite convinced that he will be an option for Saturday. This is the new information we can give. “Regarding Pascal Struijk, he won’t be an option for the weekend, but we are quite convinced that he will be back afterwards.” Press Association Share Updated at 05.56 EDT

5h ago 05.30 EDT U-turn on Afcon as tournament reverts to two-year cycle The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will revert to being held every two years after the continent’s ruling body reversed its decision taken last year to move to a four-year cycle. The African Football Confederation (Caf) said in a statement that it had: “Unanimously decided that the CAF Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to taking place every two years.” Caf said part of the reasoning for performing a U-turn on the decision was the length of time it would take for Afcon’s replacement competition, the Africa Nations League Pan-African Competition, to become financially viable. “We were also concerned by the several years required before the proposed new Africa Nations League Pan-African competition, (which was supposed to be identical to the current Afcon and take place every two years), could make the substantial financial and football development contributions for African Football and Caf competitions to be globally competitive and self-supporting,” Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in the statement. Motsepe added that the decision was also taken in the interests “of African players employed by football clubs outside Africa”. That may prove contentious with their clubs looking at losing key players every two years as opposed to four. Next year’s tournament is being co-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda and CAF said the following three would take place in 2028, 2031 and 2033. “The forthcoming Fifa World Cup will take place in 2030 and in accordance with the Fida tradition, the final tournament of the Afcon and other confederations national team competitions may not take place during the year of the Fifa World Cup,” said Motsepe, explaining the three-year gap between the 2028 edition and the scheduled 2031 tournament. AFP Share

5h ago 05.20 EDT Manchester City’s hopes of avoiding the ‘punishment round’ of the Women’s Champions League took a blow last night. Tara Elimbi Gilbert’s late effort handed City their third consecutive draw of the league phase and the English champions now probably need to wins on each of the last three matchdays to avoid the knockout phase play-offs in February. “Annoying is not the right word but it’s a little bit a feeling of ‘argh’,” said City manager Andrée Jeglertz, post-match “We deserved more, I think, but that’s how it is in the Champions League. When you dominate games and you don’t score, the opponent will take their chances and that’s what they did.” Read Tom Garry’s full report from the Joie Stadium: PSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopes Read more Share

Sports.title: The academy system needs a refresh but now is the time for Carrick to trust in youth | David Pleat
Sports.content:
Watching Manchester United succumb meekly against Como and Bournemouth brought to mind questions and comparisons with yesteryear. Two of United’s most famous eras were built around their youth players: the Busby Babes and the Class of ’92. Could this be a moment for Michael Carrick to give their most talented academy products a meaningful chance?

In February 2025 I saw United beat Arsenal 3-2 in the FA Youth Cup at the Emirates Stadium. Jack and Tyler Fletcher did well for United and so did Harry Amass, a signing from Watford. Max Dowman, a generational talent, starred for Arsenal.

Not one of that United team has established themselves in the first team. Amass, a left-back, has two substitute appearances this season. The winger Shea Lacey, part of the same under-18s squad, has come on four times and got a Carabao Cup start.

Supporters, not least at Old Trafford, like players from the academy. The two United youth products who are regulars, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford, are well established. I look at some of the club’s big signings and wonder: do they see themselves as real Manchester United players? With youth-team products you get spirit and identity – a deep pride in the shirt. That isn’t enough but to really assess them they need a proper chance.

You have to give a player a minimum of three starts in a row to see whether they have the potential to be a regular. Some players at United and elsewhere get an occasional Carabao Cup start and that’s it.

It is interesting that JJ Gabriel, a highly rated 16-year-old at United, and his advisers appear to think he could be better off elsewhere. Other young English players have made similar moves. Noni Madueke, for instance, left Tottenham for PSV at 16, got games and came back to sign for Chelsea, then Arsenal.

This is a wider issue than what is going on at United. The purpose of a youth system should be to produce players for the senior team – not to be a trading post, a way of raising funds to buy often mediocre players from abroad.

Tottenham have brought through internationals including Sol Campbell, Ledley King, Harry Kane and Andros Townsend over the past 30 years or so. This season their only homegrown player with a Premier League appearance is Mikey Moore, and he was sent back on loan – this time to Cologne – in August.

The loan system can be beneficial – look at Kane. I saw him at Leyton Orient on his first loan from Spurs and wasn’t sure he had the pace for the highest level. When he came back injured from a loan at Norwich, his rehab work, including weights in the gym, left him feeling fitter and quicker.

It got to a point where Tim Sherwood, Tottenham’s technical coordinator, was banging on the door for Kane to get a first-team chance. He got it, took it and this week won the Ballon d’Or.

Often as an academy player you need a sympathetic manager and strong advocate. Three players Spurs acquired for their academy were sold this summer: Alfie Devine to Preston and Will Lankshear and Ashley Phillips to Middlesbrough. Were they not deserving of an opportunity?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Will Lankshear moved to Middlesbrough from Tottenham this summer and is currently the Championship’s top scorer. Photograph: Aidan Hunter/Action Plus/Shutterstock

Liverpool have fielded a scouser every season since 1892 but named a 25-man Premier League squad in August without a player born in the city. They do have young English players and two – Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni – have started non‑Carabao Cup ties this season, but looking across the Premier League I worry our national team talent pool is being eroded.

The academy system needs refreshing. Principally, under-21 football should be scrapped. There are 18-year-olds retained only so clubs have a big enough squad to support the one player who could become a diamond. A boy should be released at latest 18. Those who stay should be in the first team or on loan.

Young players need the competitiveness of senior football as soon as possible. Academy football is tidy and highly technical but has little resemblance to the frenetic, physical senior game. It also doesn’t test whether a boy has the mentality to cope in a tough dressing room where older players don’t want you taking their place.As a young player at Nottingham Forest I dribbled in training past an older teammate who warned: “Do that again, son, and I’ll break your leg.” It’s not like that any more but you need a certain character.

Too many over-18s are released from Premier League academies and want an EFL club without having the CV for that. Can they cope physically? Can they be trusted by a manager who has a short time to do well or faces the sack?

Top managers are also under pressure to win and so can be reluctant to give youth a chance. As a minimum they should be watching academy games when they can and asking: “Who have you got who could become a first-team regular?” Some managers separate themselves from the academy as if it’s another club.

Carrick watching United’s under‑21s this week showed he does take an interest. Now is his moment to be brave.

Sports.title: Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
Sports.content:
Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament.

Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s ambitionwas to have equality for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.” There had, therefore, been widespread hope across the women’s game that 2027’s prize pot would match the men’s on at least a per-team basis.

There were 48 teams at the men’s event and 32 women’s teams will participate in Brazil next summer, so a women’s pot two-thirds the size of the men’s $655m would have been regarded as parity, but it is understood the women’s prize money will be about a third of the men’s.

That does mark a substantial increase. Some sources with knowledge of the extensive negotiations that have taken place in recent weeks are privately praising the rise, but one senior female source described the news as a “huge missed open goal” by Fifa. No decision is expected to be confirmed until December’s Fifa council meeting.

Sky News, which revealed that Fifa would not match the men’s prize fund, has reported that the women’s pot is being targeted to double from $110m in 2023 to $220m, which would be a more than seven-fold increase on the 2019 women’s finals in France. Fifa prize money to the men’s teams this year included $50m for the winners, Spain.

View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino in Auckland in October 2022 for the draw for the 2023 Women's World Cup. Photograph: Shane Wenzlick/Reuters

Senior Fifa officials are understood to have spoken to some leading female players to outline its wider investments in the women’s game and explain the decision, which is believed to be related to the commercial income the 2027 event will generate.

Infantino has previously criticised broadcasters for not paying more for the televisions rights for the women’s tournament, which in 2023 reached 933 million viewers on linear television and 895 million on streaming platforms, according to Fifa. The final between England and Spain in Sydney had a global live audience of 67 million and reached 222 million people overall, Fifa said.

Fifa did not comment when contacted by the Guardian but sources at the governing body said there would be further enhancements to the women’s club benefits programme and additional money ringfenced for the players who take part in the tournament.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was confirmed this month that 2027’s Women’s World Cup teams will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those who played at the men’s tournament. The preparation money has been more than doubled to $2.5m each.

Every player will be guaranteed business class or chartered flights, and their own hotel room rather than having to share, which Fifa says brings the provisions in line with the men’s World Cup.

Sports.title: ‘Where we want to be’: Le Bris stays positive as faltering Sunderland face Coventry reunion
Sports.content:
Twenty seconds of stoppage time remained when Enzo Le Fée picked up the ball and kissed it before taking a corner. As intended, the Frenchman’s perfect, right-footed delivery dropped into the corridor of uncertainty that leaves goalkeepers torn between leaving their line or standing firm.

It also dipped at the right moment for Dan Ballard to power a header in off the crossbar. Extra time in the 2025 Championship playoff semi-final second leg was almost over and Sunderland had secured a 1-1 draw that consigned Coventry to a 3-2 aggregate defeat.

As an outpouring of the loudest, most raucous emotion imaginable left the Stadium of Light feeling as if it was literally shaking, Régis Le Bris momentarily looked bewildered. By the time joyous comprehension began spreading across the Sunderland manager’s face, Frank Lampard was already a study in misery. Sunderland were on their way to Wembley, leaving Coventry in the Championship for another year.

Le Bris always believed that, at heart, football managers must be storytellers, and, suddenly, he had created the most compelling narrative of his career.

His players bought into his vision to such an extent that, having beaten Sheffield United in the playoff final, they finished seventh in the Premier League last season, qualifying for the Europa League.

Everything went so well it appeared almost a fantasy but now this magic carpet ride looks in peril of ending. Much hinges on whether Sunderland can secure only their second league win of the season at Lampard’s 19th-placed, finally promoted, Coventry on Saturday.

“There’s always a new story and a new chapter to write,” said Le Bris. “This game will be an exciting one with our intention to be us, show up with our identity, our pillars, our foundations and, after that, the game will be the game. Coventry have won twice in the Premier League so they are competitive. The Premier League is a new chapter for them but they are still efficient.”

Perhaps overstretched by the demands of European football, Sunderland have proved alarmingly inefficient at times this season. So much so that Nordi Mukiele, the former Paris Saint-Germain defender, recently accused his teammates of turning “arrogant”.

Clear the air dressing-room talks ensued and Le Bris seemed much happier after last Sunday’s 0-0 home draw with Leeds. “We saw Sunderland on the pitch today,” said the 50-year-old. “We showed we want to embrace the challenge. We were ourselves.”

A manager arguably let down by this summer’s recruitment refuses to fret about a demanding itinerary that, given Wednesday night’s 3-2 Carabao Cup win against Brentford, has just become even more congested.

“You won’t hear me complaining about this new journey, the busy schedule,” said Le Bris. “This is exactly where we want to be, with the opportunity to play regularly in Europe, to be competing in the Premier League and the domestic cups too.

“It’s demanding, but it creates the conditions to get better, to evolve and to be more proactive.”

If his attempts to introduce a more attacking style this season have produced mixed results, Sunderland’s manager has been hampered by the club’s failure to sign a long-coveted right winger, and a Premier League-ready striker capable of competing with Wilson Isidor as Brian Brobbey’s understudy. Recent injuries to Brobbey and Isidor have exposed a glaring lack of cover in this department.

While Florent Ghisolfi, Sunderland’s director of football, presided over some brilliantly radical recruitment immediately after promotion, backroom churn at the Stadium of Light has seen two previously key transfer market experts leave in the past year.

The formerly influential sporting director, Kristjaan Speakman, departed amicably once it became apparent there was too much overlap with Ghisolfi’s role. Stuart Harvey, the head of player recruitment, also left by “mutual consent.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen ‘Sunderland’s story is important and something we’ve analysed,’ Frank Lampard said in August. ‘To see how they played last season gives us inspiration.’ Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

Now the technical director at Stoke, Harvey was very highly regarded, with his intelligent use of data said to have played a significant part as he and Speakman helped lift Sunderland from League One to the top tier.

Ghisolfi, recruited from Roma, has an exceptional European contacts book and remains much admired. Yet in the case of Kevin Danso, a Tottenham loanee defender who will sign permanently next summer, his decision to prioritise height and power this summer has possibly proved questionable. Although an excellent character off the pitch, Danso has made some worrying individual errors as Sunderland have struggled in the absence of the hamstrung Ballard.

Paradoxically, the team’s one relatively diminutive summer signing - the £30m former Lyon winger Malick Fofana - has struggled to make an impact on the left. That said, a much-improved Carabao Cup performance against Brentford hinted of better things to come from the 21-year-old Belgium international.

The richly talented Le Fée remains integral to Le Bris’s plans, but constructing the right framework to bring out the best in a playmaker reportedly close to a senior France call-up has proved tricky at times.

It does not help that Granit Xhaka has not quite been his usual imperious self this season. Maybe at 34, age is catching up with the defensive midfielder, and perhaps Switzerland’s World Cup journey took his toll on the international captain? Certainly Xhaka’s recent suspension from the Switzerland squad after his admission of purchasing a fake Covid vaccination certificate has been an unwelcome distraction.

Le Bris, now working with a new set-piece coach, could do with having Xhaka back to his best at Coventry, and is also hoping Mukiele recovers from a minor throat injury to start.

There is a certain irony that, in August, Lampard described the Wearsiders as a post-promotion role model. “Sunderland’s story is important and something we’ve analysed,” he said. “To see how they played last season gives us inspiration.

“But now it is up to us to write that story for ourselves.”

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1

Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes held clear-the-air talks this week. Fernandes was an unused substitute against Bournemouth after criticising Carrick’s tactics during the Champions League defeat at Como but it seems the situation has been resolved – for now. Dropping Fernandes did not do United any good against Bournemouth, who ran riot at Old Trafford, and the captain is expected to return to the starting lineup for the trip to Chelsea. If that happens, he owes Carrick a performance. Fernandes has been poor this season and it is time he did his talking on the pitch. Jacob Steinberg

Chelsea v Manchester United, Saturday 12.30pm (all times GMT)

2 Maresca wary of another City slip

Since Manchester City were found guilty of serially breaching Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team have won four games (including Wednesday’s Carabao Cup shootout victory over Brighton) and lost two. Saturday’s 2-1 reverse at Aston Villa was their first Premier League defeat and should another follow in their rematch with the Seagulls, the manager may start to fear the guilty verdict and possible sanctions (demotion to the Championship, for example) becoming a distraction to his players. There is a precedent for City initially responding well to adversity, before it then affected results. After Rodri sustained a serious knee injury against Arsenal in September 2024, Pep Guardiola’s team went undefeated in seven matches, winning six. But then the wheels clattered off, with one victory and 10 defeats in the next 13. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Brighton, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Manchester City and Brighton meet again on Saturday after an entertaining Carabao Cup contest in midweek. Photograph: Gary Oakley/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

3 Hamer keen for Coventry chance

The last time north-east opposition visited the CBS Arena, Frank Lampard’s side had no trouble finding the net, but their four goals against Newcastle on 12 October make up two-thirds of their league total for the season. Perhaps the most creative player at the club has spent most of this campaign watching from the bench. Gustavo Hamer, who created 12 goals for his Sheffield United teammates in the Championship last season, has asked to play for the under-21s to get his minutes up. “Myself and the staff have been really, really impressed by his approach, his training, his ethic,” Lampard said before Hamer came on as an 86th-minute substitute in last weekend’s defeat by Fulham. Will he get more than four minutes off the bench against the only team beneath Coventry in the table? Billy Munday

Coventry v Sunderland, Saturday 3pm

4 Evanilson’s value clear for Bournemouth

Beating Milan and then Manchester United made for a halcyon week in Bournemouth’s history. Winning at Old Trafford and defeating Aston Villa in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday all followed Marco Rose’s first Premier League win, against Sunderland on 18 October, which came as a great relief. The project is back on course. Eli Junior Kroupi, a late substitute last Sunday, has returned to the squad. In the Frenchman’s absence Evanilson has been on his best run of form since joining the club. He has four goals from five matches, and a tight-angled finish to make it 3-0 at United belied his reputation as a player who could score more. The Brazilian is a capable line leader, with Kroupi able to work the space his partner’s tireless running creates. When Sturm Graz were defeated in the Europa League, Evanilson served as support striker for the raw Álvaro Rodríguez. There is little starry about a club-record signing whose work ethic has been important to Rose’s early weeks in charge. John Brewin

Bournemouth v Leeds, Saturday 3pm

5 Forest still searching for finishing touch

Brentford’s early-season charge has slowed, with no wins from their last three and a disappointing draw at Hull last week – although only Liverpool have beaten Keith Andrews’ team this season in the Premier League. A 1-1 draw at Ipswich last Friday heightened frustrations at Nottingham Forest, with Liam Delap’s scoring touch continuing to desert him and an unmarked Murillo missing a free header the best of a host of unconverted chances. The better opportunities tended to arrive from the flanks, with Daniel Muñoz overlapping from wingback as the supplier for Neco Williams’ goal. After a decent start to the season for Morgan Gibbs-White in terms of chance creation, he was crowded out by Ipswich’s packed midfield. Oliver Glasner’s formation, founded on a defensive trio, seeks to bring the best from playmakers and ball-players. It brought results from Eberechi Eze and Adam Wharton at Crystal Palace but Gibbs-White and Forest are yet to prosper. Better finishing would certainly help a team stuck in the bottom three. JB

Brentford v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm

6 Promoted rivals are sitting comfortably

Two promoted teams and two positive managers meet at the MKM Stadium on Saturday. “There will be ups and downs, this is normal,” said Hull’s Sergej Jakirovic last week. “We showed already that we can compete.” Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil is similarly enthusiastic. “They’re an incredible group,” he said of his players this week. “We’re not carrying anybody in that, there’s no one getting dragged along by this group.” Both teams kick off in mid-table, though with the awareness of the importance of defeating opponents with similar ambitions. While other Championship graduates have been too readily accepting of their fate, both have grasped the nettle and shown off their survival instincts. Manchester City’s potential punishment could create an opportunity, leaving just two relegation spots to avoid. Hull’s initial hot streak has cooled, though last week’s draw with Brentford was useful. Against Forest, Ipswich made up for their lack of fluidity by showing the staying power to claim a point. JB

Hull v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

7 Tottenham’s Tel keen to ‘work, work, work’

Despite landing in the Premier League in January last year, Mathys Tel’s goal against Chelsea felt like an arrival of sorts. The 21-year-old was highly rated as a youngster at Bayern Munich but has found the net just seven times in 50 league games since joining Spurs, initially on loan. Against Chelsea he picked the ball up in his own half and drove forwards 40 yards before finding the bottom corner from the edge of the box. Spurs fans will want more from Tel who, unlike many of his teammates, is rarely injured. “I think I can still do better,” he said after the 2-0 win at Chelsea that made it two on the spin for Spurs. “I can always do better. I need to work, work, work, work.” Crystal Palace come off the back of victory at Fulham in the Carabao Cup – the head coach, Pierre Sage, has been backed by the board after a tricky spell in the league. BM

Tottenham v Crystal Palace, Saturday 5.30pm

View image in fullscreen Mathys Tel enjoyed a breakthrough moment for Spurs with his solo goal at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Shaun Brooks/CameraSport/Getty Images

8 Jackson offers striking blueprint for García

Álvaro Arbeloa is at last getting somewhere with Fulham. After going without a win in his first six league matches, the Spaniard has collected six points against Hull and Coventry. Goals remain in short supply, though, and the form of the £40m striker Gonzalo García – seven games without scoring – is concerning. Arbeloa’s past relationship with García at Real Madrid is not proving as beneficial as Unai Emery’s knowledge of Nicolas Jackson’s game. That pair worked together at Villarreal, where Emery gave Jackson his La Liga debut. “Unai taught me everything about football,” Jackson said on signing from Chelsea in the summer. With four goals in five Premier League games, including a double against Manchester City last Saturday, Jackson is one of the form strikers in the country. “He was shooting a lot of balls over the crossbar,” Emery said. “Now he’s getting better.” BM

Aston Villa v Fulham, Saturday 8pm

9 Iraola’s Liverpool side look four-midable

“Let’s try to finish this four-in-a-row in the best way,” said Andoni Iraola on Wednesday as thoughts turned from the Carabao Cup penalty shootout win over Chelsea to Arsenal’s impending visit to Anfield. Three consecutive home wins in different competitions, and in quick succession, have helped build momentum at Liverpool, although seven wins from the last eight (including Chelsea) shows the process had already begun. Iraola has handled his first intensive run of Champions League, Premier League and Carabao Cup fixtures expertly, rotating in every game while continuing to produce results. Noticeably, there has been no drop-off in Liverpool’s physical intensity either. The manner of Arsenal’s title triumph last season – and the general shift towards more aggressive, urgent football in the Premier League – were factors in Liverpool’s decision to change head coaches in the summer, and the results are paying off quickly. Iraola will be facing questions about a title challenge should four-in-a-row finish as he hopes on Sunday. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Arsenal, Sunday 4.30pm

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool side have won their last five games in all competitions, including Wednesday’s penalty shootout win over Chelsea. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock

10 Pickford out to frustrate Newcastle again

David Moyes described it as “out of this world”, Alan Shearer talked about a world-class intervention, and Jordan Pickford agreed it ranked as “up there with my very best”. Rewind to March and Everton are beating Newcastle 3-2 on Tyneside when, in the 94th minute, Sandro Tonali unleashes a vicious and technically perfect volley. To the astonishment of everyone inside St James’ Park, Everton’s goalkeeper throws out his right hand and tips the ball over the crossbar. Pickford’s teammate Jarrad Branthwaite said it was “the best save I’ve ever seen” and Moyes can only hope his England goalkeeper proves in similarly defiant mood at a time when his international place is under a little pressure from the Leeds goalkeeper, James Trafford. Not that Pickford will lack inspiration; the lifelong Sunderland fan always enjoys frustrating Newcastle, as he did again in Thursday’s Carabao Cup victory. Matthias Jaissle’s team, and their midfield, are still adapting to life after Tonali and face a testing rematch at St James’ Park on Monday. Louise Taylor

Sports.title: PSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopes
Sports.content:
You cannot miss half a dozen big chances at Women’s Champions League level and expect to get away with it. That is the harsh lesson Manchester City learnt on Thursday against Paris Saint-Germain, who extended the English champions’ wait for their first win in Europe this season by striking late to secure a point at a disappointed Joie Stadium.

City’s third draw from three Champions League games so far this season really ought to have been a victory. Instead, their hopes of a top-four spot and with it automatic qualification for the quarter-finals are looking increasingly slim.

They thought they had won the game through Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s 85th-minute penalty, but conceding sparked PSG into life and they snatched a point with a scrappy equaliser three minutes later as their substitute Tara Elimbi Gilbert found the net from close range.

How, therefore, should we look upon City’s season? Are they the team that is unbeaten in all competitions? Or the team without a win in Europe? Both ring true, and although they are still likely to progress to the knockout stages, they will have been hugely frustrated with their profligacy.

“There are a lot of things in this game we are pleased with. The result is not what we wanted, of course. Maybe we should kill the game earlier,” the City manager, Andrée Jeglertz, reflected. “Annoying is not the right word but it’s a little bit a feeling of ‘argh’. We deserved more, I think, but that’s how it is in the Champions League. When you dominate games and you don’t score, the opponent will take their chances and that’s what they did.”

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw converts her penalty to give Manchester City the lead. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Draws away to Bayern Munich and at home against Real Madrid in their first two games were certainly not poor results, against strong opposition and with theoretically kinder fixtures to come, so there was no need to panic, but City’s 11th-placed position in the table, only one above the final qualification spot, before kick-off will nonetheless have looked a little concerning to some of their supporters. They ended the night 10th.

Jeglertz was positive about their chances: “We got drawn against six teams and we have played the three toughest of them, I think, so now we have three games that we have the opportunity, again, to get the points we need to qualify for the next round. So that’s our goal and nothing has changed.”

Nonetheless, this latest draw was a blow. PSG sought to frustrate City in the first half, and succeeded after riding out an early storm. Shaw’s header dropped wide at the far post from Aoba Fujino’s third-minute cross, as the home side made a bright start but were unable to score while on top. Shaw fizzed a low strike narrowly wide 11 minutes later after terrific play from Lauren Hemp. City controlled possession but did not test the PSG goalkeeper, Oliwia Peda, until the second half.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Quick Guide Roundup: Barcelona stay perfect, Juventus win again, Paris FC and Häcken draw Show Barcelona laid down another marker in their defence of the Women’s Champions League with an 8-0 win thrashing of the Danish champions, HB Køge. A Caroline Graham Hansen penalty and a goal from Ewa Pajor, who finished second in the Ballon d'Or behind her recently departed teammate Alexia Putellas, had the holders in command by half-time in Denmark. Esmee Brugts, Patri Guijarro, Clara Serrajordi, Kika Nazareth and Clàudia Pina, who grabbed a brace, all scored in the second half to complete the rout. Barcelona, who won the women's club award at the Ballon d'Or to go with Pere Romeu's coach of the year prize, remain top of the league phase with three wins from three by an aggregate score of 19-2, while despite the heavy defeat Køge remain in the playoff places. Juventus struck twice late on to get the better of Austria Vienna 4-1. Goals by Matilde Pavan and Alba Redondo put Juve seemingly in control before Lotta Cordes reduced the deficit with 12 minutes left, but Kysha Sylla and Júlia Bartel struck in the final nine minutes. This second straight away win puts Juventus fifth, a point off the last automatic quarter-final qualification spot, while Austria Vienna sit 15th and two points off the playoffs. Paris FC and Häcken shared the spoils in the French capital after Anna Anvegard scored in the fourth minute of stoppage time to cancel out Evelyne Viens’ early opener and grab the Swedish champions their first point in Europe this season. They and Paris FC both remain outside the playoff spots. Photograph: Sebastian Elias Uth/Ritzau Scanpix Denmark Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

This tricky game came in a testing week for City, sandwiched between last Sunday’s Manchester derby – where they dropped points for the first time this season after conceding a late equaliser – and this Sunday’s mouthwatering game away to in-form London City Lionesses and their Ballon d’Or winner, Alexia Putellas, who sit just one place and three points behind them in the WSL. Nobody in sky blue could afford to think about that game yet, though – PSG were no pushovers.

Straight after the restart, Fujino went close as she latched onto Kerstin Casparij’s clever ball and shot over from a tight angle. Fujino, a livewire throughout the night, also saw a shot blocked by Thiniba Samoura, as the hosts began to ask tougher questions. Soon they were creating chance after chance.

Shaw’s powerful low shot was turned behind by Peda. From the resulting corner, curled in expertly by Alex Greenwood, Shaw had a free header but was unable to connect. Mary Fowler then scuffed wide as frustrations began to mount. Shaw headed wide again moments later.

Surely the WSL’s top goalscorer was not going to fire a blank? Indeed not. She finally broke the deadlock after winning a spot-kick, brought down by Griedge Mbock Bathy, and then fired her penalty low to the keeper’s right. But that triggered PSG to attack with vigour for the first time in the match and they were soon level, bursting the City bubble.

Sports.title: Inter and Milan unveil plans for new shared stadium to replace San Siro
Sports.content:
Inter and Milan have unveiled plans for their new Generali Stadium, which will replace the shared San Siro venue from the 2031-32 season.

The stadium, sponsored by Generali – Italy’s largest insurance company – will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost the two clubs €1.2bn (£1bn). The plans were revealed at a gala event at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco on Thursday – but some fans in attendance voiced their opposition to San Siro being demolished.

Shortly before the briefing began, a group of Inter fans walked into the courtyard of the castle and unfurled a banner reading: “You will never extinguish the lights at San Siro,” and chanting: “Hands off San Siro.” Work on the new stadium is set to begin in 2028, on the site of the existing 75,000-capacity venue.

The Generali Stadium will be shaped “low in the body, and rises up at either end” behind the goals, the architect Norman Foster said. David Manica, a stadium specialist who collaborated with Foster on the project, added that the steep-sided design aims to bring fans as close to the pitch as possible.

“The most important thing that we realised when we designed this project is that San Siro is a feeling,” Manica said. “It’s more than a building, it’s a feeling … we brought all the seats as close as possible to the field. They could not be any closer, it’ll actually feel as though you’re sitting on the grass.”

View image in fullscreen An artist’s impression of a concourse inside the planned 71,500-capacity arena. Photograph: Foster + Partners

The stadium will also be capable of hosting NFL international games, rugby matches and concerts. Milan and Inter paid €197m to acquire the current San Siro stadium and its adjacent parking arenas. The current ground will be largely demolished once construction work nears completion.

Also known as the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, San Siro opened in 1926 and is the largest sports stadium in Italy. It is one of European football’s most famous venues, but requires extensive modernisation despite undergoing a number of renovations during its lifespan.
