The Generali Stadium could be used as a venue for Euro 2032, which is being jointly hosted by Italy and Turkey. Foster and Manica previously worked together on the new Wembley Stadium, while the architect’s Foster + Partners firm also designed the plans for Manchester United’s proposed new 100,000-capacity home.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership makes first UK move to remove Saturday 3pm broadcast blackout
Sports.content:
The Scottish Premiership has made the first move in what is expected to be a coordinated attempt from the UK’s domestic leagues to remove the Saturday afternoon broadcast blackout by inviting bids to televise all of its matches in the next rights cycle from 2029.

A tender document issued by the Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) last week is understood to have given broadcasters an option to bid for live rights to all matches, including games kicking off at 3pm on Saturdays, the domestic broadcast of which is currently prohibited under Article 48 of Uefa’s statutes.

The Guardian revealed last year that the Premier League and English Football League were eager for the blackout to be lifted because they have concluded that selling more matches to broadcasters is the best way to raise revenues, a view that also appears to have taken hold in Scotland.

The SPFL’s invitation to tender, first reported by Sports Business, is understood to give bidders the flexibility to bid on the basis of the blocked hours governed by Article 48 not being in place.

A source with knowledge of the tender said it appeared increasingly unlikely that the four British Football Associations would apply blocked hours in their territories after 2029.

UK broadcasters are prevented from showing live football between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays when 50% of games in the top two divisions take place during that period, a provision that means 3pm kick-offs can be broadcast on FA Cup weekends and on weekend bank holidays over Christmas.

The UK is the last country in Europe to invoke Article 48, which allows associations to stipulate a period during which matches cannot be televised live in their territory.

While the English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish FAs are responsible for applying Article 48, they will be guided by the wishes of the clubs.

UK broadcasters can currently show up to 270 Premier League matches, 1,059 EFL games and 82 from the Scottish Premiership, amounting to 35% of fixtures across the season.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Premier League chief executive, Richard Masters, said in August the subject of lifting Article 48 was a live discussion. “We’ve got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change,” he told TalkSport. “It’s not a decision for now. It’s a decision we’ve got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do. I’d say in about 18 months’ time we’ll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not.”

Sports.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes decision on Leeds future amid Man United rumours
Sports.content:
Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is set to sign a new contract, talkSPORT understands.

The 29-year-old has enjoyed a resurgence since moving to Elland Road in the summer of 2025, scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances.

4 Dominic Calvert-Lewin looks set to extend his stay at Leeds Credit: Getty

Calvert-Lewin penned a three-year deal until 2028 when he joined the Whites, but is now expected to extend his stay at the club.

This will come as a huge blow to Manchester United, who had made the striker a target for the January transfer window.

Calvert-Lewin's Man United links

talkSPORT understands the Red Devils are looking at bringing in a forward in January after Benjamin Sesko was ruled out for an extended period.

Sesko is understood to be out until the New Year at the least with a shin issue he picked up before the international break.

With Joshua Zirkzee United's only fit senior striker, they now appear to be looking for a back-up option to sign.

However, Michael Carrick's struggling side look set to miss out on one identified target in Calvert-Lewin, who is expected to extend his stay at Leeds.

The striker has impressed since joining Leeds from Everton last summer, netting 18 league goals across 43 outings.

With his latter years at the Toffees heavily disrupted by injuries, Calvert-Lewin managed to reach top form again in his first year at Elland Road, scoring 14 Premier League goals last term.

This saw him earn an England recall after a five-year absence, although he missed out on selection for the 2026 World Cup.

He has made a bright start to this season's campaign, bagging four goals in eight outings, including a second-half equaliser in a 1-1 draw with United earlier this month.

4 The continued absence of last season's joint-top scorer Benjamin Sesko led United to consider Calvert-Lewin Credit: Getty

Calvert-Lewin's form this season saw him picked for the Three Lions' most recent Nations League matches, winning his 14th cap in their 3-0 victory over Czechia earlier in October.

Brazil warns against Calvert-Lewin move

Calvert-Lewin's contract update comes just hours after talkSPORT's Alan Brazil warned Man United against signing him in January.

That's despite the striker's five goals in all competitions being a greater tally than the Red Devils' top scorers Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo - who have four each.

United's lack of goals is one of a number of factors in their woeful start to the season, which has left Michael Carrick clinging onto his job - though he is set to be on the touchline against Chelsea on Saturday.

But despite the attacking firepower Calvert-Lewin would offer, Brazil claimed the Red Devils would only view him as a short-term option.

He said of the forward on talkSPORT Breakfast: “I think he's done really well. First and foremost, I'm delighted that he's over his injuries, because there was a player there, always.

4 Calvert-Lewin earned his 14th England cap in the Autumn international break Credit: Getty

4 The striker's contract news is another blow to Man United boss Michael Carrick, who is short of options at centre-forward Credit: Getty

“The way he moves, the way he hangs in the air. And he just couldn't get himself 100 per cent, could he?”

Brazil then continue: "Dominic, don't take this the wrong way, because you're playing really well and you're a threat to any defence.

"But would this be a stop-gap for Man United if they went in and plunged a bit of money?"

Sports.title: Jack Grealish career at a crossroads amid Everton disciplinary action
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish finds himself at a crossroads in his football career.

The 31-year-old was dropped from Everton's squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup clash at home to Newcastle United due to an unauthorised training absence.

5 Jack Grealish is at the centre of a conflict with loan club Everton Credit: Getty

The club officially categorised the omission as a ‘breach of club discipline’.

Grealish had previously missed the weekend's 2-0 defeat to Arsenal due to illness.

Following the Toffees’ win over 3-1 Newcastle to book their spot in the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, boss David Moyes refused to provide any further details on the issue.

However, Moyes did reveal that he supported the decision on Grealish, while highlighting that the club has ‘really good values’ that everyone must adhere to.

Discussing Grealish’s current plight, talkSPORT’s chief football correspondent Alex Crook said the star has let his manager down.

“If you look at Jack Grealish's career since that Treble win for Manchester City when we were all laughing and joking at the time about how much he enjoyed the celebrations, his career has nosedived since then,” Crook said.

“He’s been given a second chance at Everton, by all accounts he loved playing for David Moyes last season and I think Moyes has every right to feel let down by this.

“I think Jack Grealish finds himself at a crossroads now. Does he want to be taken seriously as a footballer or does he want that party boy reputation to define the rest of his career?”

Close friend and former Aston Villa teammate of Grealish, Gabby Agbonlahor preferred to remain coy about the issue until the full details have been revealed.

He did, however, state that Grealish will know the extent of his actions and would have issued an apology to Moyes and his teammates.

5 Moyes and Grealish had enjoyed a fruitful working partnership until recently Credit: Getty

Has Grealish let Moyes down?

“We don’t know exactly what has happened. Do we know that he missed training, has that been confirmed by anyone?” Agbonlahor said.

“If that is the case then obviously he has let his manager and his teammates down, he’ll understand that.

“I know how much he loves playing for Everton Football Club. He was so excited to go back there.

“I saw him away in Mallorca in the summer, he was training hard. That kid loves football.

“But if he has let David Moyes down, I'm sure he'll apologise; I’m sure he’s been fined.

“If he’s missed games for it, I’m sure David Moyes will have him back involved in the next game and he’ll have some making up to do.

5 Grealish has registered two goals and six assists in 26 appearances Credit: Getty

5 Gabby Agbonlahor is hoping Grealish and Everton can sort out their differences

“I’m sure he will, hopefully his performances will make it up to a manager that really loves him.

“It’s both ways.”

Jack the lad

Grealish has often adopted the privileged position of somewhat overstepping the realms of professionalism away from the pitch while maintaining the affection of the masses.

Few others have been able to boast those same entitlements, however, Agbonlahor says Grealish should not be treated any differently than any other player.

“I don’t think he should be treated differently, I think every player should be treated the same,” the former Aston Villa striker added.

“I just feel that we don’t know the definite ins and outs of it.

5 Grealish has a strong relationship with Everton fans despite his loan agreement Credit: AFP

“He loves those fans. That’s one of the reasons he went back to Everton, he told me. The reception he got from the fans he loves everything about Everton.

“But can we not just look at the negatives of missing training? I’d like to point out some positives.

“There was a £10,000 donation that Jack did.

“He’s the nicest kid you’ll meet. He cares about people.

“If someone’s going through a crisis he’s got a GoFundMe [page] to try and raise £100,000. He’s gifted £10,000 of his own money.

“I don’t know many footballers who would do that.”

Sports.title: Premier League hero’s nephew linked with top-flight transfer after blistering start to campaign
Sports.content:
Premier League hero’s nephew linked with top-flight transfer after blistering start to campaign

Kelvin Yeboah, the nephew of Leeds hero Tony, is catching the eye of Premier League and European sides, talkSPORT understands.

The 26-year-old forward has enjoyed a stellar year at Minnesota United in the MLS, putting him on the radar of clubs beyond the US.

3 Kelvin Yeboah has been one of the MLS' standout performers in 2026 Credit: Getty

With 18 goals in the MLS this season, Yeboah currently ranks fourth in the MLS goalscoring charts.

He is in illustrious company here, with football icon Lionel Messi topping the leaderboard with 25 strikes for Inter Miami.

FC Dallas' Petar Musa and Philadelphia Union forward Milan Iloski are the only other players who have scored more than the Minnesota star.

And a move across the pond could now be on the cards for Yeboah, who is approaching the final year of his contract in America.

The Ghana-born striker penned a three-and-a-half year deal with the Loons back in 2024, which expires in December 2027.

Interest in Kelvin Yeboah

According to talkSPORT's Alex Crook, Yeboah is likely to be on the radar of Premier League clubs and clubs in Europe when the January rolls around.

A former West Ham youth player, he has plenty of experience in Europe before, having enjoyed a six-year spell continent with various clubs after leaving English semi-professional team AC London in 2018.

From there, Yeboah joined Austrian Bundesliga side WSG Tirol, before going on to sign for league rivals Sturm Graz in 2021, where he scored 17 goals in 34 league games.

A move to Genoa followed in 2024, but the hitman spent most of his two years on their books out on loan.

Yeboah had spells with Genoa, Augsburg and Montpellier before jetting into Minnesota two-and-a-half years ago.

3 Yeboah has scored 34 goals in 70 games for Minnesota Credit: Getty

Yeboah legacy

With Yeboah's potential suitors currently unclear, it remains to be seen whether a Premier League club will offer him a shot in England.

Everton are one side who could be in the market for a striker, with Thierno Barry their only natural player in the position after missing out on signing Folarin Balogun on transfer deadline day.

Meanwhile, given his family ties, Leeds fans would surely welcome another Yeboah joining their ranks.

His uncle, Tony Yeboah earned a reputation as a Premier League cult hero thanks to a memorable two-and-a-half years at Elland Road between 1995 and 1997.

During this time, the Ghanian scored 24 goals in 47 Premier League appearances for the club, which includes some spectacular efforts.

Perhaps the best of them all was his wonderstrike against Liverpool in August 1995, where Yeboah smashed a volley off the underside of the bar and into the back of the net.

3 Tony Yeboah gained a reputation for the spectacular during his time at Leeds Credit: Getty

The Leeds icon has served as an inspiration for his nephew, with Kelvin previously revealing how he hoped to follow in his footsteps.

Speaking to GOAL in 2022, Kelvin said: "Growing up, I remember my Dad putting on videos of my uncle playing football, and singing songs about him!

"Me and my brothers would watch these goals all the time. I especially remember seeing the goal against Liverpool.

"It was a beautiful image to have in the back of your mind all the time, of my uncle scoring goals in the Premier League.

"It was a great source of inspiration. To have someone close to you that's already done it, it just makes you believe that maybe you can make it as a professional too."

Sports.title: Is Wesley Fofana the worst BlueCo signing at Chelsea? Ranking the top six duds
Sports.content:
Is Wesley Fofana the worst BlueCo signing at Chelsea? Ranking the top six duds

BlueCo have been relentless with their spending as the custodians of Chelsea Football Club.

Close to £2billion worth of signings have come through the doors at Stamford Bridge since the 2022 takeover but, unfortunately for the powers at be, there have been numerous misses among the hits.

7 Chelsea have overseen a multitude of signings, and it's fair to say a select few have not worked out at all Credit: Getty

Cole Palmer, Moises Caicedo and Joao Pedro are the standout arrivals with goals and game-winning displays aplenty, and look set to be joined by Morgan Rogers, who has nine goals and assists in 11 games.

His latest contribution came from the penalty spot against Liverpool on Wednesday night in a Carabao Cup tie which ended with Chelsea getting beaten 6-5 in the shootout at Anfield.

It was Wesley Fofana who was tasked with the decisive spot-kick, one that he sent on a trajectory towards the upper rows of the Kop End.

Dejected and despondent, the centre-back crouched with his head in his hands seconds after a moment that encapsulated just how disappointing and underwhelming his time at Chelsea has been.

Fofana, who also gave away the penalty for Liverpool's goal in normal time, is one player who will be considered as a miss during BlueCo's ownership, but where does he rank in a list of their worst signings? - talkSPORT.com has made its judgement...

6. Filip Jorgensen - £20.7m

Signed from Villarreal in 2024, goalkeeper Jorgensen squandered an opportunity to nail the no.1 spot at Chelsea when competing against the occasionally shaky Robert Sanchez.

The Dane started in all but one of the matches during their 2024/25 Conference League title run, but featured on just 11 occasions in the Premier League across two seasons.

Jorgensen notably produced a howler against Paris Saint-Germain in last season's Champions League as he passed the ball straight into the path of Bradley Barcola, before being lobbed by Vitinha.

This happened at 2-2 in the first leg of the last 16 tie, and Chelsea lost 5-2 on the night before being thrashed 8-2 on aggregate in a result that summed up their horrendous campaign.

Another big mistake occurred at Aston Villa as he let a Marco Asensio shot squeeze through his hands in the 89th minute to lose the match 2-1, with Jorgensen having only one Premier League clean sheet in 11.

7 Jorgensen has not been able to make the most of his limited chances in goal for Chelsea and made some big errors Credit: Getty

His inclusion in this list may be considered harsh, but the 24-year-old has never established himself as a reliable pair of hands or performed well enough to be part of the club's long-term future.

Jorgensen is now on loan at sister club Strasbourg, and will return at the end of this season with the experienced Emi Martinez and starlet Mike Penders to compete with - both of whom are better options.

5. Joao Felix - £42.6m

Chelsea should have seen the warning signs over Felix when he was sent off 58 minutes into his Premier League debut and scored four goals in 20 matches during his 2022/23 loan from Atletico Madrid.

However, the west Londoners opted to bring him to the club on a permanent deal in 2024 and, once again, the Portuguese forward flattered to deceive.

Felix, who was once the fifth most expensive transfer in history with a £113m move from Benfica to Atletico, made only three starts in the league and was frustrating to watch in front of goal.

He joined AC Milan on loan less than six months on from his return to Chelsea, and a sale to Al Nassr followed at the end of the season.

7 It remains a mystery as to why Chelsea chose to bring Felix back to the club after a poor first spell Credit: Getty

The 2019 Golden Boy winner is a technically gifted player once tipped for stardom on the world stage, but he rarely showed any glimpses of his quality in a blue shirt.

Chelsea's decision to re-sign Felix was questionable to say the least, and they will have rued it when assessing such an inconsistent and disillusioned second spell that could have been avoided.

4. Mykhailo Mudryk - £90m

Arsenal looked set to sign Ukrainian winger Mudryk during the 2023 January transfer window, but it was Chelsea who landed a deal with Shakhtar Donetsk.

He joined midway through a season in which no player managed to cover themselves in glory and, whilst he assisted two goals, he did not find the back of the net himself.

Mudryk eventually scored for the first time in October that year, only for subsequent goalless periods to diminish any argument in favour of Chelsea getting their money's worth for the near £100m purchase.

In December 2024, the 25-year-old was provisionally suspended for a failed drugs test and he remained away from the pitch until earlier in 2026 when his case was resolved.

This meant that Mudryk was unable to play professional football for a year-and-a-half, a missed opportunity for him to show improvement and justify why Chelsea spent so much on his transfer.

However, given that money talks, a tally of ten goals and 11 assists in 73 matches across all competitions before his suspension is simply not enough for such an expensive player in an attacking position.

7 Mudryk missed out on months of football due to his suspension but, when he has played for Chelsea, he has not hit the heights Credit: Getty

3. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang - £12m

With 68 Premier League goals scored in 128 appearances for Arsenal, the signing of Aubameyang looked relatively shrewd given he added experience to a Chelsea squad that began to decrease in average age.

The striker also worked with their then head coach Thomas Tuchel at Borussia Dortmund and made his debut in the German's last match in charge, a shock 1-0 Champions League defeat to Dinamo Zagreb.

Aubameyang did go on to score three goals in consecutive matches, but they would turn out to be his only strikes for the club.

Graham Potter gave him limited minutes throughout the rest of the campaign and even omitted the Gabon star from his 25-man squad for the Champions League knockout stages.

With one Premier League goal scored, Aubameyang had the worst domestic campaign of his career at Chelsea after previously hitting highs of 19, 31 and 22 in France, Germany and England.

7 Aubameyang was a shadow of his former self during a short and frustrating spell at Chelsea the lacked an impact in front of goal Credit: Getty

Aubameyang could have rediscovered his fine form from Arsenal if Tuchel remained at Chelsea but, alas, hindsight is a wonderful thing.

In the end, he joins a list of strikers including Alvaro Morata, Radamel Falcao and Gonzalo Higuain to move to Stamford Bridge with big reputations and do anything but what was expected of them.

2. Alejandro Garnacho - £40m

Manchester United fans were riled up in June 2025 when Garnacho posted an image on social media of him wearing an Aston Villa shirt with Marcus Rashford's name on the back.

This came after he fell out of favour with Ruben Amorim and was told to find a new club, which turned out to be their Premier League rivals Chelsea.

With one goal scored in 24 league outings, Garnacho has been one of the most frustrating players to watch in a royal blue shirt.

In the days after a dismal performance during a 1-0 defeat against his former club in April, talkSPORT reported that Chelsea were already willing to sell the winger.

7 Garnacho is still young at 22 years old, but there is little to suggest why Chelsea should keep him for the long run Credit: Getty

Chelsea came to the acceptance that his move has been unsuccessful but, similar to Felix, there were signs that this was a likely outcome as he had a sour end to his United career.

Garnacho was criticised for his attitude having gone straight down the tunnel when being substituted after a Patrick Dorgu red card in a season where he found the target in the league only six times.

He eventually got his wish and moved to Chelsea, only to be listed for transfer less than a year later and sign for Villa on loan for the 2026/27 season.

The deal includes a conditional obligation to buy for Villa, something that is reported to be easily achievable - but he is yet to make a single start and has played just 92 minutes of football in total.

As things stand, Garnacho will return to Chelsea next summer with an uncertain future at the club, one where many fans will probably be happy to see the back of him.

1. Wesley Fofana - £75m

BlueCo's most expensive signing in their first window at Chelsea was Fofana, who made the switch from Leicester City a year after they beat the Blues in the FA Cup final.

A knee injury disrupted his debut season, and then he didn't play a single minute in the 2023/24 campaign due to an ACL injury, one that can be very difficult to properly return from due to lengthy recovery.

7 Fofana is a signing that cost Chelsea so much money, and his performances have not justified the fee that was paid Credit: AFP

However, it is tough to pinpoint a performance from any of his 78 Chelsea appearances that suggests the club did well to make him their most pricey defensive signing ever.

Fofana has only managed to keep 11 Premier League clean sheets in his four active seasons so far, the last of which came during the 2-0 home win over Brentford in January.

He has not come off the bench in their last three league fixtures and did little, if anything, to convince Xabi Alonso of giving him another start anytime soon against Liverpool.

Fofana clumsily gave away a penalty just moments after Rogers put Chelsea ahead when he handled the ball, with Cody Gakpo netting his effort from 12 yards.

Then, during a moment of pressure in the shootout, he smashed his penalty way off target and sent it into the crowd of jeering Liverpool fans to confirm his side's exit from the competition.

It summed up his Chelsea career - a big-money arrival on a reported £220,000-a-week contract that has been given plenty of chances to impress but not taken them, albeit whilst dealing with injury issues.

Fofana still has a little under three years left on his contract and, if the club were to sell him, they are unlikely to recoup a fee close to what they paid Leicester in 2022.

There isn't much to celebrate with him off the pitch either due to his various driving offences, so it will have to take something special for him to transform his time at Chelsea for the better.

Sports.title: Where to watch Bayern Munich v Borussia Dortmund as Harry Kane looks to celebrate Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Where to watch Bayern Munich v Borussia Dortmund as Harry Kane looks to celebrate Ballon d’Or

Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane will hope to lead Bayern Munich to derby glory against Borussia Dortmund this weekend.

Kane claimed the prestigious prize at the glitzy ceremony in London on Monday night and now returns to his day job with a huge clash.

3 Kane's Bayern take on rivals Dortmund this weekend Credit: Getty

Bayern and Dortmund are currently locked at the top of the Bundesliga table, both remaining unbeaten this season on 17 points.

Both sides will hope to lay down a huge marker in the title race with victory in the 141st Der Klassiker.

Bayern beat Dortmund in the Super Cup in August and also won both league clashes last season.

Where to watch Bayern v Dortmund

The first Der Klassiker league clash of the season will take place on Saturday, October 31.

Kick-off at the Allianz Arena is scheduled for 5:30pm UK time.

The match will also be shown on Sky Sports Football from 5:20pm.

talkSPORT’s GameDay Live with Adrian Durham, Scott Minto and Micky Gray will have the latest news from Germany too.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

3 Guirassy will hope to fire Dortmund to derby glory Credit: AFP

Bayern v Dortmund team news

Bayern will be without Luis Diaz, who is sidelined with a muscle injury.

Jamal Musiala remains a doubt as he continues his recovery from a hamstring problem while Manuel Neuer is another fitness concern with a foot issue.

Joshua Kimmich and Aleksandar Pavlovic are expected to be available.

Manager Vincent Kompany will not be in the dugout as he continues his recovery following a recent hospital stay, meaning assistant coach Aaron Danks will take charge.

Dortmund are expected to be without Emre Can, who remains sidelined with a knee injury, while Ramy Bensebaini is a fitness concern after picking up a thigh knock.

3 Kane has become just the fourth Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or Credit: AFP

The visitors could also be without goalkeeper Alexander Meyer, who is doubtful through illness.

Kane's special week

Kane became the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 during Monday’s ceremony in London.

He will hope to celebrate that landmark achievement with a big display in the derby and add to his ten goals in 12 games so far this season.

Kane said: "Not many people would have thought it, and maybe even I wouldn't have thought I'd be this far.

"I had to go through many ups and downs, especially early in my career. I was never the person that people thought was going to be the superstar like some of the guys now.

"I had to bide my time and work hard, a lot of times it was me against my own mind and I had to come through it, I had to show self-belief, determination.

"I think that grounded me even when I did make it at the highest level to keep improving and keep getting better."

Sports.title: Chelsea are get-out-of-jail-free card for under-fire managers ahead of Michael Carrick visit
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has been given a stay of execution as Manchester United boss - and he couldn't have asked for a better next opponent.

The 45-year-old is set to be on the touchline at Stamford Bridge on Saturday as his Red Devils side take on Chelsea, live on talkSPORT.



6 Carrick has managed to keep his role and will be on the touchline at Stamford Bridge when his side face Chelsea on Saturday Credit: Getty

Carrick appeared destined for the sack after the club fell to a 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

However, it is understood that the Man United board being split over whether to hire Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann played a part in the decision to keep the 34-cap England international on.

Carrick will be in charge for Chelsea game

The Red Devils are set to embark on a horror run of fixtures over the next three weeks, with a Champions League clash with Roma sandwiched between top-flight games against Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool.



"Michael Carrick staying on may be a surprise to us all," Adrian Durham, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent, told Breakfast.

"I think if they bring in Eddie Howe, they bring in a Nagelsmann, and they get off to a really shocking start in those tough fixtures, that's not great for the new man.



"So in some ways, I'm deeply cynical about this.

"I think the people making the decisions at Manchester United have thought, well, let Michael Carrick take those bad results and that difficult run of games and then we'll get rid of him.

"I think that's what's gone on, to be honest with you."

But it is not all doom and gloom for Carrick, as many managers have been here before; on the brink, and next up is Chelsea.



6 Carrick appeared to be waving goodbye at Old Trafford on Sunday as fans chanted his name - but he has not been sacked after the loss to Bournemouth Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta (Arsenal, December 2020)

The Premier League manager of the year was under huge pressure on the first anniversary of his first game in charge of the Gunners.

Arsenal spent Christmas in their lowest league position since 1982, and had gone seven consecutive top-flight games without a win.

Ahead of welcoming Chelsea on Boxing Day, 2020, the club had not won a Premier League game since November 1, and were languishing in 15th in the table after a run of five defeats and two draws.



Arteta rolled the dice with six changes and trusted in youth, with then-19-year-old pair Bukayo Saka and Gabriel Martinelli starting alongside 20-year-old Emile Smith Rowe.

His brave team selection paid off, as Arsenal beat Chelsea 3-1 to move six points clear of the bottom three - and it was Frank Lampard who was sacked a month later!

6 Arsenal ended a desperate 56-day wait for a Premier League victory with Saka on the scoresheet Credit: Getty

Daniel Farke (Leeds, December 2025)

The Whites boss was being geared up for the sack just months after returning Premier League football to Elland Road.



Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers were even named as potential replacements following a run of four straight defeats.

A 3-2 defeat to Manchester City left Leeds in the relegation zone by the end of last November with eight defeats from 13 matches.

Yet at the Etihad, Farke reverted to a 3-5-2 formation at half-time, with his side two goals down, and played with two centre-forwards.

The German persisted with that set-up in Leeds next match, which was deemed pivotal to his future, and it paid dividends as the club downed Chelsea 3-1 to transform their season.



6 Leeds' win over Chelsea proved a turning point in Farke's tenure since the club returned to the Premier League Credit: Getty

Erik ten Hag (Man United, December 2023)

Carrick's predecessors have also benefitted from a timely clash with Chelsea - as evidenced by the past two in the Old Trafford hot seat.

Three years ago, Ten Hag was navigating a crisis at Man United, which even saw four journalists banned from his Blues press conference.

A 1-0 loss to Newcastle left the club seventh in the Premier League, while they were also bottom of their Champions League group.



But Man United earned a much-needed win over Chelsea, courtesy of a Scott McTominay double to ease the pressure on Ten Hag.

The Dutchman used the victory as a platform for a second-half surge to FA Cup silverware, which kept him in situ until October 2024.

6 Ten Hag claimed the 2-1 victory over Chelsea 'sent a message to fans' amid questions about team unity Credit: AFP

Ruben Amorim (Man United, September 2025)

Even the man from whom Carrick inherited the Old Trafford gig directly used a win against Chelsea to briefly hold onto the job.



Man United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe flew into the club’s Carrington training ground three days before Amorim's side faced the Blues and stressed to the Portuguese the need for on-field results to improve.

Following a 3-0 Manchester derby defeat the week prior, the Red Devils had won just one of five matches across all competitions.

It followed their worst season in Premier League history in the 2024/25 campaign, as United finished 15th with just 42 points.

6 Jamie Redknapp claimed Man United's 2-1 win over Chelsea was the biggest win of Amorim's reign at Old Trafford Credit: Getty



Yet amid growing calls for Amorim to be sacked, the now-AC Milan boss masterminded a 2-1 win over Chelsea at Old Trafford.

It proved the catalyst for a run of four Premier League wins in their next five matches, but it proved to be a false dawn as he was given his marching orders at the start of this January.

Sports.title: Sir Patrick Stewart’s death to be marked with minute’s applause before EFL match
Sports.content:
Sir Patrick Stewart’s death to be marked with minute’s applause before EFL match

Huddersfield have announced that a minute's applause will be held before Saturday’s clash with Bradford in memory of Sir Patrick Stewart.

The Hollywood icon, best known for starring in Star Trek and X-Men, passed away on Wednesday aged 86 following a battle with Alzheimer’s.



3 Huddersfield paid a touching tribute to Stewart following his passing

From nearby Mirfield, Stewart was a lifelong Huddersfield fan, and was often spotted attending their games.

He was in attendance at Wembley in 2017 for the Terriers' Championship Play-off final victory that sealed their promotion to the Premier League

Stewart was arguably the Yorkshire outfit's most famous supporter, and his last public appearance came at one of their games.



With his declining health leading him to retreat from public life in the final two years of his life, the actor was pictured watching his beloved club away to Crawley at Broadfield Stadium in November 2024.

EFL clubs to honour Stewart

Following the news of Stewart's passing, Huddersfield paid an emotional tribute and have now confirmed they will be remembering him before their next game against Bradford.



The Terriers travel to Valley Parade on Saturday in the 12:30 kick-off, where the two Yorkshire clubs will observe a minute's applause.

This will be in memory of both Stewart and former EFL goalkeeper John Vaughan, who passed away earlier in October and previously worked as a goalkeeping coach for both clubs.



A Huddersfield statement on X read: "Tomorrow, we'll join Bradford City in a minute’s applause ahead of kick-off to remember John Vaughan, who sadly passed away earlier this month.

"Representing both Town and Bradford across his coaching career, we'll come together to honour him before the first whistle.

"We'll be wearing black armbands in memory of 'Vaughany' and lifelong Town supporter Sir Patrick Stewart, who sadly passed away on Wednesday.

3 Both Stewart and John Vaughan will be remembered before kick-off at Valley Parade on Saturday Credit: Getty



"You'll always be Terriers."

Saturday's clash will see Bradford look to move level with league leaders Huddersfield, currently sitting three points behind in fourth.

Huddersfield's moving tribute

Stewart died in his home in Los Angeles surrounded by his wife Sunny following a short battle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, according to his spokesperson.

Tributes immediately flooded in from across the world for the actor, whose illustrious career on stage and screen spanned over 60 years.

He shot to fame in 1987 as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and later Professor Charles Xavier in the “X-Men” films.



In a heartbreaking tribute, Huddersfield wrote: "All at Huddersfield Town are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of lifelong supporter Sir Patrick Stewart.

3 The actor became a household name for his role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek Credit: Getty

"Our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this sad time. A titan of his craft and a legend and hero to millions worldwide, his legacy will live on.

"Fiercely proud of his Yorkshire roots, Sir Patrick was a Terrier in every sense, and we’re proud to have counted him as one of our own.



"Once a Terrier, always a Terrier."

Sports.title: Arsenal are essentially Everton if you remove their most important player
Sports.content:
Arsenal are essentially Everton if you remove their most important player

Arsenal are no better than Everton when Declan Rice is not on the pitch.

That is the bold take of talkSPORT’s Adrian Durham following the Gunners’ shock Carabao Cup exit at League Two minnows Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.



3 Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao despite having many of their big guns on show Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Mikel Arteta’s side were dumped out of the competition on penalties after a tense 1-1 draw in a match that saw teenage star Max Dowman sent off five minutes from time.

But it was the absence of another Gunners midfielder that was the most eye-catching aspect of the defeat.

Rice was rested for the match at the Highbury Stadium and despite Arteta having introduced captain Martin Odegaard and £75million summer signing Bruno Guimaraes as second-half substitutes, Durham says the outcome only emphasises the England international’s importance to Arsenal.



“I started to wonder what went wrong for Arsenal because they had a lot of chances, they had a lot of the ball,” Durham told talkSPORT’s Fiery Fridays podcast.

“On the balance of play, 59 touches in the opposition box. Not that many shots on target (7), a couple of great saves from the [Fleetwood] keeper.



“You could look at [Kai] Havertz and [Viktor] Gyokeres who both started. Gyokeres got a goal but it was really scrappy. He didn't know too much about it.

“Neither of them performed particularly well but I was thinking, how can this happen? This miracle.



“It’s the preserve of English football cup competitions that the champions, who took PSG all the way to penalties, go to a side in the bottom half of League Two that aren't very good.

"They haven’t got particularly good players, lost to Exeter at the weekend, lost at home to Rochdale a few weeks ago and this side knocked Arsenal out of the cup. How can it happen?

“I had a look at the Arsenal make-up and there’s one man that I thought was key to everything and it’s just enhanced his reputation even more by being there.

3 Durham believes Declan Rice is now Arsenal's most crucial player Credit: Getty



“And that is Declan Rice.”

Durham then likened an Arsenal side without their £100m man to that of David Moyes’ Toffees.

He added: “My hot take this week is that fundamentally, without Declan Rice, Arsenal become Everton. That’s what happens.

"There’s some good players at Arsenal and there's some good players at Everton. It’s not necessarily the biggest insult in the world

"Everton are trying to get to the European places; they're not a relegation team anymore but without Declan Rice, Arsenal are basically Everton.



“You see, Declan Rice is underrated. If you look at his numbers they are absolutely phenomenal. His assist rate in the Premier League this season is incredible.

3 Rice has registered four assists and one goal from 12 games this season Credit: Getty

“If you look at his assists since he got to Arsenal they are amazing. His goal involvements, 50 plus inside three and a bit seasons.

“For a central midfielder who’s not always in advanced positions the ground he covers, the knowledge of the game, the running of the game.



“Everything about him is world class and we’ve been underrating him for a long time.

“So in a week where we’ve had a Ballon d’Or winner in Harry Kane and in a week where Jude Bellingham produced an amazing bit of skill to get a winner for Real Madrid, we’ve got some great English players.

“Declan Rice is right up there with them and I think without him, Arsenal lack something seriously needed in their team and in their midfield.”

Sports.title: 'We're not in Disneyland!': Mikel Arteta fires warning at Arsenal wonderboy Max Dowman, 16, after red card - and says it's not first time it's happened
Sports.content:
'We're not in Disneyland!': Mikel Arteta fires warning at Arsenal wonderboy Max Dowman, 16, after red card - and says it's not first time it's happened

Mikel Arteta has told 16-year-old Max Dowman 'we are not in Disneyland' as he insists his age does not give him a free pass following his red card against Fleetwood.

Dowman reacted to a heavy challenge in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night and was sent off for the second time this month, having also seen red while representing England's Under-19s.

Arteta appeared to have words with the youngster as he trudged off the pitch before the Gunners were beaten on penalties, and on Friday he suggested Dowman should have kept his cool under provocation.

'When I don't win, you know what the reaction is? I'm p***** off, big time, you know,' said Arteta. 'We need to be ready for it. This is the environment, and this is the reality. Otherwise, we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland.

'We're in the Premier League at this level, and we look after him so much like you cannot imagine.

'But at the same time, we're going to demand of him the same as anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Otherwise, the rest of the boys, what are they going to tell me?'

The Gunners did appeal against the red card after Tuesday's exit but were yesterday told it had failed, and Dowman will serve a three-match ban - starting with Sunday's trip to face Liverpool at Anfield.

Arteta said: 'My reaction comes in a moment of heat and extreme frustration because I know the consequences, especially for Max. And it's something that we discussed just before we went out because it's not the first time that happened, it happened another time this month with England.

'And it will continue to happen unfortunately, because the way he plays and the way he attracts opponents. We need to be able to tell each other the things as they are, because he's 16, and we have to be very protective of him, but at the same time, very straight with him with what to expect from him.'

Sports.title: Kumar Sangakkara opens up on Ryanair 'race storm': Cricket legend reveals how 'rude' Dublin staff berated him and his wife before boarding - as he submits 2,000-word complaint to budget airline
Sports.content:
Kumar Sangakkara opens up on Ryanair 'race storm': Cricket legend reveals how 'rude' Dublin staff berated him and his wife before boarding - as he submits 2,000-word complaint to budget airline

Kumar Sangakkara has opened up on what he believes was the racist treatment he and his family received during an argument at check-in at Dublin airport after a member of Ryanair staff told them: ‘You people with your kinds of passports should expect this.’

Sangakkara, who scored 12,400 runs in a glittering 134-Test career with Sri Lanka, was preparing to fly back to Bristol following a two-day trip to celebrate his 49th birthday when he says he was spoken to rudely by a woman at the check-in desk following confusion over an e-visa.

He says he went out of his way to make ‘doubly sure’ he was following the correct procedure with his family’s Sri Lankan passports.

But despite being assured two hours earlier by staff at the visa check desk that he didn’t need to reproduce the e-visas on his mobile phone at the boarding gate – a process that can take several minutes – and despite already clearing security, he was still told to step aside and download the e-visas after he arrived at the gate.

Sangakkara told Daily Mail Sport: ‘I said to one of the lady’s colleagues, “I will do this, but it is a bit of a procedure.” I also said: “We went to your visa desk just to avoid this confusion. They gave us one message, and it’s a bit confusing to passengers. But give us time.”

Kumar Sangakkara has hit out at Ryanair over an alleged racism storm at Dublin Airport

The cricket legend claims a member of staff berated him and his wife during boarding

‘As I was accessing the e-visa on the side, this lady from behind the desk raised her voice so the entire area could hear and said: “Hurry up! Hurry up! You have to do this quickly, otherwise I’m going to close boarding. Hurry up and get this done. Step aside now.” Sangakkara asked for more time to access the e-visas, only to be told once again to hurry up, at which point he told the lady she was being ‘very rude’.

He says she responded by saying he was being ‘argumentative and aggressive’, adding: ‘I’m going to treat you as a threat to other passengers on board and not board you.’

Sangakkara says: ‘And then she made the comment that you people with your kinds of passports should expect this.’

At this point, Sangakkara’s wife, Yehali, said: ‘You do realise what you said is so offensive, right? We are trying to access our passports, and you are shouting at us here in front of all these people. And you just made a very offensive comment. We’ve had such a good trip to Dublin, met such nice people. The only rude person we have met is you.’

The Sangakkaras were eventually allowed to board, but not before Kumar asked for the lady’s name so he could register a formal complaint. He says she replied: ‘I don’t have to give you my name. And if you keep asking for this, I’m not going to board you because I will consider you a threat.

‘Then my wife explained step by step why we were in Ireland, all of which she didn’t even have to do. But she was very calm, very measured, and she explained to her how rude it was, how offensive her remark was, because to us, I would take that as a very racist comment.

Sangakkara has filed a 2,000-word complaint to the budget airline over his treatment

‘Ryanair said I had refused to show my visa, which is completely untrue. I would completely understand if I had been an a** and refused, but I never play the race card for the sake of it, and this was an offensive comment.’

Earlier, Ryanair had insisted: ‘This passenger refused to provide the required visa documentation when requested by a gate agent carrying out mandatory immigration checks. Following completion of these checks and verification of this passenger’s eligibility to travel, this passenger travelled on this scheduled flight from Dublin to Bristol (28 Oct).’

Sangakkara has since filled out a Ryanair complaint form, explaining in 2,000 words the events of Wednesday, and says he was told to expect a response from the airline within eight days.

He added: ‘We had a lovely time in Dublin. It’s a beautiful city and we had two great days. And this one person on the way back does this, and then says that I refused to show my visas. It is a very bad representation.

‘I didn’t go into this looking for any publicity. It’s just a case of this is wrong, and it shouldn’t have happened – to me or to anyone.’

Sports.title: Jack Grealish has let his team-mates down: This self-inflicted episode shows he lacks the hard graft and humility so desired by David Moyes - and the team were better off without him, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Hard graft, humility and fighting for team-mates: three qualities not shown by a certain Jack Grealish this week. They are also a trio of traits demanded by the Premier League's most experienced boss, David Moyes, who banished the once £100million man Grealish to the naughty step for missing training without permission. News of his latest act of ill-discipline dominated every conversation on the Merseyside waterfront before this full-blooded contest with Newcastle but Grealish was not missed a jot as his youthful and energetic replacements put on a show. Goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry were enough to send Moyes and Co to the Carabao Cup quarter-final and within sight of their first trophy since 1995, something the 63-year-old boss and these loyal fans crave above anything. Moyes made the decision to drop and fine Grealish alongside chief executive Angus Kinnear. It is unknown if he will return for Monday's league game, also against Newcastle. The boss would not comment on the situation but said he supported the club decision to drop him. 'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it,' he said. 'All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. Jack Grealish let his Everton team-mates down, with the star suffering another setback 'From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job. It's a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them. There's humility about us tonight.' Giant-slayers Fleetwood Town are up next. Given the way they toppled champions Arsenal on Tuesday, that will be no easy feat, but a trip to Highbury is all that stands between the Toffees and a first domestic cup semi-final since 2015-16. Newcastle, meanwhile, look a pale imitation of the great team that beat Liverpool to win this competition in 2025 and the jury remains out on Matthias Jaissle. He lambasted his side's lack of maturity and said: 'It is shocking and it is frustrating as well. 'You need to be more mature and more clinical in these situations. Just clear it. It is a learning process but we don't have the time, we need to learn fast, especially with these young lads which is not an excuse any more.' Fans around the country have tended to see the Carabao Cup as a chance to save some money in recent years and Everton supporters have grumbled at Moyes and former boss Sean Dyche for having a similar attitude with line-ups. But a full house of 51,894 here – including 8,000 of the travelling Toon army – indicated that both teams were taking this seriously. Both mid-table with inconsistent form, this was a real chance for success. Even the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, knew that and was in attendance alongside his wife Marie-France. There was an obvious joke to be made around this week's budget, which has given a helping hand to those in need this winter. Given the Grealish-shaped hole in Moyes's team and the obvious lack of numbers in multiple positions, the Everton top brass might have fancied getting in Burnham's ear to get the chancellor's phone number and ask for a leg-up too. Hackney volleyed in his first goal for the club following his summer move from Middlesbrough Thierno Barry added Everton's third in the second half to set-up a tie against Fleetwood Town Matthias Jaissle's side will seek revenge when the sides meet again in the league on Monday Prime Minister Andy Burnham was among those celebrating as Everton bid to end their trophy drought Moyes has had to muddle through the season with a dearth of outfielders following a botched transfer window, but he has made the best of a tricky situation – one that was not helped by Grealish's actions. Any frustration at those off-the-field issues was parked on the night, though, as Everton found themselves two ahead at half-time. It was a scoreline to leave Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle cursing after a string of missed chances. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Pickford 7; Rohl 6, Tarkowski 7, O'Brien 7, Mykolenko 7 (Maitland-Niles 86); Hackney 8, Garner 7; Dibling 7 (Johnson 77), Dewsbury-Hall 8 (Norgaard 86), George 8 (Alcaraz 77); Barry 7. Subs not used: Travers, King, Keane, Armstrong, Graham. Scorers: Garner 34, Hackney 45, Barry 69. Booked: Hackney, Dewsbury-Hall, Mykolenko, Pickford, Tarkowski. Manager: David Moyes 8. NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5, Schar 5, Burn 6, Hall 6; Gonzalez 5 (Steur 81), Ramsey 5 (Joelinton 46); Murphy 5 (Toure 67, 6), Willock 5, Barnes 7 (Elanga 46, 6); Osula 5 (Wissa 46, 6). Subs not used: Pope, Botman, Bamba, Thiaw. Scorers: Burn 88. Booked: Schar, Burn, Joelinton. Manager: Matthias Jaissle 5. Referee: Farai Hallam 7. Attendance: 51,894. As it was, Everton weathered the storm thanks to Jordan Pickford and several last-ditch blocks. Despite Newcastle's territorial advantages, the Toffees settled and were first to strike on 34 minutes. It came through Grealish's direct replacement for a starting berth, Tyrique George, winning possession and, via Hackney, feeding Garner to pass into the far corner. Hackney soon turned from provider to goal-scorer, although referee Farai Hallam might claim an assist. Good officiating saw him play an advantage when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was hauled down when charging goalwards. Barry picked up a loose ball and fed Hackney who volleyed home, making it look easy when he could have easily fired over the bar. Seconds earlier, Harvey Barnes had been denied by Pickford but Newcastle were undone by a motoring counter-attack. Moyes would be delighted with the two goals but arguably more buoyed by the defensive rearguard that followed. Jaissle responded by throwing on three half-time changes in Yoane Wissa, Joelinton and Anthony Elanga. None of them worked as Everton played with their hearts on their sleeves in a warrior-like defensive display that had this new stadium rocking like rarely before. James Tarkowski put his body on the line and Sunderland lad Pickford made several inspired stops. Barry put the icing on the cake on 69 minutes when Garner robbed Amar Dedic of possession and Dewsbury-Hall teed up the No9 to finish with composure and help his team one giant step closer to ending that trophy drought. No Grealish? No problem. The Manchester City loanee, who showed his admirable side earlier in the day when he gave £10,000 to help an ill fan, has let his team-mates down with this latest episode. But with a collection of young talents thriving, mixed with some soldier-like experienced heads and a boss with an appetite for silverware, Everton do not need Grealish right now. This night was one to forget for him and Jaissle's work-in-progress Newcastle, who are a shadow of the halcyon days of Eddie Howe's cup-winning side, despite pulling one back late on through captain Dan Burn's header. Everton fans including Mr Burnham, meanwhile, will have March 21 and a potential final at Wembley circled in their diaries.
