Sports.title: Perez performs Cadillac show run in Mexico City – in a car from F1: The Movie | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Sergio Perez performed a show run in his home country ahead of this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix.

The Cadillac driver took to the streets of Mexico City along the Paseo de la Reforma. Over 100,000 fans were estimated to have attended the event.

The event promoters billed this as Perez’s fourth appearance in a Formula 1 car on the streets of his home country. However it appears Perez was not in fact driving a real F1 car.

Teams ordinarily use older cars to conduct show runs and ‘Testing of Previous Cars’. As this is Cadillac’s first season in F1 they have no such cars available.

The team therefore used one of the cars used to film “F1: The Movie”. These cars were based on Formula 2 chassis – the filmmakers purchased six for this purpose – and used bodywork modified by the Mercedes F1 team.

Cadillac yesterday confirmed Perez will continue to drive for them until at least 2029. He will make his 300th start in his home race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez this weekend.

“Being able to celebrate my 300th grand prix here is extraordinary,” said Perez. “A lot had to happen for this to become a reality, and being able to share this moment with everyone who has supported me, in such an iconic place as Reforma, makes it incredibly special to me. Thank you to Cadillac and everyone who made this possible.”

Sports.title: Fans “pay a bit less attention” to Formula 1 as calendar gets longer – Sainz | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Carlos Sainz Jnr suspects the growing size of the Formula 1 calendar may not be helping to make the sport more popular.

F1 has increased the number of rounds to 24, though only 23 are scheduled to happen this year due to the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. The number could fall further if either of the final two rounds are cancelled.

If the final rounds go ahead as planned, F1 will hold nine events in just eleven weeks. Sainz says he would have enjoyed more regular races when he was younger but suspects it may have become a turn-off for some fans.

“I think if I were a fan, I would love it because the more F1 I can watch on TV, the better,” he said. “I remember when I was a kid and there were only 16 races in the calendar, or 18. I used to miss Formula 1 [because it was not on] for a lot of weekends.

“But we also need to consider as a sport if that’s something that maybe is also counterproductive. Sometimes you need to miss the sport to get people engaged. When you get so many races in a row, people or the sport can maybe feel a bit like a league, like the Premier League rather than the Champions League. So maybe you pay a bit less attention to the matches or to the races in this case.

“So, it’s more a philosophy for the sport to consider whether you want to keep having so many races in a row.”

However Sainz, a director of the Grand Prix Drivers’ Association, is also concerned about the effect F1’s long calendar has on the teams’ staff.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“More important than that, I think as the GPDA, we’ve been told more or less that 24 races, 25 races is the limit of the championship that they’re willing to go for. I don’t know if that will be the case, the more offers there are to keep increasing venues. But I think that is the limit.

“I think it’s more about the members of the team that are going to spend only three or four days at home, or five days at home every month. And it’s the people in the teams that get the tougher end rather than the drivers. I think we are in a more privileged position in that sense.

“So, let’s see. I have the motivation to do however many races we need to do. I have the will to race. I love racing. But it is true that this end of the triple header, with three triple headers in a row, is going to be tough for the body, tough for the people, tough for the mind.”

Sports.title: Pointless Warburton Clash Wastes What Little Time Carlos Adames Has Left
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames begins his Zuffa Boxing journey with a matchup tailored to set up future UK bouts rather than create instant box office excitement. Ring Magazine officially confirmed that the WBC middleweight champion will meet Gerome Warburton on November 14, headlining Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 13 in Saudi Arabia.

This non-title contest takes place above the middleweight limit. Former bantamweight champion Jason Moloney meets Andres Teran on the undercard. News of the matchup leaked on October 19, so today’s press release simply rubber stamps what everyone already knew.

Adames (25-1-1, 18 KOs) gets his chance to make an impression with his new promoter. Building real buzz with Warburton in the opposite corner remains a tough sell. The Welsh fighter sits at number seven in the WBA middleweight rankings, though that ranking looks better on paper than it resonates with mainstream fight fans.

Warburton (18-2-2 KOs) comes into the fight with back-to-back wins over Nathan Heaney. Those victories opened the door for this spot, yet Adames marks a massive upgrade in difficulty. With only two knockouts on Warburton’s entire resume, the promotion cannot rely on a knockout artist angle.

The real motive here seems clear. Zuffa wants to prep Adames for bouts against stablemates Denzel Bentley and Aaron McKenna. Warburton serves as the first British obstacle before Zuffa rolls out bigger names from across the pond. While neither matchup is official, the blueprint makes sense.

Zuffa already has these fighters under contract. Adames gives Bentley and McKenna a legitimate champion to target. A dominant showing against Warburton hands the promotional team fresh footage to roll out for the next phase.

Still, convincing audiences to tune in for the current plan is a different story. Bentley and McKenna give British spectators a hometown reason to care, but domestic ties do not guarantee a massive gate or monster television ratings. In the United States, neither matchup feels like a breakout attraction for Adames.

Bentley’s status complicates things even further. He risks losing his WBO belt after failing to secure a date with mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez. Strip away that belt, and an Adames clash loses much of its luster.

McKenna presents another route, yet the middleweight division continues struggling with star power. Matching in-house talent creates reliable action, but it rarely draws casual viewers into the weight class.

This is classic in-house recycling that completely ignores both the clock on Adames’ career and what actual ticket-buying fight fans care about.

Adames is 32, fights roughly once a year, and carries zero commercial crossover. Handing him Gerome Warburton in a non-title catchweight does nothing. It does not sell tickets, it does not draw eyes to a broadcast, and it certainly does not move the needle for casual viewers who have never heard of the guy. Fans know a glorified sparring session when they see one, so they simply tune out.

The logic of using Warburton as a stepping stone to Denzel Bentley or Aaron McKenna is just as flawed. That entire sequence assumes the public is clamoring to see Adames clean out the British domestic scene. They are not. Bentley and McKenna are solid operators, but neither is a global draw capable of transforming Adames into an attraction.

If the payoff at the end of the tunnel is lukewarm to begin with, burning four to six months on a preliminary warm-up against Warburton makes zero promotional sense.

Time is working against them. With his history of lengthy layoffs, Adames cannot afford to spend prime months ticking boxes for low-profile regional setups. If Zuffa wanted to make a real statement with their middleweight investment, going after recognized names like Tim Tszyu or Vito Mielnicki Jr. would have delivered immediate legitimacy.

Putting Adames in with names fans actually follow forces attention onto the division, creates genuine stakes, and gives Zuffa an immediate return on their money.

Instead, they went the safe, budget-conscious route. The problem is that safety breeds indifference. When the opening move fails to capture anyone’s imagination, the matches lined up behind it end up dead on arrival anyway.

Sports.title: Ben Davison: Help Or Hindrance To His Heavyweights?
Sports.content:
It is rare for a trainer to attract as much publicity as his fighters. However, that is precisely what Ben Davison has succeeded in doing this year. For the uninitiated, Briton Davison is the trainer of heavyweights Moses Itauma, Fabio Wardley and Anthony Joshua.

Ben Davison’s profile as a trainer of heavyweights, though, really skyrocketed when he trained Tyson Fury from 2017 – 2019. During this time, many credited Davison for being responsible for The Gypsy King’s successful return to the ring after an absence of two and a half years, which Fury spent battling his demons and putting on weight.

Indeed, Davison was Fury’s trainer for his world title fight against Deontay Wilder in Los Angeles on 01 December 2018, resulting in a draw, and Wilder retaining his WBC title as the defending Champion. Fury performed well in this fight, proving that he is a talented boxer.

However, he felt there was something missing, and adjustments needed to be made. This fight demonstrated Fury’s skills as a boxer. The Gypsy King was, though, astute enough to know that just being a good boxer was not going to win him any rematch with The Bronze Bomber, famous for his legendary right hand.

Fury therefore changed trainer, enlisting the help of SugarHill Steward, the nephew of the famous Emanuel Steward, who had trained former World Heavyweight Champions Lennox Lewis and Wladimir Klitschko. The Brit did this in the hope that he would be not just a skillful boxer, but also become a ferocious puncher to combat the threat Deontay Wilder posed.

This plan worked. When Fury fought Wilder in their rematch on 22 February 2020 in Las Vegas, Fury beat Wilder by TKO in the 7th Round to win the WBC world title and the vacant The Ring heavyweight title.

Then, again with SugarHill Steward as his trainer, Fury successfully defended his WBC world title and The Ring heavyweight title against Deontay Wilder. This time, Fury went one better and beat Wilder by knockout in the 11th Round of their world title fight on 09 October 2021, also in Las Vegas.

Up to Fury’s last two fights against Wilder, The Gypsy King was not known to have the punch power to become a knockout artist. Under Steward’s tutelage, this situation changed, and Fury’s decision to leave Ben Davison was vindicated.

After Tyson Fury, Davison became the trainer of former World Champion Anthony Joshua. This is where things become interesting, as Davison was in AJ’s corner for his challenge for the IBF world title against then-champion Daniel Dubois. This all-British clash took place on 21 September 2024 at Wembley Stadium in London, England.

Joshua was having trouble in this fight, suffering knockdowns in the 1st, 3rd and 4th Rounds. In the break between the 4th and 5th Rounds, Davison seemed to advise Joshua to take a chance, coming out with the now-infamous “roll the dice” comment to his fighter.

When Davison was questioned about what he meant by this comment in a recent interview with the boxing commentator Spencer Oliver, Davison informed Oliver that the intention was for Joshua to throw a double jab and then a right uppercut at Dubois. Doing this, however, would leave Joshua’s chin exposed.

As the insightful YouTube channel Chris Talks Boxing explains, it would have been better for Davison to have advised AJ at that stage to stay out of trouble for a couple of Rounds, and rely on the jab, giving both trainer and fighter a chance to review tactics at the end of the 5th Round. In this way, Joshua would have conserved energy for the later Rounds, which was necessary, given that he had been in the wars up to that point.

As we know, however, Joshua tried to throw a right uppercut early in the 5th Round, but was caught on the chin by Dubois, forcing the former two-time World Champion to the canvas, and unable to beat the count in the same Round. It would therefore appear that Ben Davison’s tactics in this fight were at best clumsy, and at worst reckless.

Turning now to Moses Itauma, Davison has been his trainer since 2023, and was in Itauma’s corner for his fight for the vacant IBF world title against Filip Hrgović on 29 August at The O2 Arena in London, England. Up to this fight, Itauma had not been past the 6th Round in any professional fight.

Further, Itauma admitted publicly that he had not sparred 12 continuous Rounds, which is bizarre to say the least. On fight night, Itauma ran out of gas and lost to Hrgović by TKO in the 9th Round. In his recent interview with Spencer Oliver, Ben Davison mentioned that Moses Itauma is inexperienced, inferring that this is a possible reason for his loss to the Croatian.

As Chris Talks Boxing again rightly states, however, Itauma may be inexperienced, but it is his trainer Ben Davison’s responsibility to “manage” this lack of experience to get the best out of his fighter. Inexperience on the part of Itauma is therefore no excuse for Davison not preparing the young man adequately for a 12 Round fight.

Finishing with Fabio Wardley, Ben Davison was his trainer for both Wardley’s world title fights against Daniel Dubois this year. Both fights ended in TKO losses for the Ipswich man. Wardley lost his WBO world title to Dubois by TKO in the 11th Round on 09 May at Co-op Live in Manchester, England.

It was a respectable performance by Wardley. However, the rematch on 17 October at The 02 Arena in London, England was a much more one-sided affair, with Dubois winning by TKO in the 2nd Round. This last fight prompted former three-weight World Champion Duke McKenzie to go on the record saying that Ben Davison should seek help from “someone more technically minded” in training Wardley – hardly a ringing endorsement of Davison as a trainer.

Taking Davison’s record with all these heavyweights into account, it is clear that a pattern is emerging. The pattern is that Ben Davison seems unable to step up to the plate when it comes to training heavyweights for world title fights. Boxing is a results-driven sport, or at least it should be. In this regard, Davison has been found wanting, with one draw and four losses in all the Heavyweight world title fights he has been a trainer in.

This represents a 80% loss ratio with not one win. It is, of course, easy to criticize. In his last two Heavyweight world title fights, however, Ben Davison has thrown in the towel to save his fighters from further punishment. You don’t need to be a rocket scientist to come to the conclusion that there is definitely room for improvement.

Ultimately, though, it is for Davison’s heavyweights to decide whether he stays or goes!

Romer Cherubim

Freelance journalist

UK

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Must Get Ben Whittaker’s Next Move Right
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn needs to find Ben Whittaker a fight that prepares him for a world title shot, and Conor Wallace remains the obvious choice. At 29, Whittaker needs meaningful rounds against opponents who can expose his weaknesses, followed by evidence that he can correct them.

Anthony Yarde is among the opponents Hearn has mentioned for Whittaker, although the meeting does not establish that a fight between them is being negotiated.

Plotting what’s next 🌎 https://t.co/AWWFNVJk3p — Eddie Hearn (@EddieHearn) October 29, 2026

Whittaker earned his IBF mandatory position by beating Wallace on October 3, but the closing rounds weakened the case for sending him straight into a title fight. He controlled much of the contest before fading and getting hurt late, leaving a very different impression from the one he had built earlier.

“For me, no, he needs another fight,” Hearn said after the bout, naming Yarde, Wallace and the Joshua Buatsi–Willy Hutchinson winner as possibilities.

That leaves Hearn with a decision about what Whittaker actually needs. Another quick stoppage against an overmatched opponent would offer little preparation for championship opposition. Wallace forced him to work over the distance and exposed weaknesses that a better fighter could punish earlier.

A rematch would give Whittaker the chance to show he can finish strongly against someone who already knows how to hurt him. Wallace would have reason to attack sooner, having allowed Whittaker to collect too many of the early rounds before making his strongest effort.

Trainer Andy Lee cited COVID during the buildup to their first fight. If illness contributed to Whittaker’s late decline, facing Wallace again would provide an opportunity to demonstrate the difference a healthier preparation makes. It would also address the controversy surrounding a chaotic final round in which Whittaker went to the canvas three times without a knockdown being scored.

Yarde would bring a bigger domestic name and a heavier punching threat. That makes him an interesting option, but potentially a dangerous choice for someone who just struggled when Wallace increased the pressure. Whittaker would need to retain his concentration and defensive discipline when tired.

The Buatsi–Hutchinson winner would provide another demanding route. However, Hearn should be careful about treating any of these opponents as a convenient bridge to a title shot. Whittaker’s last performance showed why he needs the work.

Moving away from Wallace could also carry a cost with fans. Hearn has mentioned the rematch, but choosing someone else would leave the impression that his unbeaten fighter is leaving unfinished business behind.

Whittaker has time to improve at 29. His next fight needs to show that improvement, and beating Wallace more decisively would give Hearn something firmer to sell when the world title opportunity arrives.

At Whittaker’s age, a fighter does not develop an engine or an iron will out of nowhere. Those traits are either built into the foundation during the amateur days, or they simply do not exist. Whittaker entered the professional ranks with massive fanfare, an Olympic pedigree, and a style built entirely around showboating, reflexes, and athletic arrogance.

That works beautifully against overmatched opposition or journeymen who stand frozen in front of him. The moment a fighter stops watching the dancing, plants their feet, and marches forward with hard physical pressure, the entire facade begins to crack.

Liam Cameron proved it first. Cameron is a gritty, durable operator who made Whittaker uncomfortable by simply refusing to respect the theatrics, dragging him into physical trench work until that bizarre spill out of the ring brought a premature end. Instead of treating that as a warning light on the dashboard, Matchroom went right back to soft touches.

The Popeye Rivera matchup in Brooklyn was prime evidence of Hearn trying to protect the investment with harmless opposition rather than preparing him for genuine world caliber operators.

Conor Wallace brought that reality back to the surface in vicious fashion. It was not just a case of getting tired. Whittaker looked completely depleted, mentally rattled, and physically incapable of handling heavy incoming fire once the fight entered the championship rounds. Spending the twelfth round touching the canvas multiple times without the referee counting knockdowns was embarrassing for a guy calling out the division elite.

Whittaker does not possess the luxury of two or three developmental years to rebuild his gas tank and learn how to fight inside a phone booth. If he steps into the ring with a puncher like Anthony Yarde, or goes anywhere near the division monsters like Artur Beterbiev or Dmitry Bivol, the outcome is predictable. Those men do not wait around for nine rounds before turning on the pressure. They hunt you down from the opening bell.

If Hearn sends him into a rematch with Wallace and Whittaker runs out of gas again, the entire promotional work pops for good. What we saw down the stretch on October 3 might simply be Whittaker’s absolute ceiling under real pressure.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Gets Showcase Treatment Against Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia against Nikita Zon looks thin for a pay-per-view co-feature. Munguia supplies the name recognition, but Thursday’s press conference offered little proof that his challenger can keep the second biggest bout on Saturday’s Riyadh card competitive.

Richard Schaefer confirmed Munguia against Zon will take place immediately before Canelo Alvarez faces Christian Mbilli. That gives the WBA super middleweight title bout a prime broadcast position, yet the promotional pitch leaned on Zon entering with twelve victories and ten knockouts.

“I watched some of his fights. He’s strong, incredible power, as obviously 10 knockouts show,” Schaefer said during the media session. “I call him actually the new Siberian Rocky.”

Schaefer praised Zon’s power and stoppage record without naming a single credible opponent who proves he belongs in the ring with Munguia. Buyers heard he possesses danger, yet received zero evidence to evaluate that claim.

From a competitive standpoint, it is a gross mismatch. Munguia has logged 48 professional bouts, headlined major cards, and shared the ring with elite competition. Zon has exactly 13 fights, spent his entire career on regional Russian cards, and has never faced anyone remotely close to world class.

Slapping the moniker “the Siberian Rocky” on a completely untested fighter does not make him a threat. It is a fabricated sales gimmick designed to distract from the reality that Zon has done nothing to earn a shot at a belt on a massive international stage. Munguia should blow right through him inside five rounds, and anything less would actually look bad for Munguia.

“I came here to win and I’m leaving with nothing less than a victory. I will become the new world champion,” Zon said through a translator.

That served as his loudest quote, delivering standard bravado expected during fight week. He provided zero tactical detail on what vulnerabilities he intends to target against Munguia.

Munguia kept his comments just as brief. Asked if taking on a challenger with twelve bouts invites complacency, he pointed to his work with trainer Eddy Reynoso.

“I can just say that I’m ready. I had a great camp along Eddie. We prepared strongly,” Munguia stated through a translator. “It will be a great fight. You will see the best version of Jaime Munguia.”

The fighters offered little interest for the event. Schaefer tried filling that void by selling Zon as a raw puncher receiving a life-changing shot against an established Mexican name.

For viewers spending money on the broadcast, that pitch sounds empty. Munguia scoring a routine knockout over an untested opponent helps his record, but a premium slot requires legitimate drama. Watching an established contender cruise through a soft assignment leaves little intrigue.

As for why this fight is happening, it comes down to this. It is about keeping Munguia winning while minimizing any real risk. After picking up the WBA title against Armando Resendiz in May, his team wants him active and collecting paydays without putting him anywhere near dangerous 168-pound contenders like Osleys Iglesias, Diego Pacheco, or Hamzah Sheeraz.

Zon represents the path of least resistance for Munguia: an opponent with zero profile who will stand in front of him and provide highlight-reel footage. Boxing fans are completely exhausted by this specific brand of cynical matchmaking, which is exactly why the fight has generated virtually zero pulse online or in ticket sales.

Promoters seem to operate under the delusion that casual fans will see a gaudy knockout record, hear a goofy nickname like the “Siberian Rocky,” and instantly buy in. Today’s boxing public is far too savvy for that trick. Everyone recognizes an artificially manufactured record compiled in remote regional shows when they see one.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Gives Shakur Stevenson A Muratalla Escape Route
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley just offered Shakur Stevenson a convenient exit, one that spares him from a dangerous matchup with minimal reward. Raymond Muratalla brings serious heat without anywhere near the $15 million purse Bradley claims Stevenson wants. Stevenson could get caught, maybe even stopped, or grind out a safety-first decision that leaves fans booing anyway.

Heading back down to lightweight might not double his money, but it gives him cover. It lets him chase a different target under the banner of championship glory. Bradley basically handed him the script: drop back to 135 pounds, then unify the division.

“Now if he says, ‘I’m not going to fight him, and I’m going to go down, and I’m going to fight Zepeda for a belt,’ I’m cool with that. I’m cool with that. Stay at 135 and clean up the division. That’s what you should do,” Bradley said on his channel.

That backing carries weight while critics blast Stevenson over whether he will actually take the WBO mandate against Muratalla. Bradley opened by claiming there is “no hiding,” only to lay out the exact road map for Stevenson to walk away with his blessing.

Muratalla creates a tactical nightmare where even a victory might fail to win over frustrated fans. If Stevenson chooses to stand his ground, he gives a heavy hitter chances to connect. If he gets on his bicycle to protect the zero on his record, he only fuels the talk about being boring.

A knockout loss is a real danger here. Bradley insists he expects Stevenson to win, but picking him to prevail does not remove the physical threat, nor does it guarantee the performance builds any future buzz.

The money also looks shaky according to Bradley.

“He’s going to have to take a little bit less. It ain’t going to be $15 million. It’s going to be a lot less,” Bradley said.

From a business standpoint, retreating to lightweight makes plenty of sense. Stevenson does not even need a massive raise to justify the switch. Taking similar cash against someone his camp feels better about beats stepping into Muratalla’s crosshairs.

Dropping to 135 guarantees nothing simple, of course. Bradley’s plan means hunting down titleholders, specifically giving the green light to a tilt with William Zepeda. The real value comes down to the matchup details rather than just stepping on the scale at a lighter weight.

When a fan noted that Bradley pushed for a 135-pound return before the sanctioning body stepped in, the analyst stood firm. Stevenson can leave junior welterweight behind, but he has to plant his feet at lightweight instead of bouncing right back up after ducking Muratalla.

That bargain works for Bradley, but skeptical fight fans who want to see Muratalla get his shot will be a much tougher crowd.

Bradley supplied the public excuse by urging a chase for undisputed glory at lightweight. The real payoff is ducking a punishing clash for a paycheck that falls flat. Both realities can coexist, yet picking up another strap somewhere else will not silence the whispers about Muratalla.

Shakur’s silence is deafening, especially coming from someone who usually treats social media like a live microphone. When a fighter makes noise 24/7 about nobody wanting to get in the ring with them, going completely dark the second an actual mandatory gets called creates an awful look. It looks like battlefield freeze.

Usually, the moment a sanctioning body steps in, guys start chest-thumping about easy work, post-training clips, or talk about who is getting exposed. Instead, crickets. In combat sports, sudden radio silence often signals hesitation rather than quiet confidence. Stevenson knows Muratalla is not an aging name brought in to pad a highlight reel or a blown-up featherweight looking for a payday.

Muratalla is big, physically imposing, applies relentless forward pressure, and throws with spite. He does not care about fancy footwork or playing a game of tag to lose a decision.

Taking on a heavy-handed, high-volume puncher with everything to gain and nothing to lose requires digging into the trenches. When the reality sets in that there is no massive eight-figure check waiting on the other side to justify that kind of physical punishment, battle nerves kick in fast.

Right now, his camp is likely running the numbers and looking for every possible exit route. Dropping back down to 135 to claim an undisputed crown sounds a lot more heroic in a press release than admitting you want no part of an absolute buzzsaw at 140.

Sports.title: Richard Schaefer Oversells Canelo Alvarez’s Christian Mbilli Choice
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez looks to have picked the softer option in Christian Mbilli, though nobody expects an easy night at the office. Mbilli gives Canelo clear lanes to time counters, letting him steal rounds on the scorecards even if he gets outworked. Osleys Iglesias, on the other hand, represents a far more unforgiving matchup.

Promoter Richard Schaefer repeatedly praised Canelo at Thursday’s final press conference for picking Mbilli to give fans the best fight possible. That narrative ignored how slim the pool really was. With WBA titlist Jaime Munguia practically off the table due to gym loyalty, plus a vacant WBO belt, Canelo really only had Mbilli or IBF champion Iglesias to consider.

“Because I do not believe in shortcuts. I have been a champion for many years. I just want to fight the best,” Canelo said when asked about the decision.

Even if Mbilli throws a hundred punches a round, Canelo knows how judges score fights. A crisp, explosive counter shot that snaps an opponent’s head back often wins rounds over flurry work that lands to the body, head, or gloves. Against Mbilli, Canelo has a clear path to win rounds on the cards.

Iglesias is an entirely different problem, and arguably a far more punishing one. The Cuban is a rangy, hard-hitting southpaw who controls real estate with a stiff jab and detonates with a lead right hook. Canelo struggling against disciplined boxers with length and movement is well established.

Following Iglesias around the ring while absorbing straight lefts, right hooks, and jabs would be grueling, with very few clean openings to fire back. Iglesias brings real knockout danger without needing to smother himself on the inside to get it. Iglesias brings the bigger punch, but he also possesses the technical skill to dominate without hunting for a knockout.

Canelo risks trailing, missing, and soaking up damage without landing enough in return to keep pace. Reaching the final bell would still leave him battered. That is a projection, yet the Cuban’s length, precision, and power make it a very real danger.

Mbilli brings heat of his own. His swarm could pin Canelo against the ropes for long stretches. The difference is that Mbilli’s relentless forward motion keeps him squarely in range for Canelo’s signature counter rights and body hooks.

That gives Canelo a realistic path to victory. Mbilli can throw and land three as many punches, but judges often reward Canelo’s cleaner, harder single shots. Activity does not guarantee points, and Mbilli will offer plenty of targets for flashier work.

Canelo would get far fewer looks against Iglesias. He would need to evade the jab, close the gap, and connect before Iglesias moves away or fires back with something harder.

“I just need to be myself, and that is how I am going to win this fight,” Mbilli stated.

He could be right. Mbilli’s furious engine could easily overwhelm the veteran if Canelo cannot punch with enough authority to slow him down. Calling him the better option is far from guaranteeing a Canelo win.

Canelo never admitted to dodging Iglesias over stylistic concerns, and this remains a personal breakdown of the matchup. Still, Schaefer’s spin invites a reality check. Between the two champions on the table, Canelo selected the opponent who gives him room to land and a much clearer route to a victory on the cards.

It still could be controversial if Canelo wins a decision against Mbilli, but at least he would see the final bell, and his face wouldn’t be as beat up as it would be against Iglesias.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley’s Canelo Massacre Pick Ignores Reality
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley expects Canelo Alvarez to completely destroy Christian Mbilli, but that forecast fits the fighter Canelo used to be, not the one we see in the ring today. While his counterpunching remains lethal, blowing out an energetic pressure fighter requires relentless, high-gear output that recent outings just do not support.

Bradley argues that veteran savvy and sharp timing will punish Mbilli’s defensive flaws. That prediction hinges on Canelo avoiding the ropes and dictating action in the center of the ring.

“Canelo by massacre. Canelo by massacre. That’s what I got. He might even stop him,” Bradley said on Into the Storm. “Canelo is not gonna throw more punches than Mbilli, but his punches gonna be way more accurate, way more sound, way more placed than Mbilli.”

Bradley points to a glaring habit in Mbilli’s approach. When Mbilli bites on feints, he tends to dip his head and stare at the canvas, opening himself up to clean hooks and uppercuts. The expectation is that Canelo will time those flaws, threading counters through the incoming storm to force a late stoppage.

Still, even peak Canelo rarely battered elite competition into submission the way Bradley imagines. Older versions of Shane Mosley and Miguel Cotto went the full twelve. Gennadiy Golovkin lasted thirty-six rounds with him across three meetings, including the trilogy finale when Golovkin was forty. Different styles produce different results, but boxing history shows that defensive openings do not immediately guarantee a blowout.

Bradley fought in that very same era, so his viewpoint might lean on respect for his peer group. That does not discount his technical breakdown, but it does raise questions about whether his prediction relies on an outdated version of the Mexican star.

Seeing an opening is completely different from exploiting it through twelve fast-paced rounds. Canelo might spot the exact counter he wants, yet lack the stamina to deliver it over and over. A single crisp shot might turn heads, but it will not magically halt the next wave of pressure if Canelo cannot command real estate.

“As long as Canelo keep his back up off the ropes and keep the fight in the center of the ring,” Bradley added, suggesting Canelo should handle the assignment smoothly.

The eye test over the past few years undercuts any idea that Canelo is going to command the center of the ring against a relentless motor like Mbilli. Ever since the Jermell Charlo fight, Canelo’s legs have steadily abandoned him. What used to be deliberate ring generalship has turned into an older fighter looking for a place to lean.

Once the clock hits round six, his default setting is backing straight into the ropes, shelling up behind the high guard, and letting the ropes do the work of keeping him upright.

Against Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga, William Scull, and Terence Crawford, that exact pattern played out. Canelo cannot sustain footwork to dictate geography anymore, and he certainly lacks the conditioning to maintain the work rate required to keep an aggressive dog off his chest. His stamina dictates that he fights in brief, explosive bursts, spending the remaining two minutes of every round resting and waiting to time a single big counter.

That strategy works when hand-picking opponents who either freeze under the lights or lack the punch volume and inside craft to make him pay for taking rounds off. Munguia had the volume but zero defensive awareness or punching power; Berlanga was hesitant and limited; Scull had nowhere near the offensive pop or pedigree to capitalize. They were tailor-made style matchups designed to let Canelo coast on reputation and single heavy shots.

Mbilli is the complete opposite of a hand-picked rest stop. He does not care about getting countered; he never stops throwing, and he thrives precisely where Canelo now camps out: on the inside, chest-to-chest, hammering away at the ribs and arms.

If Canelo’s only plan is to retreat to the ropes and look for single uppercuts while Mbilli fires non-stop for twelve rounds, relying on the judges to favor low-volume potshots is going to be a very dangerous game.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Reveals Shakur Stevenson Vanished After Ring Stunt
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson gathered all the buzz for a potential O’Shaquie Foster bout without stepping into the ring. By stepping through the ropes following Foster’s win over Raymond Ford in May, Stevenson ignited major public anticipation. Yet Foster reveals his team pushed for the bout, waited, and met total silence.

That recent past demands a sharper look at Stevenson’s latest words. Foster just took down Emanuel Navarrete, and Stevenson quickly voiced fresh interest. Boxing enthusiasts ought to pause before celebrating, keeping Foster’s prior experience in mind.

“We kept asking. We didn’t hear nothing. We didn’t hear nothing,” Foster said on the Ariel Helwani show. “We held out for a little bit. We didn’t hear nothing. Tyrone didn’t hear nothing.”

Foster explained that talks never progressed to discussing weight classes. He expressed total readiness to step up to lightweight or junior welterweight, clearing away a major hurdle for a 130-pound titleholder looking upward.

“We didn’t even get that far, but I didn’t care,” Foster noted. “Like, I honestly didn’t care whether it was 135, 140. Either one. It didn’t matter to me.”

It looked like pure clout chasing from Shakur, plain and simple. Walking into another man’s spotlight right after a hard-earned victory creates the illusion that you want the fight next. Fans get excited, the broadcast cameras lock onto you, and you get all the free publicity without taking an ounce of risk. Then, the second Foster’s camp actually reached out to make the fight happen, Shakur vanished into thin air. Total silence.

Once Foster beat Navarrete, Stevenson offered public compliments along with a fresh challenge.

“Hell of a fighter. He will never give me my credit, but I’ll be real tonight. He showed his level,” Stevenson stated in a social post read on air. “That’s a challenge that would get me out of bed. Let’s do it whenever he’s ready. I’ll be here after his undisputed run.”

That is what makes Stevenson’s latest comment after Foster beat Navarrete look so empty. Saying he will fight Foster “whenever he’s ready” completely flips the reality of what happened. Foster was ready months ago, even offering to jump up in weight to make it effortless for Stevenson. Shakur was the one who went missing.

For now, Foster’s sights remain locked on unifying all four belts at 130 pounds. Chasing undisputed status puts Foster in control rather than hanging on Shakur’s schedule. Foster can hunt the remaining belt while Stevenson figures out whether his online comments translate into real business.

Ghana News.title: CSIR communiqué calls for urgent shift from scientific research to scalable commercial technologies
Ghana News.content:
In a major policy declaration issued at the conclusion of its maiden National Scientific Conference, the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) has called for an immediate paradigm shift in Ghana’s science, technology, and innovation (STI) ecosystem.

The official communiqué, finalized following two days of intense deliberations at the Ghana Academy of Arts and Sciences in Accra, asserts that while Ghana possesses substantial scientific and technological capability, national development hinges on converting that capability faster and at scale into market-ready products, services, and policies.

Held under the theme "Harnessing Science, Technology and Innovation for Sustainable Development in Ghana," the summit brought together 321 registered participants from all 13 CSIR research institutes, alongside representatives from executive government, industrial leaders, academic researchers, and international development partners.

A total of 194 scientific papers were presented – comprising 101 oral presentations, 74 poster displays, and 19 virtual sessions – organized across seven thematic areas aligned directly with Ghana’s national development priorities.

The conference featured key addresses and policy perspectives from top government officials, research administrators, and economic advisers, reflecting a unified consensus across state institutions to elevate the role of applied science in national development.

Delivering remarks at the opening, the Minister for Environment, Science and Technology (MEST), Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, underscored the state's mandate to foster an environment where scientific discovery directly advances socio-economic growth.

Support for this vision was echoed by key leadership within the scientific community, including: Ing. Mark Anthony Taylor, Chairman of the CSIR Governing Council; Prof. Paul Pinnock Bosu, Director-General of CSIR; Prof. Marian Dorcas Quain, Deputy Director-General of CSIR; and Engr Dr Collins Okrah, President of the CSIR Research Staff Association (RSA).

Keynote addresses provided strategic framing for aligning scientific output with national macroeconomic priorities.

Presidential Adviser on the 24-Hour Economy, Mr Augustus Goosie Tanoh, detailed the necessity of embedding technology into continuous industrial operations.

Chief Executive of the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission, Dr George Smith-Graham, addressed structural remuneration issues facing state researchers.

Additionally, an address on behalf of the Ag. Administrator of the Ghana National Research Fund (GNRF), Prof. Abigail Opoku Mensah, was delivered by her deputy, Prof. Ziblim, signaling the operationalization of dedicated state research financing.

Deliberations across the conference's seven thematic sessions yielded several foundational observations regarding the current state of research and industrial development in Ghana. Delegates agreed that Ghana’s socio-economic challenges are inherently interconnected, necessitating a transition away from isolated institutional research toward multidisciplinary, coordinated, and demand-driven scientific programs.

Central to the communiqué's findings is the insistence that commercialisation, technology adoption, and measurable socio-economic impact must be placed at the center of CSIR’s core mandate.

The conference observed that achieving scientific excellence and retaining domestic research talent depend on four structural pillars:

Predictable and Sustained Financing: Overcoming reliance on short-term funding through dedicated state mechanisms. Modernized Infrastructure: Equipping laboratories across all 13 institutes with modern diagnostic and analytical tools. Competitive Compensation: Providing remuneration packages that reflect the specialized expertise of scientists to prevent brain drain. Continuous Professional Development: Establishing clear pathways for career progression and technical training.

Furthermore, delegates highlighted that digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence (AI), when deployed responsibly and ethically, offer unprecedented opportunities to boost research productivity and operational efficiency across the scientific ecosystem.

Policy Directives for Government: Financing, Talent Retention, and IP Protection

To create an enabling environment for innovation, the communiqué outlines specific actionable recommendations for government policymakers, prioritizing predictable research funding and institutional protections.

The analytical matrix below summarizes the primary policy directives formulated by the conference to guide state intervention and legislative support:

Focus Area Policy Directive & Action Required Sustained Investment Guarantee predictable, long-term state funding for research programs, physical infrastructure, and scientific talent development. GNRF Operationalization Ensure the newly operational Ghana National Research Fund is adequately resourced and awards grants transparently via competitive processes. Regulatory & IP Frameworks Strengthen legal and policy frameworks governing technology adoption, intellectual property rights, and commercial licensing. Remuneration & Retention Reform researcher compensation structures to match specialized qualifications and stem the outflow of scientific talent from Ghana.

In response to national development priorities, the communiqué calls on the CSIR Governing Council and Management to execute sweeping internal structural reforms across its 13 constituent institutes.

Chief among these internal measures is breaking down historical silos by establishing joint, multi-institute research initiatives focused on major national challenges. These joint programs will share research infrastructure, pool expert personnel, and operate under unified arrangements for funding, progress reporting, and impact tracking.

To modernize its digital capabilities, CSIR management has been directed to establish a state-of-the-art CSIR Data Centre and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, supported by strict ethical, security, and governance protocols. Additional managerial directives include:

Strengthening the CSIR Endowment Fund: Expanding staff participation and ensuring transparent fund management for research, capacity building, and institutional growth.

Standardized Validation Pathways: Setting rigorous procedures for validating market-ready technologies, commercial licensing, and continuous socio-economic impact monitoring.

Institutionalizing the Annual Conference: Establishing the National Scientific Conference as a permanent annual platform for cross-sector knowledge exchange, commercial partnership, and investment attraction.

Cross-Sector Collaboration: Industry, Academia, and National Flagship Programs

Addressing researchers directly, the communiqué stresses that scientists must prioritize demand-driven, multidisciplinary projects with verified pathways to market adoption. Institutes are instructed to compile and publish comprehensive catalogues of market-ready technologies—detailing technology readiness levels (TRLs), unit production costs, regulatory compliance status, and target user demographics.

Scientists are also urged to compete aggressively for international research grants while upholding scientific integrity and responsible AI usage.

To translate these scientific outputs into national economic gains, the communiqué outlines tailored frameworks for industry, higher education, and executive government bodies:

Private sector actors are called upon to partner with CSIR in co-defining research priorities, validating new technologies, and funding technology incubation, pilot production facilities, and local manufacturing lines to enhance industrial competitiveness and create jobs.

Academic and development partners are urged to expand collaborative research initiatives, joint postgraduate training, infrastructure sharing, and joint technology development projects aimed at elevating Ghana’s indigenous scientific capacity and reducing long-term technological dependence.

The communiqué mandates structured collaboration between CSIR, sector ministries, and the 24-Hour Economy Secretariat to launch joint demonstration projects across strategic value chains:

Agriculture and Agro-Processing: Modernizing post-harvest handling, localized food processing, and storage systems. Aquaculture and Marine Science: Advancing sustainable fish breeding, feed formulation, and aquatic ecosystem management. Energy and Strategic Industrial Sectors: Deploying renewable energy applications and industrial value chains. National Flagship Alignment: Directly powering state initiatives, including the Feed Ghana flagship program and the 24-Hour Economy drive.

Three Fundamental Shifts for Ghana’s Future

The communiqué, formally signed by Engr Dr Collins Okrah, President of the CSIR Research Staff Association, and Dr Jennifer Afrifa Yamoah, Association Secretary, concludes with an unequivocal commitment to put Ghanaian science at the service of national development.

The summit summarized its vision for the future of Ghanaian science in three decisive operational shifts:

From Fragmented Excellence to Coordinated Impact — Unifying institutional research across disciplines to solve national priorities as one consolidated scientific force. From Research to Market — Shifting focus from academic publication alone to validating, licensing, and scaling commercial technologies. From Innovation to National Transformation — Translating technological breakthroughs into sustainable economic growth, job creation, and industrial self-reliance.

With the adoption of this communiqué, CSIR positions itself as the key technical engine behind Ghana's socio-economic evolution, asserting that national prosperity will be forged where scientific discovery meets industrial application.

Ghana News.title: No hostel, no auditorium: Dr Hilla Limann Technical University freshers use walkway for orientation
Ghana News.content:
Hundreds of freshers at Dr Hilla Limann Technical University in Wa in the Upper West Region have been forced to hold their orientation under an open walkway due to the university’s lack of an auditorium.

The situation is among several infrastructure challenges confronting the institution, which is also the only technical university in Ghana without a completed student hostel.

Vice-Chancellor, Prof Hamidatu Saaka Dramani, disclosed the challenges during a visit by Parliament’s Select Committee on Education, appealing for increased government investment to improve facilities and support the university’s growth.

She said the absence of adequate infrastructure was affecting the institution’s ability to provide students with a full university experience and expand enrolment.

“Finance has always been a big challenge for a young Technical University like ours. But we feel we could also do well internally like the bigger Technical Universities if our hostel is completed,” she said.

An 18-year-old hostel project

At the centre of the university’s accommodation challenge is a 1,000-bed hostel project that had been abandoned for 18 years.

Although renovation works have resumed, Prof Dramani said the university was still struggling to provide accommodation for its students, many of whom have to rent rooms in the surrounding community.

She said the lack of hostel facilities had become a major obstacle to attracting and retaining students who want to experience campus life.

“As I mentioned earlier, we have now the 18-year-old abandoned hostel; work is now ongoing steadily, and we are really happy with the progress. I mean currently we are still the only Technical University without a hostel, and we have hammered on this over and over again,” she told the committee.

Beyond accommodation, she said students wanted an environment where they could live, socialise and learn alongside their colleagues.

“The kind of new students we have, they want to have the university feel. They want to play, they want to learn at the same time, they want to interact with colleagues,” she said.

“When there is no hostel facility, they say, ‘I can stay in my father's house, I've been in that house for a very long time, I just want to have the university feel’, and that is where Dr Hilla Limann will really get a big challenge.”

Hostel capacity reduced from 1,000 to 600 beds

The Education Committee visited the hostel site, where renovation works resumed about four months ago.

However, the prolonged period of abandonment has affected the building’s structural integrity, forcing engineers to reduce its design from four floors to three.

The adjustment will bring the facility’s capacity down from the initial 1,000 beds to 600.

Prof Dramani said the university was also struggling with inadequate workshop space as new equipment continued to arrive for its technical programmes.

“In fact, last month trucks kept coming with automobile equipment. Currently, the small workshop space that we have is being taken away by only two departments. Mechanical machine shop alone, we have about twenty machines sitting in there and so many other equipment,” she said.

Education Committee members raise concerns

Members of the parliamentary committee said the challenges were evident during their visit, particularly the use of an open walkway for the freshers’ orientation.

The MP for Offinso North, Dr Fred Kyei Asamoah, said the arrangement was unlike anything he had encountered at a university.

“This is the first time I'm seeing this number of students using such an area as an auditorium for freshers,” he said.

The committee’s Vice-Chairman, Joseph Kwame Kumah, MP for Kintampo North, who led the delegation, also acknowledged the absence of a proper auditorium.

“We have come to see with our naked eyes that for lack of an auditorium, an improvised auditorium is being used here,” he said.

Mr Kumah commended the Education Minister for facilitating the resumption of renovation works on the hostel project.

“You can hear the noise in the background; that is work that is ongoing to quickly see to the renovation. I would like to thank the Minister of Education for quickly seeing to the renovation works,” he added.

VC appeals for more funding

Prof Dramani appealed to the government to provide additional funding to complete the hostel facilities and expand workshop space to support teaching and learning.

“We are really just making a humble appeal; even if nothing happens at all, those two hostels that are given to us by the government should really be completed as soon as possible. And if that is done, I think that will go a long way to really increase our enrolment. If we get an additional workshop space, it will really help our teaching and learning,” she said.

She maintained that the university was academically prepared for expansion, noting that all its programmes had been accredited.

The institution is also expanding from four faculties to seven, with plans for new faculties in Intelligence Systems, Agriculture, and Geosciences and Mining.

The proposed Geosciences and Mining faculty is expected to benefit from the presence of the Azumah Gold Mine, which could serve as a practical learning environment for students.

‘We cannot pray our way out’ — Kyei Asamoah

A former Director-General of the Commission for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (CTVET), Dr Kyei Asamoah, said technical education required greater financial commitment because of its practical nature.

He argued that government must invest substantially more in technical and vocational education than in conventional academic institutions.

“TVET is a bit expensive. Applied education helps students acquire skills. We cannot pray our way out; we cannot memorise our way out. We need to invest in TVET,” he said.

He added that expanding technical education in the region could help equip young people with employable skills and reduce the need for them to migrate to southern Ghana in search of opportunities.

“Where the sun is, that is where the money is. If we can train and get our young ones employed here, they will not be moving down south,” he said.

Committee proposes Tamale Technical University model

The committee’s Chairman urged the university's management to consider adopting a financing arrangement used by Tamale Technical University, where contractors pre-financed projects and were subsequently reimbursed by the government.

“Tamale Technical University has been able to go into a memorandum of agreement where the contractor used his own money and has been able to move faster than the government could do, and later the government refunded the money,” he said.

He stressed that the absence of student accommodation at a technical university was a major concern that needed urgent attention.

“For a whole institution like a technical university not to have hostels for students, then we go nowhere,” he said.

The Chairman also said the university could attract students from neighbouring countries, including Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire, if its infrastructure and technical facilities were improved.

Vice-Chairman Joseph Kwame Kumah pledged that the committee would lobby for the institution to receive the necessary support.

He also called for greater motivation for lecturers who choose to work in Wa, acknowledging the challenges of attracting and retaining teaching staff outside major urban centres.

“It is not easy to be in Wa and teach. People would like to move to Accra and Kumasi. The potential here is so huge. If attention is paid here, it will become an institution of its own. We are going to do proper lobbying for this school,” he assured.

Ghana News.title: Gender Minister engages Obuasi SHTS students affected by allegations, assures them of support
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, has engaged students affected by the alleged sexual abuse at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), assuring them of the government’s support as investigations into the matter continue.

The engagement provided an opportunity for the Minister to listen to the students’ concerns and reaffirm the Ministry’s commitment to ensuring their welfare and addressing their individual needs.

Dr Lartey stressed that the safety, dignity and well-being of the students remained paramount, noting that supporting them required sensitivity, confidentiality and a coordinated response.

She also underscored the need to protect the students from further distress, stigma and victimisation while the relevant authorities investigate the allegations.

The Minister assured the students that the Ministry would continue working with the Ghana Education Service (GES), social welfare officers, health professionals and other stakeholders to ensure they receive the necessary support.

The engagement forms part of the Ministry’s broader response to the allegations, which includes the deployment of an advance team made up of officers from the Department of Social Welfare, the Domestic Violence Secretariat and the Department of Children.

The team is expected to engage the affected students and their families, assess their needs and coordinate appropriate interventions.

The Ministry reaffirmed its commitment to protecting children’s rights, supporting affected students and working with relevant institutions to strengthen child protection systems and ensure that schools remain safe environments for learning and development.

The Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) says it is prepared to confront any threat to the country’s security and defend its territorial integrity against external aggression.

The assurance was given by the General Officer Commanding the Southern Command, Brigadier General Edward Awaribey, at the 2026 Static and Firepower Demonstration held at the Battle Training Camp in Bundase.

He said the military had maintained a high level of operational readiness through continuous training, improved equipment and the adoption of lessons from security operations across the region.

Brigadier General Awaribey stressed that the Armed Forces remained committed to protecting the country and would respond firmly to any attempt to undermine its stability.

“Let me use this opportunity to assure the nation that the Ghana Armed Forces remains motivated, mission-oriented, mission-ready, highly trained, well-equipped, and prepared to respond decisively to any form of aggression or destabilisation,” he said.

The demonstration brought together military personnel and showcased the Armed Forces’ equipment, firepower and operational capabilities, highlighting its preparedness to deal with evolving security challenges.

Ghana News.title: Techiman North moves to end post-harvest losses with new storage facilities and irrigation plans
Ghana News.content:
In a significant move to bolster the local agricultural sector, the Techiman North District Assembly has announced ambitious plans to establish modern storage facilities and develop irrigation systems.

The District Chief Executive (DCE), Johnson Kwabena Adom, unveiled these plans during his address at the Third Ordinary Meeting of the Third Session of the Fourth Assembly on Thursday, October 29.

Addressing the assembly at the main conference hall in Tuobodom, the DCE emphasized that while the district is making strides in various sectors, the sustainability and growth of agriculture remain a top priority.

He outlined a strategic vision aimed at not just increasing production, but also protecting the livelihoods of farmers and ensuring food security.

The DCE's address highlighted a comprehensive approach to tackling the perennial challenge of post-harvest losses, a major concern for farmers in the district.

"To address post-harvest losses, Management is planning for the establishment of a modern storage facility to improve the preservation of agricultural produce and reduce wastage," Hon. Adom stated. "This initiative is expected to help farmers preserve their produce and minimize losses, particularly during periods of excess supply."

This commitment to storage infrastructure is part of a broader strategy that also focuses on water security for farming. The Assembly's development project list includes the drilling and mechanization of multiple boreholes with solar-powered systems across various communities, including Akonkonti-Nyamebekyere, Brentu, Bridgeso, and Dampa.

While these are primarily for potable water, the DCE’s emphasis on agricultural support signals a clear recognition that water availability is critical for year-round farming and a stepping stone towards more robust irrigation systems.

He further noted that the Assembly is collaborating with development partners to support agro-processing initiatives, which will create ready markets for raw produce and add value to the agricultural value chain. He acknowledged the crucial role of the Member of Parliament in attracting additional agro-processing factories to the district, a move expected to create reliable markets for local farmers.

Beyond infrastructure, the DCE detailed several programmes designed to directly empower farmers.

Under the government’s Feed Ghana Programme, he reported that 1,500 bags of fertilizer were distributed to 783 farmers in the third quarter of 2026 alone. The beneficiaries included 268 females and 515 males, demonstrating a commitment to supporting all segments of the farming community.

The DCE also announced that the district has been selected to benefit from the Ghana Women and Youth Employment and Social Cohesion (GWYESCO) Programme. This initiative, in partnership with GRATIS Foundation, will provide competency-based technical training to artisans, agro-processors, and smallholder farmers.

"This initiative is expected to strengthen the Assembly’s local economic development agenda by building the capacity of artisans, agro-processors and smallholder farmers, particularly women and youth," Hon. Adom explained, adding that it will promote "employment creation, enterprise development, improved productivity, increased income opportunities, technology adoption and stronger local value chains."

Looking ahead, he reaffirmed the Assembly's commitment to celebrating and rewarding the district's farmers. He proudly recalled that the overall best farmer in the district last year received a brand-new vehicle and announced that the 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration would be held on Friday, 4th December 2026, under the theme "Our Farmers, Our Food, Our Culture."

He called on all assembly members, corporate organizations, and development partners to support the celebration, underscoring the vital role farmers play in the district's development.

The address painted a picture of a district on the move, with a clear focus on building a resilient agricultural economy. By tackling post-harvest losses head-on through storage and irrigation, and by investing directly in the skills and resources of its farmers, the Techiman North District Assembly is working to ensure that the fruits of the land translate into lasting prosperity for its people.

Ghana News.title: Health Ministry calls for stronger measures to tackle lead poisoning
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Health has called for stronger regulation, public education and collaboration among key institutions to prevent lead poisoning and protect children from its harmful effects.

The call was made at the launch of the 2026 National Lead Poisoning Awareness Week, held under the theme, “From Detection to Prevention”.

Speaking on behalf of the Minister for Health, the Ministry’s Chief Director, Mr Desmond Boateng, described lead poisoning as a serious but preventable public health threat that requires coordinated action beyond the health sector.

He warned that exposure to lead could affect children’s brain development, learning abilities and behaviour, while also causing kidney and cardiovascular problems in adults.

Mr Boateng identified lead-based paints, mining activities, battery recycling, electronic waste and contaminated consumer products as some of the common sources of exposure.

He said the government’s priorities included intensifying public education, protecting vulnerable communities, strengthening the capacity of health workers to detect and manage lead exposure, and enforcing regulations to control the substance at its sources.

The Deputy Country Representative of UNICEF Ghana, Madam Emmanuelle Collet, called for the establishment of a coordinated national surveillance system to identify children exposed to lead, trace sources of contamination and ensure unsafe products were removed from the market.

The awareness week is expected to promote practical measures to reduce lead exposure and strengthen efforts to safeguard public health.

The Ministry of Health is collaborating with Pure Earth, Vital Strategies, the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), the World Health Organisation (WHO), the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) and the Ghana Health Service (GHS) to strengthen public education, surveillance and regulatory enforcement.

The initiative places particular emphasis on protecting vulnerable populations, especially children, from the harmful effects of lead exposure.

Ghana News.title: Gender Minister engages Obuasi SHTS authorities, community leaders over alleged sexual abuse
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, has engaged authorities of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) and community leaders on measures to protect students and support those affected by allegations of sexual abuse at the school.

The engagement focused on the welfare and safety of students, restoring trust within the school community and strengthening child protection systems to prevent similar incidents.

During the visit, Dr Lartey stressed that protecting children required more than the existence of laws and policies, emphasising the need for effective implementation, institutional collaboration and timely responses to concerns affecting their safety.

She assured that the Ministry would continue working with the Ghana Education Service (GES) and other relevant institutions to strengthen child protection structures and improve students’ access to counselling and other support services.

The Minister said the welfare of the affected students remained a priority as investigations into the allegations continued. She added that the Ghana Health Service was also involved in addressing their health needs as part of the coordinated response.

Dr Lartey further disclosed that the police were investigating the matter and assured that anyone found culpable would be prosecuted in accordance with the law.

She stressed that affected students must receive the necessary support without being subjected to further victimisation.

As part of the visit, the Minister also met key community stakeholders, including religious leaders, traditional authorities, Parent-Teacher Association representatives, Assembly Members, civil society organisations and old students of the school.

She outlined steps taken by government institutions to address the matter and reaffirmed the Ministry’s coordinating role in ensuring a coordinated response.

Dr Lartey called on parents, guardians and the public to report wrongdoing and raise concerns about the safety and welfare of children, noting that child protection was a shared responsibility involving families, schools, communities and state institutions.

She also appealed to media practitioners to exercise restraint when reporting cases involving children, particularly those relating to sexual abuse.

The Minister expressed concern that the publication of some affected students’ full names had caused distress to their families and made further engagement more difficult.

She urged the media to protect the identities and dignity of the children, stressing that responsible reporting was essential to safeguarding their welfare and supporting efforts to address the allegations.

Meanwhile, continuing students have started returning to the school, with measures being taken to strengthen security and rebuild trust between students and teachers.

The Minister appealed to parents and students to cooperate with school authorities as efforts continue to restore a safe and conducive learning environment.

The visit also involved the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service, whose participation highlighted the importance of collaboration between the education sector and child protection institutions.

Dr Lartey reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to protecting children in schools, homes, churches and communities, and said the Ministry would continue working with relevant institutions to support affected students and strengthen child protection arrangements.

Ghana News.title: There’s no ‘dumsor’ in Ghana; there’s adequate power -Mahama tells Ghanaians in Russia
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama says Ghana is no longer experiencing power outages, popularly known as dumsor, following efforts by his government to address the financial challenges that threatened electricity supply.

He said the administration had cleared its outstanding debts to Independent Power Producers (IPPs) and introduced a payment system to ensure suppliers are paid promptly for electricity delivered to the national grid.

Addressing Ghanaians in Moscow, Russia, President Mahama said the government inherited about US$1.7 billion in unpaid obligations to IPPs, as well as arrears for gas supplied from the Jubilee Field and by ENI.

He said the debts had created tensions, with some power producers threatening to suspend electricity supply.

“With regard to energy, I can report that there’s no dumsor in Ghana. Everybody has adequate power. And that’s one of the areas that has been quite dramatic in terms of its management,” he said.

The President added that the government was now up to date with payments to IPPs.

“I’m happy to announce that we have cleared the IPP debt. That is, we are current. Any energy they supply today, we’re paying them,” he said.

He said a separate payment arrangement had also been introduced to address the remaining obligations, with initial payments followed by further settlements as they fall due.

According to President Mahama, the new arrangement has helped rebuild trust between the government and power producers while ensuring a more stable electricity supply.

He maintained that Ghana currently has sufficient power to meet the country's needs.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
