World.title: 2027: INEC receives over 4,800 claims, 600 objections on voter register
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has received over 4,800 claims and about 600 objections on the preliminary voter register, with a promise that the discrepancies will be corrected before the final register is certified on December 15, 2026.

INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this on Friday when the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Pre-Election Fact-Finding Mission paid a courtesy visit to the commission’s headquarters in Abuja. The mission is led

by Victor Bockarie Foh, a former Vice-President of Sierra Leone.

Amupitan said the claims, received at the registration areas where the register was displayed as of Thursday, were mainly corrections and other minor matters.

On objections, he said the commission had received “about 600 complaints on the register” through electoral officers and Resident Electoral Commissioners from the various wards. He added that “the display of the register online is also confirming some of the complaints we had earlier received.”

According to hum, the register now stands at over 103 million registered citizens, adding that it is a huge figure, and that the discrepancies noticed would be corrected so that “the register will be properly cleaned up” ahead of the final list.

The commission completed three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise and recently ended the physical display of the preliminary register at registration areas nationwide. It has also published the register on its online portal, display.inecnigeria.org, “for public scrutiny, claims, and objections.”

He again restated that the Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are scheduled for Saturday, February 6, 2027.

He said the commission will deploy personnel and technology across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, covering 774 Local Government Areas, 8,809 Registration Areas (Wards) and 176,846 polling units.

Amupitan said the commission had executed nine of the 14 major milestones in its Revised Timetable and Schedule of Activities for the election.

He said INEC had also moved “away from administrative assumptions” by personally conducting zonal readiness assessment tours. It has covered the South-West in Lagos, the North-West in Kaduna, the South-East in Enugu and the North-East in Gombe, and the team is heading to Port Harcourt for the South-South. The North-Central, the last zone, will be visited next week.

He said the tours had shown that some areas needed higher deployments than planned because of terrain and security challenges.

Amupitan disclosed that the commission is planning a mock accreditation across the country, which he said should hold “some time in November.” He said it would test accreditation and the transmission of results simultaneously in all the states, to be sure the commission can “cure the problem of glitch that took place in 2023.”

On technology, he said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) will be deployed for dual biometric accreditation, by fingerprint and face. The commission has also introduced a new electronic verification platform, eEC8A, for results transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

He said a safeguard has been introduced so that results are authenticated at the polling unit before they go to the portal. He explained that discrepancies had emerged in the past as results moved from the polling unit to higher levels of collation.

On staff welfare, Amupitan said the commission had secured approval for the Consolidated Election Management Body Salary Structure, which takes its workforce out of the regular civil service scale. It also secured a 150 per cent increase in state operational overheads.

In return, he said, the commission maintains “zero tolerance for administrative negligence, extortion, or partisan compromise.” That policy is backed by Oaths of Neutrality under Section 26 of the Electoral Act 2026.

On security, he said the commission is working with the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and the Armed Forces through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security

(ICCES). The framework uses early risk-mapping tools to secure polling units, protect ad-hoc staff, particularly members of the National Youth Service Corps, and guarantee access for all voters, including persons with disabilities.

He said the commission is also finalising plans for internally displaced persons, “to ensure inclusivity.”

Amupitan, who said he has been in office for one year, having been sworn in on October 23 last year, said the commission had conducted four main off-cycle elections and 16 by-elections in that period. He said these gave INEC the chance to test its plans and equipment. “The mistakes of the past cannot be allowed to repeat themselves,” he said.

He told the ECOWAS delegation the commission welcomes the deployment of long-term and short-term ECOWAS election observation missions. “We welcome your scrutiny. INEC has no candidate and no political party. Our sole allegiance is to the rule of law, the sovereign will of the Nigerian electorate, and the democratic progress of our nation”, he said.

World.title: Ancelotti omits Alisson as Brazil name squad for November friendlies
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti has named a youthful 26-man squad for November friendlies against Japan and Singapore, leaving out Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker while insisting he remains the country’s best goalkeeper.

The squad was announced on Thursday at the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) headquarters in Rio de Janeiro. Brazil will face Japan on November 14 and Singapore three days later, as Ancelotti continues rebuilding the team after its disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.

“We don’t need to test Alisson. We know him very well. He’s the best goalkeeper,” Ancelotti said. “When the Copa América starts, he’ll be called up. Like Alisson, all the others will be.”

Ancelotti said the November matches would give him an opportunity to assess younger players and refresh the squad. The selection includes nine players of Olympic age and 15 under 23.

“We need to make the most of 2027 to carry out this renewal,” he said, adding that he expected Brazil to have a more established team by the time preparations for the 2028 Copa América and World Cup qualifying intensify.

Chelsea forward Estêvão has retained his place despite limited playing time at club level. Ancelotti said Brazil would continue monitoring the 19-year-old and allow him to develop at his own pace.

The squad also includes maiden call-ups for Corinthians midfielder André and Cruzeiro defender Jonathan Jesus. Manchester City forward Allan is among the other young players selected.

No players from Flamengo or Palmeiras were called up following an agreement with the CBF, as the clubs are competing in a tight domestic title race. Atlético Mineiro players were also left out.

Full Squad:

Goalkeepers: Bento (Al Nassr), Lucas Perri (Torino), Pedro Morisco (Coritiba).

Defenders: Arthur Dias (Athletico Paranaense), Carlos Augusto (Inter Milan), Douglas Santos (Zenit), Gabriel Magalhães (Arsenal), Jair Cunha (Nottingham Forest), Jonathan Jesus (Cruzeiro), Vanderson (Monaco), Vitor Reis (Manchester City), Wesley (Roma).

Midfielders: André (Corinthians), Andrey Santos (Manchester United), Bruno Guimarães (Arsenal), Danilo (Botafogo), Gabriel Bontempo (Santos), João Gomes (Aston Villa), Marlon Gomes (Shakhtar Donetsk).

Forwards: Alisson Santana (Shakhtar Donetsk), Allan (Manchester City), Estêvão (Chelsea), Raphinha (Barcelona), Rayan (Bournemouth), Endrick and Vinícius Júnior (both Real Madrid).

World.title: NDC urges INEC to remove deceased Nigerians from voters’ register
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to remove the names of deceased Nigerians from the voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party’s National Presidential Campaign Council (NPCC) raised concerns over reports that deceased Nigerians, including prominent figures such as Raymond Dokpesi, Ifeanyi Ubah, Muhammadu Buhari and Rotimi Akeredolu, still appear on the register.

In a statement on Friday, signed by its spokesperson, Dr Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, the council questioned the accuracy and integrity of the voters’ register and called on INEC to explain when it was last comprehensively updated.

The council also urged Nigerians and political parties to exercise their legal rights by filing objections against names believed to have been wrongly retained on the register.

It called on INEC to establish an online portal for publishing names under objection, allowing affected individuals who are alive to respond, and making public the procedure for challenging questionable entries.

The statement read: “Reports that deceased Nigerians, including prominent figures such as Raymond Dokpesi, Ifeanyi Ubah, Muhammadu Buhari and Rotimi Akeredolu, still appear on the voters’ register raise serious questions about its accuracy and integrity.

“These are just a few names. What about the 774 local government areas across Nigeria? How many deceased persons remain on the register? When was it last comprehensively updated? Is this an oversight, institutional failure or something more troubling?

“INEC has the legal responsibility to cleanse the register, especially if it has been notified by citizens. The electoral body owes Nigerians answers. We demand a credible, up-to-date and verifiable voters’ register ahead of the 2027 elections.”

The council said INEC, as a publicly funded institution, must demonstrate efficiency, professionalism and accountability in managing the electoral register.

It further called for an independent audit of INEC’s processes and mechanisms, citing concerns over the credibility of the 2023 general elections.

“The 2027 election is too critical for unanswered questions about the very foundation of our democracy. No excuses. No complacency. No questionable register. INEC must do its job,” the statement added.

World.title: 48 terrorists, one soldier killed in foiled attacks on troops in Borno, Yobe
World.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

Barely 24 hours when scores of Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists were killed in separate encounter in communities of Kukawa and Marte local government areas of Borno state, about 48 terrorists were neutralised by Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI while attempting to infiltrate military positions in Bitta Gwoza LGA of Borno State and North East Theatre Training School (NETTS),

Buni Yadi, Gujba LGA of Yobe State between 29 and 30 October 2026.

Unfortunately, the engagements recorded one soldier who paid the supreme sacrifice, with two others sustained minor injuries.

This was disclosed on Friday in a press statement signed by the Acting Media Information Officer Headquarters Joint Task Force North East Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni.

He said: “Troops of OPHK have dealt a major blow to Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists, foiling their attacks on military positions in Bitta Gwoza LGA of Borno State and North East Theatre Training School (NETTS),

Buni Yadi, Gujba LGA of Yobe State between 29 and 30 October 2026.

“In Bitta, troops decisively disorganised an attempted terrorist assault on the night of 29 October 2026. The combined response of ground troops and air support overwhelmed the attackers, thwarting their plan and inflicting heavy casualties.

“In a related development, troops launched a successful counter-attack against a large concentration of ISWAP fighters who attacked NETTS Buni Yadi on same 29 October to the early hours on 30 October 2026.

“The approximately five-hour engagement was coordinated by the Theatre Command, with effective integration of Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance (ISTAR) capabilities, alongside air and ground assets.

“The decisive counter-offensive resulted in 48 terrorists killed, with troops recovering a substantial cache of weapons and ammunition.

“Recovered items include 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four General Purpose Machine Guns (GPMG), one 60mm mortar, 105 AK-47 magazines and two video cameras.

“Also recovered were 30 rounds of 12.7mm armour-piercing incendiary ammunition, 2,738 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, 223 rounds of 7.62mm NATO ammunition and 2,054 rounds of PKT ammunition.

“The engagements recorded one soldier who paid the supreme sacrifice. May his soul rest in peace. Also the two others who sustained minor injuries are responding to treatment. The morale of troops remains high as they sustain operations against terrorist elements across the theatre”. Goni stated.

The latest operational successes according to the statement further demonstrate the troops’ combat effectiveness, operational coordination and determination to deny terrorists freedom of action.

The heavy losses suffered by the insurgents and the recovery of their weapons and ammunition Goni said, constitute another significant setback to their operational capabilities.

World.title: 29-year-old Nigerian man killed as tree crushes car in London
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

A 29-year-old Nigerian man, James Abiwon, has died after a tree fell on his car during Storm Boelo in Mill Hill, north London.

According to Metro UK, Abiwon was driving along Dollis Road at about 12.30pm on Sunday when the tree came down in strong winds. Emergency crews, including police officers, firefighters, paramedics and an air ambulance, responded, but he was pronounced dead at the scene.

His cousin, Tyrrell Okolo, described him as “a master of everything” and a devoted family man. Abiwon was a tech sales executive who had earned a degree from the University of Essex. He was also a semi-professional footballer with Aldershot, a musician with about 40,000 YouTube viewers and a mentor to many, his cousin said.

Abiwon had been preparing to celebrate his 30th birthday with a padel tournament. The event will now go ahead in his memory, with proceeds going to support his family.

His close friend, Kwame Affum, 29, said the two had played padel together just two days before the crash. “I’m trying hard to get my head around this,” he told Metro UK. A friend had messaged Abiwon shortly before the accident about money they owed him for the court, but he did not reply, prompting concern.

Affum said Abiwon loved sport, was a good footballer and supported Arsenal. He had earned a first-class university degree and recently won an award at work. “He was full of energy and talent,” Affum said. “He was going to celebrate his 30th birthday in two weeks. It just seems impossible this has happened.”

A witness who laid flowers at the scene told Metro UK that she heard a helicopter and went outside to find the fallen tree covering the road, with the car trapped beneath it. Abiwon’s girlfriend and best friend arrived while rescuers were still at the scene. The witness said they were shaking as they waited and hoped he would be brought out.

The witness said Abiwon’s aunties and other relatives arrived later and were inconsolable. She described him as clearly well loved and said the community had lost one of its own.

Traffic on Dollis Road was reportedly heavy at the time, as roadworks on a nearby street had diverted more vehicles onto the route. A neighbour whose home overlooks the scene said: “If it had been 10 minutes later, it could have been me.”

The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to Dollis Road at about 12.40pm on Sunday after reports that a tree had fallen onto a moving car. Police are working with the local authority and coroner to establish the circumstances surrounding Abiwon’s death.

Storm Boelo brought gusts of up to 84mph across parts of the UK over the weekend. A 60-year-old man was also killed by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, while others were injured.

World.title: FBI offers over N6m reward for information on wanted Nigerian woman
World.content:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced a $5,000 (approximately ₦6.7 million per exchange rate as of when this report was published) reward for information leading to the arrest of a Nigerian woman, Emuobosan Emanuella Hall, who is wanted in the United States for failing to report to prison to serve a 96-month sentence over money laundering and fraud offences.

Hall, who was born in Nigeria on October 10, 1980, was convicted of conspiracy to commit money laundering and conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud in connection with a romance scam involving multiple victims.

According to the FBI, Hall was charged in April 2024 over her alleged role in laundering funds obtained from victims through the romance scam.

She was arrested in Georgia and subsequently released on bond before pleading guilty to the charges.

Hall was sentenced in January 2026 to 96 months (eight years) in federal prison. However, she failed to report to the designated correctional facility in March 2026 to begin serving her sentence, prompting US authorities to issue an arrest warrant.

The FBI said a federal arrest warrant was issued on March 31, 2026, by the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana in New Orleans, following the bond violation charge.

She was subsequently charged through a criminal complaint on April 14, 2026, with failure to appear for service of a sentence and was indicted on the same charge on October 23, 2026.

The FBI said Hall also goes by the aliases Emuobosan E. Hall, Emuobosan Emanuella Erih and “Mobo”.

The agency disclosed that she has links to Warri and Oleh in Delta State, as well as Abuja, Nigeria. She also has reported ties to London, Gloucester and Croydon in England, and Atlanta, Georgia, in the United States.

According to her FBI wanted notice, Hall is 5 feet 6 inches tall, weighs approximately 87 kilogrammes, has black hair and brown eyes, and speaks English and some Yoruba.

The FBI is offering a reward of up to $5,000, equivalent to approximately ₦6.73 million, for information leading to her arrest, based on an exchange rate of about ₦1,346.22 to the dollar on October 30, 2026. CxRates+1

The agency has urged anyone with information about Hall’s whereabouts to contact its nearest FBI office or the American Embassy or Consulate.

World.title: ‘I was warned not to buy car or house’ — Nigerian Pastor recounts ritual wealth
World.content:
Pastor Joel Olasunkanmi, an Ogbomoso based cleric, has recounted how his pursuit of wealth through ritual practices allegedly led to a life changing car accident that resulted in the amputation of his leg.

Olasunkanmi shared his experience during an interview with BBC Yoruba, saying he turned to a ritualist while pursuing what he described as vain and worldly things.

According to the pastor, his involvement in the practice lasted about five years, during which he was instructed to find a young woman he deeply loved and carry out a ritual involving her.

“Thirty years ago, I took some steps that made God angry. It was while I was searching for vain and worldly things that I became disabled. I had a car accident on May 26, 2001,” he said.

Recounting the instructions given to him by the ritualist, Olasunkanmi alleged that he was asked to find a woman he loved, have sexual intercourse with her and use a white handkerchief to wipe her private parts before presenting it to the ritualist.

“The ritualist I sought told me to look for a young lady that I so much loved. I searched for her, had sex with her and used a white handkerchief to wipe her genitals. I took it to the man,” he recounted.

He said the ritual eventually brought him wealth, although he claimed he did not fully understand how it happened. However, he alleged that the ritualist placed restrictions on how he could spend the money.

“I did become rich. I did not know how it happened. But I did become rich. But I was told I could not buy a car or house from it,” he said.

The pastor further disclosed that the vehicle involved in the accident that eventually led to the amputation of his leg was indirectly connected to him because he had provided the money used to purchase it for another person.

“At the end of the day, the car that hit me was indirectly mine because I was the one who bought it for him. At the end of the day, my leg was amputated,” he said.

Reflecting on his experience, Olasunkanmi urged young Nigerians to exercise patience and avoid seeking quick wealth through questionable means.

“I implore the youths of today to be patient in everything they do,” he advised.

Vanguard News

World.title: APC Youth Stakeholders Back Dayo Israel, Warn Against Undermining His Office
World.content:
Folalumi Alaran in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) National Young Stakeholders Forum has passed a vote of confidence on the party’s National Youth Leader, Hon. Dayo Israel, warning against attempts to undermine his office or create parallel centres of influence within the party.

The forum also defended Israel’s facilitation of campaign mobilization vehicles for selected youth leaders, describing the initiative as part of efforts to improve the reward system within the party’s youth wing ahead of the 2027 general election.

The forum stated this in a press conference addressed by its National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Shehu Attah, at the Progressive Institute, Garki, Abuja, on Thursday.

It expressed concern over what it described as persistent attempts by some vested interests to weaken the party’s national youth structure for personal and other considerations.

The forum, comprising young stakeholders and founding members of the APC across the six geopolitical zones, said the party’s strength depended not only on electoral victories but also on respect for established institutions, internal democracy, fairness and the rule of law.

It commended Israel for establishing the APC Youth House and Nest Resource Centre, which it said had pioneered digital skills development, capacity building and vocational training, alongside town hall meetings and empowerment programmes.

The forum also highlighted the Renewed Hope Conversations initiative launched in tertiary institutions, describing it as a platform for bridging the gap between the Federal Government and young Nigerians by bringing students, policymakers and senior government officials together to discuss government policies and obtain feedback.

According to the forum, more than 100 party youths and some youth leaders across the country have benefited from overseas capacity-building and training programmes over the past two years.

It said the programmes were among efforts to address demands for an improved reward system within the party’s youth wing.

The forum further commended Israel for facilitating campaign mobilisation vehicles for selected youth leaders and distributing buses to others, saying the initiatives would encourage young party members to work for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election.

“This has sent a strong signal within the youth wing that the era of ‘monkey dey work, baboon dey chop’ is gone with the wind,” the statement said.

The forum warned that attempts to weaken the office of the National Youth Leader through factional manoeuvres or personal power struggles would be resisted.

It urged aggrieved party members to channel their complaints through appropriate party authorities rather than engage in actions capable of provoking tensions or deepening divisions.

The forum acknowledged that disagreements and competing interests were normal in a large political organisation such as the APC but maintained that such differences should be resolved through established procedures.

It called on APC youths nationwide to close ranks behind Israel and focus on mobilizing support for Tinubu’s re-election rather than engaging in internal disputes.

World.title: At Umrah, Tinubu Prays For Sustainable Peace, National Unity, Stability And Harmony In Nigeria
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Friday morning performed Umrah in the holy city of Makkah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, offering prayers of gratitude to Almighty Allah and seeking His continued guidance and protection for Nigeria.

During the spiritual exercise, the president circled the Holy Ka’abah at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram, in worship, devotion, and thanksgiving to Almighty Allah for His blessings on Nigeria and her people.

Fielding questions from newsmen shortly after the spiritual exercise, Tinubu said: “I believe this Umrah is very significant for the love of our people, commitment to the job and our country, Nigeria; commitment to the will of Allah that His words must prevail, and that there’s no other God but Him and He’s the only one that makes a human being what he can be and what he would be in life.”

He prayed for sustainable peace, national unity, harmony and stability in Nigeria, asking Almighty Allah to guide the country’s leaders with wisdom, strengthen the bonds of brotherhood among Nigerians, and grant the nation lasting relief from insecurity and other challenges.

“I am grateful to Allah for being able to perform this Umrah. We have just prayed for our nation, for everyone to live in peace and harmony, happiness and faith in God Almighty,” the president said.

He expressed hope that Nigeria would continue to make progress towards economic prosperity, social development, and a more secure future for all its citizens.

Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to building a peaceful, united, and prosperous nation where every Nigerian, regardless of faith or background, can live in safety, dignity and harmony.

The president also called for sustained commitment and collective efforts towards nation-building, emphasising the need for Nigerians to harness the country’s diversity as a source of strength in advancing national development, peace and security.

He stressed the importance of drawing on the nation’s collective strengths and shared aspirations to build a more secure and prosperous country.

“Our strength is our diversity, and we continue to build on that for the prospect and security of the country,” the president stated.

Tinubu also reflected on the spiritual significance of the pilgrimage, saying: “And we are giving it to our minds and our spirits in every way possible.”

On the president’s entourage during the Umrah were top government officials including Governors of Niger, Mohammed Umaru Bago; Bauchi, Bala Mohammed; Katsina, Dikko Umaru Radda; and Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Atiku Bagudu, among others.

Tinubu had arrived Saudi Arabia Thursday night via the King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah, where he was received by Nigeria’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi Arabia’s Head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir.

His visit to Makkah is devoted to performing the religious rites associated with Umrah and offering prayers for Nigeria’s peace, unity, stability and continued progress.

President Tinubu is expected to return to Nigeria next week following the completion of the spiritual exercise.

World.title: 2027: Adeleke Inuagurates Campaign Committee for Sen. Oyewumi’s Re-election
World.content:
Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has inaugurated the campaign committee for the re-election of the Osun West Senatorial District lawmaker, Senator Lere Oyewumi.

The governor, represented by his deputy, Prince Kola Adewusi, described Oyewumi, who is the Deputy Minority Leader of the Senate, as a responsible lawmaker who has made the administration and the state proud through quality representation.

He charged members of the newly inaugurated committee to work with total loyalty and commitment to secure victory for the party.

The governor said, “Senator Oyewumi is a responsible person and we are proud of what he is doing in Osun West. We are calling on our people to re-elect him come January 16, 2027.

“I want to appeal to the members of the campaign committee to work hard and ensure the victory of Senator Lere Oyewumi. There is nothing like 99.9 percent loyalty. Your loyalty should be 100 percent.”

In his acceptance remarks, Senator Oyewumi thanked Governor Adeleke for his leadership, which he said has made campaigning easy for Accord candidates.

The lawmaker said, “Adeleke is a pathfinder, and his re-election has shown that Osun people love him, and that love will translate to victory for all Accord Party candidates in the general election.

“In my three and a half years in the red chamber, I have learned a lot. What I thought was not possible has been proven to me to be possible. So I am more prepared, more equipped and more determined to give my best to every community in Osun West Senatorial District.”

Oyewumi also promised to consolidate on his achievements, stating, “For the people of Osun West, more development is coming – better roads, improved schools and hospitals, clean water, and solar streetlights that will light up every corner of the district.

“When I contested in 2023, I didn’t have money to give anybody, both in my primary and general elections, yet they voted for me overwhelmingly. That is one encouragement that is pushing me to ensure I do not disappoint them.

“Our students will get more empowerment. We will not forget our artisans, market women, farmers and the elderly.”

Earlier, the Director General of the campaign committee, Adesoye Oyetunde, said the senator has not disappointed his constituents.

He said, “Oyewumi has not disappointed us. Out of the 10 local governments we have in this senatorial district, the Senator tarred roads in eight of them. In the remaining two, he has already flagged off construction.

“There is no local government in Osun West where Oyewumi has not built classrooms. In terms of healthcare, farm inputs and other interventions, the Senator has done a lot for his people, and I know he will do more.”

World.title: Enugu LG Chairmen Pledge Support for Mbah’s Devt Agenda
World.content:
The 17 Local Government Area chairmen in Enugu State have pledged their support for Governor Peter Mbah’s development agenda, describing his administration’s achievements in education, healthcare, infrastructure and economic growth as significant milestones.

The Chairman of Igboeze South Local Government Area, Honourable Ugo Ferdinand Ukwueze, stated this while reacting to the governor’s presentation of his administration’s mid-term performance update on its manifesto and social contract with the people.

Ukwueze said the achievements demonstrated the administration’s commitment to transforming Enugu State through innovation, strategic investments and improved service delivery.

He identified the construction of 268 Smart Green Schools and 260 Type Two Primary Healthcare Centres across the state’s wards as major interventions aimed at strengthening education and healthcare delivery.

The council chairman also commended the recruitment of 2,250 health personnel to improve access to medical services and support round-the-clock operations at primary healthcare facilities.

He noted that the establishment of advanced diagnostic services, including MRI, CT scans and mammography, would help reduce medical tourism and position Enugu as a destination for specialised healthcare.

On economic development, Ukwueze cited the revitalisation of United Palm Products Limited, the return of Sunrise Flour Mills to full operation through a public-private partnership, and investments in aviation, agriculture, energy and animal husbandry as initiatives expected to create jobs and boost the state’s economy.

He also highlighted ongoing tourism projects, including the development of the Nsude Pyramid, Ovu Lake Resort, Akpofu lakeside development and Akwuke Beach Resort, saying the initiatives would strengthen the state’s tourism potential and attract investments.

On the development of the state’s coal resources, the chairman said the proposed energy projects could open new opportunities for industrial growth.

Addressing concerns over taxation, Ukwueze urged residents to disregard what he described as misleading narratives about the introduction of new taxes.

He explained that the government was harmonising statutory charges and implementing reforms to address multiple taxation.

According to him, the state government has pledged to publish the harmonised charges for public scrutiny, while small businesses would benefit from measures designed to simplify tax administration.

The chairman also pointed to the reported increase in the state’s internally generated revenue from N25 billion to N400 billion, describing it as evidence of improved revenue mobilisation.

He called on residents to sustain their support for the governor’s development programmes, stressing that the success of the administration’s agenda required collective responsibility.

Speaking on behalf of his colleagues, Ukwueze said the 17 council chairmen had adopted the governor’s manifesto as a shared social contract, with measurable performance indicators to guide implementation at the grassroots.

He added that local government councils, in line with their constitutional responsibilities, would work with the state government to deepen development, improve service delivery and strengthen Enugu’s position as an investment destination.

The event was attended by political leaders, religious and traditional institutions, private-sector representatives and other stakeholders, who also expressed support for Mbah’s administration.

World.title: Tinubu Writes Senate, Seeks Confirmation Of Six Executive Directors For NMDPRA
World.content:
* Okays appointment of Jumoke Gafar as board secretary/legal adviser



Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has nominated six executive directors for the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA).

Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, in a release issued on Friday, disclosed that the president has forwarded a letter to the Senate for the confirmation of the six executive director-nominees.

Three nominees are being reappointed, while three are new and once the Senate approves them, all nominees will serve a five-year term.

The renominated executive directors are Mr Abiodun Adeniji, Executive Director, Finance and Accounts; Mr Ogbugo Kalu Ukoha, Executive Director, Distribution Systems, Storage and Retailing Infrastructure; and Dr Mustapha Lamorde, Executive Director, Health, Safety, Environment and Community.

The new executive directors are: Mr Mobolaji Tajudeen Musa, Executive Director, Hydrocarbon Processing Plants, Installations and Transportation Infrastructure; Ms Ogechukwu Modie, Executive Director, Economic Regulations and Strategic Planning; and Mr Said Abutalib, Executive Director, Corporate Services and Administration.

The president urged the Senate to consider the nominations expeditiously to ensure institutional continuity and strengthen the Authority’s oversight capacity.

Tinubu also approved the appointment of Mrs Jumoke Gafar as Secretary to the Board/Authority and Legal Adviser, subject to completing the statutory processes under Section 46 of the PIA.

In April, the president had appointed Rabiu Abdullahi Umar as the agency’s chief executive.

World.title: Can Roads Alone Constitute Development in Benue?
World.content:
Simon Shenge

There is hardly any doubt that roads are important to the development of any society. Good roads connect communities, facilitate the movement of people and goods, reduce transportation costs and open up opportunities for trade and investment. For a state like Benue, where agriculture remains central to the livelihood of a large proportion of the population, functional roads are particularly important.

But rural development is much more than roads.

This is the point that deserves the attention of the Benue State Government as it implements its development agenda and allocates public resources. If the state’s development budget is increasingly dominated by road construction at the expense of other essential sectors, there is a need for a careful reassessment of priorities.

A road is a means to development; it is not development in its entirety.

The real test of rural development is whether the farmer can produce and earn a decent income, whether the child can attend a functioning school, whether a pregnant woman and sick people can access a properly equipped health facility, whether communities have access to clean water, and whether young people can find opportunities that give them hope for the future.

Benue people cannot eat roads. They cannot be treated for illness by roads. They cannot drink water from roads. Their children cannot receive quality education from roads. These are not arguments against road construction. On the contrary, they are arguments for a more balanced approach to development.

The danger of a one-sector development strategy

There is growing concern among citizens and stakeholders that road construction has received disproportionate attention in the government’s current development priorities, while other sectors that directly affect the daily lives of rural people appear to have received less attention. If this perception is correct, it deserves urgent consideration.

Rural development must be integrated. Roads should connect farms to markets, but there must first be productive farmers, functioning agricultural extension services, access to inputs, storage facilities, processing opportunities and markets. A newly constructed road leading from a farming community to an urban centre is of limited developmental value if farmers still struggle with insecurity, poor access to agricultural inputs, inadequate storage and low farm- gate prices.

Similarly, a road leading to a health centre cannot replace the doctors, nurses, medicines, laboratory facilities, electricity, water supply and diagnostic equipment required to make that health centre functional. Benue’s hospitals are sick, they have been sick for years and unlike buildings, constructions of roads, human life cannot be rehabilitated after they are lost.

The same principle applies to education. A road can take a child to school, but it cannot teach that child. Rural schools require classrooms, teachers, learning materials, electricity, sanitation and other basic facilities.

Development, therefore, should not be measured simply by the number of kilometres of roads awarded or constructed. It should be measured by the quality of life that public investment creates for ordinary citizens.

What happens to the rural farmer?

This question is particularly important in Benue.

The state is widely regarded as an agricultural hub, yet many farmers continue to face challenges that go beyond access roads. They need improved seeds, fertilisers and other inputs; access to affordable credit; extension services; irrigation where appropriate; mechanisation; storage and processing facilities; security; and reliable markets.

A farmer who produces more than his family can consume should not be forced to sell his produce cheaply because of inadequate storage or lack of access to profitable markets.

The ultimate objective should be to move the farmer from subsistence to sustainable commercial agriculture. This requires investment across the entire agricultural value chain.

Indeed, a well- designed rural development strategy should make roads serve agriculture—not replace agricultural investment.

Healthcare cannot be left behind

The situation of rural healthcare also deserves very serious attention. Across many communities, the mere existence of a primary health facility does not necessarily mean that quality healthcare is available. A health centre may have a building but lack essential and functional equipment, anesthesia and sterilization, medicines, personnel, electricity, water or functional diagnostic facilities.

For a rural mother, the difference between a functioning health centre and an empty building and outdated equipment can be the difference between life and death. Therefore, while roads may improve access to healthcare facilities, government must equally ensure that those facilities are properly equipped and staffed. There is little comfort in having a good road to a health facility that cannot provide the services a patient needs.

Education is an investment in Benue’s future

Education must also remain at the centre of the state’s development agenda. Every rural child deserves access to quality education regardless of the local government area in which he or she lives. Government investment should therefore extend beyond the construction or rehabilitation of roads to classrooms, teachers, instructional materials, digital learning opportunities, water and sanitation facilities, and other conditions necessary for effective learning.

The long- term prosperity of Benue will NOT be determined only by the roads we construct today. It will also be determined by the quality of the human beings who will inherit and manage the state tomorrow. A road has a useful lifespan. An educated healthy child can contribute to society for generations.

Water is not a luxury

Access to clean and safe water remains another fundamental component of rural development. Communities need water for drinking, sanitation, agriculture, health and other domestic purposes. When government investment focuses heavily on physical infrastructure while basic water needs remain unmet in communities, the definition of development becomes incomplete.

A truly rural development-oriented budget should therefore ask a simple question: What does the ordinary rural household receive from government investment? If the answer is primarily a road, then the question must be asked: what about the school, the health centre, the water supply, the farm, the market and the livelihood?

Roads must be completed too

There is also another important dimension to the conversation.

Even the argument for prioritising roads becomes difficult to sustain if major road projects remain incomplete for extended periods. Government should therefore not only announce new road projects but also ensure that existing projects are not only completed but with high standard and brought into actual use.

The people should be able to see and use the benefits of public expenditure.

It is understandable that infrastructure projects require substantial resources, particularly in an economy facing inflation, rising construction costs and competing demands. This makes prioritisation even more important. Scarce public resources should be deployed in a manner that produces the widest possible social benefit.

A plea for balance, not confrontation

The administration should be encouraged to continue investing in roads where they are genuinely necessary, particularly those connecting rural communities to farms, markets, schools, hospitals and economic centres. But road infrastructure should form part of a broader development framework rather than become the framework itself.

The state needs a development strategy in which roads connect communities, agriculture creates wealth, schools build human capital, hospitals protect lives, water sustains communities, and industries create employment. That is what integrated rural development should look like.

The governor’s legacy should be broader

Every administration ultimately leaves behind a legacy. For the present administration, that legacy should ideally be measured not only in kilometres of roads constructed but in the transformation of the lives of Benue citizens. Years from now, citizens should be able to say that during this period, their communities received functioning schools, better healthcare, improved agricultural productivity, potable water, employment opportunities, security and infrastructure.

They should remember roads, certainly—but they should remember what those roads enabled. A road that takes farm produce to market is valuable. A road that takes a sick person to a functioning hospital is valuable. A road that connects a child to a good school is valuable. But the road itself is only part of the story. The ultimate purpose of government is not to build infrastructure for its own sake, but to use public resources to improve human lives.

Benue therefore needs a development budget that does not ask whether roads should be built or whether schools, hospitals, agriculture and water should be funded. It should ask how all these sectors can work together to produce sustainable development. This is not a call to abandon roads. It is a call to build roads without abandoning the people who use them.

It is a call to ensure that while the government builds the physical infrastructure of Benue, it also builds the human capacity, economic opportunities and social services that will make those roads meaningful. And ultimately, it is a call to the government of the day: please do not let the understandable urgency of road construction swallow the equally urgent needs of education, healthcare, agriculture, water, employment and other sectors that determine the everyday welfare of our people.

Benue deserves roads. But Benue also deserves a complete

development agenda.

* Shenge, a public affairs analyst, writes from Abuja

World.title: VFD Group’s Nine-Month Profit After Tax Jumps 96% to N13bn As Earnings Strengthen
World.content:
VFD Group Plc has reported a 96 per cent year-on-year increase in profit after tax to N13.00 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up from N6.63 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

The Group’s unaudited financial results, approved by its Board of Directors, also showed that profit before tax rose 92 per cent to N15.34 billion from N7.99 billion, while gross earnings increased 35 per cent to N81.88 billion from N60.72 billion.

The strong earnings performance reflects growth in the Group’s investment activities, improved operating efficiency and the continued expansion of its financial asset portfolio.

Earnings per share nearly doubled to 75 kobo from 38 kobo, while profit attributable to shareholders increased 97 per cent to N9.52 billion, highlighting the improvement in earnings available to the Group’s owners.

Investment Income Drives Earnings Growth

A breakdown of the results shows that net investment income, the Group’s largest revenue contributor, rose 59 per cent to N72.18 billion from N45.45 billion a year earlier. Net revenue increased 42 per cent to N77.52 billion, while operating profit advanced 47 per cent to N58.53 billion.

The Group also recorded improvements in operating efficiency, with its cost-to-income ratio declining to 24.5 per cent from 26.9 per cent. Impairment charges fell 44 per cent to N1.29 billion, supporting the growth in operating profit.

However, finance costs increased 36 per cent to N43.33 billion, reflecting the cost of funding the Group’s expanding investment portfolio. Despite the higher funding costs, profit before tax nearly doubled, demonstrating the strength of earnings growth during the period.

Total assets rose 30 per cent to N577.64 billion as at September 30, 2026, from N445.81 billion at the end of December 2025. Investment in financial assets more than doubled to N217.08 billion, while funds under management increased 84 per cent to N142.52 billion.

Shareholders’ funds also grew 87 per cent to N130.02 billion, reflecting a stronger capital position as the Group continued to expand its investment activities.

Parent Company Profit Rises to N6.18 billion

At the parent company level, VFD Group Plc recorded a significant improvement in profitability, with profit after tax rising to N6.18 billion from N300 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

Gross earnings increased 84 per cent to N36.52 billion, while net investment income rose 123 per cent to N32.53 billion. Profit before tax climbed to N7.23 billion from N350 million, and earnings per share increased to 49 kobo from two kobo.

The company’s shareholders’ funds rose 131 per cent to N94.30 billion, while borrowings declined 14 per cent to N108.02 billion. Its borrowings-to-equity ratio consequently fell to 1.1 times from 3.1 times at the beginning of the year.

The improvement at both Group and parent company levels points to stronger earnings, although the sustainability of the performance will depend on investment returns, funding costs and the Group’s ability to deploy capital profitably.

N50.67bn Rights Issue Supports Expansion Strategy

The results come as VFD Group continues to deploy the proceeds of its N50.67 billion rights issue, raised to strengthen its capital base and support its growth strategy.

During the third quarter, the Group also raised N22.75 billion through an A1-rated commercial paper issuance, providing additional funding for its investment activities.

In another strategic development, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved Anchoria Capital Group as a capital market holding company, supporting the Group’s efforts to consolidate and expand its capital market operations.

Commenting on the results, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of VFD Group Plc, Nonso Okpala, said the near-doubling of profit after tax reflected stronger performance from the Group’s core investment activities, alongside efforts to strengthen its financial position and build a more sustainable business.

He said: “Our profit after tax has almost doubled, reflecting stronger performance from our core investment activities. Beyond the numbers, we have continued to strengthen the Group’s financial position, deploy the capital raised and build the leadership structure required to sustain our performance.

“The appointment of Mrs. Emezie-Ezigbo as our first Deputy Managing Director is an important milestone. It reinforces our commitment to building an institution with the leadership depth, governance and capacity to deliver sustainable value over the long term.”

VFD Group Appoints First Deputy Managing Director

In a move to strengthen executive leadership and succession planning, VFD Group appointed Mrs. Ijeoma Emezie-Ezigbo as Deputy Managing Director, effective October 5, 2026. She is the first person to occupy the position since the Group’s establishment.

Emezie-Ezigbo brings more than two decades of experience in corporate finance, mergers and acquisitions, transaction advisory and business valuation across West Africa and Canada.

Before her appointment, she served as Partner and Head of Transaction Services, West Africa, at KPMG Nigeria. She is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria and an Associate of Chartered Professional Accountants of Ontario, Canada.

Her appointment forms part of the Group’s broader effort to strengthen governance, deepen its executive leadership and establish a structured succession framework across its businesses.

Focus Shifts to Sustainable Growth

Looking ahead, Executive Director, Finance, VFD Group Plc, Folajimi Adeleye, said the Group would focus on disciplined capital deployment, funding efficiency, leadership succession and the expansion of its capital markets business.

He noted that the rights issue had strengthened the parent company’s capital position, with shareholders’ funds increasing significantly and borrowings declining.

“As we enter the final quarter of the year, our priorities remain clear: deploy capital responsibly across our investment businesses, improve funding efficiency, strengthen leadership succession and continue expanding our capital markets operations through Anchoria Capital Group,” Adeleye said.

World.title: Navy Inaugurates Maternity Ward to Boost Healthcare, Civil-Military Relations
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

In a significant demonstration of its commitment to community development and civil-military cooperation, the Nigerian Navy has inaugurated a newly constructed maternity ward and healthcare facility at the Primary Health Care Centre in Abwor-Dyis, Lankan District of Mupun Chiefdom, Pankshin Local Government Area of Plateau State under the Chief of the Naval Staff Special Intervention Quick Impact Project (CNS-QIP).

The Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, who was represented at the ceremony by the Chief of Administration, Naval Headquarters, Rear Admiral Jonathan Mamman, said the project reflects the Navy’s commitment to strengthening civil-military cooperation and supporting community development.

Mamman noted that the facility, which comprises male and female wards, a maternity section, a nurses’ station and a labour room, is aimed at improving access to quality healthcare, particularly for expectant mothers and newborns in the community.

He commended the Chief of Naval Engineering, Rear Admiral Nanmanle Damtong, for identifying the community’s healthcare needs and facilitating the project under the CNS-Q of the facility and ensure its proper maintenance.

Speaking at the inauguration, Rear Admiral Damtong said the project was executed in response to a request by the community, which identified maternal healthcare as its most pressing need.

He explained that the intervention was carried out after consultations with community leaders and approval from the local government.

In his goodwill message, National President of the Mupun Cultural Development Association Worldwide, Haruna Wale, lauded the Nigerian Navy and the CNS for the initiative, describing it as a vital contribution to healthcare delivery in the area.

He said the project would improve maternal and newborn care services while further strengthening the relationship between the Nigerian Navy and the Mupun people.

The project is one of several community-focused interventions being implemented nationwide by the Nigerian Navy under the leadership of Vice Admiral Abbas to promote national development, social cohesion and stronger ties between the military and local communities.

World.title: South African wine shines at The Savoy’s new Beaufort Wine Bar
World.content:
The Savoy's Beaufort Bar has been reborn as the Beaufort Wine Bar, with more than 170 wines by the glass. On opening night, South African wine stood proudly alongside the great names of France. Image: The Savoy's Beaufort Bar

Romain Audrerie greeted us with a Montrachet surprise, quickly followed by a welcome glass of English sparkling rosé.

The famous Beaufort Bar, built on the hotel’s old cabaret stage, has turned its focus from cocktails to wine.

For a South African in London, the best part was simple. Our wines are on the list, and they hold their own.



The jet-black and gold Art Deco room still feels like a night at the theatre. What has changed is what is in your glass.

The full list runs to more than 250 wines from 18 countries, with vintages from 1975 to 2025. Coravin technology lets the team pour rare bottles without pulling the cork. It means you can explore serious wines one glass at a time.

Romain is head sommelier and manager of the Beaufort Wine Bar. He brings more than 15 years in international hospitality.



He was part of the opening team at Chiltern Firehouse and later global wine director for André Balazs Properties. We were spoilt from start to finish.

South African wine on the Beaufort Wine Bar list

My wine collection includes every vintage of Vin de Constance ever made, so I let that one pass.

Instead, Romain poured the 1996 Château d’Yquem, a rare treat by the glass. Thirty years on, it was rich and golden, with caramel, honey and dried apricot.



It is a very different style to Vin de Constance, which is made from Muscat and feels fresher and more floral. Seeing Cape wine on the list at The Savoy, among the most famous labels in the world, was a proud moment.

RELATED | A moment captured: Tasting history at Klein Constantia

For the rest of the evening, I stuck to my go-to favourites, a selection of great French reds. That is no slight on the Cape. South Africa and France have shared a glass for centuries, from the Huguenots who settled in Franschhoek to the Bordeaux names now invested in the Cape.



“South Africa is one of the most exciting wine countries in the world right now,” says Romain.

“You have more than three centuries of history in Constantia and a new generation pushing boundaries in the Swartland. I wanted our guests to discover that. A great South African wine can sit next to a great Bordeaux and hold its own.”

The South African wines on the Beaufort Wine Bar menu

Romain’s list has nine South African wines, and four are poured by the glass.



It is a smart selection. New-wave names from the Swartland sit alongside top estates and the Cape’s most famous sweet wine.

There is a bonus South African link too. The Ice Cyder on the sweet list comes from The Newt in Somerset, the English sister estate of Babylonstoren, owned by South Africans Koos Bekker and Karen Roos.

For South Africans, Vin de Constance carries real pride. It revives the sweet wine of Constantia, which Napoleon loved and Jane Austen mentioned in Sense and Sensibility. Seeing it on a list at The Savoy feels like a homecoming of sorts. It is back at the great tables of Europe, where it always belonged.



Klein Constantia’s Matt Day on the Beaufort Wine Bar

Matt Day has been winemaker at Klein Constantia since 2012. He is only the third winemaker since the estate was revived in the 1980s. Klein Constantia also has strong French ties. Bordeaux figures Hubert de Boüard of Château Angélus and Bruno Prats are among its shareholders.

“We are always proud to be on the wine list at The Savoy,” says Matt.

“It is one of the great hotels of the world, and the Beaufort has always been a special room. It was a privilege to visit the room with Nicolas Schell in June as they prepared for launch. South African wine belongs alongside the classics of France. We are delighted to support The Savoy, and Romain and the team at the Beaufort.”



READ | Why is Klein Constantia Africa’s top vineyard? Here’s what the world just decided

Is the Beaufort Wine Bar worth a visit?

Yes, especially for a special occasion. Prices reflect The Savoy address, but the huge by-the-glass list means you can explore without committing to a bottle. There is food too. Charcuterie and Jamón Ibérico are carved tableside from a custom flywheel slicer trolley, and there is a caviar selection.

For South Africans in London, it is a chance to raise a glass of home in one of the city’s grandest rooms. Ask Romain and his team what is pouring from the Cape. Four South African wines are poured by the glass.



Beaufort Wine Bar, The Savoy, Strand, London WC2R 0EZ.

A big thank you to my son Tanguy, who works at The Savoy, for inviting my wife and me. It made the night extra special, and a lot kinder on the wallet.

World.title: AmaZulu join Orlando Pirates as they partner with Amstel
World.content:
AmaZulu have officially announced that they have partnered with Amstel although the length of the deal is undisclosed.

The Amstel logo will feature on the sleeves of AmaZulu shirts starting from this weekend when they take on Golden Arrows.

AmaZulu President Sandile Zungu said this partnership is not only built on visibility but values and trust between the parties.



Usuthu have just become the second PSL team to partner with Amstel after Orlando Pirates in August 2025.

Amazulu partner with Amstel

“Today is an important moment for the club. We’re welcoming a new partner, but we are also reflecting on what AmaZulu Football Club stands for and where we want to go next,” said Zungu.

“The standing that Amstel and Amazulu Football Club enjoy today has been earned over time. Both understand that respect tells gold.

“This gives us a strong foundation for a partnership that can grow with meaning rather than simply visibility. It is not just about visibility. The strongest partnerships do not ask either side to become something else.”

“They build on values both already recognised. This partnership creates an opportunity to add value where it matters the most – around the team, our supporters and the wider Amazulu community,” added Zungu.

World.title: Cape Town Zombie Walk: Will the weather be a trick or a treat?
World.content:
Halloween revellers prepare for Cape Town’s annual Zombie Walk on Saturday, with mild weather expected. Image: Unsplash

Zombies, ghosts and other spooky characters will take over the streets of Cape Town on Saturday, 31 October, as the city celebrates Halloween with its annual Zombie Walk.

The latest forecast points to a pleasant afternoon, with sunny breaks, some cloud and little chance of rain during the walk.

Weather forecast for cape town’s Zombie Walk

Cape Town can expect a maximum temperature of between 22°C and 24°C on Saturday.



Conditions will become cooler towards the evening.

The forecast shows a mixture of sunshine and cloud during the afternoon.

By 18:00, temperatures could drop to around 20°C before falling further to approximately 19°C by 19:00.

Rain appears unlikely during the procession, with the hourly forecast showing virtually no chance of precipitation between 16:00 and 18:00.

Will the weather affect Halloween costumes?

The mild afternoon temperatures should make walking outdoors relatively comfortable, particularly for those wearing elaborate Halloween costumes.

Comfortable shoes and drinking water will also come in handy for anyone planning to walk through the city centre.



When and where will the Zombie Walk take place?

The annual event takes place on Saturday, 31 October, at the Company’s Garden area along Government Avenue in Cape Town.

According to the organisers, participants can begin gathering from 16:30, with a welcome and safety briefing scheduled for 17:00.

The procession is expected to get underway at approximately 17:20 and continue until around 18:00.

The free event welcomes people of all ages, including families and their pets.

The weather looks favourable for Saturday’s walk. Participants should prepare for changing temperatures as the afternoon turns into evening.

World.title: Sipho Chaine cementing his legendary status at Orlando Pirates
World.content:
Orlando Pirates goalkeeper Sipho Chaine is slowly but surely cementing his legendary status at the club.

Chaine joined the Sea Robbers as an underrated goalkeeper from Chippa United in September 2022.

At the time, Pirates had Richard Ofori as their No.1 with Siyabonga Mpontshane as the club’s second choice goalkeeper.



However, he worked his way up, and since making his debut in 2022, Chaine never looked back as he became the club’s No.1.

He has won a whopping eight trophies with Pirates – five under Jose Riveiro and three under Abdeslam Ouaddou.

Now, Chaine has joined some of the Pirates goalkeeping legends with his trend of keeping cleansheets for fun.

According to OptaJabu, Chaine is now sitting on 27 cleansheets since the start of 2026; the most by any of the previous Pirates goalkeepers in the PSL era.

His 27th cleansheet across all competitions came in Pirates’ 3-0 win over Milford FC the Carling Knockout Cup on Tuesday.

Chaine is the first Pirates goalkeeper to achieve this feat, and he has already surpassed the legendary Williams Okpara who recorded 25 cleansheets in 1999.



In 2025, Chaine came short of breaking Okpara’s then record as finished that year with 24 cleansheets.

The first time Chaine actually overtook the former Nigeria international (16) with 17 cleansheets was in 2024.

Overall, Okpara was impressive in three consecutive years for Pirates – 1997 (19), 1998 (16) and 1999 (25).

Furthermore, Moeneeb Josephs also left a huge mark with 20 cleansheets in all competitions for the Sea Robbers in 2009.

The late Senzo Meyiwa recorded 18 cleansheets for Pirates in 2013.

SIPHO CHAINE HAS MOST CLEANSHEETS BY AN ORLANDO PIRATES GOALKEEPER

World.title: ‘Premium’ upgrade for Durban’s long-haul travellers from King Shaka Airport
World.content:
Durban’s long-haul travellers will soon have a new premium cabin option, with Emirates introducing its Premium Economy cabin on daily flights from King Shaka International Airport.

From 1 March 2027, Emirates will deploy its Airbus A350 on its daily Durban-Dubai service, bringing Premium Economy to its third South African gateway after Cape Town and Johannesburg.

The move means all three of Emirates’ South African gateways will offer the premium cabin.



What is changing for Durban passengers?

The new aircraft will introduce Premium Economy on the Durban route, giving passengers an option between Economy and Business Class.

The Premium Economy cabin has a 2-4-2 seating configuration, with cream leather seats offering additional legroom and recline compared with Economy Class.

Passengers will also have access to:

In-seat charging points

A wood-finished side cocktail table

A 13.3-inch personal entertainment screen

A 35kg check-in baggage allowance

Up to 10kg of carry-on baggage

Dedicated check-in

Priority boarding at King Shaka International Airport

Popular international connections from Durban

Emirates said a significant proportion of travel to and from Durban involves people visiting friends and family internationally.



Passengers travelling through Dubai can connect to destinations including Thailand, Indonesia, India, France and the UK.

Premium Economy was introduced on Emirates’ Cape Town and Johannesburg routes in September 2025.

According to the airline, the cabin has maintained a healthy load factor on both inbound and outbound services over the past year, with demand coming from both leisure and corporate travellers.

World.title: Dakar Rally finds a safer new home – in Portugal
World.content:
South Africa's driver Henk Lategan and co driver Brett Cummings ride during the prologue of the 47th Dakar Rally, in Bisha, Saudi Arabia, on January 3, 2025. Image: Valery HACHE / AFP

Portugal and Morocco will host the 2027 Dakar Rally the organisers announced on Friday after it was moved from Saudi Arabia following repeated attacks on the kingdom by Yemen’s Houthis.

The Dakar Rally is moving to Portugal and Morocco for the 2027 edition. Image: Giuseppe CACACE / AFP

The drivers, motorcyclists and truck drivers will tackle the prologue and first special stage in Portugal followed by 11 stages of the gruelling rally – covering almost 8 000km with 4 341km of specials – in Morocco.

It is the first time since 2007 that the rally, created in 1978, returns to Africa.



READ | Lewis Hamilton questions Rwanda as venue for African Grand Prix

Endurance rally

“Although it has been moved, the 49th edition of the Dakar will still meet the sporting standards which has always made the event the most demanding of endurance rallies,” said race director David Castera.

“Despite the short amount of time we have had we have put together a real Dakar.



“The competitors will discover the kingdom (Morocco) from one end to the other.

“We are going to explore all its unique features on a route whose size we haven’t seen before.”

The race, formerly called the Paris-Dakar, used to be follow a route from the French capital to the Senegalese capital Dakar.



But security threats along its route in North Africa meant that from 2009 it was held in South America, and from 2020 in Saudi Arabia.

Back to Saudi Arabia in 2028

Organisers said they intend to bring the rally back to Saudi Arabia in 2028 to celebrate its 50th edition.

The moving of the Dakar Rally is just the latest sporting event in the region to be affected by conflict in the Middle East.



An exhibition tennis tournament due to feature Novak Djokovic, Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev has been postponed until late December.

The WTA Finals were also scheduled to be held in Riyadh next month but will instead take place at Indian Wells in the US.

This season’s Formula One grand prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia.



The final round of the World Rally Championship in Saudi Arabia next month has also been scrapped.

The last two races of the F1 season in Qatar (November 29) and Abu Dhabi (December 6) are still on the calendar, as is the Qatar MotoGP next month, but they are the subject of intense internal debate.

However, the mouth-watering WBC super-middleweight title bout between champion Christian Mbilli and Mexican legend Saul ‘Canelo’ Alvarez is going ahead in Riyadh on Saturday.



Strikes

Dakar Rally organisers had hoped to keep the 2027 race in Saudi Arabia by working on a new route in the northern part of the country.

But the latest strikes, including one targeting Riyadh airport this month, which killed 13 people and injured hundreds more, have rendered that impossible.

In recent weeks, Houthi attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure have reached a scale unprecedented since the start of the conflict in Yemen in 2014.



By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Orlando Pirates have 10, how many Kaizer Chiefs players have scored this season?
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have had 10 different goalscorers in the Betway Premiership. Kaizer Chiefs also have their own list of players in goalscoring contributions tally this term.

The two sides meet on Saturday in the highly anticipated Soweto Derby. Kick-off is set for 15:30 at the FNB Stadium.

KAIZER CHIEFS HAVE EIGHT DIFFERENT LEAGUE GOALSCORERS

Coach Fernando Da Cruz’s side have enjoyed goals from eight different players in the Betway Premiership this season.



Unsurprisingly, Wandile Duba tops the chart with three goals. ““I am very happy for Duba; he is a young player who sometimes has a lot of ups and downs, so he must improve his consistency,” coach Da Cruz told SABC.

“He is a young player who is very good, and he is able to drop back and make deep runs. He is very good in front of the goal, but he must continue to work hard and listen to the coaches, and maybe if he does this, he can become a player for Bafana Bafana,” the Frenchman added.

Hot on Duba’s heels are Mduduzi Shabalala and Lebohang Maboe with two strikes each.



Full list:

Wandile Duba (Striker): 3 goals

3 goals Mduduzi Shabalala (Forward): 2 goals

2 goals Lebohang Maboe (Central midfielder): 2 goals

2 goals Siphesihle Ndlovu (Central midfielder): 1 goal

1 goal Mfundo Vilakazi (Forward): 1 goal

1 goal Langelihle Phili (Winger): 1 goal

1 goal Flavio Da Silva (Striker): 1 goal

There’s some clarity to note on Faiz Abrahams. His spectacular free-kick against Siwelele FC was subsequently credited as an own goal against Samukelo Xulu. The ball struck the post before rebounding into the net off Xulu’s head.

As a result, Abrahams does not feature among Kaizer Chiefs’ eight league goalscorers.



ORLANDO PIRATES MUST WATCH MORE THAN ONE PLAYER

For the Buccaneers, the challenge will be containing an Amakhosi attack that has received contributions from different areas of the pitch.

Duba, Shabalala and Maboe are among the players who can trouble the opposition, while the likes of Vilakazi and Baartman provide additional attacking options.

The Buccaneers will be aware that derbies are rarely decided by statistics alone. However, keeping Amakhosi’s attacking players quiet will be an important part of their preparations.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs hat-trick heroes in the PSL era
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs attacker Wandile Duba netted a hat-trick to help his team beat TS Galaxy 3-0 in the Carling Knockout Cup on Tuesday.

As a result, Duba joined a growing list of Amakhosi players to have scored a hat-trick in the PSL era.

On the night, Duba netted his treble in the second half after what appeared to be a very difficult first half for the Glamour Boys.



Now, 22-year-old engraved his name on the history books of the club, joining the likes of Pollen Ndlanya and the late John ‘Shoes’ Moshoeu among many others.

Ndlanya netted four hat-tricks during his time with Chiefs, and overall, he netted six in the PSL era.

Current Sporting Director Kaizer Motaung Jr netted two hat-tricks for the club, and they were against Maritzburg United and Bloemfontein Celtic.



Before Tuesday’s match, the last player to have scored a hat-trick for Amakhosi was Caleb Bimenyimana who scored his treble from the penalty spot against Stellenbosch FC in 2022.

Furthermore, retired Bafana Bafana strikers Mark Williams and Lehlohonolo Majoro scored four goals each in a single match for Chiefs.

It is also worth mentioning that legendary Marks Maponyane also scored a hat-trick in knockout match against Durban City in 1988.



According to Chiefs, the late Ace Ntsoelengoe remains the player with most hat-tricks scored (14) in the club’s history.
