World.title: Government recommits to promoting sustainable agriculture
World.content:
Seed Control and Certification Institute (SCCI) Senior Seed Officer, Zombe Sikazwe, says Government reaffirmed its commitment to promoting sustainable agriculture, crop diversification and the empowerment of women farmers as part of efforts to strengthen Zambia’s food security and agricultural resilience.

Speaking during the Zambia Traditional Seed and Food Festival, Mrs Sikazwe said the government is shifting its agricultural agenda from focusing mainly on production to promoting sustainable, resilient and inclusive agricultural practices.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government had identified agroecology, agricultural diversification and women empowerment as key priorities in transforming the agricultural sector.

She said the Eighth National Development Plan and the National Agriculture Policy prioritised agroecology as a pathway towards sustainable agriculture.

Mrs Sikazwe said the Ministry of Agriculture is promoting farming practices that restore soil health, conserve water, encourage the use of indigenous seed varieties and reduce dependence on expensive external inputs.

She said SCCI will continue ensuring that farmers have access to certified, diverse and climate-resilient seeds, including traditional and improved varieties suitable for agro ecological farming systems.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government is moving away from overdependence on maize production by promoting crops such as soybeans, sunflower, groundnuts, cowpeas, sorghum, cassava and high-value horticultural crops.

She said the diversification agenda also included integrating livestock and aquaculture into farming systems to create additional income opportunities, employment and resilience against climate-related shocks.

Mrs Sikazwe said the Comprehensive Agriculture Transformation Support Programme (CASP) has placed crop diversification at the centre of its implementation strategy.

She further said the government recognised women as key players in the agricultural sector, noting that they contributed more than 60 percent of farm labour and played a central role in household food security.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government is prioritising support for women-headed households through the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP), improved access to finance and land, women-focused agricultural extension services and training.

She said deliberate efforts are also being made to ensure women are included in seed systems and agricultural value chains.

Mrs Sikazwe added that sustainable agriculture could only be achieved through the combined efforts of government, farmers, the private sector, non-governmental organisations and cooperating partners.

Meanwhile, Gabriel Mapulanga who was representing a Consortium of Civil Society Organizations has called for increased investment in traditional seed systems, saying indigenous seeds are critical to strengthening Zambia’s food security, improving nutrition and building resilience to climate change.

Father Mapulanga said traditional seeds such as sorghum, millet and cowpeas had the potential to help communities withstand drought and other climate-related challenges.

He said the loss of indigenous seed varieties is gradually threatening Zambia’s agricultural heritage, as some traditional crops are becoming less common in farming communities.

Father Mapulanga noted that the disappearance of traditional seeds also meant losing indigenous knowledge on how to grow, preserve, store and prepare traditional foods.

He said women play a critical role in preserving indigenous seeds and traditional food knowledge, describing them as key custodians of the country’s food systems.

Father Mapulanga said traditional foods such as sorghum, millet, cowpeas, bondwe and wild fruits such as masuku are important sources of nutrition but are increasingly being marginalised due to changing food consumption patterns.

He observed that the growing consumption of highly processed foods has contributed to reduced dietary diversity and increased nutrition-related health challenges.

Father Mapulanga said traditional seeds should not be viewed as outdated, but rather as practical solutions to climate change and food security challenges because of their ability to withstand harsh weather conditions and their nutritional value.

He, however, said farmers continued to face challenges such as the high cost of irrigation equipment, limited access to affordable processing technologies, inadequate agricultural extension services and restricted access to seed markets.

He called for increased investment in farmer-managed seed enterprises, affordable agricultural technologies for rural women and policies that protect farmers’ rights to save, exchange and sell traditional seeds.

Father Mapulanga said farmers should be given the freedom to preserve and use their own seeds, adding that seed sovereignty is important to achieving national food sovereignty.

He urged policymakers to integrate gender-inclusive agroecological approaches into national agricultural strategies and support farmer-led seed systems alongside conventional agricultural methods.

He has also called on the private sector, academic and research institutions to work with women-led cooperatives in developing markets and affordable processing technologies that would help retain economic value within local communities.

Women farmers have called for greater recognition and support for traditional seed systems, saying indigenous crops are essential to strengthening food security, preserving agricultural knowledge and building resilience to climate change.

The women farmers’ representative Esther Mumba said women are not merely beneficiaries of agricultural development but key leaders, innovators and custodians of traditional seed and food knowledge.

Mrs Mumba said women play a critical role in selecting, preserving and exchanging seeds, as well as passing indigenous farming knowledge from one generation to another.

She said women farmers remained central to household food security through the production of vegetables, legumes, small grains and other traditional crops.

She however, noted that farming had become increasingly challenging due to unpredictable rainfall patterns, declining soil fertility, rising input costs, increased pest attacks and limited access to reliable markets.

Mrs Mumba said the severe drought experienced during the 2023/2024 agricultural season had exposed the vulnerability of the country’s food system when it depended heavily on a limited number of crops.

She also highlighted indigenous vegetables such as bondwe, chiwawa, kalembula and katapa, saying they contributed to dietary diversity and represented an important part of Zambia’s food heritage.

Mrs Mumba said traditional seeds carried valuable knowledge and biodiversity, adding that some indigenous crop varieties had characteristics that made them suitable for different local growing conditions, including dry environments.

Mrs Mumba said increased support for farmer-managed seed systems, community seed banks, seed conservation and the exchange of traditional seeds among farming communities and young people.

She further urged stakeholders to recognise and protect farmers’ rights while ensuring that women’s knowledge and experiences are represented in agricultural policies and programmes.

Mrs Mumba said women farmers are also adopting agro ecological practices such as compost making, crop rotation, intercropping, mulching, tree planting and water harvesting to improve soil fertility and protect the environment.

She said combining traditional farming knowledge with modern technologies and scientific research will help farmers improve productivity, conserve biodiversity and reduce dependence on expensive external inputs.

Mrs Mumba has since called for stronger support for traditional seeds and farmer-managed seed systems through policies and programmes that recognise community seed banks, indigenous seed varieties and farmers’ knowledge.

She has also urged the government to increase investment in agro ecology and climate-resilient agriculture through practical extension services, water harvesting technologies, small-scale irrigation, soil restoration initiatives and affordable farming equipment.

Mrs Mumba further called for improved access to land, finance, training, technology and decision-making opportunities for women farmers, including young women entering the agricultural sector.

World.title: ZAQA commends public for exhibiting positive compliance levels
World.content:
The Zambia Qualifications Authority (ZAQA) has commended members of the public and other stakeholders for the high levels of compliance with their qualifications verification process.

In an interview with ZANIS TV, ZAQA Corporate Communications Specialist, Inutu Mwanza, says the authority’s mandate is being adopted, as they continue to receive applications from people seeking to pursue higher education and employment opportunities.

“Many people are complying, as we all know, it’s mandatory for you to verify your qualifications,” she said.

Mrs Mwanza stated that the authority is collaborating with higher learning institutions to enforce a system integration that will enable the availing of learner records to the authority to avoid delays in verification.

“Legally we are the custodian of all qualifications in the country,” she said.

Mrs Mwanza noted that the system has significantly improved learner record availability by digitizing the verification process.

She further encouraged all those who have not yet verified their qualifications with the authority to do so, stating that once verified, their certificates will have no expiry.

World.title: ECZ announces resignation of three candidates for Mandevu Parliamentary by-election
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ), has announced the resignation of three candidates from the Mandevu Parliamentary by-election.

According to a public notice issued by ECZ today, 30th October 2026, the candidates who have resigned are Mr Ntazana Musukuma Mutungwa of the Leadership Movement (LM), Mr Daniel Chisenga of the Forum for Democracy and Development (FDD), and Mr Daniel Daka, an independent candidate.

The Commission disclosed that the three candidates resigned through letters dated 28th October 2026, which were served on the Commission on 29th October 2026.

Following the resignations, Mr Adrian Banda of the United Party for National Development (UPND) remains the only validly nominated candidate in the race.

However, in accordance with Regulations 20(3) and 52(2) of the Electoral Process (General) Regulations, 2016, Mr Banda will be declared duly elected as Member of Parliament for Mandevu Constituency without the need for an election, effective 5th November 2026.

World.title: Africa: From Commonwealth Connections to Economic Opportunity - Expanding Africa-Caribbean Trade Linkages
World.content:
guest column

When Commonwealth leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda this November, they will confront rising trade tensions, geopolitical shocks and supply chain disruption alongside longstanding challenges, such as high debt, limited affordable finance, climate exposure and poor connectivity.

Across Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean, these pressures make diversifying markets, attracting productive investment and building resilience through trade even more urgent. They also increase the importance of regional and cross-regional value chains that can withstand disruptions to established trade relationships.

One opportunity lies in plain sight: stronger Africa-Caribbean economic connections. Shared history, culture and diaspora relationships provide a foundation, as do common ambitions to diversify exports, add value locally and create opportunities for small businesses, including those led by women and young entrepreneurs.

The institutional landscape is also changing. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is building a framework for trade including goods, services, investment and digital commerce, while the Caribbean is deepening the CARICOM Single Market and Economy.



Connecting these integration efforts across the Atlantic could help firms aggregate supply and demand, build scale, and develop regional value chains. and access larger markets. A bigger, more integrated market can improve the commercial case for investment and the economics of cross-regional trade.

Forthcoming analysis by the International Trade Centre (ITC), undertaken with the support of Afreximbank, points to considerable unrealised trade potential between Africa and the Caribbean. But the numbers tell only part of the story.

In a survey of 1,175 businesses and business support organisations only 10% of African companies and 12% of Caribbean companies reported trading with the other region. Yet among those that did, 79% of African firms and 82% of Caribbean firms described their experience positively or very positively. The challenge is less about potential than removing barriers to scale.

Businesses struggle to access reliable market information, trusted partners and appropriate finance, as well as to navigate standards and move goods efficiently.

These constraints are not new. Low trade volumes weaken direct transport links; poor connectivity raises costs; limited commercial relationships restrict information; and smaller transactions are harder to finance.

The priority is to tackle these challenges in a comprehensive way.

Physical distance remains particularly costly. ITC estimates freight costs on African exports to the Caribbean at almost 20% of shipment value, compared with just over 8% for African exports globally. Caribbean exports to Africa face costs approaching 22%. Limited routes and fragmented networks continue to undermine viable trade. Scheduled direct air services between Lagos and Barbados, launched in 2026, illustrate how improved connections can support business travel, tourism and wider services.

Access to finance depends not only on the availability of capital, but on whether viable opportunities can be connected to appropriate financing. Businesses need guidance on available funding and lender requirements, and financial institutions need appropriate instruments and ways to manage risk. Trade finance, working-capital facilities, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms can all bridge these gaps.

Payments also matter, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Slow, costly or uncertain transfers can derail transactions. More efficient cross-border payment systems would reduce both transaction costs and risks. Africa's Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) offers useful lessons for simplifying payments as financial links with the Caribbean deepen.

Beyond trade volumes, value creation extends beyond goods. Services, digital solutions and the creative industries can generate more value within both regions. Africa and the Caribbean have globally recognised cultural assets and extensive diasporas, yet much of the creative value is captured elsewhere. Creators and firms need finance, workable payments, intellectual property expertise, distribution channels and direct access to buyers and investors. Supporting creative businesses, rather than only promoting cultural exchange, would generate more revenue and help jobs remain in local economies.

Governments and institutions can create the enabling environment, but businesses will ultimately determine whether a new chapter in Africa–Caribbean economic relations succeed, especially for SMEs.

Commonwealth trade and investment platforms can connect policymakers, investors, entrepreneurs and business leaders. They offer a way to identify obstacles that no single firm or government can resolve alone. Success, however, means introductions becoming contracts, investment reaching viable enterprises and businesses entering new markets.

The Commonwealth brings an existing economic advantage to this endeavour. The opportunity is to make that advantage work more deliberately for Africa–Caribbean commerce, where physical distance, limited market information and still-thin commercial networks continue to constrain trade.

Through its Working Group on Trade and Investment, member countries are developing a workplan to expand intra-Commonwealth commerce. Cooperation on compatible regulations, mutual recognition of standards and qualifications, and simpler border procedures can help realise these gains.

Close 

ITC's work on investment promotion and digital trade to women's economic empowerment, small-state resilience and emerging Africa–Caribbean business linkages can advance this agenda. Afreximbank's Global Africa vision brings the finance, investment and commercial infrastructure required to turn diaspora ties into sustainable economic relationships.

These capabilities are complementary. Trade policy can open markets; finance helps businesses act; and enterprises sustain commercial relationships.

The practical test is clear: identify viable opportunities, mobilise investment, resolve logistics, finance and payment barriers, connect SMEs to customers and investors, use digital trade to overcome distance and retain more value within regions. Progress should then be measured in transactions, market access and sustainable business relationships.

As leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda, they can demonstrate how a connected Commonwealth can convert partnerships into investment, enterprise and shared prosperity.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Police Inspector, 11 Others in Kebbi
World.content:
Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities.

The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse.

A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said, "the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities," he said.

Though the police said five people were killed in an attack on October 26, while seven others died in attacks on October 28 in the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi area of the state, bringing the total to 12, including a police inspector, locals who spoke under condition of anonymity said over 23 people actually lost their lives in the Lakurawa/Mamudawa attacks on the communities of Koko Besse and Shanga areas of Kebbi.

A source said, "They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted."

He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026.

A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, "I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities. Some of them who fled for safety during the attack are just returning on the assurance by the security agents and government that measures are being put in place to ensure our safety."

He called on the government to come to their aid as some of the residents have nowhere to stay.

Another resident, Aliyu Tailor Besse, said the attack was carried out by the Lakurawa terrorists group.

"What happened was that after attacking communities in Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government, they started moving along the River Niger up to Koko Besse area.They were attacking communities along the River Niger as they moved towards Besse community. Many people were killed in the attacks. Prior to the attacks, those who saw them moving along the River Niger banks had raised an alarm calling on residents of the communities along the area to vacate. Some left, but many others stayed behind," he said.

Daily Trust gathered that a few days before the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi attacks, suspected members of the Lakurawa group also attacked Lafagu and other communities in Boya area of Kaoje, killing the village head, Alhaji Saidu Mujeli, and six others before leaving the area through the River Niger bank to attack other communities in Besse and Shanga.

It was gathered that despite the establishment of an army battalion in Kaoje to curtail the activities of terrorists, attacks have continued.

Police confirm attacks

Speaking to our correspondent, the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, said "it's true that the attack happened but it did not happen in one day and not in one community. It started from the 22nd of this month. The casualties recorded was not in a single attack. They attacked many of the communities in the riverine area and that's why the figure of those killed rose to 12. A police inspector and 11 others were killed in the attacks."

He said members of the Lakurawa terrorists group had earlier attacked communities along the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi axis on 22nd of October, but security operatives repelled them. He said they later carried out attacks on the communities of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi on October 26 and 28.

"Although the joint security teams repelled the attacks, seven people unfortunately lost their lives, including a police inspector," he said.

He added that earlier, members of the Yan Sakai, had invaded Samanaji Market and killed Fulani traders.

"Our police tactical teams deployed by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Besse, responded promptly to restore peace and prevent further carnage. However, three Fulani people lost their lives, while a police inspector sustained injuries in the line of duty," he said.

The state police spokesman said a tactical team of the police had been deployed to the troubled communities and normalcy is gradually returning to the area.

"The police have launched investigation into the attack and is following up on the attackers," he said.

'Attacks sign of frustration'

A security expert, who retired as a Captain in the Nigerian Army, Shehu Abubakar, told our correspondent that the attacks carried out by suspected members of the Lakurawa group in some communities of Kebbi, is a sign of frustration.

"You should understand that a battalion of the Nigerian Army was recently established at Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government to curtail activities of the bandits and Lakurawa, operating in the area. The Lakurawa must leave the area to find a convenient place as base to carry out their attacks. They carried out their attack on the communities along the River Niger bank while migrating to another area to avenge the presence of the army base at Kaoje.

"They can no longer stay close to the area where the battalion is located. They migrated from Kaoje, through the bank of the River Niger, moving through communities of Samanaji, Dutsinmari, Zaria Kalakala, to where they started their attacks at Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi. Now that they seem to have been displaced, the security agencies operating in the state should follow them up in every move they make so that they don't get a convenient place to settle. That way, they may be frustrated to move out of the state," he said.

Military bases in Kebbi

In the last two years, six Forward Operation Bases were established in Sakaba,Zuru,Yauri, Augie and Kaoje. The Battalion in Birnin Kebbi was upgraded to an Armoured Brigade, just as there is a battalion in Zuru.There are also army units in parts of Kaoje and other areas to strengthen military operations in the troubled communities of Augie, Danko Wasagu, Mahuta, Argungu, Arewa, Bagudo and Dandi, but the spate of killings occasioned by bandits and Lakurawa attacks remain a growing concern among residents.

Close 

Kebbi's killing fields

On Wednesday of last week, a large number of bandits invaded Dirin -Daji in Sakara Local Government Area of the state. It took the combined efforts of the security agencies in the area to disperse the attackers.

A week before the Kaoje district attack, three people were killed at Kasabo, a community in Saminaka, Yauri Local Government Area of the state. The community was attacked by the bandits in the early hours of the day when people were preparing to go about their daily activities. A resident, Aminu Usman, said their attackers came in large number to invade the community and that they killed three people while many others escaped through the bush.

A few days before the attack at Kasabo, suspected members of the Lakurawa terrorists group attacked the site of the construction company handling the Badagry-Ilela Supper Highway project at Gubba in Maiyama Local Government Area of the state, killing two soldiers and a Chinese national. The attackers were said to have crossed into Kebbi from Kebbe area of Sokoto, to carry out the attack, it was gathered.

Efforts to get comments from the state government proved abortive, but a top government official who does not want his name in print told our corespondent that the state government was working closely with security agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attacks.

He said, "Governor Nasir Idris has been up and doing on issues of security on the state. No fewer than 109 armoured vehicles and other logistics have been procured for security agencies to fight insecurity in the state."

World.title: Africa: AFCON Every Two Years Again As CAF Reverses Decision
World.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle.

The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation's Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026.

The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition.

CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable.



In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation's 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent.

"The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa," he said.

Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition.

He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future.

Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament.

The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year.

Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries' ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027.

He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa's cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together.

"The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa's rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa's 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world," he said.

"The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa," he added.

World.title: Ethiopia: As Tens of Thousands Flee Ethiopia to Kenya, UN Agency Warns of Growing Humanitarian Needs
World.content:
A map showing the location of Kenya (in orange) and Ethiopia (in green).

Geneva — The UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) says humanitarian needs are growing in an unfolding crisis on the Kenya–Ethiopia border as ongoing clashes on the Ethiopian side have forced tens of thousands of people to cross into Kenya in search of safety.

Significant cross-border movements at Moyale have been reported since Oct. 22.

“According to local authorities, up to an estimated 50,000 people have crossed into Kenya,” said Fatima Mohammed-Cole, the UNHCR Representative in Kenya.

“The figure remains fluid as registration and verification efforts continue, amid reports of further crossings,” she said in a statement.



Many of those fleeing are women and children.

The UN official said that while some affected people are staying with relatives and in host communities, others have sought shelter in temporary locations such as schools and churches.

- FOOD: THE URGENT NEED

“Food remains the most urgent need, alongside safe drinking water, emergency shelter, sanitation and health care,” said Mohammed-Cole.

UNHCR has deployed an emergency team to Moyale and is working closely with the Kenyan government.

It is working alongside the UN migration agency, IOM; the UN children’s agency, UNICEF, the UN World Food Programme, the Kenya Red Cross Society, and other humanitarian partners, to support the national and local response.

UNHCR said it is mobilising emergency relief supplies, including essential household items and temporary shelter materials, to support nearly 12,000 people, with efforts underway to increase assistance as needs grow.

The agency is supporting ongoing assessments of protection and humanitarian needs.

“We are also working with the authorities and partners to identify safer accommodation options, further away from the border, for those fleeing violence,” the UNHCR official said.

According to Chatham House researchers, “Although Tigray has seen conflict before, this time there is a risk that hostilities could extend into Eritrea and Sudan,” they wrote.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Global Nursing Head Flags Dangers of Misinformation After Killing of Congo Ebola Nurse
World.content:
A nurse prepares a bed for a suspected case of Ebola in the isolation unit at Bwera Hospital, Kasese District (file photo).

Geneva — The International Council of Nurses (ICN) head has warned of the lethal dangers that misinformation poses to the nursing profession following the killing of a nurse in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DR Congo), who was responding to an Ebola case.

ICN chief executive Howard Catton said the "tragic news" was a reminder that prevalent misinformation was particularly dangerous for healthcare staff after young men armed with machetes killed the nurse.

"Health misinformation and the breakdown of trust in science is now a deadly risk for nurses and health workers," Catton posted on the media platform X on Oct. 29.

The UN's Ebola coordinator and the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) on Oct. 29 deplored the killing of the nurse working to fight the disease in the DRC four days earlier.



In an interview with AllAfrica, Catton also warned that community health workers often supplant nurses and may be seen as an easy, cheap substitute for a skilled nursing workforce in parts of Africa.

"There is both the migration of registered nurses from the continent of Africa and unemployment of nurses in Africa," said Catton.

"So, as we see this growth in community health workers, we also know that registered nurses continue to leave Africa for high-income countries in Europe or North America."

At the same time, many nurses on the continent remain unemployed.

Catton cited UN figures showing Africa's health workforce grew to 5.72 million in 2024, up from 4.3 million in 2018, noting that such progress is not keeping pace with demand.

ONLY 46 PERCENT OF WORKFORCE NEEDS

"The African region currently has only 46 percent of the health workers it needs," said the head of the international nursing group.

Catton visited African countries last year, and some leaders said what is happening is making it harder for them to improve their healthcare systems.

"To us, this is starting to feel like a form of neo-colonialism because we're having valuable resources which are being taken; we're not being adequately compensated for them," said the nursing head, conveying the sentiment some African leaders expressed to him.

The WHO's Africa 2026 report says an estimated 943,000 trained health workers across the African region were unemployed in 2024.

That is, as the continent faces severe staffing shortages and meets only 46 per cent of its overall health workforce needs.

"We are training more health workers than ever before, yet too many remain unemployed while millions go without care," said Dr Mohamed Yakub Janabi, the WHO regional director for Africa.

"Without bold investment and coordinated reform to plan, train and retain health workers, progress toward universal health coverage will remain out of reach," said Dr Janabi, speaking in Ghana in May.

Close 

The WHO estimates a global shortage of at least ten million healthcare workers by 2030, and some organizations project an even larger shortfall, writes Pooja Kumar, a global leader at the McKinsey Health Institute.

She notes, though, that the global healthcare workforce shortage is not evenly distributed.

"For example," Pooja says, "Africa has 17 percent of the world's population but accounts for 52 percent of the global shortage."

World.title: Chad: France and Chad Rebuild Military Ties With Planned Air Force Training
World.content:
Two French fighter jets and a transport aircraft will soon make a stopover in Chad and carry out "training activities", the French army has said, as the two countries seek to rebuild ties.

The stopover will take place as part of a joint military exercise involving the armed forces of Côte d'Ivoire, Gabon and France in November.

Xavier Rival, a spokesman for the French chief of defence staff, said Thursday that two French Mirage 2000 fighter jets and a French CASA transport aircraft would make a technical stopover in Chad.

"It will be a short visit that will also provide an opportunity to conduct training activities," he said.



Relations between France and Chad began to deteriorate in mid-2024.

They reached breaking point when Chad's leader Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno formally terminated his country's military cooperation agreement with France in November 2024.

The move led to the complete withdrawal of French troops from the country in early 2025.

Mending ties

Rival said France's cooperation with Chad had resumed, "in full respect of Chad's sovereignty".

He said the French armed forces would help develop the capabilities of the Chadian air force.

"France's objective is to contribute to efforts against regional instability," he added.

Chad had been one of France's last military footholds in the Sahel, a region where Paris once deployed more than 5,000 soldiers as part of its anti-jihadist Operation Barkhane, which ended in November 2022.

Coups between 2020 and 2023 forced France to withdraw from Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, as the juntas in those countries drew closer to Russia.

France and Chad have since sought to revive their ties, while expanding them to include economic and cultural cooperation as well as military assistance.

Algeria and Chad cement stategic partnership with raft of bilateral deals

'New step forward'

President Emmanuel Macron hosted Déby for talks in mid-October as part of ongoing efforts to rebuild the relationship. It followed another visit in January.

During Déby's most recent trip, France and Chad signed a declaration of intent to renew their defence cooperation.

"We are taking a new step forward and formalising the strengthening of our defence partnership, in line with a renewed relationship," Macron posted on social media platform X, after hosting Déby at the Élysée Palace.

Close 

"We are building a partnership based on mutual respect and practical cooperation for the benefit of our peoples."

France and Chad sign 'renewed' defence partnership following two-year hiatus

Macron has sought to renew France's engagement with Africa after years of strained ties with former French-speaking colonies.

On the economic front, France's main employers' federation Medef hosted a France-Chad business forum in September, bringing together 250 companies to encourage investment.

The Élysée said Medef is planning to send a delegation to Chad in the coming months.

Under an ambitious national development plan to diversify its economy, Chad says it aims to raise €26.5 billion in public and private investment and boost its GDP by 60 percent by 2030.

(with newswires)

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 30, 2026
World.content:
Rwandan Man Convicted in U.S. for Lying About 1994 Genocide Role

A Rwandan man, Eric Nshimiye, has been convicted in the United States of perjury and obstruction of justice after lying under oath about his involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide. A federal jury in Boston found that Nshimiye concealed his alleged participation in attacks against the Tutsi community while testifying in the 2019 immigration fraud trial of his former university classmate, Jean Leonard Teganya. Nshimiye fled Rwanda for Kenya in 1994 and was admitted to the U.S. as a refugee the following year. Evidence presented at his trial showed that, while a student at the University of Rwanda in Butare, he took part in attacks on the Tutsi people, including by striking them on the head with a club. Nshimiye faces up to five years in prison for each of four perjury counts and up to 10 years for obstruction of justice. He is expected to be sentenced on 26 January 2027.

Tinubu Heads to Saudi Arabia to Pray for Nigeria



Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has travelled to Saudi Arabia to perform the lesser Hajj pilgrimage, known as Umrah, where he is expected to pray for Nigeria's peace, unity and stability. The presidency said that the visit will provide an opportunity for spiritual reflection and prayers for the country's continued progress. Tinubu's trip comes as Nigeria prepares for general elections, with insecurity and economic challenges expected to dominate the campaign. His media aide has dismissed speculation that the visit is intended for medical checks, insisting that it is a religious journey. The next elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027. Tinubu's main challengers will again be former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi.

U.S. Seizes $750,000 in Kenyan-Linked Student Aid Fraud Probe

US authorities have seized more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency linked to an alleged international student financial aid fraud scheme involving Kenyan nationals. The seizure forms part of Operation Ghostbusters, an investigation into a network accused of using stolen American identities to submit fraudulent student aid applications and divert millions of dollars in grants and loan refunds. The US Justice Department has charged five defendants, with investigators alleging that Kenyan-based conspirators worked with individuals in the US to transfer proceeds through bank accounts and overseas networks. Authorities said that the wider investigation has identified more than $32 million in losses. Cooperation with Kenyan law enforcement agencies is continuing to trace funds and pursue suspects.

Rights Group Urges Mali to Release Missing Junta Critic and Son

Human Rights Watch has called on Mali's military authorities to disclose the whereabouts of former government minister and junta critic Mountaga Tall and his son, Cheick Mamadou Tall, six months after their abductions. Unidentified gunmen reportedly seized Mountaga in Bamako on 2 May. His son disappeared two weeks later after being told he could deliver belongings to his father. Their whereabouts and condition remain unknown, with authorities yet to acknowledge detaining them. Human Rights Watch said that the disappearances reflect a wider crackdown on political opposition and dissent under Mali's military junta. He urged authorities to ensure their safety and release them.

Sudan Accuses Ethiopia of Backing Drone Attacks

Sudanese authorities claim that 162 drone attacks launched from Ethiopian territory have killed more than 400 civilians and 102 military personnel, amid allegations that Ethiopia is supporting the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Officials said that the attacks have targeted several locations across Sudan, destroying schools, hospitals, health centres and fuel stations. However, the claims have not been independently verified. Sudan has accused Ethiopia of allowing drones to operate from bases near its border. He warned that the attacks threaten regional stability and efforts to enable displaced people to return home. Ethiopia has previously rejected allegations of supporting the RSF, describing them as unfounded. Sudan's Defence Minister has also accused more than 20 countries of providing the paramilitary group with logistical support, funding, mercenaries and drones.

Close 

Guinea-Bissau Busts Trafficking Ring Behind Fake Migration Scheme



Police in Guinea-Bissau have dismantled an alleged human trafficking network that lured approximately 70 people from across West Africa with promises of employment and opportunities to migrate to Europe. More than five suspects have been arrested following an operation on 21 October. Authorities allege that victims from countries including Mali, Sierra Leone, Guinea, Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire were defrauded, held against their will and pressured into recruiting others into fraudulent pyramid schemes. Some women were reportedly threatened with sexual exploitation and prostitution. Victims have been rescued; however, many remain stranded in Guinea-Bissau because they cannot afford to return home. Human rights organisations have raised concerns about inadequate shelters, psychological support, and financial assistance for survivors.

World.title: Mali: Critic of Mali's Junta Forcibly Disappeared Six Months On
World.content:
Locate, Release Mountaga Tall and His Son

Six months after their abductions, Mountaga Tall, an outspoken critic of Mali's junta, and his son, Cheick Mamadou Tall, remain missing, their fate unknown, and the Malian authorities silent. Every day that passes without news raises fears for their safety and deepens their family's anguish.

Unidentified gunmen abducted Tall in Bamako, Mali's capital, on May 2. Tall's son went missing on May 16 after receiving a call informing him that he could deliver belongings to his father, who was reportedly being held at an undisclosed location.

Radio France Internationale reported in July that the United Nations Committee on Enforced Disappearances had urged Mali's authorities to locate and protect Tall and his son.



International media suggest that Malian intelligence services may be holding Tall in a secret facility. Malian authorities, however, have neither acknowledged detaining Tall or his son nor provided information about their location, legal status, or health, despite requests from Tall's family and a legal team.

Tall, who was a government minister between 2014 and 2017, was initially aligned with Mali's military authorities but later emerged as a critic of the junta who opposed the military-led government's dissolution of political parties.

The disappearances of Tall and his son fit a broader crackdown on political opposition, media and dissent under Mali's military junta, which seized power in 2021. Authorities have suspended and banned media outlets, dissolved civil society groups, ended multiparty politics and subjected critics to arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance. Since Tall's abduction, other political figures and their relatives have reportedly been abducted by masked gunmen, a modus operandi associated with Malian intelligence services and some remain missing.

Under international human rights law, an enforced disappearance occurs when state authorities or their agents detain a person and then refuse to acknowledge the detention or disclose the person's fate or whereabouts, thereby placing the person outside the protection of the law. Victims of enforced disappearance face a heightened risk of torture and execution.

Enforced disappearance inflicts profound suffering on families, leaving them uncertain about whether their loved ones are alive or dead and denying them justice. Malian authorities should immediately disclose the whereabouts of Mountaga Tall and his son, ensure their safety, and release them.

Ilaria Allegrozzi, Senior Sahel Researcher

World.title: E. coli outbreak lands 3 in hospital, health officials investigate link to pumpkin patch
World.content:

Three children are in intensive care with E. coli infections as health officials investigate a possible link to a California pumpkin patch that closed just days before Halloween.

Five cases of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection have been confirmed, potentially originating from Brookshire Farms in San Luis Obispo, according to an Oct. 27 advisory issued by the County of San Luis Obispo Public Health Department.

The suspected exposure period is Oct. 16 through Oct 26.

FDA WIDENS CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK INVESTIGATION TO SIX MORE STATES AS CONFIRMED CASES TOP 6,000

Health officials advise that anyone who visited the pumpkin patch between those dates should monitor for gastrointestinal symptoms.

"We are working diligently to identify the source of these infections to protect the health of our community," said County Health Officer Dr. Christy Mulkerin in the news release.

"We encourage anyone who may have been exposed and is experiencing symptoms consistent with E. coli infection to seek immediate medical attention."

CLICK HERE TO 

Typical symptoms of E. Coli include cramping, severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea and signs of dehydration, which usually begin within three to 10 days of exposure.

Young children under 10 are typically at the highest risk for complications, which can include hemolytic uremic syndrome, a serious condition that damages blood cells and can lead to kidney failure, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Dr. Tyler Evans, an infectious disease physician and founder of Wellness Equity Alliance in California, warned that diarrhea can lead to dehydration and fatigue.

"The diarrhea is really the key component here, and the stomach cramps," he told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Evans said younger children and older adults can be particularly vulnerable, emphasizing the need to closely watch children younger than 5.

Speaking generally about potential exposure routes at pumpkin patches, Evans said E. coli can spread when bacteria from feces reach someone’s mouth.

He pointed to potentially contaminated food or water, animal contact and person-to-person transmission as possible transmission routes.

Evans also noted that not all E. coli bacteria cause illness. The confirmed cases in this investigation involve Shiga toxin-producing E. coli.

"One of the most effective ways that we can prevent this is washing your hands," the doctor added.

The farm has voluntarily closed as a precaution while investigators work to identify the source of the infections, determine whether the cases are connected and assess whether others may be at risk, according to the county health department.

World.title: Travel influencer, 24, killed after pickup truck is swept away in terrifying river crossing
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A 24-year-old travel influencer was killed after a pickup truck carrying a group of travelers was swept away while crossing a river in Nicaragua.

French traveler Emma Marie Laurent was one of three women who died after the vehicle was caught in strong currents following heavy rainfall, according to news agency Jam Press.

The group was traveling through El Manzano, a community in the northwestern department of Chinandega, when they attempted to cross the Nahualapa River at around 1 a.m. on Oct. 9, the same source reported.

AMERICAN TOURIST FALLS 1,000 FEET TO HER DEATH WHILE CHASING PERFECT MOUNTAIN PHOTO

Recent rainfall had caused the river to rise, creating dangerous conditions before the vehicle attempted to cross.

The driver, identified as Mexican national Martin Gerardo García Girón, reportedly stepped out of the pickup to assess the water level before attempting the crossing, according to Jam Press.

The water reportedly came close to the driver's knees, but the current swept the pickup away and caused it to overturn.

The driver survived, though accounts have differed on whether other passengers also made it to safety, according to Jam Press.

Authorities were investigating the circumstances surrounding the crossing.

CLICK HERE TO 

Nicaraguan co-President Rosario Murillo offered condolences to the victims' families following the deaths.

"This is a tragedy," Murillo said, according to reports.

"We express our solidarity and our call to remain vigilant and, in the face of such tragedies, to express our full solidarity."

Murillo also warned about the dangers of crossing rivers during Nicaragua's rainy season.

"Rivers are deceptive; one thinks they are calm and, suddenly, the current comes, and we have tragedies like this that bring mourning to families," she said, according to Jam Press.

Laurent had developed an online following by sharing her travels around the world, including glimpses of life on the road from her van.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

She described herself as "your barefoot BFF" on Instagram, where she had nearly 43,000 followers at the time of her death, Jam Press reported.

Laurent appeared to have shared her final social media post on Oct. 2, uploading a video from a recent trip to Portugal.

In the post, she reflected on the importance of appreciating everyday moments.

"I think the most beautiful people, inside and out, are those who know how to admire the world around them," Laurent wrote in French.

Following news of her death, social media users left messages of remembrance beneath the post.

"Gone far too soon," one person commented.

World.title: AI-powered cyberattacks fuel 'Black October' fears
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Startup founder Colin Parsons woke up to roughly 50 billing notifications he never expected. He reported that his OpenAI and Anthropic accounts had racked up $449 in charges he didn't recognize. It was an expensive surprise that highlights how quickly stolen credentials can become a financial headache.

His experience comes as hackers increasingly use artificial intelligence to automate attacks at speeds that leave security teams scrambling. Meanwhile, researchers have uncovered dangerous weaknesses in software that helps power millions of websites.

Some cybersecurity professionals are calling this turbulent period "Black October." The name may sound dramatic, but the developments behind it deserve attention. And while many attacks target large organizations, the consequences can eventually reach your personal accounts. Here's what's happening, how AI-powered cyberattacks are changing online security and what you can do to protect yourself.

Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will share five practical ways to protect your trip and your wallet this holiday travel season. You’ll learn how to secure your phone and personal information, find better travel deals, avoid common scams, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

Join us Saturday, October 31, at 11 AM ET / 8 AM PT. Register free now at CyberGuyLive.com.

BILL GATES SOUNDS ALARM ON AI-POWERED CYBERATTACKS, WARNS OF 'NEGATIVE SURPRISES' WITHIN A YEAR

Why cybersecurity experts are calling it Black October

October 2026 has delivered a troubling wave of cybersecurity developments. Hackers have gained access to more powerful tools, while researchers have uncovered serious weaknesses in widely used software. Security professionals are reportedly struggling to keep pace with increasingly automated attacks. Some have started calling the current wave "Black October."

The term describes a series of cybersecurity emergencies rather than a single coordinated hacking campaign. The biggest concern is speed. Traditionally, hackers needed significant time and technical expertise to investigate potential targets. They also had to develop attack methods and analyze the information they obtained. Now, AI tools can automate portions of that work. Some can operate continuously and pursue multiple potential targets at once. As a result, companies may have less time to respond when criminals discover a way into their systems.

Microsoft exposes AI cyberattacks moving at machine speed

One of the clearest examples comes from Microsoft. On Oct. 21, Microsoft Threat Intelligence revealed that a China-state-aligned hacking group called Storm-0940 had used an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX. The open-source tool can automate security testing tasks, including investigating networks and identifying potential weaknesses. In the hands of criminals, those capabilities can accelerate attempts to gain unauthorized access.

According to Microsoft, the group used ARTEX to target hundreds of organizations across multiple industries. Several attacks resulted in unauthorized privileged access to cloud systems. In multiple cases, attackers reached that level of access in less than three hours. Although many attempts failed, the successful intrusions demonstrate how quickly AI-assisted attacks can unfold.

Hackers launch thousands of login attempts per minute

Between Oct. 10 and 14, Microsoft recorded more than 151,000 failed login attempts in one campaign targeting 327 accounts across eight organizations. At its peak on Oct. 11, attackers generated approximately 2,900 failed login attempts per minute. The technique, known as password spraying, involves trying passwords against multiple accounts to identify a working login.

Importantly, Microsoft did not observe successful logins during that specific campaign. However, it documented unauthorized access and suspicious activity in other environments associated with the same threat group. Microsoft also connected Storm-0940 to a compromise involving ConnectWise, a company that provides software used by IT service providers. Attackers exploited access associated with ConnectWise cloud applications to attempt entry into customer environments. Some then carried out further activity through Microsoft cloud services, including changes that could help them maintain access.

Microsoft cautioned that suspicious access does not automatically mean customer information was stolen. Nevertheless, the activity reveals how AI can help attackers move quickly once they obtain usable credentials.

A $449 AI account scare shows the financial danger

The risks become more personal when you look at what happened to Colin Parsons. Parsons reportedly woke up to roughly 50 notifications about charges involving OpenAI and Anthropic. He reported $281 in unexpected OpenAI usage and another $168 involving Anthropic. Both credentials were associated with OpenCode, an AI coding platform he used.

On Oct. 17, OpenCode disclosed a security incident involving its Console service. The company said unauthorized access to a legacy system may have exposed third-party AI provider keys stored by some users. The company reportedly notified affected customers and advised them to revoke their credentials.

OpenCode said the incident affected approximately 1.4% of its Console users who had connected external AI providers. The disclosure concerned credentials stored in Console, rather than keys stored locally in OpenCode's desktop or command-line applications. Other users also reported unexpected charges, although the amounts have not been independently verified. OpenCode associated its incident with a large-scale AI model distillation attack, but it has not publicly established exactly how the reported unauthorized usage occurred.

The concern is straightforward. If someone obtains a working API key, they may be able to use a paid AI service and generate charges against the account owner's billing arrangement. For people who depend on AI tools for work, that can become expensive before they realize anything has happened.

WINDOWS MALWARE USES GROK AI TO HELP STAY HIDDEN, RESEARCHERS SAY

A massive website security scare adds to Black October fears

While hackers are becoming more capable, AI-assisted security research is also uncovering dangerous weaknesses in software that supports the internet. On Oct. 21, developers released emergency fixes for two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language widely used to operate websites.

The vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are collectively known as PHP2Shell. Under certain conditions, the flaws could allow attackers to execute malicious code on vulnerable servers without first signing in. Successful exploitation could expose sensitive information or give criminals control over affected systems.

The potential impact is enormous because PHP powers roughly 70% of websites whose server-side programming language is known. However, that does not mean 70% of websites were hacked. It also doesn't establish that attackers could successfully compromise every website using PHP. The vulnerabilities affect PHP installations handling web requests, but successfully exploiting them can require complex technical conditions.

Federal agencies issue urgent security warnings

The situation prompted warnings from U.S. cybersecurity authorities. On Oct. 23, the FBI issued a public alert urging organizations to patch affected systems immediately. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency also called for urgent updates. The PHP project released fixes in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Website administrators running older unsupported versions need to obtain appropriate vendor-supported fixes or migrate to a supported release.

Meanwhile, several government organizations in Europe temporarily took websites offline as a precaution. However, the situation became clearer as researchers investigated. On Oct. 23, the Netherlands' National Cyber Security Centre said exploiting the vulnerabilities appeared more complicated than initially feared. The agency lowered its assessment of the likelihood of widespread exploitation.

Also on Oct. 23, PHP disclosed a separate vulnerability, CVE-2026-115560, involving an unusual combination of server settings and application code. The project recommended a temporary configuration change while it prepares a fix through its regular release process. Website owners should continue following official PHP security guidance rather than assuming the emergency has completely passed.

Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike also reported seeing attempted attacks, but said it had not observed successful exploitation of PHP2Shell in its investigations at that point. Other security researchers, including Amazon Threat Intelligence, observed suspicious exploitation attempts beginning before the patches became publicly available. Those attempts remain important even without proof that they successfully compromised real systems.

However, new evidence emerged over the following days. On Oct. 24, security researcher Adel Karimi documented successful PHP2Shell exploitation against specially configured test servers, known as honeypots. The attacks launched 35 command shells across three honeypots. Although those findings did not establish how many real-world websites had been compromised, they demonstrated that attackers could successfully exploit the vulnerability under certain conditions.

Then, on Oct. 26, CISA added both PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The designation confirms that federal authorities recognize evidence of active exploitation. It also reinforces the urgency of installing security updates, even though the full extent of attacks against real-world systems remains unclear.

AI is helping hackers, but security researchers are using it too

There's another side to this story that deserves attention. Artificial intelligence helped researchers investigate the PHP vulnerabilities before the October emergency. According to the PHP Foundation, developers had identified early signs of one underlying problem during a security investigation in 2024. However, the team struggled to develop a reliable solution. Additional research in 2026 exposed the seriousness of the issue.

The foundation worked with researchers and used AI-assisted security tools, including technology from Anthropic and OpenAI, to examine PHP's code. Researchers from security companies Calif and Wiz also contributed important findings. The PHP Foundation says these reports helped clarify the vulnerabilities' potential impact and accelerated the work needed to release fixes.

AI can therefore help defenders identify dangerous weaknesses before criminals exploit them. The challenge is ensuring security teams can investigate the findings and distribute fixes quickly enough. That challenge is becoming more urgent.

What AI-powered cyberattacks mean for your personal information

You may be wondering how any of this affects you if you're simply checking email or shopping online. The concern starts with the companies holding your information. When hackers compromise a business, they may gain access to stored customer information. Depending on the systems involved, that could include email addresses or passwords. Financial details may also be exposed. Criminals can use stolen information to launch convincing scams or attempt to take over existing accounts.

Meanwhile, AI makes it easier to produce personalized phishing messages. Attackers can incorporate leaked information into emails that appear to come from a company you recognize. Some criminals also use AI-generated voices to impersonate people and pressure their targets into making payments.

However, a security vulnerability affecting a website doesn't automatically mean your personal information has been exposed. The actual risk depends on whether attackers successfully gained access and what information they obtained. That's why it helps to focus on the steps you can control.

HACKERS HIDE DANGEROUS FAKE AI DOWNLOADS BEHIND GOOGLE ADS

8 ways to protect yourself from AI-powered cyberattacks

You can't personally fix security problems affecting large companies. However, you can strengthen your accounts and reduce the potential damage if criminals obtain your information. Here are seven precautions I recommend taking now.

1. Secure your most important accounts first

Start with your primary email account. Criminals who gain access to it may be able to reset passwords for other services you use. Create a strong, unique password for every account. A reputable password manager can help you generate and store those passwords. Next, enable multifactor authentication wherever it's available. Passkeys and hardware security keys offer especially strong protection against phishing. Authenticator apps are another useful option. Avoid relying on passwords alone.

2. Check whether your passwords have been compromised

Your phone may already have tools that can identify passwords exposed in known data breaches. On an iPhone, open the Passwords app and review its Security section. Android users who save passwords through Google can review warnings in Google Password Manager. If a password has been exposed, change it directly through the company's official website or app. Also update any other accounts using that same password. Our article explains how to find compromised passwords on iPhone and Android. Remember, a compromised-password warning does not necessarily mean someone has accessed your account. However, it gives you a chance to replace a vulnerable login.

3. Watch your accounts for suspicious activity

Enable transaction notifications through your bank and credit card providers. Also review recent sign-ins on your email accounts and other important services. Watch for unfamiliar devices or changes to your recovery information. If you spot unauthorized activity, contact the provider through its official website or app. Change affected credentials and revoke unfamiliar sessions where possible. Don't wait for several suspicious charges before investigating.

4. Review which apps can access your information

Many people connect third-party apps to their Google or Microsoft accounts without thinking about the permissions they're granting. Over time, those connections can accumulate. Some applications may retain access even after you've stopped using them. Open your account's security settings and review connected applications. Remove access you no longer need or recognize. However, if a service you use has announced a security incident, follow its specific recovery instructions. Simply disconnecting an app may not revoke credentials that attackers already obtained.

5. Use strong security protection and monitor your identity

Strong antivirus software can help detect malicious downloads and block dangerous websites. However, antivirus protection cannot prevent every account takeover or stop a company from experiencing a data breach. That's why monitoring your financial information is also important. Consider placing a free credit freeze with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion to help prevent criminals from opening new credit accounts in your name. Keep in mind that a freeze won't protect accounts you already have. If you use AI services that require API keys, review your usage regularly. Revoke credentials that may have been exposed and set billing alerts or limits where the provider supports them. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

6. Consider using a personal data removal service

Data brokers collect and sell personal information, including phone numbers and home addresses. Criminals can use those details to make AI-generated scams more convincing. A personal data removal service can help remove your information from people-search sites and data broker databases, making it harder for scammers to find. However, it can't erase information from past breaches or prevent cyberattacks. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

7. Keep your devices and software updated

Enable automatic security updates on your phone and computer. Keep your browser current, too. Updates frequently fix vulnerabilities that criminals may try to exploit.

8. Be skeptical of urgent security messages

AI-generated phishing messages can look remarkably convincing. They may contain personal information that makes them appear legitimate. Be cautious if someone unexpectedly claims your account has been compromised or demands immediate payment. Instead of clicking a link, open the company's official app or visit its website directly. Never share a verification code with someone who contacts you unexpectedly. Criminals often create pressure because they want you to act before checking the details.

Kurt's key takeaways

What concerns me most about this wave of AI-powered cyberattacks is the speed. Microsoft documented attackers gaining privileged access in less than three hours. That's a frighteningly short window for companies to react. At the same time, AI is helping security researchers uncover weaknesses before criminals exploit them. But here's what worries me. We trust companies with enormous amounts of personal information, yet we're often left dealing with the fallout when their security fails. I believe those companies need to be held more accountable. Until then, protecting our accounts and staying alert to suspicious activity remains our best defense.

If AI allows hackers to attack thousands of accounts in minutes, should companies face tougher penalties when they fail to protect our personal information? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

World.title: Netanyahu's bloc falls short as longtime allies reportedly weigh move that could end his rule
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Israel's final election count has confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its parliamentary majority, but whether opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot can assemble a government to replace him remains an open question as negotiations begin behind closed doors.

The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position.

Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. Final voter turnout reached 77.9%, according to the Central Elections Committee results.

ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW

But the numbers leave neither major bloc with the 61 seats required for a majority, opening a complex political struggle involving potential partnerships with Arab parties, ultra-Orthodox lawmakers or a unity government bringing together longtime rivals.

A source familiar with opposition discussions, who spoke to Fox News Digital on condition of anonymity, described the outcome as a "bitter stalemate," but not an impossible political situation.

The source said opposition leaders are approaching coalition negotiations with patience and experience rather than treating the inconclusive results as a defeat, arguing that the next government could depend on their ability to forge partnerships that previously seemed unlikely.

FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER

Ultra-Orthodox allies explore a break with Netanyahu

In a potentially significant development Friday, Israeli journalist Yishai Cohen of Kikar HaShabbat reported that Rabbi Dov Lando, a leading ultra-Orthodox religious authority, had instructed lawmakers from Degel HaTorah, part of United Torah Judaism, to open discussions with the opposition.

According to the report, the objective is to reach an arrangement protecting the status of yeshiva students amid the longstanding dispute over mandatory military service.

Channel 12 reported that figures within the ultra-Orthodox party were considering allowing an Eisenkot-led minority government to survive through outside parliamentary support, potentially breaking with Netanyahu.

"Our votes are not in Netanyahu's pocket," party figures told Channel 12, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language report.

However, the office of United Torah Judaism Chairman Yaakov Asher denied that any instruction to begin negotiations had been issued.

Such an arrangement would represent a significant shift from the party's longstanding alliance with Netanyahu. Eisenkot's pledge to expand military conscription among ultra-Orthodox men remains a major obstacle, although Channel 12 reported that party figures were willing to consider a compromise on the issue.

The source familiar with opposition discussions told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot's camp had been preparing for the possibility of cooperation with ultra-Orthodox parties well before the election, suggesting that some of the options now being discussed had already been under consideration behind the scenes.

According to the source, such an arrangement could require compromises over military service and potentially outside parliamentary support from Arab lawmakers, bringing together political factions whose positions appeared irreconcilable during the campaign.

FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE

Arab parties signal flexibility, but obstacles remain

Another possibility rests with the Arab parties, which nearly doubled their parliamentary representation from 10 to 19 seats following a surge in turnout.

But the prospects of an Arab-backed government have drawn conflicting assessments.

Channel 12 reported Thursday that Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas had expressed deep skepticism about the possibility of establishing an Eisenkot-led minority government supported by Arab lawmakers.

Israeli political commentator Amit Segal also argued that the available options had narrowed considerably, identifying a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity government or another election as the two principal remaining possibilities.

Mohammed Majadla, head of the news division at Radio Nas and a Channel 12 political commentator, offered a different assessment in an interview with Fox News Digital, arguing that both Ra'am and the Joint List were prepared to use their parliamentary influence to prevent Netanyahu from returning to power.

"The two Arab lists agree on two things," Majadla said in the Hebrew-language interview. "First, they are prepared to do everything within the political process to ensure Netanyahu does not return to power."

According to Majadla, that could include joining a coalition, providing outside parliamentary support or abstaining from key votes.

He said their second shared priority was avoiding another election, which Arab political leaders fear could reverse their gains.

"The ball is now in Eisenkot's court, not in the Arab parties' court," Majadla said. "As far as the Arab parties are concerned, I can tell you they are truly prepared to do everything to make this happen."

Majadla suggested that public declarations should not necessarily be treated as final positions, particularly as parties seek leverage during coalition negotiations.

The difficulties extend beyond the Arab parties. Eisenkot's potential partners include politicians who strongly oppose cooperation with ultra-Orthodox factions, while several opposition leaders campaigned against relying on Arab lawmakers to govern.

NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING

Unity government or another election?

A national unity government involving Likud and Yashar would offer a more straightforward mathematical route to a majority, but would require Eisenkot to reconsider his campaign pledge not to join a Netanyahu-led government.

For Netanyahu, the lengthy coalition formation process could provide additional opportunities. If Eisenkot receives the mandate to form a government but fails, President Isaac Herzog could assign the task to another candidate, potentially giving Netanyahu another chance to assemble a coalition. If successive efforts fail, Israel could face another election.

Despite the obstacles, the source familiar with opposition discussions pointed to Bennett and Lapid's experience navigating complex coalition negotiations as an important asset.

"They've both played this game many times. They know it, and they're not rattled," the source said, according to a translation of the Hebrew-language conversation.

The source suggested that Bennett's experience working with Netanyahu gives him a particular understanding of the prime minister's negotiating tactics, while Lapid brings additional experience in coalition-building.

Former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, one of the opposition's senior figures, acknowledged Friday that forming a government would be considerably more difficult than campaigning against Netanyahu.

"Now comes the truly hard part: trying to form a government," Lapid wrote on X, urging supporters to remain patient.

"It takes place in small rooms, slowly, away from the cameras," he wrote, according to a translation of his Hebrew-language statement, emphasizing the importance of negotiations conducted out of public view.

The negotiations will also unfold against the backdrop of the Trump administration's Middle East agenda.

The source familiar with opposition discussions said understanding Washington's regional priorities could become an important consideration in shaping a future government, although no specific American role in coalition negotiations has been confirmed.

The election results are scheduled to be formally submitted to President Herzog on November 4, following remaining verification procedures. The new Knesset is expected to be sworn in November 10.
