World.title: Paid to hire, paid to work: Inside India’s Rs 99,446 cr plan to reshape the formal workforce
World.content:
The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) is a central government scheme designed to encourage formal employment by offering financial incentives to both employers and employees.

It provides money to first-time workers entering jobs covered by the Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), while also rewarding companies that expand their workforce and retain new hires.

Approved by the Union Cabinet on July 1, 2025, the scheme has a total outlay of Rs 99,446 crore.

PMVBRY has two components. Under Part A, eligible first-time employees receive a one-time incentive equivalent to one monthâs EPF wage, capped at Rs 15,000.

Part B provides incentives to employers who create additional jobs. Eligible employers can receive up to Rs 3,000 per month for each qualifying additional employee. The scheme covers eligible jobs created between August 1, 2025 and July 31, 2027. Manufacturing establishments receive support for four years, compared with two years for employers in other sectors.

The government aims to incentivise more than 3.5 crore jobs over two years, including 1.92 crore first-time employees.





These are government targets, not independent estimates of jobs expected to be created.

The scheme addresses a structural weakness in India's employment landscape: the limited availability of regular, salaried work.

According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation's Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) for 2025, 56.2 per cent of India's workers are self-employed and another 20.2 per cent are engaged in casual labour.

Regular wage or salaried employment accounts for just 23.6 per cent of the workforce.

The challenge, therefore, extends beyond reducing unemployment. It is also about expanding access to stable, formal jobs that offer workers social security and a more predictable source of income. PMVBRY is the government's attempt to encourage that transition.

Where are Indiaâs jobs?

The PLFS Annual Report 2025 estimated that India had 61.6 crore employed people aged 15 and above.

Distribution of India's workforce

Agriculture remained the largest employer, accounting for 43 per cent of workers. Manufacturing accounted for 12.1 per cent, construction 12 per cent, trade, hotels and restaurants 12.9 per cent, transport, storage and communications 5.8 per cent, and other services 13.1 per cent. Mining and quarrying accounted for 0.3 per cent, while electricity, water and related services made up 0.7 per cent.

Grouped broadly, the figures put around 43.3 per cent of workers in the primary sector, including agriculture and mining.

Another 24.8 per cent are in the secondary sector, including manufacturing, utilities and construction, and 31.8 per cent in the tertiary sector, including trade, transport and other services. These are employment shares, not shares of GDP or GVA.

Employment status adds another dimension. In 2025, 56.2 per cent of workers were self-employed, 23.6 per cent were in regular wage or salaried employment and 20.2 per cent were casual labourers.

The unemployment rate for people aged 15 and above was 3.1 per cent under the surveyâs usual-status measure, while it was 9.9 per cent among people aged 15 to 29.

Year-on-year comparisons need caution. The ministry revised the PLFS sampling design in January 2025 and shifted the annual reference period from JulyâJune to JanuaryâDecember. It advises care when comparing the new series with earlier reports. The reported fall in agricultureâs share from 44.8 per cent in 2024 to 43 per cent in 2025, and the rise in manufacturing from 11.6 per cent to 12.1 per cent, are not conclusive evidence of a structural shift.

PMVBRY targets a narrower problem: formal payroll employment recorded through EPFO. It is not an employment guarantee and does not directly address self-employment, casual work or agricultural underemployment.

Why manufacturing is central

PMVBRY covers eligible establishments across sectors but gives manufacturing employers a longer incentive period. Its official guidelines say the scheme is intended to complement the National Manufacturing Mission by promoting new industries and expanding existing ones, particularly in labour-intensive manufacturing.

Under the revised national-accounts series with 2022â23 as the base year, manufacturing accounted for 14.7 per cent of GVA in 2022â23 and 2023â24, and 14.8 per cent in provisional estimates for 2025â26, according to the ministry of statistics and programme implementation. The figures are not directly comparable with estimates under the previous base year.

The employment picture is distinct. PLFS 2025 put manufacturingâs share of workers at 12.1 per cent.

Separately, the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) results for 2023â24 reported that employment in covered manufacturing establishments rose 5.92 per cent over the previous year, reaching nearly 1.96 crore persons engaged. The ASI covers registered manufacturing establishments within its survey scope, not every manufacturing worker in India.

A working paper by Sangeeta Ghosh at the Institute for Studies in Industrial Development,

Looking Through Employment Elasticities

, found employment elasticities above 0.5 in many of the 55 organised manufacturing industries it studied for the period from the mid-2000s.

Employment elasticity measures the relationship between output growth and employment growth. However, the paper also found that more than 40 per cent of new employment generated between 2008 and 2017â18 was contract employment. It focuses on organised manufacturing, so its findings cannot automatically be applied to the whole sector.

The four-year incentive window signals the governmentâs view that manufacturing, particularly labour-intensive segments, can generate sustained employment.

The National Manufacturing Mission, announced in the 2025â26 Union Budget, is part of the wider push.

What employers receive, and what startups need to know

Under Part B, employers can receive up to Rs 3,000 a month for each additional employee whose gross wages at joining are up to Rs 1 lakh, subject to the schemeâs conditions. The incentive covers eligible first-time employees and re-joiners. The amount depends on EPF wages:

Your eligibility, as an employer, for the scheme.

For employees earning below Rs 10,000, it is 10 per cent of wages, up to Rs 1,000.

For those earning more than Rs 10,000 and up to Rs 20,000, it is Rs 2,000.

For those earning above Rs 20,000, it is Rs 3,000, subject to the gross-wage ceiling.

The incentive is paid in six-monthly lump sums after the relevant six months of employment and electronic challan-cum-return filings.

The employee must stay with the same employer for at least six months, with contributions received for that period. Employers must also maintain a minimum net additional-employment threshold. Those with a baseline below 50 employees must add at least two, while those with a baseline of 50 or more must add at least five.

Incentives do not accrue for months when the applicable threshold is not met.

The baseline is central to eligibility. For existing EPFO-registered employers, it is based on average employment during the relevant period before the scheme.

For new establishments registered with EPFO between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027, the baseline is fixed at 20 employees. Only qualifying additional jobs above that baseline and beyond the applicable hiring threshold can count towards the incentive.

Startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) do not receive a separate incentive rate or automatic exemption from these rules. They can benefit if they are eligible establishments, comply with EPFO filing requirements and create qualifying additional employment.

A new establishment with a baseline of 20, for instance, cannot claim the employer incentive merely by hiring a few people while remaining below the baseline and threshold.

Consider an eligible employee with EPF wages of Rs 18,000, for whom the monthly incentive would be Rs 2,000. If the employer meets the hiring test and remains eligible for all 24 months, the notional incentive for that employee would be Rs 48,000.

For a manufacturing establishment, the incentive can continue for 48 months, making the corresponding maximum Rs 96,000. These are illustrative calculations, not guaranteed payouts.

What first-time employees receive

Part A supports first-time employees earning up to Rs 1 lakh a month with an incentive equivalent to one monthâs EPF wage, capped at Rs 15,000. The first instalment, capped at Rs 7,500, is payable after six completed months. The second follows 12 months of service and completion of a financial-literacy programme.

A portion of it is placed in a savings instrument or deposit account.

Benefits for first-time employees.

Can the incentives create additional jobs?

The central question surrounding PMVBRY is whether lowering the cost of hiring will persuade companies to create jobs they would not otherwise have offered.

Employment subsidies carry an inherent risk: governments may end up paying companies for recruitment that would have happened anyway. There is also the possibility that employers could replace existing workers with eligible employees to qualify for incentives.

These are recognised risks in evaluating employment subsidies, not evidence that such practices have occurred under PMVBRY.

The government's initial implementation figures offer an indication of the scheme's reach. In a backgrounder published on August 1, 2026, the Press Information Bureau said more than 72 lakh first-time employees had joined the formal workforce since August 2025. Nearly 30 per cent of the beneficiaries were women, while more than 15 lakh beneficiaries had received employment-linked incentives.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

These are government-reported figures.

PMVBRY is an attempt to use public money to make formal hiring more attractive, with manufacturing receiving a longer period of support. But the scale of enrolment and the amount of incentives disbursed will not, by themselves, establish whether the policy has succeeded.

The real test will be whether the scheme creates additional jobs, whether those jobs offer stable employment and whether employers retain workers after government support runs out. For India, the challenge is not simply to move more people onto formal payrolls, but to ensure that the jobs they enter are productive, secure and sustainable.

World.title: Form 7 row: Supreme Court directs EC to probe bulk applications during Uttar Pradesh SIR
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Friday directed the

(EC) to examine allegations of irregularities in the bulk submission of Form 7 applications during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in

and take necessary corrective measures.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the petitioners to submit a note to the EC detailing the "unresolved irregularities" they had flagged.

"The irregularities which have been brought to the notice of the court shall be submitted to senior counsel appearing for the Election Commission of India by way of a note. On receipt thereof, let the Election Commission examine the factual aspects, thereafter take necessary corrective steps and file a compliance report," the bench said, according to PTI.

The Supreme Court was hearing petitions filed by Congress MP Tanuj Punia and others challenging the SIR exercise in Uttar Pradesh. More than 13 crore electors were

in the final electoral roll ahead of the assembly elections scheduled in the state early next year.

that over 2.04 crore names were removed from the electoral rolls during the revision.

During the hearing, counsel for the petitioners alleged that 32 Form 7 applications had been submitted in one constituency to target members of a particular community.





Senior advocate DS Naidu, appearing for the EC, acknowledged that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed but said no action had been taken on them.

"We found that bulk Form 7 applications had been submitted. Our officers checked and cross-checked them. They were false, and we have not acted upon them," Naidu told the court.

World.title: 'Want to sow confusion': BJP targets Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc's 'Delhi Chalo' march
World.content:

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Friday launched a scathing attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of trying to spread anarchy on the streets and undermining India's democratic traditions.Addressing a press conference, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi termed the Congress leader a "Dimagi Naxal" and questioned his conduct."The Naxalites on the ground may be eliminated, but the 'Dimagi Naxals' are there in Delhi. Consider the conduct displayed by the leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi. Whether in the history of India or anywhere else in the world where conditions of anarchy prevail, you will invariably find such figures stirring up chaos," Trivedi said."In India, however, we see a peculiar situation: the leader of the opposition is seen entering the Akashvani Bhawan, lying down on the road in front of the Prime Ministerâs residence, or marching towards the Supreme Court. Statements are made suggesting that matters will no longer be settled in Parliament, but on the streets - that they will be decided not through discussion, but through resistance," he added.The BJP's Rajya Sabha member also targeted the opposition and said that its true intent was rooted in a mindset characterised by a desire for plunder after attaining power."Their (opposition) true intent - as articulated by the Prime Minister - is rooted in a mindset characterised by a desire for plunder upon attaining power, the sowing of division within society, and a deep-seated hatred for Indiaâs religious and cultural ethos."We want to draw your attention to the fact that, over the last ten to twelve years, there is hardly any institution or system in India regarding which they have not attempted to sow confusion. Why is the Congress party holding a rally on November 1? The area in Delhi where they are planning this event is a major hub for trade and commerce for all of North India - especially during this festive season, which spans from Navratri through Diwali and Chhath Puja," Trivedi said.Meanwhile, INDIA bloc's "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has been postponed to October 31 due to the rains. Rahul Gandhi asserted that the countdown to the exit of the poll body chief was accelerating.The Congress leader reiterated that "this is not multiple protests" but "one protest", with the opposition standing together to defend the Constitution."By consensus, we have decided to postpone today's programme to tomorrow because of rain. We felt that it would be uncomfortable for seniors to sit in the rain, and we would do the exact same programme tomorrow," Gandhi said at a joint press conference with INDIA bloc leaders outside Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg.

World.title: 'They plotted': Ex-Manipur CM Biren Singh blames BJP leaders for ouster, questions continued violence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former

has accused sections of the state BJP leadership of conspiring with the Congress to remove him from office. Singh also questioned the continued violence in the state since his resignation in February 2025.

In an exclusive interview with PTI, Singh said the BJP government must urgently work to "regain the lost confidence and trust of the people" ahead of assembly elections due early next year. He also claimed there was strong public demand for his return as chief minister.

"I had not been treated well since 2017. I am not accusing the Delhi leadership but sections of the state leaders who conspired against me with the Congress,â Singh told PTI.

He alleged that some party colleagues resented his elevation despite having switched from the Congress to the BJP.

âThere are MLAs who could never accept how I became CM twice after having crossed over from the Congress. They consider BJP as their property. So they plotted, planned and made me resign," he added.

Singh also challenged the argument that his removal would help restore peace in the state, pointing to continuing clashes involving Meitei, Kuki and Naga communities.





The present government, led by Y Khemchand Singh, took office in February this year.

"Now Biren is out. So, what happened now? How many Naga brothers have died? They were blaming me. They were saying I favour the majority. Now it is Christians versus Christians. Where has the European Union gone?" he asked.

His remarks come amid renewed violence in the state. Three Meitei villagers were shot dead and three others injured in an ambush by suspected militants inside a forest along the Imphal East-Kangpokpi border on Monday.

The victims were part of a group collecting firewood near Nongshum and Khongbal Tangkhul villages when the attack took place.

The killings triggered protests in Imphal, with demonstrators carrying the bodies of two victims to a sit-in outside the chief minister's official residence. Security personnel later used tear gas to disperse the crowd. The latest killings come amid escalating clashes between Kuki-Zo and Naga groups in the hill districts, with more than 50 people reportedly killed on either side over the past eight months.

NEW DELHI: The six people on board a helicopter operated by Trans Bharat Aviation died after it crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday afternoon. The helicopter was travelling from Badrinath to Dehradun when it crashed into a hillside near Chai village."All six people on board chopper that crashed in Joshimath have died, their bodies found," Chamoli Superintendent of Police Surjit Singh Panwar told PTI.The helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm. Authorities lost track of it while it was crossing the Joshimath Valley and it was subsequently reported missing near Hathi Parvat.Search and rescue teams, including personnel from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Army, police and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), were deployed to the area following reports of the crash.According to the available details, six people were on board the helicopter, including the pilot and five passengers, all reportedly from Bengaluru. Their identities are as follows:Captain HimanshuSpeaking to PTI in Dehradun, Prateek Jain, CEO of the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA), said "the helicopter took off from Badrinath for Sahastradhara Heliport at 1.14 pm today.As it was crossing the Joshimath Valley, we suddenly lost track of it on our tracking system, which we use to monitor its movements. We have also received some local information regarding the incident.""So far, nothing has been confirmed. However, according to the information available in the passenger manifest, a total of six people were on board the helicopter, the pilot and five passengers. The helicopter's location has not yet been traced. However, search and rescue teams have been mobilised in coordination with the Chamoli district administration," he said."The SDRF has also been deployed, along with a unit of the Army. As soon as the weather clears, we will send another rescue helicopter from here to locate the missing helicopter," Jain added.Local inputs about the incident also prompted authorities to initiate a search operation.Sub-Inspector Manohar Kanyal of Joshimath police post said information about the incident was received from the Joshimath sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) at 2.21 pm."At 14:21 hrs, information was received from the SDM Joshimath regarding the crash landing of a helicopter above Chai village in the Joshimath area," Kanyal told ANI."In this regard, UCADA officials stated that the location of a Trans Bharat helicopter, which was flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara, is showing near the Army Camp above Chai village. Complete details regarding the crash or crash landing are not yet available," he added.Speaking to ANI, Jain said the helicopter belonged to Trans Bharat Aviation and confirmed that the companyâs entire fleet had been grounded as a precautionary measure."A helicopter belonging to Trans Bharat Aviation departed from Badrinath for the Sahastradhara heliport at 1:14 PM. We have been unable to trace the helicopter's location since it was passing through the vicinity of the Joshimath valley. Upon receiving this information, we mobilised the Chamoli district administration, the SDRF (State Disaster Response Force), and an Army unit to the area near the incident site to prepare for a proper rescue operation," he said."As a precautionary measure, the entire fleet of helicopters belonging to Trans Bharat Aviation has been grounded...According to initial information, there were 6 people on boardâthe pilot plus 5 others. We will share further details once we have confirmation..." he added.The grounding is a precautionary step as authorities work to establish the circumstances surrounding the crash.Uttarakhand disaster management officials in Chamoli district said teams had rushed to the area to conduct search and rescue operations. Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel were dispatched to the reported crash site.The location of the helicopter and the condition of the people on board remained unclear in the initial hours after the incident. Authorities were coordinating with the district administration and other agencies to locate the aircraft and assess the situation.It was also not immediately confirmed whether the helicopter was returning after ferrying pilgrims from the Badrinath shrine.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said he was closely monitoring the situation and that a joint rescue operation was under way.In a post on X, Dhami said, "Reports have been received regarding an unfortunate helicopter crash near Chai village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, the Disaster Management Department, and the SDRF.""I am personally monitoring the situation closely. I have issued instructions to ensure that those who are critically injured are immediately airlifted to a higher-level medical facility for better treatment. I pray to God for the safety of the passengers," Dhami added.The state government said the rescue operation was being coordinated by the district administration and disaster management authorities.The crash took place amid adverse weather conditions in Uttarakhand, with rainfall and snowfall reported in several parts of the state.Television channels reported that fire and smoke were visible at the crash site and that rescue teams had reached the area. Bad weather was suspected to have contributed to the incident, though the cause had not been officially established.Kedarnath Dham witnessed the season's first heavy snowfall following continuous snowfall since Thursday, October 29. The surrounding hills were covered in snow, while temperatures in the region dropped significantly.The India Meteorological Department's Dehradun centre also forecast continued rainfall over the next few days, particularly in the hill districts.Dr CS Tomar, director of the Meteorological Centre in Dehradun, said heavy rainfall had been recorded at eight to nine places across Uttarakhand on October 29, particularly in Uttarkashi, Tehri and Haridwar districts.Tomar said similar weather conditions were expected on Friday, with a higher likelihood of rainfall in the Kumaon region."Tomorrow, on the 31st, chances of light to very light rain will persist, especially in the hilly districts. Similarly, on the 1st and 2nd (of November), light to very light rain may be witnessed at isolated places, particularly in our northern hilly districts," he said.In view of the forecast, district administrations have been placed on alert to ensure the safety of pilgrims, residents and commuters.Earlier on Thursday, District Magistrate Prashant Arya directed officials to activate the District Emergency Operations Centre (DEOC) in alert mode to monitor weather conditions and oversee precautionary measures.Authorities are also monitoring road conditions and the Gangotri and Yamunotri shrines through live CCTV cameras.The administration has appealed to devotees and pilgrims to take precautions against the cold and follow advisories issued by the administration and police.

World.title: 'I will be present in court': Anant Singh to surrender by Dec 1 after SC cancels bail; accuses Neeraj Kumar of plotting case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Expelled JD(U) MLA

on Friday said he would surrender before the court by December 1 in compliance with the

's order cancelling his bail in the Dularchand Yadav murder case.

He accused newly elected JD(U) MLC

of orchestrating the case against him and claimed that he had been deliberately implicated.

Reacting to the Supreme Court's decision, Singh said he had faith in the judiciary and would abide by its directions. He also expressed confidence that he would be granted bail again.

"We will surrender. The court is not our enemy; whatever the court has decided is acceptable to us. The court will grant us bail again later.

We have faith in the judiciary. We always had faith, and we still have faith today," Singh told reporters in Patna.

Asked when he would surrender, the Mokama MLA said, "Why should I surrender early? I have full faith in the court and the judiciary. On whatever date is designated for me, I will be present in court."

He subsequently confirmed that he would appear before the court on December 1.

Singh alleged that Neeraj Kumar was behind the legal action against him and had ensured that his name was included in the murder case.





"This incident was orchestrated by Neeraj Kumar. First, from 3 kilometres away, he got my name added to the Dularchand murder case. After that, when I had been on bail here for six months, Neeraj took the case to Delhi. We only found out after everything had already transpired. They never issued any notice or informed us of anything; they did everything behind the scenes," he alleged.

Asked whether he believed the Supreme Court's decision was the result of Neeraj Kumar's opposition, Singh said, "No, we don't believe that.

You people claim the government did it--we don't accept that. Neeraj did it."

He also accused Neeraj Kumar of being behind Yadav's murder and claimed that false witnesses had been brought forward to implicate him.

âNeeraj got Dularchand murdered himself. He orchestrated it to immediately implicate Anant Singh and send him to jail. He brought false witnesses from his own locality, made them testify,â Singh alleged.

Anant Singh recounts events leading to murder

Recounting the events of October 30, 2025, Singh claimed that he was campaigning for votes when his convoy crossed paths with a vehicle carrying Dularchand Yadav, who was supporting a Jan Suraaj Party candidate.

"During the election, we were out asking for votes. There was a Jan Suraaj candidate, and Dularchand was in that vehicle. As we were returning after campaigning, we crossed paths with Dularchand on the road.

After that, he went his way, and we went ours. When we had travelled about 4 to 5 kilometres, news spread that a clash had erupted right where we had just eaten," he said.

Singh maintained that he learnt about Yadav's murder only after returning from campaigning in another village.

According to the FIR registered at Ghoswari police station, Singh and his aides allegedly dragged Yadav out of his vehicle, shot him in the leg, assaulted him and ran him over with an SUV.

Singh has denied the allegations and previously claimed that Jan Suraaj supporters attacked his convoy first.

Singh links expulsion to dispute with Neeraj Kumar

The expelled MLA also linked his removal from the JD(U) to his differences with Neeraj Kumar, saying the party leadership had acted in support of the MLC.

"The party claims we opposed the party--we did not oppose the party, we opposed Neeraj," he said, referring to his campaign for Jan Suraaj candidate Anuj Kumar Singh against the JD(U)'s official nominee Neeraj Kumar in the Patna Graduates' constituency MLC election.

Singh expressed confidence in former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar, claiming that the developments would not have taken place had the JD(U) leader been in good health and actively involved in party affairs.

"I firmly believe that had Nitish Kumar ji been in good health and conscious of things, this would never have happened. The party wouldnât have tossed me out like a fly from milk. Now that they have expelled me, the party will reap what it sows.

They will struggle even to open their account," Singh said.

Asked if he considered the matter a case of political vendetta, he said, âNo, it isnât politics. It is personal. Itâs Neeraj. And the party backed Neeraj.â

Singh said he would not approach any political leader for intervention and would follow the court's directions.

"I will not go to anyone regarding this matter. Nowhere at all. Whatever the court directs, I will abide by the court's word.

If the court summons me, I will go to court," he said.

On the multiple cases registered against him, Singh said, âDeceitful people keep implicating me, and I keep getting justice from the courts. By count, there may be 60 or 70 cases. When the judges examine the facts, they will deliver justice to me. I have done nothing wrong.â

Supreme Court cancels bail

Earlier on Friday, the Supreme Court cancelled the bail granted to Singh by the Patna High Court on March 19, 2026, and directed him to surrender before the authorities on or before December 1.

A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PV Varale observed that the High Court had erred in granting bail without adequately considering the gravity of the offence and Singh's criminal antecedents. The bail order was challenged by Neeraj Kumar, the grandson of the deceased.

The development comes days after the JD(U) expelled Singh and his wife, Neelam Devi, for six years, citing anti-party activities. Following the action, the Bihar government removed Neelam Devi from her position on the State-Level Programme Implementation Committee and withdrew her Minister of State rank and entitlement to an official bungalow.

The party has also approached Bihar Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar seeking Singh's disqualification under the Anti-Defection Law.

World.title: Special court reserves orders on Central Crime Branch’s petition for custody of Anbil Mahesh
World.content:
A special court for Prevention of Corruption Act cases on Friday (October 30, 2026) reserved orders on a petition filed by the Central Crime Branch (CCB) for five days of police custody of former School Education Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi. The court adjourned the case to November 2.

Mr. Poyyamozhi was arrested on October 26 in a case of alleged bribery in the grant of permanent recognition to private schools during the DMK government.

Mr. Poyyamozhi was produced in the court when the petition came up before Judge L.S. Sathyamoorthy.

Opposing police custody, senior counsel Abudukumar Rajarathinam, appearing for Mr. Poyyamozhi, submitted that the former Minister had already been questioned for eight hours on September 18 and had fully cooperated with the investigators. The defence had also offered to provide any additional document, required by the investigators, leaving no reason for further custodial interrogation, he argued.

Additional Public Prosecutor Usha Rani told the court that Mr. Poyyamozhi would receive appropriate medical care in prison. She sought time to respond to his request for home-cooked food, prompting the defence to question the need for further delay.

Mr. Sathyamoorthy then questioned investigating officer Senthil about the need for custodial interrogation. The officer replied that the police must establish the movement of the alleged proceeds of the offence, examine the assets of Mr. Poyyamozhi and his family members, identify the alleged benamis, and scrutinise the property documents relating to his relatives. The investigators also need to ascertain details of events during the period when former MLA Muthukumar was absconding, he said. Muthukumar is a key accused in the case.

Mr. Senthil sought five days of custody and assured the court that the police would comply with all conditions imposed by it.

The judge reserved orders and directed that Mr. Poyyamozhi be produced before the court on November 2.

World.title: Keralam Home Minister cautions police officers against opposing Operation Toofan
World.content:
Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has warned that any police officer who takes a stand against Operation Toofan will not remain in service. Addressing a programme in Haripad on Friday, Mr. Chennithala said the initiative was launched to prevent children from falling victim to drug abuse.

According to him, Operation Toofan is one of the most important initiatives of the State government. Around 99% of police personnel are working with utmost sincerity. The initiative has received massive public support.

He added that any police personnel found to be involved in malpractice would not be spared. If anyone has tampered with seized evidence, they would not remain in service. Strict action would be taken in such cases, he said.

World.title: Forest personnel trained in mitigating man – wild animal conflict, crisis management inside forest
World.content:
A team of forest commandos from Chennai trained the forest personnel on Friday on mitigating man – wild animal conflict and rescuing the animals and injured human beings from the forests.

Since the Western Ghats from Kadayam to Sivagiri in Tenkasi district is a haven for the wild animals ranging from elephant to Guar and panther to tiger, invasion of these animals into the ranches in search of food and water often leads to serious conflicts, which had even become fatal in the past.

Despite the trenches dug in the vulnerable areas along the forest boundary and the solar electric fence erected between the ranches and the forest, wild animal invasion into the fields where the farmers raise paddy, coconut, mango, lemon and vegetables, continue and the farmers suffer crop loss. Around ten farmers or farmhands have been seriously injured in the Indian gaur and bear attack in the district in the past few years.

When the invasion intensified, AI-based cameras were installed at the porous points to monitor the movement of wild animals as they cross the forest boundary to enter the fields and initiate counter measures to chase them back into the Western Ghats.

Since wild animal invasion into the ranches close to the reserve forest boundaries of the district and consequent man – animal conflict has become perpetual story, the Tenkasi Forest Division, led by District Forest Officer R. Rajmohan organised this 2-day training programme on minimising these incidents.

“Now, the forest personnel are being trained by the members of an elite force, who are experts in mitigating these conflicts and rescuing wild animals distress and the human being injured in wild animal attack,” said Dr. Rajmohan.

The experts trained the forest personnel and anti-poaching watchers of Tenkasi district during the training session held in the jungles close to Adavinainarkovil Dam area in Vadakarai.

The training included safely crossing rivers and wild streams, camping inside the forest, night patrolling inside dense forest areas, rope climbing, rock climbing, firing with rifles, handling explosives, first-aid, monitoring movement of elephant, Indian gaur, bear, panther and tiger, judging the attitude of elephants by watching the earlobe movement and its look, safely retreating during unexpected encounters with wild elephants, Indian gaur and other wild animals during patrolling etc.

The participants, led by Dr. Rajmohan and Assistant Conservator of Forest Nellainayagam, were also trained in controlling and extinguishing forest fire with available resources.

“This session has given new outlook to our personnel in handling emergency situations inside and along the forest boundary. Since we frequently experience wild elephant invasion into the ranches, monitoring elephant movement, giving warning to the public, sending the elephants safely back into the forest, handling of equipments while rescuing injured wild animals and human beings and shifting them for treatment, forest fire control, evacuation, rapid sharing of information and coordination etc. The training has given new dimension to our personnel’s approach in their day-to-day functioning,” said Dr. Rajmohan.

World.title: Thaladi paddy raised on 1.5 lakh acres in Thanjavur district against target of 3 lakh acres, says Collector
World.content:
Paddy has been raised on about 1.05 lakh acres under the samba/thaladi season in Thanjavur district so far, according to Collector R. Revathi.

Speaking at farmers’ grievances day meeting here on Friday, Ms. Revathi said about three lakh acres were targeted to be covered under samba/thaladi seasons this year and so far the crop had been cultivated on 1,05,339 acres. About 518 tonnes of seeds were available with the Agricultural Extension Centers and another 1,712 tonnes were available with private distributors.

Adequate quantities of fertilisers including urea, DAP and complex fertilisers were available in the district. Agriculture and Revenue department officials were conducting a survey to assess possible damage to the standing crops due to the recent rain.

During the kuruvai season, paddy was raised on 1.59 lakh acres in the district and so far harvest has been completed on 1.54 lakh acres. About 83,195 tonnes of paddy had been procured so far through 234 direct purchase centers from 15,595 farmers, who had been paid ₹217. 53 crore.

For the 2026-27 kuruvai season, ₹18.35 crore was being disbursed as compensation under the prevented sowing clause of the Prime Minister’s crop insurance scheme to farmers in 49 villages in Thanjavur, Budalur, and Thiruvaiyaru taluks in the district, she said and appealed to farmers to insure their samba/thaladi crops by paying the premium by the last date of November 16.

Earlier, a cross-section of farmers’ representatives of the district urged the government to extend the last date for payment of premium for insuring the samba/thaladi crops. They demanded that tenant farmers be allowed to insure their crops too. The farmers urged the district administration to ensure 20-hour three-phase power supply to farm connections as a large number of farmers had to use motor pump sets to irrigate their crops as the water release from Mettur has been stopped.

World.title: Railway police arrest four for robbery in Salem
World.content:
The Salem Railway Police arrested four persons in connection with a robbery on Friday (October 30).

On Monday evening around 5 p.m., S. Sri Ganesan (27), a resident of Hasthampatti crossed the railway track between Salem Town and Salem Market. At that time, five persons robbed him of his 10 sovereign gold chain at knifepoint and fled.

The Railway police registered a case under Section 304 (4) of BNS and on Friday arrested M. Gunaseela (30) of Narayana Nagar in Kitchipalayam; R. Dinesh Kumar (22) of Kurinji Nagar in Kitchipalayam; D. Shariffa (37) of Karim Compound in Kitchipalayam; and G. Gautameswaran (27) of Narayana Nagar, and recovered 10 grams of gold chain and two knives from them.

The police are on lookout for one more accused, Ismail (32), who is absconding. The four were produced before the court and were remanded to prison.

Police sources said that CCTV camera footage was used to identify the accused. Their mobile tower signals were monitored, and they were found roaming at Salem Railway Junction, where they were subsequently nabbed.

There are six cases pending against the accused, Gunaseela, in various police stations in Salem City, sources added.

World.title: Teacher held for kidnapping minor girl
World.content:
A temporary physical education teacher of a government-aided school in Puliyangudi was arrested for allegedly kidnapping a minor girl student of the school.

Police said E. Isai Dravid, 22, of Paambukoilsanthai near Puliyangudi in the district was working as temporary physical education teacher in a government-aided school in Puliyangudi. As he allegedly “threatened and kidnapped” a minor girl student of the school recently, she was rescued by her family. However, the girl’s parents did not file any complaint with the police.

On getting information about this incident, the District Child Protection Committee officials filed a complaint with the Puliyangudi All Women Police, who arrested Isai Dravid on Thursday under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.

He was remanded in judicial custody and lodged in Palaymkottai Central Prison on Friday.

World.title: Crime Branch alleges ‘deliberate manipulation’ in Kerala PSC examination
World.content:
A remand report filed by the Crime Branch has alleged deliberate manipulation in the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) examination conducted for the State Planning Board.

Such allegations have been detailed in the remand report of P. Satheesh, a former deputy secretary of the PSC, who was arrested in connection with the case.

According to the report, the irregularities were purportedly carried out with the knowledge of officials, including Mr. Satheesh and another officer, R. Hari, an additional secretary, who is presently absconding.

10 questions excluded

The police allege that 10 questions were intentionally excluded from the evaluation and that the online evaluation camp was closed without restoring those questions. The investigators suspect that the questions were deliberately withheld because their evaluation could have changed the ranking of candidates and prevented certain favoured persons from securing appointments.

Meanwhile, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) has issued notice to PSC secretary Saju George to appear for questioning in connection with the case on Saturday. The Controller of Examinations will also be summoned to seek clarification on the alleged involvement of PSC chairperson M.R. Baiju and the accused officials in the case.

Notices issued

The SIT has also decided to question the remaining PSC members. Notices will be issued to 10 PSC members directing them to appear for questioning.

The investigation team has sought to clarify alleged inconsistencies in the statements given by Mr. Baiju during questioning a few days ago. He reportedly maintained that the commission had not committed any errors in the Planning Board examination and that the irregularities resulted from technical errors committed by officials.

The SIT has also been expanded to speed up the investigation. Two Superintendents of Police and one Deputy Superintendent of Police have been added to the team. The three newly registered cases have been assigned to the investigating officers as part of the expanded probe.

World.title: DGP appreciates autorickshaw driver who helped in search for missing boy
World.content:
Director General of Police (DGP) Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal appreciated Prakash, an autorickshaw driver from Chennai, who assisted in tracing a 12-year-old boy from Krishnagiri district after he ran away from home.

The police said the boy left home after a disagreement with his parents. Based on a complaint lodged by the parents, a case was registered at the Singarapettai police station in Krishnagiri district. Acting on the instructions of the Superintendent of Police, Krishnagiri, personnel began a search and safely rescued the boy within 24 hours, subsequently handing him over to his parents.

Mr. Aggarwal met Prakash and appreciated him for lending his aid in the search for the boy. He also lauded Thennarasu, Inspector of Police, Uthangarai, who conducted an effective investigation in the case.

World.title: CDF Munir, Singapore's FM discuss regional security and bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir met with Singapore’s Foreign Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan on Friday, where the two discussed regional security and avenues for bilateral cooperation, according to the military’s media wing.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said the foreign minister, who is currently in the country on an official visit, called on CDF Munir at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi.

The two leaders discussed matters of mutual interest, evolving regional and global security dynamics and avenues for bilateral cooperation, it said.

“Both sides exchanged views on regional peace and stability and underscored the importance of sustained engagement and cooperation in areas of shared interest,” the statement read.

During the meeting, CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations with Singapore, including enhancing “institutional linkages and constructive engagement for promoting regional peace, stability and security”.

The Singaporean diplomat reciprocated the commitment and lauded the professionalism of Pakistan’s armed forces. He acknowledged Pakistan’s role in regional peace and stability, ISPR added.

PM admires Singapore’s ‘remarkable economic transformation’

Earlier, the foreign minister met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, during which the premier expressed admiration for Singapore’s “remarkable economic transformation” and achievements in innovation and development.

According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening its longstanding and friendly relations with Singapore, particularly as the two countries are commemorating the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations this year.

“The prime minister expressed admiration for Singapore’s remarkable economic transformation and achievements in innovation and development. He underscored the importance Pakistan attaches to its partnership with Singapore, both bilaterally and multilaterally including within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean),” it said.

The statement said that the two sides discussed ways to enhance bilateral trade and investment and expand cooperation in priority areas, including the digital economy, fintech, infrastructure development, logistics, small and medium enterprises and the services sector. They also discussed exploring new avenues for mutually beneficial economic cooperation and enhancing people-to-people contacts.

“The two sides also exchanged views on regional and international developments and reaffirmed their commitment to continued engagement and cooperation at bilateral and multilateral fora,” it said.

Possible resumption of direct flights discussed

The meetings came shortly after Dar discussed with the visiting diplomat the possible resumption of direct flights between Pakistan and Singapore “to facilitate business travel and close contact between our peoples”.

Dar shared this while addressing a press conference alongside Balakrishnan. He began by saying that Pakistan and Singapore enjoyed longstanding and friendly ties focused on mutual respect and goodwill, and Pakistan was one of the first countries to recognise Singapore following its independence in 1965.

He noted that Balakrishnan’s visit to Pakistan was the first one by a Singaporean foreign minister in over two decades.

“I am grateful that he was kind to accept my invitation,” he said, adding that the trip was particularly significant as the two countries were commemorating 60 years of diplomatic relations this year.

“The visit reflects our shared commitment to strengthen this friendship and broaden our cooperation.”

Dar said that delegation-level talks and a restricted meeting between the two sides earlier in the day focused on strengthening political and economic ties, expanding cooperation in technology and education and promoting culture and people-to-people contact.

“We also exchanged views on key regional and international developments,” he added.

He further stated that the two sides had recognised “the considerable untapped potential in our relationship” and stressed the importance of sustained engagement.

“We agreed to hold regular bilateral political consultation and promote high-level exchanges to strengthen cooperation between our governments and institutions,” he said, adding that economic cooperation was central to the discussions.

He said “we welcomed the significant growth” in bilateral trade between the two countries and discussed ways to build on this progress further.

“We agreed to encourage closer engagement between our business communities through the exchange of business delegations and stronger links between our chambers of commerce,” he elaborated.

Moreover, Dar continued, the reopening of the Trade and Investment Office at Pakistan’s High Commission in Singapore had also been discussed.

“The reopening of the Pakistan Trade and Investment Office is a testament to Pakistan’s resolve to promote stronger B2B ties with our friendly country Singapore.”

Beyond trade and investment, he said: “We discussed the scope for closer cooperation in education, research and innovation, including digital technologies and artificial intelligence. We also considered ways to strengthen links between our universities and research institutions. We also agreed to deepen cooperation in human resource development, agriculture and climate domains.”

Dar noted that Pakistani professionals in Singapore contributed to its economy and society and served as a “valuable bridge between our two nations”.

He said, “We agreed to encourage greater cultural, academic, youth and people-to-people exchanges.”

Moreover, he said, “We also discussed the possible resumption of direct flights to facilitate business travel and close contact between our peoples.”

Pakistan’s engagement with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) as the country’s “oldest sectoral dialogue partner” also came under discussion, Dar said.

“Pakistan attaches great importance to practical cooperation with the organisation and its member states. I convey Pakistan’s best wishes to Singapore as it prepares to assume the Asean chairmanship in 2027.

“We look forward to working closely with Singapore in support of its priorities as the chair and to further strengthening the Pakistan-Asean cooperation.”

Dar said the meetings in Islamabad also presented the opportunity to share perspectives on regional and international peace and the security landscape.

“We discussed the impact of regional tensions on maritime trade,” he said, adding that secure sea routes and uninterrupted supply chains were essential to trade and economic stability.

He said the two sides had reaffirmed the central role of dialogue and diplomacy, respect for international law and adherence to the principles of the UN Charter in addressing regional and global challenges.

The DPM said he had conveyed to the visiting dignitary that Pakistan remained engaged with key regional and international partners to encourage continued dialogue and diplomacy as it was the “only viable means to resolve outstanding challenges”.

On Palestine, he said, “I expressed concern over the continued expansion of illegal settlements and efforts to alter the status of the West Bank and Al-Quds Al-Sharif. I stressed the urgent need for unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza. I reiterated firm support for an independent, sovereign, viable, and contiguous state of Palestine based on pre-June 1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital, which is the stated policy of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan”.

In the context of South Asia, Dar said he briefed the visiting dignitary on the importance of a “just, durable and peaceful settlement of the longstanding Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions”.

He concluded his speech by saying: “We look forward to working very closely with Singapore to carry forward the understanding reached today. Pakistan and Singapore’s friendship remains strong and forward-looking as we mark 60 years of diplomatic relations.

“We have committed to deepening this partnership and building a more prosperous future for our people.”

Speaking after him, Balakrishnan began by saying: “This is a significant year for Singapore and Pakistan. We have never forgotten that Pakistan was one of the earliest countries to recognise Singapore’s independence. And that’s why we are commemorating the 60th anniversary of diplomatic ties.”

Over the years, he said, there had been high-level exchanges between the two countries.

He added that “we’ve had opportunities for a substantive and productive exchange of views”.

“We’re in constant communication, far more than people realise — that we have a very effective partnership.”

Balakrishnan continued that Pakistan and Singapore had “excellent ties” at the diplomatic level.

“In fact, they are so good that it makes it even more obvious that actual trade relations — and looking at the numbers and the data — ought to be much higher. And that, I would say, is the first order of business.

“We need to facilitate greater trade and investment flows. We need to strengthen the links, especially between SMEs, between businessmen, and they need to meet, they need to know each other, they need to understand the business opportunities and the risks on both sides in Southeast Asia as well as South Asia,” he added.

Balakrishnan said governments of the two countries needed to facilitate these interactions and identify new opportunities for mutually beneficial cooperation.

“In an increasingly uncertain global environment, including on the business side of it, I think it is all the more important for our two countries to remain open, connected and constructively engaged with each other,” he said.

The two sides, he said, also discussed carbon markets, which “we think is another fertile opportunity for Singapore and Pakistan to work together”.

“It will be another promising avenue to attract investments into projects in Pakistan that reduce emissions while supporting sustainable development, and our officials are exploring opportunities in this area.”

Speaking about the exchange of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on disaster management between Singapore and Pakistan, he said it reflected “our shared commitment to strengthen disaster preparedness and response”.

Disasters, he said, were not something one wished for. “But it is something which we have to prepare for and to be acutely aware that at the rate things are going, and with the progression of climate change, this is a current and clear threat. And the more we can work together and prepare together, the more resilient we will be”.

Unfortunately, Pakistan had extensive experience in responding to large-scale natural disasters, Balakrishnan said, adding that Singapore could learn from Pakistan in how to cope with disasters and be more resilient for the future.

“Through this MoU, we hope to explore cooperation in areas including early warning systems, the sharing of best practices, strengthening search and rescue capabilities, as well as hopefully conducting joint training and exercises.

“It’s again worth remembering that disasters do not respect boundaries, do not have passports, and again, the more we can work together, the better,” he added.

Moreover, the Singaporean foreign minister said “we welcome the opportunities to deepen cooperation between our institutes of higher learning, which includes the Nanyang Technological University and the National University of Singapore with Pakistan’s National University of Sciences and Technology”.

“I want to emphasise that this is just the beginning. We hope to expand that list in due time.”

On regional and international developments, he congratulated Dar for the “incredibly valuable role that Pakistan is playing”.

“For instance, we know there is crisis in the Gulf, and in fact, most of the energy that comes through the Gulf is actually headed to the east — South Asia, Southeast Asia, and to Northeast Asia.

“And the unique, but very constructive and valuable role that Pakistan plays is the one which we commend you for, and we wish you every success because if you succeed, it’s good for all of us.”

He emphasised that international law was critical for both Pakistan and Singapore.

And in the case of Singapore, he said, “because we are an island city state and our trade volume is three times our GDP, the maritime arena is essential. And therefore, the United Nations Convention of the Law of the Sea 1982, which sets out the freedom of navigation and overflight, especially in straits used for international navigation as a right not by the grace of littoral powers — This is of acute importance to us, and we are very, very heartened that Pakistan stands in exactly the same position this issue with us”.

He noted that Singapore would take the chairmanship of Asean next year while Pakistan was already the chair of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. This, he said, would present another set of opportunities for these two regional blocs, “two dynamic, diverse regional blocs, to look for opportunities to do together”.

He then moved on to education, saying that opportunities in this area were also discussed.

“We are living in an age of a new industrial revolution, AI and digital technologies, and it is essential to ensure that our young people have the relevant skills not for yesterday’s jobs, but for tomorrow’s jobs.

“And so, this emphasis on skills and relevant qualifications and capability and human talent development is another very important area for cooperation between Pakistan and Singapore,” he added.

Talks on enhancing trade, investment cooperation

Earlier, Dar and Balakrishnan held talks and discussed ways to enhance cooperation in trade and investment, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Balakrishnan arrived in Islamabad earlier in the day. He called on DPM Dar at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The FO said in a statement that the two leaders reviewed the “longstanding and friendly relations” between Pakistan and Singapore as the two countries marked 60 years of diplomatic relations.

They underscored the importance of sustained high-level exchanges and discussed ways to further enhance cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity and skills development, while promoting business-to-business exchanges and people-to-people contacts, the statement added.

Dar and Balakrishnan also discussed cooperation at multilateral fora and Pakistan’s enhanced engagement with Asean, particularly in the context of Singapore’s forthcoming chairmanship of the body in 2027.

Moreover, exchanging views on regional and global developments, Dar emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes and advancing lasting peace and stability, the statement said.

Delegation-level talks

Later, their opening remarks from delegation-level talks between the two sides were televised, with Dar saying that the depth of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Singapore was not reflected in economic ties.

He said his focus had been on “economic diplomacy” after joining the Foreign Office, adding: “If we work together, […] I am sure we can reach a new level of economic relations.”

The DPM further suggested the Board of Investment in Pakistan could work with its counterpart in Singapore.

He said the two countries had “great cooperation” on multilateral issues and Singapore’s interest in regional issues was “greatly appreciated”.

“You remain in touch, and we keep sharing developments with you.”

He added that the two had also discussed Palestine and Kashmir issues, among other matters, in a restricted meeting.

“So I think this friendship and great cooperation will continue from our side, and I am sure you will always reciprocate, rather go a mile ahead of us,” the DPM said.

For his part, the Singaporean foreign minister recalled that Pakistan was one of the “early countries to recognise Singapore post independence”. He pointed out that Singapore was 61 years old and was commemorating the 60th anniversary of diplomatic ties with Pakistan.

According to the FO, the delegation-level talks focused on expanding trade and investment, strengthening cooperation in agriculture and food security and enhancing connectivity to promote tourism and business exchanges.

“The two sides also explored collaboration in education, vocational training, disaster management and information technology. The Singaporean foreign minister highlighted the potential of carbon markets to attract green investment to Pakistan. Dar emphasised the importance of stronger institutional mechanisms and regular follow-up to advance mutually beneficial cooperation,” it said.

“The Ministers also exchanged views on regional and global developments. Singapore’s foreign minister commended Pakistan’s sustained efforts to promote dialogue and diplomacy in the region and its important contributions to regional peace and stability,” it added.

“Both sides agreed to build on the positive momentum generated by the visit, ensure timely follow-up on the understandings reached, and sustain engagement to further strengthen Pakistan-Singapore relations across all areas of mutual interest,” it said.

After the meeting, Dar and Balakrishnan also exchanged an MoU on cooperation in disaster management between Pakistan’s National Disaster Management Authority and the Singapore Civil Defence Force in Islamabad.

“The MoU reflects the shared commitment of Pakistan and Singapore to strengthening cooperation in disaster preparedness and response and building resilience against natural disasters,” the FO statement on the document’s exchange said.

World.title: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media
World.content:
Pakistan’s armed forces targeted and destroyed several Afghan Taliban posts and military positions in areas adjacent to South Waziristan and Parachinar, state media reported on Friday, citing security sources.

According to state-run Radio Pakistan, the army “gave a befitting reply to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban along the Pak-Afghan border in the Angoor Adda area” on Tuesday.

“Using heavy weaponry, the Pakistan Army forced Afghan Taliban personnel to abandon their posts and flee,” the report said.

Citing reports, it added that several Afghan Taliban regime personnel were also killed during the operation.

“Security forces remain committed to the defence of the country and the protection of its people and there will be no compromise on national security,” the report said.

On Tuesday, Afghan security forces opened unprovoked fire on Pakistan Army border posts and residential areas in the Angoor Adda border area, which claimed the life of one local and injured a family of five.

According to officials, the firing originated from posts located inside Afghan territory and targeted Pakistani border posts with sniper, small and heavy weapons.

Sources said that Pakistani forces launched an immediate and effective retaliatory action, engaging multiple Afghan Taliban border posts, mortar positions and defensive bunkers with small and heavy arms, including artillery.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had condemned the firing, asserting that Pakistan would “never tolerate” attacks on its people or violations of its sovereignty.

Meanwhile, Pakistan had also dismissed a statement by Afghanistan’s defence ministry regarding the incident that claimed that Pakistan was the aggressor, terming it a “fabrication of lies”.

The border at Angoor Adda is one of the most important and sensitive crossings along the Pak-Afghan border, serving as a key trade route and one of the main points of public movement between the two countries.

Pak-Afghan tensions

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the action as part of Operation Ghazab lil Haq, which was launched on the night of Feb 26 in response to unprovoked cross-border firing by the Afghan Taliban.

Days later, Pakistan shot down eight drones launched from across the border that had entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.

In retaliation for the drone incursion, Pakistan conducted “precision aerial and drone strikes” in 10 locations across Afghanistan.

A demarche was also delivered to the Afghan side on Sept 26 on account of the Sept 23 airspace violation by drones, the Foreign Office said.

On Oct 1, Pakistan again carried out “well-planned and calibrated” airstrikes against terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan, the information ministry said, adding that the strikes resulted in the deaths of “multiple terrorists”.

Around mid-October, the state media reported that security forces had again responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in KP’s Upper Kurram.

It quoted security sources as saying that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban were “reportedly killed during the Pakistan Army’s retaliatory action along the Ghuzgarhi border”. The sources further said that in the Upper Kurram sector, the army targeted the Afghan Taliban’s Topsar post and Shipola base camp with artillery fire, reportedly completely destroying the latter.

World.title: Salman Ali Agha hopes Pakistan top-order turns up in tri-series final, seeks ‘perfect game’
World.content:
Pakistan batter Salman Ali Agha believes the the side have not yet displayed a complete team performance in the ongoing One-day International tri-nation series, and hopes the final against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday is where it falls into place.

The hosts’ top-order has been notably starved of runs for the series, underscoring Pakistan’s underwhelming campaign with the bat.

“Sometimes all of your players don’t score runs. Our top order isn’t scoring runs at the moment, like they used to,” Salman said during a press conference on the eve of the match, adding that they have been key performing players for the team over the last few years.

“They haven’t performed like that in this series, but tomorrow is the final and we hope that they will.”

He added that Babar Azam and Fakhar Zaman, despite their current lean patch, have been Pakistan’s best players in ODI cricket over the last decade and that the duo were “second to none.”

“They know themselves what they need to do and what they need to work on,” Salman said. He added that Fakhar had almost always come good in knock-outs and high-stakes matches like tomorrow’s final, and was “hoping he will go big.”

Salman added that the team always discusses how to put up totals of more than 3oo, and that they needed to focus on converting innings of 50 or 6o runs to big hundreds to help them post the scores they were looking for.

The fragility of Pakistan’s top order is just one of the factors that have gone into the slightly unconvincing cricket the side has played in this series, even in the matches they have won.

Salman said that head coach Mike Hesson always emphasised playing the “perfect game”, where a team aces all of batting, bowling and fielding.

He admitted that Pakistan are yet to play one of those matches so far, with performances being punctuated with batting collapses, patches of underwhelming bowling, and “lapses” in the field.

He added that the win against England last Sunday, which was brought about on the back of a sensational 10th-wicket partnership between Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf, was one they “should have won much more easily.”

The 32-year-old added that the contributions from the young players Arafat Minhas, Hassan Nawaz and Saad Baig have been key in Pakistan’s wins, calling them “amazing and very talented players” who are the “future of Pakistan.”

When asked about what the team will seek to do to offset Sri Lanka’s incredibly strong record at Gaddafi Stadium, he said: “More than stats, it is how you play on the day that decides who will win.”

“Whichever team plays well will win.”

Pakistan have been under considerable scrutiny for the elements that have been lacking this series.

However, Salman does not believe those are for a lack of trying or seriousness, especially in response to criticism about him being too relaxed.

“I am playing for Pakistan, how is it possible that I will not be serious about it? I am part of the eleven people representing a population of 25 crore.”

“I made my debut at the age of 28 or 29, and I played domestic cricket for 10 years. I know how I have reached to this stage, and to reach this point and not take it seriously is beyond me.

“Yes, you can say that my shot selection in the last three games has not been what it should be, and I admit that and I am working on it.”

When asked about how much rope out-of-form players should be given in the side, he said a “decent amount of games” that would give them a chance to “overcome” periods of failure is crucial.

“To make runs in international cricket and be consistently successful is not an easy thing to do,” he said, adding that settling into it took time and youngsters brought into the side should be given ample opportunity.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia agree to boost cooperation in oil, refineries and minerals
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed on Friday to strengthen strategic cooperation in oil storage, refinery upgrades, crude oil and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) procurement, and the minerals sector to promote bilateral economic ties, according to a statement issued by the Petroleum Division.

Saudi Arabia also announced the immediate introduction of same-day visa processing for Pakistani citizens at its embassy in Islamabad.

Pakistan has been planning to boost domestic storage for crude oil and refined products to increase its energy security. With no strategic petroleum reserves, the country has been left exposed to oil supply shocks resulting from the US-Iran war that has choked supplies through the Strait of Hormuz .

The developments were announced after Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik met Saudi Arabia’s new ambassador to Pakistan, Dr Rajeh bin Tami Al-Baqami, to discuss opportunities for enhancing cooperation in the mining, petroleum and energy sectors, including strategic oil storage, refinery upgrades, LPG supplies and commercial engagement.

The minister appreciated the longstanding strategic partnership between the two countries and said Pakistan had approved a tax-neutral bonded policy modelled on international energy hubs such as Fujairah and Singapore, according to the statement.

“Under this framework, Saudi companies can establish commercial oil reserves in Pakistan without local tax liabilities, offering an opportunity to diversify maritime transit risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab while facilitating access to Asian markets,” the statement said.

“The petroleum minister highlighted that strategic oil storage facilities in Pakistan would provide Saudi Arabia with greater flexibility in managing supply routes and accessing regional markets,” it added.

The statement further quoted the minister as saying that Pakistan planned to develop a major petroleum storage and refining complex at Hub in Balochistan under the guidance of Technip Energies UK.

“The proposed facility, supported by the prime minister and the chief of defence forces, will have the capacity to accommodate Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) and strengthen Pakistan’s potential as a regional energy corridor serving Central Asian and Chinese markets,” the statement quoted Malik as saying.

Malik also briefed the ambassador on investment opportunities under Pakistan’s ongoing refinery upgradation programme, which aims to modernise domestic refining infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and facilitate a transition to Euro-5 fuel standards.

He said the programme offered significant opportunities for Saudi investment and participation in Pakistan’s refining sector.

Appreciating Saudi Arabia’s support during recent global market disruptions, the minister thanked the Saudi authorities at Yanbu port for prioritising crude oil shipments to Pakistan.

He also discussed coordination with Saudi Aramco to increase crude oil procurement and arrange dedicated LPG shipments to meet Pakistan’s energy needs, particularly amid an anticipated rise in domestic gas demand during winter.

Both sides underscored that the strong defence and strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia provides a foundation for broader regional peace, stability and economic cooperation.

The Saudi envoy expressed Riyadh’s deep appreciation for Pakistan’s longstanding support, saying the two countries stood together in all circumstances.

The ambassador emphasised that the two countries’ defence and energy cooperation frameworks aimed to promote peace, stability and economic growth across the region.

The minister also announced that the Saudi embassy in Islamabad had introduced same-day processing of visa applications for Pakistani citizens to facilitate travel and strengthen business, cultural and people-to-people exchanges.

Malik invited Saudi Arabia’s Vice Minister of Mining, Khalid al-Mudafier, to attend the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, scheduled to be held in Islamabad on November 12 and 13, highlighting further opportunities for cooperation and investment in Pakistan’s minerals sector.

Both sides expressed their commitment to strengthening their longstanding relationship through enhanced cooperation, investment and mutually beneficial partnerships in the energy and petroleum sectors.

The minister assured the ambassador that Pakistan deeply valued its historic relationship with Saudi Arabia and remained committed to expanding cooperation across strategic sectors.

Earlier in July, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed authorities to increase the country’s strategic petroleum reserves as a cabinet committee approved amendments to the oil refining policy.

World.title: 'I will never go back to sea': 11 fishermen released from Indian captivity reunite with families in Karachi
World.content:
KARACHI: 11 Pakistani fishermen, after spending several years in Indian jails for unknowingly crossing over to Indian waters while fishing, were reunited with their families in Karachi on Friday morning.

The men were handed over through the Wagah Border by Indian authorities some two months ago. On Friday, the Edhi Foundation brought them from Lahore to Karachi by ambulance. They arrived at 11:30am at the Edhi Centre near Merewether Tower, where their families had been waiting since morning.

It was a touching reunion where the fishermen, having been jailed for between four and nine years, finally met their families.

Some, like Kamal Hassan Bengali of Machhar Colony, who was in jail in India for eight years, returned to meet new family members. But his eyes grew moist knowing that his mother would not be there to greet him when he got home.

“The day our boat was captured by the Indian coast guard was the day my mother passed away. I only learned about her passing through a letter which reached me three years later,” Kamal told Dawn, as he held his eight-year-old niece Areeba close.

“I am meeting her (Areeba) for the first time,” he added, smiling through tears.

Pakistani fishermen reunite with families at Edhi Centre on October 30. — White Star/ Fahim Siddiqi

Asked how his boat crossed over to the other side, he said that they experienced an engine failure, following which the boat drifted towards Indian waters.

All of Kamal’s seven brothers and his sister have gotten married in the last eight years. His sister Manzoora told Dawn that with their mother gone, the responsibility of finding a good match for him now fell on her shoulders.

“I will get him married soon now that he is back home,” she said.

Noor Nabi Bengali, also of Machhar Colony, who was also with Kamal on the same boat, recalled their days in Indian captivity with sadness.

“We were given bad food. The lentils and plain rice or the potato and cauliflower curry that we were fed in jail would stink sometimes because it had gone bad,” he said.

Khamiso Siddiq Mallah from Shah Bandar said that he spent almost four years in Indian captivity. Now 60, he said that he has no intention of returning to fishing now that he is back.

“I will become a labourer, but I will never go back to sea,” he said.

Abdul Rehman of Korangi said that he was in jail in India for nine years.

“I don’t remember the name of my boat,” he said when asked its name.

Pakistani fishermen reunite with families at Edhi Centre on October 30. — White Star/ Fahim Siddiqi

“I only remember the horrible jail food and the lonely days I spent behind bars in India,” he shared.

“The attitude of the jail staff toward us Pakistanis never let me forget for a minute that we were in an enemy country. They treated us worse than animals.”

Mehboob Ali Mullah of Badin, who was in jail for three-and-a-half years, said that he could not wait to see his children.

“My journey doesn’t end here. I still have to travel to my village in Badin,” he said. “I have three children back home whom I cannot wait to see.”

Basheer of Machhar Colony said that he only knew how to fish, so he could not stop doing that if he wants to earn a livelihood.

“But what I’ll do is not ever fish in Sindh. I’ll fish in Balochistan, which doesn’t touch the Indian border,” he said.

“Now that I’m back in my country, I will eat good, healthy food to gain back the 70 pounds that I lost while in Indian jail,” he added.

Pakistani fishermen reunite with families at Edhi Centre on October 30. — White Star/ Fahim Siddiqi

Meanwhile, Saleem Sabro from Thatta, who has been looking for his missing fisherman brother for five years, came to give Basheer a good look.

“He looks like my brother Ahmed Ali,” he told Dawn, explaining, “I come here whenever Pakistani fishermen return from India to see if my brother might be among them.

“Among the fishermen released last year, I came across one who had information about my brother. He told me that he was in a jail in Ahmedabad,” he shared.
